  • Calm Mind increases Tapu Fini's Special Attack and Special Defense by one stage, which can turn it into a potent wincon that is able to clean through teams with limited ways to break it.
  • Muddy Water is Tapu Fini's Water-type STAB move and is preferred over Scald for its ability to threaten two Pokemon at once. It also has a small chance to reduce the foe's accuracy, which is nifty while Tapu Fini is setting up.
  • Moonblast is a reliable Fairy-type STAB move that threatens Dragon-, Dark-, and Fighting-types. It can also cause Special Attack drops, which helps with setting up.
  • Protect keeps Tapu Fini safe from potential double targets and gives it a free turn of Leftovers recovery.
  • Scald can be used if Muddy Water's accuracy is a hindrance for you, but it should be noted that Tapu Fini can't burn grounded foes while Misty Terrain is active.

Set Details

  • 252 HP EVs and 116 Defense EVs allows Tapu Fini to survive maximum Attack Jolly Kartana's Leaf Blade and makes Arcanine's maximum Attack Wild Charge a 3HKO.
  • The 140 leftover EVs are placed into Special Defense to enable Tapu Fini to stomach a Sludge Bomb from Life Orb Nihilego and Life Orb Thunder from Tapu Koko outside of Electric Terrain.
  • If you desire a faster variant then an EV spread of 252 HP / 12 Def / 244 Spe is viable, as it enables Tapu Fini to outspeed Adamant maximum Speed Arcanine and Timid maximum Speed Xurkitree. However, this gives Tapu Fini significantly less physical bulk and gives Kartana a strong chance to OHKO with Leaf Blade.
  • Leftovers provides passive recovery to keep Tapu Fini healthy for the long haul.
  • Aguav Berry can be used to heal 50% of Tapu Fini's health should it be brought below 25%.

Usage Tips

  • This Tapu Fini set is designed to stay on the field and slowly win games, so you have to play very conservative with it.
  • Tapu Fini's natural bulk and typing allows it to switch in on many threats, but try to avoid coming in on strong neutral attacks, as you'll want Tapu Fini's HP as high as possible.
  • It's important that Tapu Fini stays as healthy as possible because it lacks a form of reliable recovery outside of Leftovers or a certain Z-Move.
  • Tapu Fini should be sent out when its counters are either not on the field or are checked by one of Tapu Fini's partners.
  • Tapu Fini often doesn't need too many Calm Mind boosts to win a game so just setting up one or two will be enough.
  • Avoid setting up Calm Minds versus Pokemon that can deal a lot of damage to Tapu Fini and instead use that time to either get an attack off, use Protect, or even just switch out.
  • Keep in mind that even with Special Attack boosts Tapu Fini still isn't dishing out too much damage until you have about four or five.
  • Be wary of Toxic users if your opponent has ways of removing Misty Terrain.

Team Options

  • Arcanine is a staple partner for Tapu Fini, as it provides much needed Intimidate support, which eases the stress from physical attackers. It's also one of the best answers to Kartana in the format because it can OHKO it with a Fire-type move, which is a huge blessing for Tapu Fini.
  • Garchomp works well with Tapu Fini, as it is one of the few Pokemon in the format that can reliably counter Alolan Muk with Tectonic Rage.
  • Kartana is a valuable partner, as it can reliably take on opposing Tapu Fini, which makes winning the mirror matchup a lot easier. Tapu Fini also keeps Arcanine in check, which Kartana very much appreciates.
  • Eevee is an interesting partner, as Tapu Fini is a fantastic recipient of Extreme Evoboost because of its stellar bulk being boosted even further and its solid type coverage being complemented by the +2 Special Attack boost. Misty Terrain also prevents the opponent from slowing down the Extreme Evoboost strategy with status.
  • While Tapu Koko can remove Tapu Fini's Misty Terrain, it is a good partner that can take on faster threats like Garchomp, Gengar, and Kartana before they can do any damage to Tapu Fini.

Choice Specs.description:
Moves

  • Hydro Pump is Tapu Fini's strongest STAB move and can plow through many opponents with its impressive power.
  • Scald is a safer alternative to Hydro Pump for when you want perfect accuracy but comes at the cost of significantly less power.
  • Muddy Water is Tapu Fini's secondary STAB move, which is good for doing decent damage to both foes at the same time along with having a chance to lower their accuracy.
  • Moonblast is Tapu Fini's most consistent STAB option, which will always OHKO non-Assault Vest Garchomp.
  • Dazzling Gleam is likely the move that Tapu Fini will use the least, as it is the weaker spread move but doesn't have the chance to miss and can hit Pokemon that resist Muddy Water.
  • Ice Beam is an option if you want to do more damage to Tapu Bulu, and it also OHKOes non-Assault Vest Kartana.

Set Details

  • Maximum Special Attack with a Modest nature is necessary to hit as hard as possible
  • Maximum HP is used in order to stick around as long as possible to get off more attacks.
  • Choice Specs amplifies Tapu Fini's damage output so that it can pick up KOs that it normally is unable to.
  • This spread has no Speed investment because Tapu Fini can't outspeed much around its Speed tier without too much investment, which would cut away from its bulk and power.
  • However, if you want a faster spread, then 156 HP / 252 SpA / 100 Spe is an option to outspeed maximum Speed Pelipper and Magnezone.

Usage Tips

  • While this Tapu Fini set is meant to be played more aggressively, you should still avoid being too reckless.
  • This Tapu Fini set has significantly less physical bulk, meaning that it's more threatened by the likes of Tectonic Rage Garchomp, Wild Charge Arcanine, and Kartana.
  • Try to find an opening against two Pokemon that can't threaten Tapu Fini too much, so that Tapu Fini can come in and start firing off boosted attacks.
  • Choice Specs Tapu Fini also works pretty well as a lead, since the lack of Speed means that it's more likely to activate Misty Terrain versus another island guardian.
  • Try to avoid spamming Muddy Water against more offensively inclined teams, since a miss will be hugely detrimental. Dazzling Gleam and Hydro Pump are more helpful in these matchups.
  • Muddy Water is more useful against defensive teams that can't handle Tapu Fini too well so that you can stick around longer and harass with accuracy drops.

Team Options

  • Arcanine is a solid partner for Choice Specs Tapu Fini, as Intimidate support keeps it a bit safer against physical attackers. Arcanine also possesses Helping Hand to further increase Tapu Fini's damage output.
  • Ninetales is a fine partner that can provide Aurora Veil to buff up Tapu Fini's bulk and Icy Wind to provide much-needed speed control.
  • Kartana is again a solid partner, as it excels at eliminating most Water-type Pokemon, which makes it much easier for Tapu Fini to consistently fire off Muddy Water and Hydro Pump. It's also very good at beating down on Snorlax and Chansey, which Tapu Fini struggles against.
  • Even with the Choice Specs boost, Tapu Fini still struggles against Alolan Muk, which makes Garchomp a good partner. Tectonic Rage + boosted Fairy-type attacks can also do incredible damage to opposing teams and is very difficult to switch into.

doublesou.overview: Tapu Fini leverages its great defensive typing and stats to secure a place at the forefront of the Doubles metagame. Though Tapu Fini is the only Island Guardian whose summoned Terrain doesn't boost the power of its attacks, its ability to block status and weaken Dragon-type attacks on grounded targets is still quite useful. With a solid movepool that contains useful attacks and utility moves alike, Tapu Fini has every tool it would need to thrive, save for a recovery move. As a result, Tapu Fini can end up being worn down somewhat easily. Tapu Fini is also a bit weak unless it's accrued a Calm Mind boost or two, but its STAB attacks are super effective on large metagame threats like Zygarde, Landorus-T, and Incineroar, so Tapu Fini fits onto most teams quite easily.
doublesou.comments:
Other Options

Tapu Fini has a fairly wide movepool with varyingly viable options. Ice Beam might seem like an odd pick when its STAB combination already hits the most common targets, Landorus-T, Zygarde, and Mega Salamence, super effectively; however, it does considerably more damage without needing a boost and also hits Amoonguss and Tapu Bulu. Choice Scarf Tapu Fini might seem a bit out of place, but when used in conjunction with Soak and a strong Electric- or Grass-type like Tapu Koko or Kartana, it can be quite valuable. Soak also has the benefit of removing the STAB bonus from foes' attacks, making them weaker. Assault Vest is another slightly strange item choice, but it fits well with Tapu Fini's access to Icy Wind and decent moves to pair it with such as its STAB attacks, Nature's Madness, Hidden Power Fire, and Knock Off; the result is a highly specially defensive Tapu Fini set with utility in speed control, Knock Off, Nature's Madness, and some decent coverage. A Choice Specs set provides considerably more damage output with Tapu Fini's decent coverage through its STAB attacks and Ice Beam, but Tapu Fini still struggles to hit neutral targets hard.

Checks and Counters

Grass-types: In addition to resisting Muddy Water, many common Grass-types also resist Moonblast, and all can hit Tapu Fini hard in return. Amoonguss, though its Spore is blocked by Misty Terrain, can be especially frustrating to handle, with Clear Smog even removing Tapu Fini's Calm Mind boosts. Tapu Bulu can use Tapu Fini to heal up with Horn Leech and typically runs sets with enough special bulk to take even a boosted Moonblast. Ferrothorn also resists Moonblast and hits physically, avoiding any potential Calm Mind boosts attempting to shield Tapu Fini from damage.

Electric-types: Tapu Fini is weak to STAB Electric-type attacks, and Z-Moves can KO even from full health. Tapu Koko, Mega Manectric, Zeraora, and Electric-type coverage users like Kyurem-B and Mega Metagross are all threatening, though none resist Tapu Fini's STAB combination, and they must fear a boosted Tapu Fini with speed control on its side.

Taunt: Losing Protect and either Heal Pulse or Calm Mind access can be a big momentum drain, and Tapu Fini can't hit most Taunt users like Tapu Lele and Gothitelle very hard.

Redirection: Heal Pulse becomes a liability instead of a tool if redirected. Amoonguss, the most common redirector, also doesn't take much from Tapu Fini's attacks anyway.

Support.description:
Moves

Nature's Madness offers consistent damage on foes that normally switch in on Tapu Fini for free like Chansey and Amoonguss, chipping enemies in range of a more offensive ally's attack. Moonblast is Tapu Fini's best Fairy-type STAB attack, helping it deal with threats such as Zygarde and Kommo-o offensively. Heal Pulse is Tapu Fini's most commonly valuable support move, either aiding a setup user like Mega Scizor in preparation for a sweep or simply keeping an important teammate healthy. Taunt stops slow setup Pokemon like Cresselia and foes trying to set Trick Room. Protect shields Tapu Fini from damage and allows it to scout the opponent's moves, stall out certain field effects, and retain solid positioning.

Icy Wind offers some speed control that also deals decent damage to Landorus-T. Scald is most notable for taking out Mega Camerupt, a threat that few Pokemon in the meta can claim to tank a hit from and return with a KO. Though Misty Terrain blocks its ability to burn foes, levitating enemies are still susceptible. Defog aids Stealth Rock-weak allies like Volcarona and Mega Charizard Y. Each of these three moves could go anywhere in Tapu Fini's moveset, but Nature's Madness should find its way on most all sets. So, Icy Wind would often replace Moonblast or Protect, Scald usually replaces Moonblast, and Defog takes the third moveslot.

Set Details

The given spread allows Tapu Fini to take less than 50% from Mega Metagross's Iron Head. With 132 EVs in Special Attack, Tapu Fini's Moonblast OHKOes an omni-boosted Kommo-o. The remainder of the EVs are dumped in Special Defense. A Wiki Berry provides significant healing to a weakened Tapu Fini, lessening the impact of it failing to learn any recovery moves. Sets with Scald in place of Moonblast can instead use a spread of 252 HP / 32 Def / 80 SpA / 36 SpD with a Calm nature, which retains the defensive benchmark but instead offers enough power to OHKO Mega Camerupt with Scald. If Tapu Fini is using Icy Wind, 16 Speed EVs are all it needs to outrun a -1 Kyurem-B.

Usage Tips

Tapu Fini functions best on bulky offense teams, keeping threatening teammates healthy and providing role compression by checking a variety of threats in one team member. Use Tapu Fini's defensive typing to switch into threatening Pokemon like Kommo-o and Kingdra, pivoting in to either threaten super effective damage or heal up an ally. If you're predicting an incoming status move like Spore or Hypnosis, switch Tapu Fini in to nullify its effect. However, keep in mind that non-grounded Pokemon aren't affected by Misty Terrain and won't be shielded from status effects. Heal Pulse is best used on teammates with setup moves or those that are especially bulky, as frail Pokemon rarely benefit from having a bit more health. Tapu Fini's damage output can be disappointing, so it should generally only attack when the move will hit super effectively. The main exception to this would be to use Icy Wind to pick off one weakened foe and chip the other. Don't use Heal Pulse if the opponent has a redirection user such as Amoonguss or Volcarona on the field, as they can steal the effect and cause your move to be detrimental.

Team Options

A wide variety of teams can benefit from Tapu Fini's presence due to its generally solid matchups and easily usable support. Teams with bulky setup Pokemon such as Mega Scizor and Mega Tyranitar that can take advantage of Heal Pulse support and the prevention of status effects will especially appreciate having this Tapu Fini as a teammate. Dragon-type Pokemon that don't use Dragon-type moves themselves, such as Kyurem-B and Zygarde, benefit from the weakening of opposing Dragon-type moves to keep them healthy. Tapu Fini doesn't need much in return from its team, but a teammate to beat Grass-types is essential, making Mega Scizor, Incineroar, and Heat Wave Zapdos solid picks. Zapdos can also use a Misty Seed set to pair with Tapu Fini and boost its staying power. Tapu Fini also has trouble breaking through opposing bulky Water-types like Volcanion and Suicune, making Zapdos an even better partner. Mega Charizard Y and Volcarona also roast Grass-type foes, and Defog Tapu Fini sets ensure they can enter the field without taking Stealth Rock damage. Landorus-T and Assault Vest Kyurem-B can aid Tapu Fini by threatening Electric-types.

Calm Mind.description:
Moves

Dealing damage to both foes is a valuable asset for setup users in Doubles, so Muddy Water is a crucial part of this set. Potential accuracy drops can also ease setup. Moonblast is Tapu Fini's strongest attack for neutral targets. It also does respectable damage even unboosted, KOing Mega Salamence after Stealth Rock damage. Calm Mind opens the door for Tapu Fini to either break through or clean the opposing team while also improving its staying power by boosting its already decent Special Defense. With Calm Mind, Tapu Fini also forces the opponent to respond by making itself significantly more threatening. Protect keeps Tapu Fini safe while its teammate takes out a threat or sets a useful field effect. It's an essential move in Doubles for ease of positioning, but it also allows Tapu Fini to stall for Leftovers recovery and improve its ability to take a hit.

Set Details

The Defense investment makes sure Tapu Fini will avoid the 2HKO from Mega Metagross's Iron Head. The remaining investment is used to improve Tapu Fini's ability to do damage. If Tapu Fini's being used on a team with Tailwind support, you may want to move 60 EVs from Special Attack to Speed so that it outruns Pheromosa under Tailwind. With Leftovers, Tapu Fini can lower its Defense investment to 72 EVs with a Modest nature and still retain the defensive benchmarks. However, Wiki Berry tends to provide considerably more recovery than the slow drip of HP from Leftovers, giving Tapu Fini a second chance to act as a switch-in.

Usage Tips

This set functions best on bulkier teams that need Tapu Fini's positive matchups but can't afford the passivity of support sets. There are two main times Tapu Fini can benefit from using Calm Mind: to put pressure on early-game or clean up late-game. If Tapu Fini provides your best chance to finish off your opponent's team in the end, avoid letting it take unnecessary damage early on, since this set has limited recovery. However, this set otherwise operates similarly to more support-focused sets. That is, Tapu Fini acts as a solid defensive pivot against some popular attackers like Incineroar and Zygarde while also using its Misty Terrain to block incoming status moves like Hypnosis and Spore.

Team Options

Grass-types are Tapu Fini's biggest obstacles for cleaning, so it needs a teammate to take on Ferrothorn, Amoonguss, and Tapu Bulu. Incineroar takes these on and also provides Fake Out support to ease setup. Other options for this role include Kyurem-B and Heat Wave Zapdos, which also provides speed control and offers Tapu Fini a way to break through bulky Water-types. Intimidate support helps Tapu Fini cushion the attacks that won't become weaker after it uses Calm Mind, and the common Intimidate users also offer valuable additional roles. In addition to the aforementioned Incineroar, Landorus-T beats Electric-types, Mega Salamence defeats Grass-types, and Mega Manectric can help against both Grass-types and bulky Water-types.

battlespotsingles.overview:
Tapu Fini has a fantastic typing offensively and defensively, with its Fairy-typing giving it a big selling point over other Water-types, giving it a Dragon-type immunity and a Fighting-type resist. While Misty Terrain isn't as game defining as the other Terrains, preventing status and weakening Dragon-type attacks is still very useful overall, especially on something as bulky as Tapu Fini. Tapu Fini's bulk and typing also makes it one of the best Blaziken answers in the metagame. However, Tapu Fini's offensive stats aren't that great, and it can have trouble competing with Suicune due to worse bulk.

Below are some sample sets. These sets are likely to be standard, but they will be expanded upon and updated as the metagame progresses.

Calm Mind.description:
• Tapu Fini is bulky enough to pull off a Calm Mind set, with Surf and Moonblast working well as complementary STAB attacks.
  • Surf is better than Scald, since Misty Terrain blocks burns, thus Surf's higher base power is superior.
  • Mist with Icium Z give Tapu Fini one chance to fully restore its health with Z-Mist.
  • Hidden Power Fire allows Tapu Fini to deal good damage to Ferrothorn.
  • Taunt is useful for shutting down recovery against bulky Pokemon such as Cresselia and Porygon2.
  • Sitrus is a reliable way to restore some health, but Iapapa Berry is a riskier alternative that restores more health when Tapu Fini reaches 25% of its HP.
  • The given EV spread ensures Tapu Fini outspeeds Jolly Alolan Marowak while giving it maximum bulk otherwise.
  • Don't be too reckless with Tapu Fini switch-ins, because while it might be bulky, it has no consistent, reliable recovery.
  • Make sure to pack in resists for Electric, Grass, and Poison-type Pokemon, as these are the kind of Pokemon that can bust through Tapu Fini's bulk.

Offensive.description:
• Nature's Madness and Z-Hydro Pump can blast through major defensive Pokemon together, such as Porygon2 and Cresselia. Z-Hydro Pump notably OHKOes Tapu Koko.
  • Moonblast is a reliable STAB that slams Dragon-types.
  • Hidden Power Fire KOs Ferrothorn after it switches into Nature's Madness.
  • Calm Mind gives Tapu Fini the power to defeat Cresselia even if it restores its health with Sitrus Berry, while Taunt shuts down recovery, letting Tapu Fini defeat defensive Pokemon even after using Z-Hydro Pump. Haze helps against Moody Pokemon and Extreme Evoboost Eevee chains.
  • The given EV spread outspeeds Jolly Alolan Marowak while giving Tapu Fini a good amount of bulk and power.
  • This Tapu Fini excels at blasting through defensive Pokemon, so consider pairing it with sweepers that can take advantage of these holes.
  • Prepare Pokemon that resists Grass-, Electric-, and Poison-type attacks, since these are commonly aimed at Tapu Fini.

cap.overview:
With good bulk and access to reliable recovery in Synthesis, Pyroak is a decent defensive Pokemon in the metagame. Its Fire / Grass typing gives it resistances to common Steel-, Electric-, Grass-, and Fairy-type Pokemon like Magearna, Jumbao, Necturna, Ferrothorn, and Celesteela while also making it one of few reliable stops to Dragon Dance Naviathan, Krilowatt, Tapu Koko, Swords Dance Caribolt, and Mega Mawile.

However, Pyroak is susceptible to every entry hazard, meaning it can be worn down quickly through repeated switches and can be troublesome to get into play. The weakness to Stealth Rock is particularly hazardous, as it significantly cuts into Pyroak's bulk and makes it much easier for Pokemon such as Colossoil and Hoopa-U to break through it. Furthermore, common Flying-, Rock-, and Poison-type attackers such as Tomohawk, Tornadus-T, Mega Tyranitar, and Mega Crucibelle can consistently force it out with their super effective attacks. Pyroak faces competition from Ferrothorn as a bulky Grass-type, which has an overall better defensive typing and offers Spikes. Finally, Pyroak fails to consistently set Stealth Rock due to the presence of Tornadus-T in the metagame.
cap.comments:
Other Options

Aromatherapy can be used to remove harmful status effects like burns and Toxic poison from teammates and Pyroak itself, but it generally struggles to find a moveslot for it. Will-O-Wisp is an option to spread burns to physical attackers much more reliably than Lava Plume, but it also competes with Pyroak's other moveslot heavily.

Checks and Counters

Residual Damage: Stealth Rock deals heavy damage to Pyroak as it switches in, cutting into its survivability as a defensive Pokemon and making it much easier for attackers to OHKO or 2HKO it. Toxic also cuts into Pyroak's bulk by placing it on a timer, although it can be remedied through Aromatherapy.

Pajantom: Pajantom is completely immune to burns and poison from Pyroak thanks to Comatose, can disable Pyroak's recovery with Heal Block, and can trap it with Spirit Shackle, leaving Pyroak helpless to a Z-Move or Toxic damage.

Flying-types: Tomohawk and Tornadus-T can easily take Pyroak's attacks and force it out with their super effective Flying-type attacks while also being able to heal off damage with Roost and Regenerator, respectively. Cawmodore, Mega Pinsir, Landorus-T, and Hawlucha can threaten it out with their Flying-type STAB when boosted, but they cannot set up on it directly because of Lava Plume.

Mega Tyranitar: Mega Tyranitar is bulky enough to take any attack from Pyroak reliably, can force it out with the threat of Stone Edge and chip it with Pursuit, and can significantly cut into its recovery thanks to Sand Stream. Keep in mind, however, that it does not like being burned by Lava Plume.

Poison-types: Mega Crucibelle and Mollux can threaten out Pyroak with their super effective Poison-type attacks and are immune to Toxic. Mollux in particular is also immune to burns and tanks Lava Plume reliably. However, they both fear Earth Power, and Mega Crucibelle does not like to be burned.

Setup Sweepers Setup sweepers such as Calm Mind Clefable, Tapu Lele, Mega Latias, and Quiver Dance Volcarona can use it as setup bait.

Fire-types: While it must be wary of Earth Power, Heatran can switch into any of Pyroak's other attacks and shut it down with Taunt. Choice Specs Volkraken can threaten Pyroak out with its strong STAB attacks, but it can't take Earth Power repeatedly.

Defensive.description:
Moves

Earth Power lets Pyroak hit Pokemon like Mega Crucibelle and Heatran super effectively. Pyroak is a very unreliable Stealth Rock setter, as its typing leaves it weak to Tornadus-T and most other hazard setters, but it can be run if there's no space to fit it elsewhere. Leech Seed can be used instead if one of Pyroak's teammates already provide this role, allowing Pyroak to passively sap away a foe's health and overall increasing Pyroak's longevity throughout the match.

Set Details

248 HP and 252 Defense EVs with a Bold nature help maximize Pyroak's physical bulk, allowing it to wall Pokemon such as Dragon Dance Naviathan, Kartana, and Caribolt. Alternatively, 248 HP EVs and 252 Special Defense EVs with a Calm nature can be used to maximize Pyroak's special bulk, helping it better take attacks from Magearna and Ash-Greninja.

Usage Tips

Switch Pyroak into resisted hits from Pokemon such as Tapu Koko, Ferrothorn, Kartana, Caribolt, and Magearna and use their switches to pressure the opposing team. Pyroak should pressure switch-ins by appropriately using Toxic, Leech Seed, and Lava Plume as they come in. Pyroak is quite vulnerable to entry hazards, so it is important to use your entry hazard remover carefully, keeping it alive to consistently get Pyroak into battle safely. If a certain switch-in like Mega Crucibelle or Heatran is predicted, it is advised to use the appropriate coverage move to deal super effective damage to them.

Team Options

Pyroak requires the removal of entry hazards from the field, particularly Stealth Rock, to maintain its longevity. Thus, Defog users such as Tornadus-T and Zapdos are appreciated. They also appreciate Pyroak's ability to threaten common switch-ins to them. Electric-types like Krilowatt, Zapdos, and Tapu Koko make good partners, as they can check dangerous Flying-types like Tornadus-T, as well as Water-types such as Arghonaut, for Pyroak while it removes Ferrothorn and Jumbao, which can otherwise stop them cold. Pyroak is a potent stop to Fairy-types such as Tapu Koko and Jumbao, so Pokemon that like them removed such as Colossoil, Tomohawk, Pajantom, and Mega Latios appreciate the support that Pyroak gives.

cap.overview: While Voodoom has access to Nasty Plot and sits in a respectable Speed tier, it faces many problems in the metagame. Voodoom needs a boost to hit anything appreciable, still doesn't hit especially hard after a boost, and doesn't have the bulk to set up multiple boosts, so it's hard to really get much damage off with it. Voodoom's STAB attacks also cannot break past setup deterrents like Arghonaut, Tomohawk, and Toxapex, meaning that sometimes it cannot even set up safely. Additionally, its abilities aren't particularly useful, as most Electric-types have some way to break through its average bulk. Thus, Voodoom is pretty much outclassed by every basically any relevant special attacker in the metagame. Not only do they have a better Special Attack stat, but they also provide their teams with better utility. For example, Tapu Lele provides Terrain control and has better STAB attacks, Ash-Greninja has access to Spikes and exerts more pressure with Battle Bond, Hoopa-U simply breaks defensive cores more easily, and Mega Alakazam has much more speed and access to Recover. Quiver Dance Aurumoth, Quiver Dance Volcarona, and Shift Gear Magearna are better special sweepers than Voodoom, as they can break open at least some of the aforementioned setup deterrents. Thus, Voodoom has no niche in the metagame.
cap.comments:
Other Options

Because the listed set is barely viable as is, Voodoom has no other options.

Checks and Counters

Faster Pokemon: Pokemon that can outspeed Voodoom are the easiest way to get rid of it. Tornadus-T, Choice Band Syclant, Greninja, Mega Crucibelle, Mega Alakazam, Choice Scarf Jumbao, and Choice Scarf Volkraken are some examples of Pokemon that can OHKO it or neuter Voodom's attempt at accomplishing anything.

Setup Deterrents: Unaware Arghonaut and Haze Tomohawk and Toxapex discourage Voodoom from setting up at all, and they wall it even if it tries to set up, meaning Voodoom is a complete liability until these Pokemon are removed.

Fairy-types: Although Voodoom has access to Flash Cannon, most Fairy-types like Clefable, Tapu Lele, Jumbao, and Tapu Bulu can tank an unboosted Flash Cannon and OHKO it back.

Bulky Pokemon: Other bulkier Pokemon like Celesteela, Magearna, and Revenankh can tank Voodoom's moves and KO it.

Nasty Plot.description:
Moves

After a Nasty Plot boost, Flash Cannon OHKOes Jumbao and Clefable. Thunderbolt and Psychic are alternative options that can break open Arghonaut, Toxapex, and Tomohawk, but then Voodoom is walled by Fairy-types.

Set Details

Life Orb is used to boost Voodoom's paltry offense to an acceptable level. While it could run a Z-Crystal, it's not worth using it on Voodoom over a teammate that can make better use of it.

Usage Tips

The best Voodoom can do is try to switch in early- to mid-game and try to wear down the opposing team. Switching into Choice Specs Tapu Koko's Volt Switch, Caribolt's Return, or Krilowatt's Thunderbolt allows Voodoom to get into play for free. If Voodoom can't safely set up a Nasty Plot and fire off an attack, it's better off double switching out, as using Nasty Plot will waste a turn. If the opponent's switch-in is bulky Jumbao or Clefable, set up to +2 and use Flash Cannon to lure and remove them.

Team Options

Dual screens Tapu Koko lets Voodoom set up more easily. Other setup sweepers like Aurumoth, Naviathan, Caribolt, and Hawlucha fit alongside Voodoom on this archetype. Stealth Rock setters like Focus Sash Landorus-T and Flyinium Z Tomohawk can help Voodoom break through opposing Pokemon more easily. Spikes setters such as Ash-Greninja, Ferrothorn, and Arghonaut can also help Voodoom achieve KOs. Voodoom can also make use of Sticky Web support from Ribombee, as many revenge killers like Choice Scarf Volkraken, Tapu Koko, and Ash-Greninja fail to outspeed it after the Speed drop. However, Voodoom allows Tornadus-T to switch in and use Defog freely, as even Thunderbolt doesn't OHKO Tornadus-T.

cap.overview: Jumbao is an incredibly diverse and powerful choice for any balance or offense team, SM CAP's defining Pokemon. Its excellent typing and bulk allow it to single-handedly check many dominant threats such as Mega Tyranitar, Ash-Greninja, and Caribolt. Trace and high Special Attack let it play both defensively and offensively. Trace gives Jumbao incredible flexibility, letting it switch freely into Heatran lacking Toxic and Steel-type coverage while exploiting common abilities like Regenerator, Swift Swim, and Beast Boost. Although Jumbao is checked by two common defensive pivots in Tornadus-T and Toxapex, it can still plow through many teams with its powerful attacks and outstanding bulk. Jumbao's one major downfall is its middling Speed, which leaves it vulnerable to revenge killers like Weavile and Mega Alakazam.
cap.comments:
Other Options

Jumbao can utilize a Choice Scarf alongside Healing Wish to land surprise KOs on faster Pokemon like offensive Tornadus-T, Weavile, and Tapu Koko while supporting teammates like Kartana, Mega Mawile, and Equilibra; however, this set is generally quite telegraphed.

Checks and Counters

Toxapex: Toxapex is easily able to tank any of Jumbao's attacks and threaten it with Toxic.

Tornadus-T: Tornadus-T freely switches into Jumbao's standard attacks and forces it out with Hurricane or Sludge Bomb. Offensive Tornadus-T must be wary of switching into Twinkle Tackle from offensive Jumbao. Twinkle Tackle even OHKOes defensive variants without Assault Vest after Stealth Rock.

Bulky Steel-types: Bulky Steel-types like Ferrothorn, Mega Scizor, and Equilibra counter Wish Jumbao, which reveals itself by activating Trace. Equilibra is especially effective, as it can use Jumbao to initiate Doom Desire, limiting Jumbao's future ability to get onto the field.

Specially Bulky Pokemon: Pokemon like Reuniclus, Chansey, and Gastrodon can stomach Jumbao's powerful special attacks and heal off any damage taken. Gastrodon must beware of the odd Jumbao set that runs a Grass-type attack, however.

Faster Pokemon: Weavile, Victini, Mega Pinsir, and Kartana all outspeed and threaten to OHKO Jumbao with their super effective STAB moves; however, all of them but Victini must scout to see if Jumbao is using a Choice Scarf. Other faster Pokemon like Mega Medicham and Mega Lopunny can KO Jumbao if it has been properly chipped; however, chipping Jumbao can be difficult given its access to Wish and Shore Up and its overall high bulk.

Wish.description:
Wish affords Jumbao ridiculous longevity and excellent utility, as it can easily keep itself and its teammates healthy throughout a match. Furthermore, Wish helps Jumbao's teammates switch into its few counters. Hidden Power Ground is used to hit Heatran and Toxapex super effectively. Fairium Z is the preferred item for pressuring Tornadus-T and allowing Jumbao to absorb Knock Off from Arghonaut and Gliscor; however, Pixie Plate lets a teammate be the Z-Move user without compromising Jumbao's offensive presence. The given EVs allow it to outspeed Hoopa-U while almost always 2HKOing Heatran after Stealth Rock with Hidden Power Ground.

Due to Jumbao's excellent bulk and versatility, it fits well on pretty much any team archetype that is not stall or hyper offense. Equilibra and Toxapex are excellent defensive options that both appreciate Jumbao easing their switches in with Wish. Equilibra notably pressures Poison-types like Toxapex with Earth Power, while Toxapex can switch into Tornadus-T. Tornadus-T itself is a good teammate for Jumbao, as it can switch into Steel-types like Equilibra and Ferrothorn, while Jumbao can pressure Mega Tyranitar for it. Mega Alakazam pressures faster Pokemon, and it notably forces Toxapex out. Reuniclus and Tapu Lele are other Psychic-types that pair well with Jumbao, pressuring Steel-types with Focus Blast; Tapu Lele additionally enjoys Jumbao's Wish. Weavile is another good choice for a fast partner, as it can hit Reuniclus and Celesteela particularly hard. Celesteela, Mega Tyranitar, and Heatran all appreciate the Wish support Jumbao provides; Mega Tyranitar is particularly notable, as its sand increases Shore Up's recovery.

Offensive.description:
Jumbao can use its near-perfect coverage and high Special Attack to run a more offensive set. Flame Burst hits Steel-types like Ferrothorn, Equilibra, Celesteela, and Magearna hard. Hidden Power Ground hits Heatran quite hard and also KOes Toxapex if it has been chipped sufficiently. Fairium Z allows Jumbao to break through Tornadus-T after Stealth Rock and a bit more chip damage.

Jumbao fits on many teams because it breaks through a number of the tier's walls like Mega Tyranitar and Ferrothorn. Psychic-types like Mega Alakazam and Tapu Lele can pressure Toxapex. Both of these Pokemon enjoy Jumbao hitting Steel-types like Ferrothorn and Mega Mawile with Flame Burst. Tornadus-T is an excellent teammate, pivoting in Jumbao with U-turn and supporting it with Knock Off. Water-types like Toxapex and Gastrodon help cover Jumbao's weakness to Fire-types. Toxapex sports amazing longevity and walls opposing Choice Scarf Jumbao, while Gastrodon notably beats Victini and Heatran. Stealth Rock allows Jumbao to more consistently break through Tornadus-T, so setters like Ferrothorn, Heatran, and Landorus-T are appreciated teammates.

pu.overview: Shiftry is an offensive force to be reckoned with as a result of its solid offensive typing, decent mixed attacking stats, and strong STAB options such as Knock Off, Leaf Storm, Seed Bomb, and Sucker Punch. Because of its mixed coverage, Shiftry manages to stand apart from other Dark- and Grass-types in the tier and is a massive threat to teams that are overly reliant on Pokemon such as Gurdurr, Mudsdale, and Regirock to check physical attackers. Shiftry becomes even more threatening under sun because of its ability Chlorophyll doubling its Speed, which allows it to also threaten opposing sun teams. It can also function well as an offensive user of Defog because its typing gives it the ability to threaten common entry hazard setters such as Mudsdale, Golurk and Regirock, allowing it to clear the field of entry hazards on the turn that they switch out. However, its great offensive typing curses it with weaknesses to common attack typings such as Fire, Flying, Poison, and Ice, and its poor bulk doesn't make matters much better. Although its Speed is far from terrible, Shiftry is outsped by common offensive Pokemon such as Primeape and Silvally-Fairy, and its main method of mitigating this in Sucker Punch isn't very reliable due to how it can be taken advantage of. Finally, as a purely physical wallbreaker, Shiftry faces competition from other Dark-types in the tier such as Absol and Alolan Raticate, both of which, while slower, are stronger.
pu.comments:
Other Options

A purely specially offensive or specially biased mixed set is an option, and Shiftry even has access to Nasty Plot to boost the power of those moves. Solar Beam can be used over Leaf Storm on the mixed set if Shiftry is on a sun team so that Shiftry has a more spammable Grass-type STAB attack that doesn't drop its Special Attack; however, it's fairly useless outside of sun, and it's less strong than Leaf Storm. Pickpocket can be used on the Choice Scarf set to steal the opposing Pokemon's item if Shiftry loses its Choice Scarf, which can be useful for crippling defensive Pokemon in the event that Shiftry takes a Knock Off. A Lum Berry can be used on the Swords Dance sets to let Shiftry ignore a status condition once and have a slightly easier time setting up as a result. It's noticeably weaker without the boost from Black Glasses or a Life Orb, though. Synthesis gives Shiftry a form of reliable recovery, taking advantage of the switches it can force, but it usually prefers having a move to hit Alolan Sandslash or remove entry hazards as the final move on the mixed set, and it struggles to find room for Synthesis on any other set. Furthermore, Shiftry really doesn't need recovery, as its main priority should be breaking as much as it can. Grassium Z can be used on the Swords Dance set to turn Seed Bomb into Bloom Doom, which can be nice for luring Pokemon like Skuntank and taking them out after a Swords Dance boost. Normalium Z can be used on non-Choice Scarf sets with Explosion to still hit hard and not lose Shiftry in the process. It should be noted that Breakneck Blitz is slightly less strong than Explosion, and this takes away from the surprise factor that Explosion has. Flyinium Z can be used with Hurricane to lure and KO Gurdurr and Hitmonchan, and Shiftry can do this easier with Nasty Plot.

Checks and Counters

Poison-types: Muk and Skuntank can all deal heavy damage to Shiftry with their respective Poison-type STAB moves and don't mind Knock Off much, and Skuntank even resists both of Shiftry's STAB types. They do have to watch out for Explosion, however, boosted in power or not.

Fighting-types: Combusken, Gurdurr, Hitmonchan, and Primeape all resist Sucker Punch and force Shiftry out due to either outspeeding it or having Mach Punch; however, none of them except for Combusken and Hitmonchan want to be brought in on Leaf Storm, Gurdurr hates losing its Eviolite to Knock Off, and none of them wants to take an Explosion. Combusken can shield itself from Explosion and obtain a Speed boost with Protect, and it resists both of Shiftry's STAB types. Primeape can generate momentum for its team by using U-turn on the turn Shiftry switches.

Faster Pokemon: Pokemon such as Kangaskhan, Primeape, Rotom-F, and Pinsir all have the power to OHKO Shiftry due to its frailty. The Choice Scarf set does deal with almost all of them, though, and when facing other sets, they have to take a Sucker Punch before they get to attack Shiftry.

Priority: As a result of Shiftry's frailty, priority often leaves dents in it or KOs it with enough prior damage. Pokemon like Abomasnow, Gurdurr, Hitmonchan, Kangaskhan, and Zangoose all threaten Shiftry with either super effective or strong neutral priority moves.

Mixed Life Orb.description:
Moves

Knock Off is one of Shiftry's two Dark-type STAB moves, and on top of hitting a lot of Pokemon that resist Leaf Storm fairly hard, it removes the opposing Pokemon's item. This effectively cripples Pokemon reliant on their Assault Vest or Eviolite to check Shiftry and its teammates, like Eelektross, Hitmonchan, and Ferroseed. Sucker Punch is the second of Shiftry's Dark-type STAB moves. It can be used to score KOs on faster but frailer Pokemon like Alolan Raichu or Floatzel after they take a bit of damage beforehand. Do keep in mind, however, that it fails if the foe doesn't attack, which can be taken advantage of by Pokemon with reliable recovery like Swanna. Leaf Storm is Shiftry's main Grass-type STAB attack, and it can be used to hit physically defensive Pokemon like Aggron and Mawile harder than its Dark-type moves, which neither of them mind all that much. Defog can be opted for if your team lacks hazard control, which is good for more offensive teams due to the pressure Shiftry puts on common hazard setters like Regirock. Alternatively, Low Kick hits Alolan Sandslash, which could otherwise take advantage of Shiftry. Explosion gives Shiftry access to a one-time physical attack with 250 Base Power at the cost of Shiftry itself. Explosion is Shiftry's best attack against Skuntank, which resists both of Shiftry's STAB types and threatens it with Poison Jab, and Explosion also has the secondary advantage of severely weakening even some of the most physically bulky non-Normal-resistant Pokemon in the tier, such as Gurdurr.

Set Details

Special Attack investment isn't necessary, as even without it, Leaf Storm hits its main targets harder than any of the physical attacks do. A Lonely nature is used to increase Shiftry's attacking power without lowering its Special Attack. A Hasty nature can be used if you wish to outspeed certain neutral-natured Pokemon such as Kangaskhan and Stoutland, though this does cause Shiftry to lose out on certain KOs. Chlorophyll doubles Shiftry's Speed under sun, making it even more threatening on and against sun-based teams. Life Orb strengthens all of Shiftry's attacks, but it comes with the downside of recoil damage.

Usage Tips

Use Knock Off a lot early on, as it's Shiftry's most reliable STAB move and cripples defensive Pokemon like Tangela by removing Eviolite, rendering it unable to check Shiftry as effectively. If you're using Defog on Shiftry, bring it in on entry hazard setters that it threatens like Bronzor and Regirock, and Defog on the turn they switch. Sucker Punch is a great tool for revenge killing, but as mentioned before, it can be exploited by Pokemon that can recover their health or set up such as Swanna and Jynx. Exercise caution when using Explosion, as Shiftry only gets one use at the move, so refrain from using it until Shiftry is no longer required and wants to dish out one last heavy hit. Shiftry is easy to wear down due to Life Orb recoil, entry hazards, and its poor bulk, so not letting it take much or any unnecessary damage is smart, especially if it's the team's only form of entry hazard control.

Team Options

Fire-types like Simisear and Turtonator break through bulkier Grass-types and physical walls like Tangela for Shiftry, while Shiftry provides entry hazard removal for them and combats the Ground-, Rock-, and Water-types that threaten them such as Carbink and Lanturn. Fighting-types like Gurdurr, Hitmonchan, and Primeape place pressure on both physical walls and opposing Dark-types for Shiftry, and it pressures Psychic-types in return. Pokemon that resist Fighting such as Musharna, Swanna, and Qwilfish synergize well defensively with Shiftry, as they handle the Fighting-types that force it out, especially those with Mach Punch like Gurdurr and Hitmonchan. They appreciate how Shiftry deals with Electric- and Psychic-types like Lanturn and Alolan Raichu. Slow users of Volt Switch like Eelektross and Lanturn work to get Shiftry in as safely as possible. Each has its own benefits: Eelektross beats Pokemon like Tangela, while Lanturn can cure Shiftry of status with Heal Bell and can check Fire-types. Entry hazard setters such as Qwilfish and Mudsdale pair well with Shiftry because hazards pressure Fire-types and faster but frailer Pokemon, which can't take Shiftry's moves as well if they are up, particularly Sucker Punch. Shiftry can even keep the entry hazards up with Explosion while either severely weakening the opposing Pokemon or securing a KO. If Shiftry's on a sun team, Sunny Day users like Liepard, Regirock, and Volbeat are definitely important. Fellow sun sweepers like Simisear and Victreebel pair well with it too. Victreebel can absorb Toxic Spikes for Shiftry, which helps it remain around for longer, and Shiftry can put holes in teams and make it easier for the other sun sweepers to finish them off.

Swords Dance.description:
Moves

Knock Off is Shiftry's main Dark-type STAB move that removes the item of the opposing Pokemon and hits a lot of Pokemon that resist Seed Bomb for neutral damage. Sucker Punch is Shiftry's secondary Dark-type STAB move, and it improves Shiftry's matchup against fast but frail Pokemon such as Alolan Raichu and Dodrio, especially after a Swords Dance. Low Kick is an option over Seed Bomb as it allows it to hit Aggron and Alolan Sandslash harder.

Set Details

An Adamant nature helps to increase Shiftry's power and give it stronger priority, but a Jolly nature can be used to let it outspeed neutral-natured Pokemon like Adamant Skuntank. Chlorophyll doubles Shiftry's Speed under sun, letting it outspeed the entire unboosted metagame as well as some Choice Scarf users like Primeape, which makes it threatening on and against sun teams. Life Orb gives all of Shiftry's moves a bit more power, at the cost of some of its health for every attack. Black Glasses is an alternative that doesn't deal recoil damage to Shiftry and still boosts the power of Knock Off and Sucker Punch, but it doesn't give Seed Bomb a boost in power.

Usage Tips

Using Knock Off a lot early on to weaken checks and remove the items of checks is good for pressuring them and making them unable to keep Shiftry in check. Finding opportunities to set up a Swords Dance on Pokemon that Shiftry forces out like Bronzor, Gastrodon, or Sableye is ideal due to their passivity. Once Shiftry manages to use Swords Dance, it should weaken and break as much of the opposing team as it can, paving the way for its teammates to and clean up. Sucker Punch allows Shiftry to check faster but frailer Pokemon as well as setup sweepers. None of them appreciate taking a Sucker Punch, especially if Shiftry uses Swords Dance beforehand. Shiftry is really frail and doesn't like taking even resisted hits when it doesn't have to, so be sure to keep Shiftry as healthy as possible when attempting to set up.

Team Options

This set has problems with physical walls due to a lack of mixed coverage, so good partners are Pokemon such as Simisear and Drampa that can severely weaken or KO physically defensive walls like Tangela and Alolan Persian. Primeape greatly appreciates Shiftry's ability to pressure Ghost-types like Sableye and Jellicent, and in return gives Shiftry set-up opportunities with U-turn. Similarly, Hitmonchan is able to check Ice- and Fire-types like Aurorus and Simisear for Shiftry, and can provide entry hazard removal to aid Shiftry in remaining alive for as long as it can. Skuntank resists both of Shiftry's STAB moves, so Ground- and Steel-types that can handle it like Mudsdale and Aggron are beneficial. Mudsdale in particular is notable because of its ability to check Fighting-types like Primeape, Hitmonchan and Gurdurr that Shiftry struggles with. Other Pokemon that check Fighting-types and can tank Fighting-type moves for Shiftry such as Silvally-Fairy, Musharna, Oricorio-G, and Swanna make for good partners, and Shiftry helps them in return by removing Eviolite from Pokemon such as Gurdurr, Type: Null and Ferroseed, making them easier to handle. Slower users of Volt Switch and U-turn such as Eelektross, Lanturn and Type: Null make for good partners due to their ability to get Shiftry in on some of the more passive Pokemon they tend to bait in, like Audino, opposing non-Ice Beam Lanturn, and Sableye, all of which Shiftry takes advantage of and sets up on. Shiftry likes entry hazards being up on the opposing side so that its moves are even harder to come in on, especially after a Swords Dance, so hazard setters like Metang and Qwilfish pair well with it. If Shiftry is being used on a sun team, Sunny Day users like Liepard, Regirock, and Volbeat alongside other sun sweepers are necessary. Sun sweepers like Victreebel and Leafeon benefit from Shiftry's presence because they are often able to weaken their shared checks, with one allowing the other to clean up as a result.

Choice Scarf.description:
Moves

Knock Off is Shiftry's most reliable physical STAB attack, hits Pokemon like Jynx and Oricorio-G for super effective damage, and removes the items of the opposing Pokemon, which is good for crippling defensive Pokemon. Rock Slide hits Fire- and Flying-types like Simisear and Swanna for super effective damage. Low Kick allows it to hit Aggron and Alolan Sandslash harder than anything else. Alternatively, Explosion is used for taking a huge portion of health from Pokemon that Shiftry lures in, like Skuntank and Gurdurr, as well as for generating momentum. Defog can also be used as a means of emergency hazard control in order to have a better matchup versus entry hazard stacking teams.

Set Details

Choice Scarf allows Shiftry to outspeed Pokemon like Jynx, Oricorio-G, and Swanna, even with an Adamant nature, which lets Shiftry hit as hard as possible. Chlorophyll doubles Shiftry's Speed under sun, making sure Shiftry outspeeds every opposing Chlorophyll user under it.

Usage Tips

Using Knock Off a lot early on is smart, as it keeps opponents from immediately suspecting Shiftry's set. Refrain from using Rock Slide or otherwise making it obvious that you're using a Choice Scarf set until need be, as this will make the set ineffective at luring in faster threats. This set isn't very common in comparison to the other two, so take advantage of how it's unexpected by luring in the faster Pokemon that normally force Shiftry out like Simisear and Skuntank and KOing them. Shiftry serves as a solid revenge killer, as well, due to its lack of reliance on Sucker Punch for picking things off, so take advantage of Choice Scarf by taking down normally faster Pokemon like Alolan Raichu and Oricorio-G. Explosion still packs a punch despite the lack of a Life Orb boost, so use it to deal heavy damage to Pokemon like Skuntank and weakened physical walls.

Team Options

Special wallbreakers like Aurorus, Drampa, and Haunter place pressure on Pokemon that Shiftry struggles with breaking, such as bulky Grass-resistant Pokemon like Tangela, Oricorio-G, and Mawile. In return, Shiftry cripples their switch-ins with Knock Off and can weaken them with Explosion, making them easier to KO. Fighting-types like Primeape appreciate Shiftry luring in and beating Flying-types and keeping out Ghost- and Psychic-types, and they beat the Dark-types that give it trouble like Alolan Raticate and Skuntank. Pokemon such as Silvally-Fairy and Musharna take on opposing Fighting-types such as Hitmonchan, while Shiftry's Explosion weakens or removes Dark- and Poison-types for them. Entry hazard setters like Ferroseed and Qwilfish make Shiftry's moves even harder to switch into, and Shiftry can keep the hazards up for longer by preventing Defog and Rapid Spin with Explosion. Qwilfish also acts as a Fighting-type check for Shiftry. Checks to Fire-types are important, as while Shiftry does outspeed them and possess good options for them, it prefers to have something to fall back on should it get locked into Leaf Blade, so Pokemon like Assault Vest Hitmonchan and Lanturn make for good partners. Checks to Ice-types are important for the same reason, so Shiftry appreciates Pokemon such as Lycanroc, Assault Vest Crabominable, and Alolan Sandslash. Shiftry also handles some of their collective weaknesses to typings like Ground, Psychic and Water. Pokemon that can easily bluff Choice Scarf sets such as Z-Lovely Kiss Jynx and Primeape pair well with Shiftry, preventing any suspicion in regard to Shiftry's set.

lc.overview: Piplup has a niche as one of the few LC Pokemon that can both set up hazards with Stealth Rock and get rid of the opponent's with Defog, giving it decent role compression. It's also a Defog user that isn't weak to Stealth Rock, allowing it to switch in more easily. Supporting this are its decent defenses and good defensive typing, letting it take resisted attacks and some neutral ones. Its access to a Water-type STAB move in Scald lets it beat most traditional Stealth Rock setters like Onix and Dwebble. However, Piplup is extremely passive, making it setup bait for sweepers like Shellder and Calm Mind Spritzee. It is also forced into performing its predictable niche, as it's outclassed as a Water-type attacker by Chinchou and defensive Staryu due to their better Speed and movepools. Piplup has access to no recovery outside of Rest, making it prone to getting worn down over time. Finally, it faces competition from Kabuto, a Water-type hazard setter with Rapid Spin, Knock Off, and Weak Armor, as well from Slowpoke and Mareanie, bulkier Water-types with access to Regenerator and recovery.
lc.comments:
Other Options

Berry Juice is an option that gives Piplup some longevity, but it removes from its bulk and consequently its ability to switch in. Brick Break can deal with Pawniard, but it's very situational and doesn't hit much else. Hidden Power Grass hits Water-types that otherwise wall Piplup, but it is very weak. Icy Wind can be used to help Piplup support its teammates with speed control, but it's much weaker than Ice Beam.

Checks and Counters

Bulky Grass-types: Despite Piplup's access to Ice Beam, Foongus and Pumpkaboo-XL can easily take one and deal heavy damage back with their STAB attacks, regaining their lost health in the process.

Taunt Users: Cottonee and Mienfoo can render Piplup near useless with Taunt, forcing it to switch in order to get another opportunity to set or remove hazards.

Electric-types: Piplup has nothing to handle Pokemon like Magnemite or Chinchou and is essentially forced to switch. Electric-types can take advantage of this and use Volt Switch to gain momentum.

Water-types: Water-types like Chinchou, Slowpoke, Shellder, and Staryu resist both of Piplup's STAB moves and completely wall it. Chinchou, in particular, can hit back hard with Volt Switch, while Staryu can spin away the hazards Piplup places.

Residual Damage: Since Piplup lacks any form of recovery, and it wants to come in often, hazards and status conditions can quickly wear it down.

Utility.description:
Moves

Stealth Rock breaks Sturdy on Pokemon like Magnemite and Onix and chips into threats like Vullaby and Ponyta. Defog removes all entry hazards, allowing Piplup to support its team. Scald gives Piplup a main STAB attack and increases its utility, allowing it to spread burns to cripple physical attackers. Ice Beam hits Grass- and Flying-types like Snivy and Doduo, but it won't do very significant damage, failing to 2HKO bulkier foes like Vullaby. Yawn can be used to put on pressure and force switches, but it makes Piplup even more of a Taunt bait and gives it no coverage against Grass-types.

Set Details

A Bold nature, 92 HP EVs, and 252 Defense EVs maximize Piplup's physical bulk, letting it tank a hit in order to set up Stealth Rock. These EVs also allow Piplup to avoid the 2HKO from any of Onix's and Dwebble's moves, unless they get lucky with Rock Blast. 148 Special Defense EVs let Piplup hit even Eviolite numbers, allowing it to take two of Staryu's Thunderbolts and avoid the 2HKO from Focus Sash Abra's Psychic. Torrent is the only ability compatible with Defog; it's rarely useful, but it does power up Water-type moves at low HP.

Usage Tips

Piplup should focus on hazard control and not be used for offensive purposes, as its offensive presence is incredibly low. It performs best when coming in on a slow Volt Switch or U-turn, as it doesn't get worn down as quickly. Piplup functions as a decent lead, as it can beat other common leads like Onix and Dwebble. It also has good bulk, so it can usually switch in on resisted and neutral hits. However, Piplup lacks recovery, so try to avoid switching it in often, especially into powerful attacks like Pawniard's Knock Off and Doduo's Brave Bird. Be careful about using Defog if there is a Pawniard on the other team, as it can switch in and get a +2 Attack boost thanks to Defiant. Finally, Defog can remove all hazards, including the ones you've set, so it can be counterproductive if used directly after Stealth Rock. Try using Defog before using Stealth Rock.

Team Options

Fire-types like Ponyta and Larvesta have great synergy with Piplup; they can muscle past bulky Grass-types like Pumpkaboo-XL and Foongus, which Piplup can't beat. They also appreciate Piplup removing Stealth Rock. Flying-types that prefer entry hazards removed, like Vullaby, Doduo, and Rufflet, all appreciate Piplup's Defog, and they can beat Grass-types as well. Grass-types like Snivy and Foongus resist both of Piplup's weaknesses and can check Water-types that resist both of Piplup's attacks. Ground-types like Choice Scarf Drilbur and Diglett can revenge kill Electric-types like Magnemite and Chinchou that threaten Piplup. Slow, bulky U-turn and Volt Switch users like Mienfoo and Chinchou can get Piplup in safely. Sturdy users like Magnemite and Onix also need hazards removed to function best. Wish passers like Spritzee and Lickitung can help keep Piplup alive to keep controlling hazards. Chinchou can switch into Electric-type Pokemon that Piplup can't beat like Magnemite and Elekid; it can also deal with opposing Water-types.

uu.overview: Empoleon has access to a variety of utility options such as Stealth Rock, Defog, and Roar, enabling it to support its team in various ways. Its incredible defensive typing and natural bulk allow it to check a multitude of common threats in the tier, including Latias, Primarina, and Mega Pidgeot. Additionally, Empoleon's ability to force out these threats provides it with a ton of opportunities to either set up Stealth Rock or clear entry hazards from the field. While Empoleon faces competition as a hazard remover from Tentacruel, which has access to Toxic Spikes, its fantastic secondary Steel typing and greater mixed bulk give it an edge. However, its typing also leaves it weak to common offensive types such as Electric, Fighting, and Ground, making it easily exploited by Pokemon like Mega Manectric, Cobalion, and Krookodile. Furthermore, Empoleon lacks reliable recovery, which makes it prone to being worn down, although moves such as Protect can be run to mitigate this. Empoleon struggles to fit all of its great status options on one set, which can leave it hurting in some matchups.
uu.comments:
Other Options

A spread with 44 Speed EVs is an option, as it can let Empoleon outspeed uninvested Scizor and use Scald on it before it can escape with U-turn.

Checks and Counters

Electric-types: Pokemon like Mega Manectric, Zeraora, and Rotom-Mow can KO Empoleon with their STAB moves. They also can take advantage of Empoleon for a free Volt Switch, gaining momentum and putting Empoleon's team further down. Rotom-Mow is particularly threatening, since it also resists Scald.

Fighting-types: Pokemon like Terrakion, Cobalion, Infernape, and Toxicroak can hit Empoleon super effectively with their STAB moves. All of them bar Toxicroak dislike switching on a potential Scald burn, however.

Special Walls: Special walls like Blissey are able to wall Empoleon and beat it one-on-one. However, they dislike having their items removed by Knock Off.

Residual Damage: Empoleon will be easily worn down if Leftovers is negated in some way. Thus, Knock Off, burn damage, and entry hazards can cripple it a lot.

Bulky Setup Sweepers: Pokemon like Suicune, Heal Bell Togekiss, and Reuniclus can beat Empoleon one-on-one. However, Empoleon can prevent them from setting up by phazing them with Roar. You must be careful to have other checks to these boosting threats, though, as Roar will no longer be a countermeasure to them once they are the last Pokemon left.

Strong Physical Attackers: Wallbreakers like Mega Sharpedo can severely weaken Empoleon and prevent it from checking other threats depending on how heavily it invests in Special Defense. Ground-types such as Krookodile and Nidoking can threaten it with their respective STAB moves but fail to OHKO it and are OHKOed back by a Torrent-boosted Scald in a one-on-one situation. They still can pressure a chipped Empoleon, however.

Utility.description:
Moves

Scald is a reliable STAB attack and has a solid chance to burn foes. Empoleon is a good user of Stealth Rock, as it is able to pressure common entry hazard removers such as Gligar and Rotom-Heat. If a Stealth Rock setter is not needed then Empoleon can use Defog to remove opposing entry hazards. Toxic stops Latias and Water-immune Pokemon such as Jellicent and Volcanion from taking advantage of Empoleon. Protect lets Empoleon mitigate its lack of reliable recovery by stalling for Leftovers healing. It also has the benefit of providing free turns to rack up Toxic damage. Knock Off can be used instead of Toxic or Roar, as it cripples Pokemon like Primarina and Hydreigon by removing their items and letting Empoleon take their hits more easily. It also eases the matchup versus opposing Empoleon and other bulky Water-types like Tentacruel by removing their passive recovery. Roar allows Empoleon to phaze setup sweepers such as Suicune, Nasty Plot Togekiss, and Calm Mind Latias.

Set Details

The given Defense investment ensures that Empoleon is never OHKOed by Cobalion's Close Combat or Krookodile's Earthquake, while the rest of the EVs and a Calm nature maximize Empoleon's special bulk, allowing it to switch into the likes of Moltres and Primarina more easily. Leftovers provides Empoleon with a form of passive recovery, improving its longevity throughout the course of the battle. Torrent is Empoleon's most useful ability, as it powers up Scald when Empoleon's HP is low.

Usage Tips

Empoleon should be used as a switch-in to threats like Latias, Primarina, and Mega Slowbro. However, it must be wary of Electrium Z Latias. It should take advantage of its ability to force out these threats by clearing entry hazards from the field or setting them up. Toxic and Knock Off should be used to cripple Pokemon like Primarina or predicted Water-immune switch-ins like Jellicent and Volcanion. Scald can be used very carelessly throughout the match, as it has a high chance to burn, which wears down foes and cripples physical attackers that try to switch in. However, against foes such as Latias it should be wary, as it needs Toxic to beat the likes of Calm Mind Latias, which can otherwise use Empoleon as setup fodder if it is lacking Roar. Avoid switching Empoleon in on a potential Scald burn or Knock Off because it will be more easily worn down without its Leftovers recovery. Protect can be used to scout Choice Scarf users like Hydreigon and Krookodile, letting you decide whether to keep Empoleon in to use Toxic or Scald, or switch to something that takes the incoming hit better. Roar should be used to prevent Pokemon like Latias and Suicune from setting up, but keep in mind that they can use Empoleon as setup fodder if they're the last Pokemon on the opposing team.

Team Options

Empoleon should be used primarily on bulkier teams that appreciate its ability to pivot into a number of threats. Wish support from Pokemon like Sylveon, Florges, and Alomomola helps Empoleon by increasing its longevity. Sylveon and Florges can also provide Empoleon with Heal Bell support to cure it of a potential burn, which heavily cuts down on its longevity. Pokemon that are weak to entry hazards, such as Mega Aerodactyl, Moltres, and Rotom-Heat, appreciate having Empoleon to reliably clear hazards. Additionally, Mega Aerodactyl can serve as a check to the Grass-, Electric-, and Fighting-types that threaten Empoleon such as Celebi, Mega Manectric, and Infernape. Checks to strong threats like Celebi and Latias are appreciated, as Empoleon can struggle to deal with Grassium Z and Electrium Z sets respectively, so Pokemon like Mega Altaria, Assault Vest Mienshao, and Choice Scarf Hydreigon make great partners. Hydreigon also appreciates Empoleon being able to check and cripple one of its best defensive answers in Primarina. If Empoleon is not the dedicated entry hazard remover, partners such as Mew, Gligar, and Mega Altaria are greatly appreciated to remove them in order to improve Empoleon's longevity. Pokemon that can sponge attacks from Fighting-types and force them out, such as Latias, Doublade, and Hippowdon, make for good partners for Empoleon. Latias is a particularly good teammate, since it can check Terrakion, Cobalion, and Infernape. Ground-types such as Krookodile, Nidoqueen, and the aforementioned Hippowdon are able to check Electric-types that Empoleon struggles with such as Mega Manectric and Zeraora. Empoleon appreciates having backup offensive checks to Pokemon like Latias and Togekiss, so Pokemon like the aforementioned Choice Scarf Krookodile and Mega Aerodactyl make for good partners.

Laser Focus + 3 Attacks.description: For full USUM 1v1 analyses, you can check out the USUM format page.

monotype.overview:
Water

Empoleon's good bulk allows it to fulfill the niche of a Stealth Rock setter and Defogger at the same time. Utility in Knock Off and Roar lets it cripple Pokemon like Chansey and phaze Pokemon like Suicune. Its amazing defensive typing gives it a resistance to ten types, an immunity to Poison-type attacks, and an important neutrality to Grass-type attacks. Although Empoleon has an amazing typing, the weakness to Ground-type attacks doesn't do it any favors, since it heavily stacks the weakness to Ground- and Electric-type moves with other balance staples like Toxapex. A lack of recovery outside of Leftovers weakens Empoleon's ability to provide Defog and Stealth Rock support and hinders its opportunity to check massive threats like Mega Diancie because it gets worn down so quickly. Empoleon also has lackluster Defense, so Pokemon like Tapu Bulu take advantage of it easily and it gets chipped at quickly by even weak physical attacks. A bad Speed stat and lackluster offensive stats make it very passive and exploitable. Stallbreakers like Mew and Gliscor take advantage of Empoleon's passive nature, preventing it from doing anything worthwhile thanks to their fast Taunt. Empoleon also has huge competition from other Pokemon like Swampert and Mantine. Swampert provides the same Stealth Rock support while also having an immunity to Electric-type attacks, which lets it check massive threats like Tapu Koko and Magnezone. On the other hand, Mantine offers much more reliable Defog support thanks to its superior bulk and access to Roost. It also provides a very important immunity to Ground-type attacks while still being neutral to Grass-type attacks like Empoleon.
monotype.comments:
Other Options

Water

Knock Off lets Empoleon cripple Pokemon like Chansey that are dependent on their item. Protect lets Empoleon capitalize on Leftovers recovery and scout against threats like Choice Band Diggersby. Toxic allows Empoleon to cripple walls like Porygon2 and Mantine.

Checks and Counters

Water

Defensive Pokemon: Empoleon struggles to beat defensive Pokemon like Ferrothorn and Toxapex, as its attacks fail to wear them down and they can chip it down throughout the match due to its lack of recovery.

Electric-types: Common Electric-types like Tapu Koko and Magnezone outspeed Empoleon and OHKO it with their STAB attacks.

Fighting-types: Fighting-types such as Terrakion and Heracross KO Empoleon with their super effective STAB attacks.

Ground-types: Ground-types like Excadrill outpace and OHKO Empoleon.

Residual Damage: Residual damage like Leech Seed, entry hazards, and weak attacks from Pokemon like Celesteela wear down Empoleon extremely quickly.

Taunt: Taunt users like Deoxys-S and Mew render Empoleon useless, as they outpace it and prevent it from performing its roles.

Wallbreakers: Wallbreakers like Choice Specs Keldeo and Choice Band Tapu Bulu outpace and OHKO Empoleon.

Utility (Water).description:
Moves

Stealth Rock lets Empoleon chip at threatening Pokemon like Kyurem-B and Mega Pinsir on the switch. Defog supports teammates like Gastrodon and Azumarill that are vulnerable to entry hazards like Toxic Spikes and Stealth Rock. Scald prevents Empoleon from being Taunt bait and helps it beat Pokemon like Mega Diancie. It also threatens physical attackers like Tapu Bulu with a potential burn. Roar lets Empoleon phaze Pokemon like Suicune and Mega Latias and rack up Stealth Rock chip damage.

Set Details

Leftovers gives Empoleon a form of passive recovery. Torrent boosts the power of Scald if Empoleon is at a third of its health or lower. Maximum HP and Special Defense EVs along with a Calm Nature maximize Empoleon's special bulk, which lets it take on Pokemon like Latios more easily.

Usage Tips

Prioritize setting up Stealth Rock early-game, especially against types like Fire and Bug. Similarly, against types like Flying and Fire, don't worry about using Defog to clear entry hazards. Instead, make sure Empoleon gets Stealth Rock up, as it is really important to chip down big threats like Zapdos and Mega Pinsir. Preserve Empoleon when you know you'll need it later on for threatening Pokemon like Mega Diancie. If Stealth Rock is up, use Roar liberally against types like Dragon and Flying that struggle with it, as it racks up chip damage quickly. Use Scald liberally to potentially burn physical threats like Tapu Bulu on the switch. Take care of setup sweepers like Suicune and Mega Latias by phazing them with Roar. Don’t waste Empoleon’s potential to check a big threat later in the game by trying to chip down opposing walls like Mega Venusaur and Celesteela. Similarly, avoid chip damage, as it wears down Empoleon quickly. Leftovers is Empoleon’s only form of recovery, so don’t recklessly switch it into attacks. Utilize Empoleon's immunity to Poison by absorbing Toxic from Pokemon like Mantine and Chansey for teammates like Gastrodon and Azumarill.

Team Options

BoltBeam Greninja helps pressure Defog users like Zapdos and Mantine that beat Empoleon. Pokemon like Lanturn and Gastrodon provide an Electric immunity for Empoleon. Toxic Spikes support from Toxapex helps pressure offensive checks to Empoleon like Infernape. Perish Song + Whirlpool Azumarill beats entry hazard setters like Ferrothorn and Toxapex that Empoleon struggles against. It can also switch into Grass-types like Choice Scarf Tapu Bulu and trap them. Stall staples like Quagsire and Lanturn provide Unaware and Volt Absorb support for Empoleon, respectively, and appreciate Empoleon's ability to chip down threats like Mega Pinsir with Stealth Rock. Dragon Dance Gyarados appreciates Empoleon's Defog support, as it's weak to Stealth Rock. Empoleon also provides its own Stealth Rock for Gyarados. In return, Gyarados provides a useful Ground immunity that helps force prediction from Choice-locked Ground-type attackers like Excadrill. Mega Sharpedo appreciates Stealth Rock support and beats Defog users like Mew that trouble Empoleon. Rotom-Wash provides a Ground immunity, a slow Volt Switch, and the ability to wall physical attackers like Gyarados for Empoleon. Manaphy appreciates Empoleon's Stealth Rock support, as it lets boosted Manaphy OHKO Pokemon like Mega Venusaur. Wallbreakers like Choice Specs Keldeo break down Pokemon like Ferrothorn that Empoleon struggles against.

ubers.overview:
• Giratina-O is one of the premier Defog users in the tier and is commonly found on many balanced teams due to a formidable combination of utility options it provides.
  • Great bulk, Levitate, and a defensive typing of Ghost / Dragon make Giratina-O a check to many physically oriented threats, such as Primal Groudon, Swords Dance Arceus formes, Necrozma-DM, Ho-Oh, and Mega Salamence.
  • When accounting for Giratina-O's solid defensive typing, enormous bulk, inability to be trapped, access to various status moves, and, most importantly, offensive presence, there are very few Pokemon in the tier that can reliably set entry hazards against, switch into, or combat it.
  • An advantageous matchup against the most relevant Stealth Rock user, Primal Groudon, is one of the major factors to Giratina-O's viability as a Defog user as well. Many Pokemon on balanced teams struggle to properly deal with Primal Groudon due to a large number of sets it can run to circumvent its checks, and Giratina-O stands as one of the safest switch-ins to Primal Groudon due to its ability to handle most variants.
  • An ability to defeat common threats like Primal Groudon, Necrozma-DM, and many support Arceus formes in one-on-one scenarios, depending on its moveset, serves as Giratina-O's other attractive trait to balanced teams that need a Defog user capable of restricting many Pokemon from taking advantage of it.
  • Giratina-O's effectiveness as a check to threats it pivots into will vary depending on its health due to its tendency to handle its foes offensively or with status moves. An average Speed tier means that Giratina-O will likely be attacked before it is able to counteract, which combined with a complete lack of recovery and an obligation to pivot into strong powerhouses like Primal Groudon makes its health management important.
  • Prevalent special attackers like Xerneas, Yveltal, and Mega Gengar and other special attackers like Lunala and Deoxys-A can easily overwhelm Giratina-O and threaten to OHKO or heavily impair it. Other common offensive threats like Marshadow and Outrage Ultra Necrozma can exploit Giratina-O's weaknesses to circumvent its bulk.
ubers.comments:
Other Options

  • A physically based set with Defog, Dragon Tail, Shadow Sneak, and Earthquake or Shadow Force provides Giratina-O with a stronger priority move and a way to 2HKO Magearna without statusing it beforehand. However, this set is helpless against Fairy-types, struggles to combat Primal Groudon, and is easily taken advantage of by Ferrothorn. Dragon Tail's inability to prevent Extreme Killer Arceus from setting up with Substitute against Giratina-O also leaves this option fairly disappointing.
  • Magic Coat can be used to reflect status and entry hazard moves from suicide leads like Deoxys-S and various Pokemon that rely on Toxic to combat Giratina.
  • Rest is Giratina-O's only form of recovery, but it can only be used effectively with cleric support, and Giratina-O has a hard time justifying its use over any listed move. As Giratina-O is immobile while asleep, Rest ends up being a detriment due to the sleep turns and its tendency to allow Giratina-O's offensive checks to switch in freely, along with entry hazard setters taking advantage of Giratina-O without fear.
  • Roar can be used to deal with setup sweepers behind Substitute and possibly make Geomancy Xerneas waste its Power Herb, but this move is very hard to fit.

Checks and Counters

Fairy-types: Both Xerneas and Magearna can switch into Dragon-type moves and threaten Giratina-O with their STAB moves. Both of them also have access to cleric moves to cure status that Giratina-O aims to spread as well. However, Choice Scarf Xerneas with Aromatherapy will be forced to heal its status right away if switched into Thunder Wave, and Geomancy variants will be punished harder if switched into said move. Arceus-Fairy has access to recovery moves to consistently switch into Giratina-O, but it has similar concerns about getting paralyzed, which will make it vulnerable to getting 2HKOed by boosted Hex from Giratina-O.

Dark-types: Offensive Yveltal can cleanly OHKO Giratina-O with Dark Pulse, and defensive variants typically carry Taunt that prevents Giratina-O from using Defog or status moves. However, Yveltal dislikes switching into Thunder Wave and Toxic, and offensive variants have to be wary about switching into Draco Meteor when Stealth Rock is up. Arceus-Dark has enough bulk to take on most Giratina-O variants, and variants carrying Refresh does not mind Giratina-O at all, apart from being forced to use Recover after switching into Draco Meteor. Tyranitar can force out Giratina-O while setting Stealth Rock and additionally guarantee a heavy hit on it with Pursuit. Even after getting burned, Tyranitar is a huge nuisance for Giratina-O due to the residual damage from sandstorm and potential Toxic.

Chansey and Blissey: Both Chansey and Blissey have enormous special bulk to take any attack from Giratina-O with ease, Natural Cure to absorb status, and Heal Bell to heal its teammates of status ailments.

Ghost-types: While Ghost-types almost never find opportunities to switch into Giratina-O, they can offensively check it if given a safe switch. Mega Gengar, Lunala, and Marshadow are all able to threaten Giratina-O, but they must be wary of Shadow Sneak and avoid switching into Thunder Wave.

Super Effective Attacks: Super effective moves like Ice Beam from Arceus formes prevent Giratina-O from effectively dealing with them, while more offensive foes like Ultra Necrozma, mixed Rayquaza, Palkia, and Dialga can threaten to OHKO Giratina-O with their super effective attacks.

Status: Giratina-O's already limited longevity is further worsened by burn and poison, and paralysis can be detrimental as well due to its potency to potentially prevent Defog.

Defog.description:
Moves

  • Giratina-O's ability to force switches with its strong attacks and check Primal Groudon makes it an effective Defog user.
  • Hex provides Giratina-O with an immensely powerful attack against statused foes. Hex is one of the major factors that contribute to Giratina-O's offensive presence due to it 2HKOing foes like Primal Groudon, Primal Kyogre, Magearna, and the majority of the support Arceus formes once they've been statused.
  • Dragon Pulse is a consistent secondary STAB move that isn't reliant on status. Dragon Pulse also has a sizable damage output despite its mediocre Base Power, doing enough damage to 2HKO most offensive Primal Groudon variants after Stealth Rock damage and outright OHKO offensive Mega Salamence.
  • Draco Meteor provides Giratina-O with a Dragon-type STAB attack with more immediate damage output, forcing recovery moves from support Arceus formes that attempt to absorb damage and threatening to OHKO Yveltal and offensive Ho-Oh after Stealth Rock damage.
