Slowbro can pivot into strong physical attackers, such as Mega Aerodactyl, Cobalion, and Infernape, and use its STAB moves instead of using Slack Off to heal itself because Regenerator enables it to recover HP simply by switching out. Slowbro should set up later in the match, after its checks and counters have been removed or sufficiently weakened. Slowbro has to be cautious of status, primarily Toxic, as this greatly hinders its ability to check these threats as well as pull off a sweep with Calm Mind in the late-game.

Team Options

Slowbro is very vulnerable to status and thus benefits from cleric support from Pokemon such as Sylveon, Togekiss, and Blissey. Pokemon like Mega Altaria, Moltres, and Empoleon can use Defog to remove entry hazards from the field, especially the Toxic Spikes that Slowbro fears. Poison-types like Nidoking, Nidoqueen, and Nihilego can similarly remove Toxic Spikes by absorbing them while the latter two can also set up Toxic Spikes of their own to wear down Slowbro's checks and help it break through bulkier teams. Specially bulky Pokemon such as Blissey and Alolan Muk can take on common Grass- and Electric-type Pokemon like Celebi, Rotom-Mow, and Mega Manectric that threaten Slowbro. Amoonguss covers Slowbro's Electric- and Grass-type weaknesses and forms the second half of a core that can take advantage of Regenerator to pivot effectively. Hippowdon and Mega Steelix can check Electric-types, and set Stealth Rock, to wear down opposing Slowbro checks. Mega Steelix is also a phenomenal check to Calm Mind Latias sets that easily beat Slowbro. In return, Slowbro resists Water- and Ice-type attacks and can set up on bulky Water-types like Suicune that try to take advantage of Hippowdon. Fairy-types like Sylveon, Mega Altaria, and Togekiss benefit from Slowbro's resistances to Fire- and Steel-type attacks and can switch in on Bug- and Dark-type attacks aimed at Slowbro. Steel-types resist Grass- and Bug-type attacks that give Slowbro trouble. In exchange, Slowbro can take on Fire- and Fighting-types like Cobalion and Infernape. Scizor, Doublade, and Klefki can make good partners for this reason, with Scizor also being able to bring Slowbro in safely with U-turn. Pursuit trappers like Mega Aerodactyl, Krookodile, and the aforementioned Scizor makes ideal partners for Slowbro, as they are capable of removing the likes of Latias and Celebi for it. Fighting-types such as Cobalion, Infernape, and Terrakion provide answers to offensive Dark-types that threaten Slowbro.

Defensive.description:
Moves

Psyshock is a secondary STAB move that threatens Pokemon such as Amoonguss, Tentacruel, and Volcanion that wouldn't mind being hit by Scald. Ice Beam is a solid option over Psyshock, as it can hit Dragon- and Grass-types such as Hydreigon and Celebi that resist Scald. Toxic is easy to spread, as Slowbro can be difficult to wear down, and can provide valuable chip toward enemy tanks such as Alomomola and opposing Slowbro. Thunder Wave allows Slowbro to support its team by crippling opposing offensive Pokemon that rely on their Speed like Latias and Hydreigon​.

Set Details

Leftovers provides Slowbro with passive recovery and helps it better check Pokemon like Terrakion and Cobalion more consistently throughout the match. Colbur Berry gives Slowbro a chance to escape Pursuit from the likes of Krookodile and stomach other Dark-type moves such as Hydreigon's Dark Pulse and punish its enemy with Scald or a status move.

Usage Tips

Slowbro can pivot into strong physical attackers, such as Mega Aerodactyl, Cobalion, Infernape, Mamoswine, and Terrakion, and fire off STAB attacks and status moves over the course of a match. Thanks to Regenerator, Slowbro doesn't need to rely on purely Slack Off for recovery. Pivoting Slowbro into Pokemon that it forces out, such as Terrakion and Gligar, is an easy way to get back health while double switching out or getting off a Slack Off. Slowbro should take advantage of its bulk and innate recovery from Regenerator to spread status with Toxic, Thunder Wave, or Scald burns. If utilizing Colbur Berry then Slowbro can risk staying in on threats such as Hydreigon and Mega Sharpedo to get off a crucial Toxic or Thunder Wave. Try to not let Slowbro take Toxic poison or a Scald burn carelessly; chip damage from status can seriously hinder its ability to remain effective throughout the match. Mew can be a prominent issue for this reason as it is able to synchronize back any status ailments Slowbro may inflict on to it. Slowbro shouldn't be used recklessly and should stay out of harm's way, as special attackers like Primarina, Celebi, and Mega Houndoom and super effective physical attacks from threats such as Crawdaunt, Mega Sharpedo, and Scizor pose a major threat.

Team Options

While Water / Psychic is a solid defensive typing, it leaves Slowbro vulnerable to VoltTurn cores, as it's weak to both Volt Switch and U-turn. Mega Manectric, Rotom-Heat, Rotom-Mow, Scizor, and Zeraora are all threatening in this manner. Mega Steelix is a solid teammate, as it is immune to Electric-type moves, resists U-turn, and may beat the aforementioned threats bar Rotom-Heat. Hippowdon also provides an Electric-type immunity and can run Rocky Helmet to punish U-turn. Special walls such as Florges and Blissey can patch up Slowbro's weakness to special attackers like Mega Manectric and Hydreigon. Cobalion and Mega Aggron freely switch into Dark-type moves like Knock Off for Slowbro and can set up entry hazards to capitalize on the switches Slowbro forces. Scizor's U-turn helps Slowbro to get into more favorable positions; for example, Infernape and Cobalion often switch into Scizor. Scizor also checks Pokemon like Latias, Mimikyu, and Mega Altaria for Slowbro. Pursuit users like Mega Aerodactyl and Choice Scarf Krookodile are able to defeat Ghost-types such as Gengar and Chandelure that can blow through Slowbro as well as trap fast Electric-types like Mega Manectric and Zeraora for Slowbro. In return, Slowbro can wear down their checks in bulky Ground- and Water-types with Toxic. Toxic can seriously cut into Slowbro’s longevity, so clerics such as Diancie, Sylveon, and Togekiss are appreciated. Slowbro synergizes well with other Regenerator users, which include Amoonguss and Assault Vest Mienshao. Both can take special hits for Slowbro while being able to rotate taking weaker hits, and Amoonguss is able to absorb Toxic Spikes for Slowbro. Dark-types such as Hydreigon, Mega Sharpedo, and Crawdaunt threaten Slowbro with relative ease, making Fairy-types good partners for it. Primarina and Mega Altaria excel in dealing with these Dark-types and can switch into them with ease. With Slowbro serving as a blanket check to the Fighting-types in the tier, Pokemon such as Cobalion, Hydreigon, and Rotom-Heat can all capitalize on Slowbro suppressing those. When Slowbro is running Thunder Wave, slower breakers like Lucario, Nidoking, and Mamoswine have an easier time dealing with faster Pokemon that it lures in, such as Latias and Hydreigon.​

Block.description:
Moves

Block allows Slowbro to trap passive Pokemon like Blissey, Alomomola, and Bronzong and potentially take advantage of them. Toxic lets Slowbro wear down Pokemon it attempts to trap, including Swampert, Quagsire, and Alomomola, along with common switch-ins, such as Latias and Hydreigon. Alternatively, Calm Mind allows Slowbro to take advantage of passive Pokemon such as Klefki and Mega Aggron by boosting its Special Attack and Special Defense and potentially sweeping. It should be mainly used with Slowbronite, however, because Mega Slowbro is significantly bulkier and stronger than Slowbro, so Mega Slowbro finds it easier to sweep. Scald is a reliable and spammable STAB move that allows Slowbro to potentially burn its target and cripple physical attackers like Mamoswine and Crawdaunt. Scald also allowing it to punish Steel-types such as Cobalion and Mega Aggron that are immune to Toxic. Despite having access to Slack Off, Rest is Slowbro's preferred recovery move because it allows Slowbro to beat passive Pokemon such as Swampert and Empoleon that may rely on status ailments like Toxic to beat it.

Set Details

252 HP EVs in tandem with 252 Defense EVs and a Bold nature make Slowbro as physically bulky as possible, which allows it to take on physical attackers such as Terrakion and Krookodile better. Colbur Berry is used to surprise Dark-types that normally check Slowbro such as Mega Houndoom and Hydreigon and helps reduce its susceptibility to Pursuit.. Alternatively, Leftovers can be used for a passive form of recovery to help handle offensive threats like Mamoswine and Infernape better as it is otherwise reliant on Rest and Regenerator. Slowbronite allows Slowbro to Mega Evolve, which boosts Slowbro's Defense and Special Attack and makes it an even more dangerous sweeper. Hence, it should mainly be used with Calm Mind. Furthermore, Mega Slowbro's ability Shell Armor makes Mega Slowbro even harder to break while boosted. Slowbronite also weakens opposing Knock Off damage on Slowbro. Waterium Z can be used to give Slowbro a strong Water-type STAB attack that lets it OHKO or severely weaken certain threats such as Terrakion and Scizor while also lowering the damage dealt to Slowbro by Knock Off, but should be opted for as a last resort. Regenerator is Slowbro's preferred ability because it allows Slowbro to pivot into physical attackers such as Terrakion and Mamoswine better mid-game.

Usage Tips

Early-game, Slowbro should be pivoted into physical attackers it can take on such as Mamoswine and Infernape. Do not reveal Block early-game because this set partly relies on the surprise factor on unsuspecting passive Pokemon. Use Block on passive Pokemon like Klefki, Mega Aggron, Alomomola, and Empoleon and take advantage of them with Toxic or Calm Mind. However, scouting for Roar is mandatory; otherwise, Block's effect will be removed and the foe could attempt to play around Block to prevent Slowbro from eliminating any Pokemon. Additionally, use Block with caution because of its low PP. Use Scald to wear down switch-ins as well as trapped Pokemon. Attempt to inflict Steel-types with a burn because they are immune to Toxic. Use Scald with caution, as if Slowbro inflicts a burn on a Pokemon it wants to cripple with Toxic, it will be harder to wear that Pokemon down, and Slowbro will waste PP trying to KO them. If using a Colbur Berry, Slowbro should attempt to badly poison a Dark-type foe that normally checks it, such as Mega Houndoom or Hydreigon and allows it to stay in on Krookodile and weaken it with Scald. If using Slowbronite, do not Mega Evolve immediately because then Slowbro loses Regenerator, which makes it harder for it to repeatedly pivot into physical attackers like Terrakion and Infernape. Toxic should be used early-game to wear down Slowbro's main checks, including Mega Manectric, Hydreigon, and Latias. It should also be used on trapped Pokemon such as Mantine and Blissey to eliminate them as quickly as possible. Calm Mind should mainly be used against trapped foes like Klefki, Sylveon, and Bronzong to attempt a sweep. Make sure to not set up with Calm Mind variants if there are Pokemon like Mantine and Volcanion that are immune to Water-type coverage, although the latter also has no way of breaking through Slowbro. If running Waterium Z then use Hydro Vortex to KO certain threats, including setup sweepers that may try to avoid the KO from Scald and set up, such as Infernape and Scizor. Rest should be used to maintain Slowbro's longevity. However, it should be mainly used against trapped foes, as Slowbro can otherwise easily be taken advantage of by setup sweepers such as Scizor and Latias. Furthermore, Rest should generally not be used early-game so Slowbro's set isn't revealed. Instead, take advantage of Slowbro's ability Regenerator to retain longevity. Similarly, do not stay in on setup sweepers that do not mind status ailments, such as Reuniclus, Refresh Mega Altaria, and Togekiss.

Team Options

Slowbro mainly fits on defensive teams because of its ability to trap opposing passive Pokemon that are troublesome like entry hazard setters such as Mega Aggron and Empoleon and clerics such as Sylveon and Blissey. Ground-types such as Mega Steelix and Hippowdon pair well with Slowbro because they check Electric-types such as Mega Manectric and Zeraora and block opposing Volt Switch. They can also set up Stealth Rock, which synergizes well with Regenerator to help wear the opposing team down. Amoonguss pairs really well with Slowbro because it also has Regenerator. By switching frequently between Amoonguss and Slowbro with Stealth Rock up, you can wear down the opponent's team while preserving your team's PP. Amoonguss can also pivot into Electric- and Grass-types, such as Mega Manectric, Rotom-Mow, and Tsareena. Fairy-types such as Sylveon, Florges, and Klefki pair well with Slowbro because they can switch into hostile Dragon- and Dark-types, such as Latias and Hydreigon. Sylveon and Florges can also provide Slowbro with Wish support, which allows Slowbro to pivot into physical attackers more easily, and Heal Bell support, which allows Slowbro to be cured of a status ailment without revealing Rest. Hazard removers such as Rotom-Heat, Hydreigon, and Tsareena can clear entry hazards that are hostile to Slowbro, which allows it to pivot in better and take better advantage of Regenerator. Hydreigon and Rotom-Heat also being able to check Grass-types that Slowbro struggles with such as Celebi and Amoonguss. Dark-types such as Hydreigon and Krookodile can pivot into Ghost-types that check Slowbro, such as Chandelure and Gengar, respectively. Lastly, setup sweepers such as Scizor and Latias appreciate Slowbro trapping problematic defensive Pokemon such as Mega Aggron, Klefki, and Mantine.

Tank.description:
Moves

Scald is Slowbro's main STAB move, capable of spreading burns and dealing decent amounts of damage at the same time. Ice Beam is mandatory coverage, allowing Mega Slowbro to nail Grass-types like Rotom-Mow and Celebi as well as Dragon-types like Hydreigon, Mega Altaria, and Latias for super-effective damage so it isn't walled by many of the tier's most capable Pokemon. Psyshock is a secondary STAB move that hits many Pokemon that resist Scald for at least neutral damage, such as Primarina, Suicune, and Tentacruel, as well as dealing more damage to potent special walls like Blissey. Fire Blast can also be used in the third slot, allowing Slowbro to OHKO Scizor and deal neutral damage to Pokemon that resist both Scald and Ice Beam like Empoleon. Keep in mind, however, that forgoing Psyshock in this third slot will leave Slowbro incapable of touching Tentacruel and walled by a few Pokemon that resist Water-, Ice-, and Fire-type attacks like Mantine and Jellicent. Finally, Slack Off is mandatory in the last slot, giving Slowbro reliable recovery that allows it to stay healthy over the course of a match and, when coupled with its non-Mega ability, Regenerator, enables it to repeatedly switch into threats it walls such as Infernape and Cobalion. Thunder Wave is another option for the third slot, hitting common offensive switch-ins to Mega Slowbro such as Volcanion and crippling them with paralysis, but it gives up a very nice offensive move in either Psyshock or Fire Blast to do so, so it's not recommended. Toxic is also an option for the third slot, crippling common bulkier switch-ins such as Alomomola and other Mega Slowbro, which take very little damage from any of Slowbro's offensive options.

Set Details

252 HP EVs maximize Slowbro's overall bulk while 76 Defense EVs and a Bold nature capitalize on Slowbro's naturally high Defense. The remaining EVs are placed into Special Defense. Slowbronite ensures Slowbro can Mega Evolve, which boosts its defenses significantly, while Regenerator is used pre-Mega as an excellent defensive ability so Slowbro remains healthy over the course of a match.

Usage Tips

This Slowbro set should be used to repeatedly switch into threats it is able to check, like Infernape, Cobalion, Mamoswine, and Mega Aerodactyl. For the majority of the game, Slowbro should not Mega Evolve, as Regenerator is such an important ability that enables it to keep switching in and out of the majority of the tier's physical attackers, which is more important than the extra stats given by Slowbro's Mega Evolution. Pre-Mega, Slowbro should consistently utilize Scald to spread burns and its coverage moves to spread damage and cripple its most common switch-ins. If a dangerous Pokemon such as Haxorus or Swords Dance Terrakion requires Slowbro to Mega Evolve to check with boosted Defense, Slowbro should Mega Evolve. Keep in mind that Mega Evolving means Slowbro loses Regenerator, so it should typically only be done late in the match.

Team Options

Grass-types such as Celebi can easily knock out Slowbro, so pairing it with Fire-, Dragon-, and Steel-types like Moltres, Latias, and Scizor is generally a good idea. Pairing Slowbro with a strong Ground-type like Hippowdon or Nidoqueen helps Slowbro because it is naturally weak to Volt Switch from users like Mega Manectric and Zeraora. Special walls such as Blissey and Florges are good partners for Slowbro, since its Special Defense is naturally relatively low and many of the tier's strong special attackers can easily break through it. Slowbro can also take the strong physical attacks aimed at Blissey and Florges. Heal Bell users, including Togekiss, Sylveon, and the aforementioned Florges and Blissey are good partners, since Slowbro is weak to status due to its lack of Leftovers recovery and lack of immunity to Toxic or Will-O-Wisp. Fairy-types like the aforementioned Togekiss and Sylveon can help Slowbro deal with Dark-types like Hydreigon and Mega Sharpedo that can easily break through it, and Slowbro can beat the strong Steel-types like Mega Aggron and Cobalion that threaten these Fairy-types. Steel-types such as Bisharp, Scizor, and Stakataka are capable of checking Psychic-types like Latias and Celebi that can give Mega Slowbro troubles. Strong offensive pivots such as Hydreigon and Scizor that appreciate Slowbro's ability to pivot into offensive threats that may revenge kill them make good teammates and can patch up Slowbro's somewhat lackluster offensive pressure.

Special Attacker.description:
Moves

Scald is Slowbro's main way to deal damage, capable of spreading status and not giving many of the tier's most common offensive Pokemon free switch-ins. Slack Off provides reliable recovery and allows Slowbro to stay reasonably healthy the entire game, especially when paired with its pre-Mega ability, Regenerator. Ice Beam is Slowbro's best coverage move, allowing it to hit Grass- and Dragon-type Pokemon that resist Scald such as Celebi, Mega Sceptile, and Latias. Psyshock is Slowbro's secondary STAB move and hits Tentacruel for super effective damage while dealing neutral damage to a lot of Pokemon that resist Scald such as Suicune and Volcanion. Fire Blast allows Slowbro to OHKO Scizor while also providing excellent neutral coverage with Scald and Ice Beam, so it can be used over Psyshock.

Set Details

Maximum Special Attack investment allows Slowbro to hit as hard as possible and utilize its Special Attack boost from Mega Evolution. 44 Speed EVs allow Slowbro to outspeed Doublade. 212 HP EVs maximize Slowbro's overall bulk and are left over from its Special Attack and Speed investment. Regenerator is used pre-Mega, allowing Slowbro to stay healthy before it Mega Evolves.

Usage Tips

This Slowbro set should be Mega Evolving early, as the Special Attack boost upon Mega Evolution is the main reason to use this set. Slowbro can be switched into physical and special attackers that it walls, such as Cobalion, Terrakion, and Nasty Plot Infernape, but keep in mind that without maximum HP or any Defense investment, it will be significantly less bulky than a defensive set. Scald should be used as much as possible, as it is capable of spreading status and helping Slowbro wear down the opposing team. Slowbro should use its coverage moves to smack common switch-ins such as Celebi and Mega Altaria, and try to do as much damage in its Mega forme as possible with the Special Attack boost. Keep in mind that without Regenerator, Mega Slowbro is very easily worn down, so try to keep it healthy and keep entry hazards off of the field as much as possible. Avoiding Toxic is paramount to avoiding getting Slowbro worn down, so make sure not to switch it in if there is any threat of a Toxic coming its way.

Team Options

Steel-types such as Scizor and Cobalion make solid partners, as they can check the Dragon- and Fairy-type Pokemon that can threaten out Mega Slowbro, while Mega Slowbro can check the Fire- and Ground-type attackers that often threaten these Pokemon. Rapid Spin and Defog users such as Tentacruel, Tsareena, and Rotom-Heat make good partners because Mega Evolving early makes Slowbro especially vulnerable to being worn down by Stealth Rock and Spikes. Heal Bell users such as Togekiss and Sylveon are good partners, as Mega Slowbro is very susceptible to being worn down by poison and burn damage. Sylveon can also provide Wish support to support the fact that Mega Slowbro can't take advantage of Regenerator upon Mega Evolving early. Ground-type Pokemon that can switch into Mega Manectric and Zeraora and stop Volt Switch momentum are good partners for Mega Slowbro; therefore, Pokemon such as Hippowdon, Rhyperior, and Krookodile make solid partners. Special walls such as Florges and Empoleon make good partners for Mega Slowbro, as it often succumbs to pressure from high-powered special attackers such as Latias and Hydreigon. Pursuit users such as Scizor, Krookodile, and Assault Vest Bisharp make great partners as they can trap and remove Ghost- and Psychic-types such as Gengar and Celebi.

Future Sight Attacker.description:
Moves

Future Sight is a great STAB move to support Pokemon like Terrakion, overwhelming their defensive answers and improving the team's matchup against stall. Scald is an easy-to-use STAB move that can spread burn. Slack Off gives Slowbro sustainability, which is especially important after it Mega Evolves and loses Regenerator. Ice Beam gives Slowbro solid coverage to hit Water-resistant foes like Hydreigon, Latias, and Altaria, preventing them from healing, pivoting in, or setting up freely.

Set Details

Slowbro is able to hit as hard as possible while retaining some bulk with the provided spread. The Speed investment allows Slowbro to outpace slow Pokemon like Doublade and Amoonguss. Psychium Z can be used with Future Sight to allow another Pokemon to Mega Evolve and immediately threaten Pokemon like Amoonguss.

Usage Tips

Slowbro should wait to Mega Evolve to gain value from Regenerator. It can use Future Sight or chip foes with Scald and immediately switch out without much consequence thanks to Regenerator; it should only Mega Evolve when it needs the extra strength or bulk to check Pokemon like Mega Aerodactyl. To help wallbreakers break past their checks more easily, Slowbro should prioritize setting up Future Sight, which is especially effective against stall. Slowbro can effectively utilize its coverage as long as it avoids Toxic, as it is worn down too quickly otherwise. Given Slowbro's usual passivity, it is actually able to lure Pokemon like Celebi and Mega Altaria that can normally sponge uninvested hits with ease. Slowbro must also remain wary of Pursuit trappers like Krookodile and Alolan Muk and try to stay out of range of a Pursuit KO. As Slowbro lacks investment in Defense, it should be careful against physical wallbreakers it would normally handle like Swords Dance Terrakion.

Team Options

Future Sight Slowbro thrives in conjunction with other wallbreakers to pressure their switch-ins. Choice Band Terrakion makes for a great example; upon taking a Future Sight, Gligar is 2HKOed by Stone Edge, and Alomomola can no longer safely scout it. Other Fighting-types such as Infernape and Mienshao are consistent partners as well, as they threaten Pokemon that can sponge Future Sight comfortably, like Blissey or Latias. Amoonguss makes for a reliable partner, as it sponges strong physical hits from Pokemon that could otherwise overwhelm offensive Slowbro, like Terrakion, and checks Primarina, which Slowbro cannot threaten without Psychium Z. Amoonguss also forms a Regenerator core with Slowbro, and generates free turns to set up Future Sight through Spore. Steel-types like Cobalion and Scizor are appreciated to answer the bulky Fairy-types such as Florges and Sylveon that can take anything Slowbro throws at them. Slowbro's Future Sight support also helps Cobalion beat Amoonguss. Scizor is able to check Celebi, which can be especially bothersome to Slowbro if Celebi is running Recover. Slowbro is also rather vulnerable to VoltTurn cores, so Pokemon like Hippowdon and Rhyperior are very useful for being able to take hits from Rotom-Heat and Mega Manectric. Hippowdon also takes hits from Terrakion and Scizor and can use Whirlwind to cause additional disruption with Future Sight. Slowbro appreciates Pursuit trappers like Scizor or Choice Scarf Krookodile to remove Pokemon that can overpower it such as Latias and Gengar.

ubers.overview:
• Mega Slowbro has amazing physical bulk combined with a nice typing that allows it to check threats such as Swords Dance Ultra Necrozma, Mega Lucario, Rayquaza, Mega Salamence, and some Arceus formes.
  • Thanks to its pre-Mega ability Regenerator, Slowbro can act as a pivot before it Mega Evolves.
  • After it Mega Evolves, Shell Armor prevents Slowbro from taking critical hits, which, combined with its access to Slack Off and Iron Defense, makes it easier to stall out physical attackers in the tier.
  • It has a decent Special Attack stat, being able to OHKO Mega Salamence with an uninvested Ice Beam.
  • However, Slowbro struggles against most of the metagame and requires too much to overcome its flaws, being only useful as a dedicated check to some threats, making it usually an inferior choice against other defensive Pokemon such as Toxapex, Celesteela, support Arceus formes, and Lugia.
  • Slowbro has average special bulk and somewhat common weaknesses that leave it weak to most of the common special attackers in the tier such as Primal Kyogre, Yveltal, and Mega Gengar, which can easily trap Mega Slowbro.
  • Even though Slowbro has a decent Special Attack stat, the lack of a boosting move or STAB move if not using Scald makes Slowbro passive and leaves it easily walled by most Steel-types in the tier and Primal Kyogre.
  • Slowbro's low Speed makes it move after virtually any Pokemon in the tier.
ubers.comments:
Other Options

  • Psyshock is an option that allows Mega Slowbro to hit Mega Gengar on the switch, OHKOing it most of the time; beat Mega Lucario more quickly; and do some damage against Primal Kyogre.
  • Fire Blast can be used to hit Steel-types such as Ferrothorn and Mega Scizor, since they are immune to Toxic, and it also allows Mega Slowbro to always OHKO Mega Lucario and 2HKO Arceus-Steel most of the time after Stealth Rock damage.
  • Calm Mind allows Slowbro to act as a bulky late-game sweeper, but Slowbro lacks a moveslot for this move.

Checks and Counters

Shadow Tag: Mega Gengar and Gothitelle can trap Mega Slowbro with Shadow Tag, easily beating it.

Dark-types: Dark-type Pokemon such as Yveltal and Arceus-Dark can easily beat Mega Slowbro with STAB moves.

Ghost-types: Ghost-types such as Lunala, Giratina-O, and Bulk Up Marshadow can easily threaten Slowbro with their STAB moves. Lunala beats it with Moongeist Beam, Giratina-O 2HKOes it with Draco Meteor or Hex, and Marshadow can set up and beat it with Soul-Stealing 7-Star Strike.

Toxic: Toxic limits Slowbro's longevity, making it unable to stall out threats on its own and check Mega Lucario.

Bulky Steel-types: Bulky Steel-type Pokemon such as Ferrothorn, Celesteela, Mega Scizor, Klefki, and Arceus-Steel are able to beat Slowbro because it's very weak offensively and can't do much damage to them.

Primal Kyogre: Primal Kyogre can threaten Mega Slowbro with Thunder. Calm Mind sets can also use Slowbro as setup fodder, though they have to be careful of Toxic.

Physical Wall.description:
Moves

  • Toxic is used to put opposing Pokemon on a timer.
  • Scald is a reliable STAB move that can burn foes and enables Slowbro to beat Swords Dance Necrozma-DM. Scald also helps against Steel-types in general, as they are immune to Toxic; 2HKOes Mega Gengar; and makes it easier for Slowbro to beat Ho-Oh.
  • Ice Beam makes Slowbro able to check Mega Salamence, Zygarde, and Rayquaza more reliably.
  • Foul Play is another attacking option that allows Mega Slowbro to check some boosting threats like Necrozma-DM more reliably but makes it more passive.
  • Slack Off allows Slowbro to keep itself healthy to check physical threats.
  • Iron Defense boosts Slowbro's Defense, allowing it to beat boosting Pokemon such as Ultra Necrozma, Arceus, and Mega Lucario one-on-one.

Set Details

  • 248 HP and 44 Special Defense EVs allow Mega Slowbro to survive two consective Overheats from Primal Groudon.
  • The remaining EVs are put into Defense with a Bold nature, allowing Mega Slowbro to check physical threats more easily.
  • Slowbronite is used to make Slowbro Mega Evolve.
  • Regenerator allows Slowbro to work as a pivot before it Mega Evolves, giving it an extra recovery option.

Usage Tips

  • Slowbro should be used as a pivot prior to Mega Evolving in the early- and mid-game.
  • Prioritize spreading Toxic early-game or double around to prevent Slowbro from being used as entry hazard or setup fodder.
  • It should only Mega Evolve when it's necessary to use its higher Defense.
  • Mega Slowbro should prioritize using Slack Off after it takes some damage, as being forced out weakened makes it harder for Mega Slowbro to check what it's supposed to due to the lack of Regenerator.
  • Slowbro should switch immediately into boosting threats it's supposed to check, as if they are allowed to set up more than once, they might be able to beat Slowbro.
  • It should avoid being hit by Toxic at all costs, as Toxic will limit its longevity and make it easier for offensive Pokemon to get past Slowbro.
  • Since Slowbro's Special Defense is not particularly good, it shouldn't be used to take special hits from Pokemon such as Primal Kyogre and Xerneas.
  • Be careful when playing against Mega Gengar and Gothitelle, as they can easily trap Mega Slowbro and open the path for Pokemon such as Ultra Necrozma and Mega Lucario to win the game.

Team Options

  • Pokemon that check Xerneas like Magearna and Necrozma-DM are required, as Mega Slowbro gives Xerneas a somewhat free setup opportunity.
  • Ferrothorn can check Z-Geomancy Xerneas, provide Spikes support for Mega Slowbro, and work as a Primal Kyogre check and an emergency check to Ultra Necrozma if Slowbro is weakened.
  • Fairy-type Pokemon such as Xerneas and Magearna can help Slowbro by checking Dark-type Pokemon like Yveltal and Arceus-Dark that can easily threaten Slowbro with their STAB moves; Xerneas and Magearna can also carry Aromatherapy or Heal Bell to cure Mega Slowbro from a status condiction.
  • Dark-type Pokemon such as Yveltal, Alolan Muk, and Tyranitar can help by checking Ghost- and Dark-type Pokemon. Alolan Muk and Tyranitar in particular can help by Pursuit trapping Mega Gengar, which can trap Mega Slowbro. Alolan Muk also absorbs Toxic Spikes, which cripples Slowbro.
  • Rest Zygarde can check Steel-type Pokemon and absorb status for Mega Slowbro.
  • Entry hazard control from Pokemon such as Giratina, Lugia, and Arceus-Dark can help, as hazards, mainly Toxic Spikes, make it harder for Mega Slowbro to check opposing Pokemon; Arceus-Dark can also check Ghost-type Pokemon.
  • Gothitelle can trap and beat most defensive Pokemon Slowbro can't deal with.
  • Chansey and Blissey can usually sponge special attacks for Slowbro and cure it from status condictions with Heal Bell.
  • Slowbro can't do much against most Steel-type Pokemon, so Pokemon that can check them such as Primal Groudon, Arceus-Ground, and Ho-Oh are appreciated. Arceus-Ground can also check Swords Dance Primal Groudon and provide Defog support.

ru.overview: Slowbro's excellent defensive typing and great defensive stats allow it to act as a physical blanket check to key offensive Pokemon in the tier like Metagross and Tyrantrum. Its resistance to Fighting-type moves is particularly noteworthy, letting it switch into various threats such as Passimian, Toxicroak, and Bewear with ease. This is achieved thanks to Slowbro's exceptional longevity; its combination of Regenerator and Slack Off ensures it will be able to pivot into physical attackers throughout the whole match. Unfortunately, Slowbro faces competition from the other Water- and Psychic-types in the tier, such as Milotic, Mantine, and Necrozma, although unlike the former two, it is able to avoid passivity issues due to its decent Special Attack combined with a good offensive movepool. Although its typing blesses it with important resistances, it is also cursed with multiple weaknesses to common offensive typings like Grass, Dark, and Electric, which makes Slowbro vulnerable to powerful threats like Shaymin, Mega Blastoise, and Raikou. Additionally, it can get chipped for big damage or removed from the game entirely by trappers such as Drapion and Escavalier. Slowbro is also unable to dent most Water-types like Milotic and Mega Blastoise unless running the niche Grass Knot or Toxic. Finally, its mediocre Special Defense stat leaves it unable to wall specially offensive threats such as Noivern and Nidoqueen.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Protect allows Slowbro to avoid Pursuit mind games, bait Z-Moves, and rack up Leftovers healing. However, it is important to note that Slowbro really needs all its coverage to hit its targets. Waterium Z can prevent Slowbro from being crippled by Trick users like Medicham and Metagross, reduce the damage from Knock Off from the likes of Machamp, and allows Slowbro to drop a Water-type nuke that heavily dents most offensive Pokemon such as Drapion, Pangoro, and Escavalier. Thunder Wave allows Slowbro to punish fast attackers and cleaners like Virizion and Mismagius on the switch. Rindo Berry lets Slowbro deal with Grass-types better, particularly Virizion, which takes substantial damage from Slowbro's Psyshock. Yawn can force switches versus Pokemon it loses to and help another teammate set up.

Checks and Counters

Grass- and Electric-types: Grass-types such as Shaymin, Roserade, and Virizion can all threaten to KO Slowbro with their STAB moves. Although most fear switching into Ice Beam or Psyshock, they become far more solid checks if they're running Synthesis. Although Electric-types are somewhat uncommon, Raikou, Mega Ampharos, and Rotom-Mow can all switch into it with ease and obtain momentum with Volt Switch, or in Raikou's case, set up with Calm Mind. Mega Ampharos can even switch in on its base forme to weaken Ice Beam.

Water-types: Slowbro is unable to dent Water-types unless running Toxic or Grass Knot. Most offensive Water-types carry super effective moves like Mega Blastoise's Dark Pulse or Araquanid's Leech Life, while defensive Water-types can take advantage of Slowbro by Defogging, recovering, or passing Wish.

Specially Offensive Pokemon: Due to Slowbro's mediocre Special Defense, special attackers like Noivern and Nidoqueen can easily break through it.

Toxic: Toxic puts a timer on Slowbro's time on the field and negates Regenerator's healing effect. It forces Slowbro to either switch constantly or use Slack Off more than it would like. Additionally, Toxic completely invalidates Calm Mind variants from sweeping.

Defensive Pivot.description:
Moves

Psyshock hits many Pokemon that resist Scald, such as Virizion, Roserade, and Toxicroak. Ice Beam targets Grass-types like Shaymin and Mega Sceptile, along with Dragon-types such as Noivern, that resist Scald and take little damage from Psyshock. Calm Mind can be used to make Slowbro a bulky setup sweeper and wall more specially offensive threats like Necrozma. Grass Knot allows Slowbro to hit Water-types like Milotic, Mega Blastoise, and Slowking, which otherwise completely wall it. Toxic lets Slowbro whittle its defensive checks such as Mega Blastoise, Cresselia, Mandibuzz, and non-Refresh Milotic.

Set Details

Leftovers allows Slowbro to passively regain health every turn, which can ease pressure off repeated uses of Slack Off or constant switching. Alternatively, Colbur Berry is an option that helps it when faced with a Dark-type like Drapion or Pangoro or Pokemon with Dark-type coverage like Mega Blastoise, Toxicroak, Machamp, and Donphan. Regenerator allows Slowbro to pivot into most neutral physical attacks with ease and takes pressure off using Slack Off repeatedly.

Usage Tips

Unlike other defensive Pokemon, Slowbro should avoid spamming Slack Off due to its ability to regain health through Regenerator; this usually makes attacking with its STAB moves or Ice Beam more beneficial, although neglecting Slack Off completely isn't ideal either. Use Slack Off when Slowbro can't KO the opposing Pokemon quickly and its HP is low. Scald should be used most of the time due to its decent power and useful chance to burn. However, if the opposing team has a Water-resistant Pokemon such as Shaymin, Goodra, or Roserade, try to predict if the opponent will switch into it and use the appropriate coverage move. Slowbro should exploit its access to Regenerator and high Defense by switching into Pokemon it walls or threatens such as Toxicroak and Zygarde-10% throughout the game, forcing them out and regaining most of the health lost in the process. Slowbro should avoid staying in on special attackers such as Gardevoir and Ninetales due to its mediocre Special Defense stat, which means most decently strong special attacks can severely dent it. Walls such as Registeel and Cresselia often run Toxic to cripple Slowbro and severely limit its longevity on the field. Scout for potential Toxic users before sending Slowbro out to beat them.

Team Options

Dragon-type Pokemon such as Dragalge and Goodra appreciate Slowbro's ability to deal with most physical Dragon-types like Zygarde-10% and Tyrantrum, while they easily switch into Grass- and Electric-types like Shaymin, Roserade, and Raikou. Fairy-types like Florges and Diancie can deal with most Dark- and Bug-types that Slowbro struggles with, such as Pangoro and Yanmega. Pokemon that invite the Pokemon Slowbro walls appreciate its ability to wall them. Some examples include Salazzle baiting in Flygon and Virizion luring Toxicroak. Mega Abomasnow appreciates a switch-in to dangerous Fire-, Fighting-, and Rock-types, and in return it can switch into Grass- and Electric-type attacks thrown at Slowbro, as well as pressure the Water-types Slowbro hates. Specially defensive Pokemon such as Florges and Bronzong can take pressure off Slowbro from checking special attackers like Gardevoir and Noivern. Additionally, Florges can provide Aromatherapy support to rid Slowbro of pesky status, while Bronzong can set Stealth Rock to further support the whole team.

ou.overview: Through its unique typing, solid physical bulk, and perfectly-fitting ability in Regenerator, Slowbro brings incredible defensive value to its team, checking premier physical attackers such as Mega Charizard X, Mega Medicham, Mega Swampert, Mega Lopunny, Gliscor, Landorus-T, and Hawlucha. Slowbro also has a respectable Special Attack stat and can spread status via Scald, Thunder Wave, and Toxic, preventing it from being overly passive. It has a great variety of moves it can slot on and even a variety of items, often running Leftovers, various Z-Crystals, and Slowbronite. Despite this, Slowbro is threatened by many prominent special attackers, such as Ash-Greninja, Tapu Koko, Serperior, and Mega Charizard Y, and even physical attackers like Kartana and Tapu Bulu if they can get in safely. Additionally, Slowbro hates status conditions and especially Toxic Spikes, so a lot of players decide that the poison-immune, Toxic Spikes-clearing Toxapex is much less hassle to fit onto a team.
ou.comments:
Other Options

Slowbro can use Zap Cannon in combination with Electrium Z to OHKO Greninja as it switches in as well as hit other Electric-weak Pokemon like Manaphy and Tapu Fini hard; however, outside of these interactions, it is a largely inconsistent move, and Slowbro already has so many moves that it wants to run.

Checks and Counters

Electric-types and Electric-type Coverage: Electric-types such as Tapu Koko and Zapdos and Pokemon like Magearna and Life Orb Clefable can threaten Slowbro out with their super effective Electric-type attacks, targeting its weaker Special Defense.

Grass-types: Grass-types like Serperior and Ferrothorn can easily beat Slowbro one-on-one; however, they must be wary of being statused as they switch in, as well as of Flamethrower in the case of Ferrothorn and Kartana.

Status: Slowbro needs to steer clear of poison and, to a lesser extent, burn, as they cut down on its staying power dramatically and can prevent it from checking Pokemon it's tasked with. Slowbro is particularly susceptible to Toxic Spikes, which can entirely prevent it from switching in safely.

Dark-types: Slowbro can be easily threatened out by Dark-types like Ash-Greninja, Weavile, and Mega Tyranitar if they can switch in safely.

Special Wallbreakers: Powerful special attackers like Mega Charizard Y and Tapu Lele can easily threaten Slowbro out due to its middling Special Defense stat.

Defensive.description:
Moves

Scald is Slowbro's most common STAB move, fishing for burn against anything it doesn't outright threaten and preventing physical attackers like Kartana and Tapu Bulu from switching in comfortably. Slack Off, in conjunction with Regenerator, ensures that Slowbro can stay healthy enough to check the physical attackers it's tasked with. Ice Beam threatens out Swords Dance Gliscor and hits Serperior and Hawlucha super effectively, and it can be powered up with Icium Z to OHKO Hawlucha and Swords Dance Gliscor. Future Sight is great support for offensive teammates, threatening Pokemon like Toxapex and preventing double switches into the likes of Mega Medicham. It's also the most powerful Psychic-type attack to use with Psychium Z, with Shattered Psyche threatening weakened Toxapex and hitting hard neutrally. Thunder Wave is the most instantly punishing status option, stopping threats like Ash-Greninja, Mega Alakazam, and Serperior from wanting to switch in. Toxic is similarly good at punishing switches and is especially great at stopping setup sweepers like Mega Charizard X, Mega Latias, Volcarona, and Cresselia from getting out of control. Protect lets status damage rack up on foes, scout Choice-locked attackers, and lets Slowbro gain additional Leftovers recovery. Flamethrower hits Ferrothorn and Mega Scizor hard, additionally scorching any Kartana brave enough to switch directly in. Counter is a niche option, biting back instantly with an OHKO when Slowbro is hit by strong physical attacks like Thunder Punch from Mega Medicham, +1 Dragon Claw from Mega Charizard X, and most importantly boosted Earthquake from Swords Dance Gliscor.

Set Details

Slowbro generally prefers to run maximum HP and Defense to deal with prominent physical attackers, but the Psychium Z variant can use a spread of 252 HP / 244 Def / 12 SpA to OHKO physically defensive Toxapex with Shattered Psyche.

Usage Tips

Slowbro can be thrown into physical attackers like Mega Lopunny and Mega Medicham liberally early-game, as Regenerator makes it easy for it to keep healthy. It's important to note that while Regenerator does a great job, Slowbro does need to be careful about preserving its HP when tasked with handling multiple physical attackers; Pokemon like Mega Swampert, Hawlucha, and Excadrill can break through if Slowbro takes enough prior damage. Although Slowbro is a great switch-in to Mega Medicham, it does need to be careful of the Thunder Punch variant, which can 2HKO it after Stealth Rock, especially in Electric Terrain. Make sure Slowbro regularly throws off status-inflicting moves, like Scald, Thunder Wave, and Toxic, to prevent common threats like Greninja and Kartana from switching in unpunished. Future Sight is a great option to not only threaten Psychic-weak Pokemon like Toxapex and Hawlucha but also ease the task of getting teammates in safely if they need to heal in a pinch.

Team Options

Slowbro is best suited for balance teams that otherwise struggle to handle physical threats, as it serves as a blanket check to many such threats. It has a superb partnership with Chansey, as it can check Pokemon like Mega Medicham and Mega Charizard X that threaten Chansey, while Chansey invalidates special attackers like Ash-Greninja, Volcarona, and Mega Charizard Y for Slowbro. Gliscor appreciates Slowbro checking Mega Swampert, Hawlucha, and Mega Medicham, and in return, it feasts on Pokemon like Toxapex and Chansey that threaten Slowbro with status, either setting up on them with Swords Dance or clearing their entry hazards with Defog. Toxic Spikes are the bane of Slowbro's existence, so counterplay to them, such as Defoggers like Tornadus-T and Gliscor or Poison-types like Toxapex and Amoonguss, is required. Tornadus-T is an especially good partner, as it can check Grass-types like Kartana and Tapu Bulu while forming a Regenerator core with Slowbro. Magnezone can remove the aforementioned Kartana as well as Ferrothorn, which can pester Slowbro variants lacking Flamethrower with Spikes and Leech Seed.

Paper Shell (Mega).description:
Moves

Slack Off becomes even more crucial for Mega Slowbro, allowing it to continue to keep healthy after Mega Evolution, as it loses out on Regenerator. The extra base Special Attack after Mega Evolving allows Ice Beam to OHKO Landorus-T, Garchomp, and utility Gliscor, as well as Swords Dance Gliscor after Stealth Rock. Psychic takes a more direct approach against Fighting-types, OHKOing Hawlucha, as well as being Slowbro's best STAB move to hit neutrally. Calm Mind makes great use of Mega Slowbro's ability, Shell Armor, which takes away counterplay via critical hits, improving its consistency as a Calm Mind sweeper. Toxic is a more all encompassing punish that catches the likes of Calm Mind Mega Latias and Cresselia as well as other threats like Kyurem-B and Rotom-Wash. Future Sight enables offensively minded teammates by compounding damage with their attacks, helping them break through opposing walls.

Set Details

Using maximum HP and Defense investment and a Bold nature makes the most out of Mega Slowbro's Defense increase; however, a spread of 252 HP / 168 Def / 88 SpA can be used to 2HKO Mega Charizard X with Psychic.

Usage Tips

It's important not to understate how little Mega Slowbro wants to lose Regenerator, and there are many matchups where it's best to never Mega Evolve at all. The main benefit that Slowbro gets from Mega Evolving is a significantly higher Defense stat, which allows it to survive monstrous physical attacks like +1 Leaf Blade from Kartana and +2 Devastating Drake from Garchomp in a pinch. Mega Evolution also comes in handy when Slowbro has been chipped down, giving it extra consistency against the likes of Excadrill and Hawlucha. Additionally, Mega Evolving improves Slowbro's offensive prowess, letting it OHKO Pokemon that non-Mega Slowbro cannot, like the aforementioned Garchomp, and giving it an ability that better synergizes with Calm Mind. It's best to only Mega Evolve when necessary, keeping Regenerator for as long as possible.

Team Options

Mega Slowbro is often fit onto balance teams that cannot fit another Mega Evolution, as it can often be hard to justify using Slowbro as your Mega Evolution when it's already so good. Good team support options for Mega Slowbro are incredibly similar or the same as those for its non-Mega variant. Cleric support from the likes of Chansey and Clefable comes in handy, especially after Mega Evolving, as Regenerator no longer soaks up passive damage.

monotype.overview:
Psychic

Slowbro's high Defense and Water typing makes it a good defensive pivot on Psychic teams, able to easily check threats such as Diggersby and Excadrill. In addition, Slowbro's ability Regenerator complements its role as a defensive pivot by healing it every time it chooses to switch out, extending its longevity throughout the battle. Furthermore, upon Mega Evolution, Slowbro's massive Defense and access to Calm Mind allow it to serve as a potent wincon late-game, and its ability, Shell Armor, supports its ability to sweep with Calm Mind by protecting it from critical hits. Slowbro also helps in the Steel matchup because it is a good switch-in to Excadrill and can threaten many Steel-type Pokemon such as Mega Scizor and Ferrothorn with Fire Blast and Heatran with Scald. Mega Slowbro also does well in matchups such as Poison, as it is able to directly take on every Poison-type with Calm Mind-boosted Psychic and takes little damage from Alolan Muk's attacks while removing it with Scald. However, despite its high physical bulk, Slowbro's Special Defense stat is lackluster, leaving it open to many special attackers such as Latios and Landorus. Being a Water-type leaves Slowbro weak to Electric- and Grass-type attacks, a trait exploited by common metagame threats such as Tapu Koko and Tapu Bulu. Mega Slowbro is vulnerable to status conditions, namely Toxic, which greatly hinders its role as a setup sweeper, and it faces competition from other Mega Evolutions on Psychic such as Mega Latias and Mega Gallade, with the former punching holes in types such as Normal and the latter doing well in matchups such as Water and Flying.

Water

Mega Slowbro is a great sweeper for Water-type teams with Calm Mind, as its good natural bulk, access to Regenerator as a pre-Mega ability, and reliable recovery in Slack Off allow it to set up relatively easily. Mega Slowbro's Psychic typing allows it to threaten key Pokemon on Poison teams like Mega Venusaur and Toxapex, both of which can be difficult to for Water teams to overcome. Mega Slowbro's abilities complement its sets and the roles it plays, with its great pre-Mega ability in Regenerator combined with Slack Off allowing it to effectively act as a defensive pivot and its Shell Armor enabling it to set up with Calm Mind and Iron Defense without fear of critical hits. Mega Slowbro has an impressive Defense stat of base 180, which allows it to take on strong wallbreakers that would otherwise muscle through defensive cores on Water teams like Mega Gallade and Choice Band Diggersby. Its defensive capabilities are further improved due to Scald, as it can burn physical threats with the move, making it incredibly hard to break past. However, Mega Slowbro has a mediocre Special Defense stat, which makes it vulnerable to strong special attackers such as Latios and Tapu Koko, although it can beat most of them after a few Calm Mind boosts. Mega Slowbro also possesses weaknesses to types such as Dark and Bug along with Grass and Electric, compounding Water's weaknesses. Mega Slowbro is very slow, which means it will always take a hit before moving and is pressured by strong wallbreakers like Choice Specs Hydreigon. It is reliant on setup moves like Calm Mind and Iron Defense to pose as a threat, so Taunt users such as Mew and Jellicent can shut it down. Mega Slowbro is also susceptible to status moves such as Toxic, which greatly hinder its ability to set up and act as a defensive pivot, but this is not an issue if it is running Rest.
monotype.comments:
Other Options

Psychic

Rocky Helmet can be used on Slowbro instead of a Colbur Berry because of its ability to punish physical attackers, and Leftovers is an option to increase Slowbro's overall longevity; however, not using a Colbur Berry hinders Slowbro's ability to check Dark-type Pokemon such as Mega Sharpedo well. Ice Beam is an option over Thunder Wave to hit Dragon- and Flying-type Pokemon such as Dragonite and Garchomp; however, dropping Thunder Wave means that Slowbro cannot cripple Pokemon such as Mega Sharpedo and Hydreigon by spreading paralysis. An Iron Defense / Calm Mind / Scald / Rest set can be used, as Iron Defense lets Mega Slowbro wall setup sweepers such as Gyarados, Calm Mind raises its Special Defense, and Rest makes it immune to status, making Mega Slowbro very hard to knock out after it accumulates a few boosts. However, Rest makes Mega Slowbro vulnerable to attacks while it sleeps. Psyshock can be used over Psychic to hit more specially defensive Pokemon such as Mantine, although most specially defensive Pokemon have ways of dealing with Mega Slowbro, like Haze in Mantine's case.

Water

Sleep Talk can be used on the Rest set over Iron Defense; however, this forces Mega Slowbro to lose out on augmenting its Defense, allowing it to be more easily broken through by setup sweepers like Bisharp.

Checks and Counters

Psychic

Electric-types: Electric-type Pokemon such as Tapu Koko, Magnezone, and Alolan Raichu deal immense damage to Slowbro with their STAB attacks and can grab momentum using Volt Switch.

Grass-types: Grass-type Pokemon such as Mega Venusaur, Tapu Bulu, and Celebi threaten Slowbro with their Grass-type attacks, although some of them such as Breloom and Ferrothorn can't afford to get hit by Fire Blast.

Bug-types: Bug-type Pokemon such as Scizor, Heracross, and Volcarona threaten Slowbro with their STAB attacks. However, most Bug-type Pokemon are afraid of getting hit by Fire Blast or Thunder Wave.

Special Wallbreakers: Special wallbreakers such as Gengar, Blacephalon, and Hydreigon do immense damage to Slowbro because of its poor special bulk. However, Mega Slowbro is able to take on special attackers after boosting several times with Calm Mind.

Toxic: Toxic users such as Gastrodon, Chansey, and Swampert wear Slowbro down by using badly poisoning it with Toxic. Being badly poisoned puts Mega Slowbro on a timer, preventing it from sweeping late-game.

Specially Defensive Pokemon: Specially defensive Pokemon such as Mantine, Zapdos, and Chansey wall non-Calm Mind Slowbro, while Mega Slowbro cannot do much in return due to Toxic and Haze making an attempt to sweep futile.

Haze and Phazers: Pokemon such as Toxapex and Mantine that carry Haze check Mega Slowbro by wiping out its stat boosts, while phazers such as Whirlwind Skarmory and Roar Swampert force Mega Slowbro to switch and remove its stat boosts.

Taunt: Taunt users such as Mew and Hydreigon lock Slowbro into attacking moves, which means it cannot heal itself with Slack Off, cripple Pokemon with Thunder Wave, or set up with Calm Mind.

Water

Electric-types: Strong Electric-type Pokemon such as Alolan Raichu, Tapu Koko, and Magnezone pose a huge threat to Mega Slowbro by easily KOing it with STAB moves.

Grass-types: Grass-type Pokemon such as Mega Venusaur, Celebi, and Tapu Bulu can easily check Mega Slowbro with super effective STAB moves and either KO it or render it severely weak.

Dark-types: Mega Slowbro has a hard time against Dark-types such as Hydreigon and Greninja, as they can easily check it, especially prior to setting up.

Toxic: Toxic puts a stop to Mega Slowbro if it lacks Rest by putting it on a timer.

Special Attackers: Strong special attackers, such as Mega Charizard Y and Blacephalon, can hit Mega Slowbro hard prior to setting up due to its average Special Defense stat.

Stallbreakers: Stallbreakers such as Jellicent and Mew can easily shut down Mega Slowbro by utilizing Taunt, as Mega Slowbro has to rely on setup moves to be a threat.

Haze Users and Phazers: Haze users such as Mantine can easily negate stat boosts of Mega Slowbro and waste its PP, making it hard for Mega Slowbro to beat them. Similarly, phazers such as Swampert and Empoleon can phaze out Mega Slowbro with Roar and negate its stat boosts.

Water-immune Pokemon: Water-immune Pokemon such as Mantine, Cradily, Seismitoad, and Gastrodon easily check the Iron Defense set, as that set has only Scald as an attacking move.

Defensive Pivot (Psychic).description:
Moves

Scald is Slowbro's main attack and can cripple physical attackers like Gyarados and Mega Lopunny with a burn. Slack Off is a form of reliable recovery and is used to ensure that Slowbro stays healthy throughout the battle. Thunder Wave is used to cripple fast Pokemon that cannot otherwise be beaten through Scald and Slack Off like Hydreigon, Greninja, and Latios. Fire Blast is used to hit Steel- and Grass-type Pokemon like Scizor, Bisharp, and Ferrothorn.

Set Details

Maximum HP and Defense EVs along with a Bold nature are used in order to let Slowbro serve as an effective physical wall. Colbur Berry is the preferred item on Slowbro, as it gives Slowbro the ability to take a Dark-type attack, which can be crucial when checking huge threats like Mega Sharpedo and Bisharp. A huge reason why Slowbro is an effective pivot lies in its ability Regenerator, which keeps it healthy throughout the duration of the game by healing it a bit every time it switches out.

Usage Tips

Send Slowbro in to soak up physical attacks like Mega Lopunny's Return and Excadrill's Earthquake and shield your other Pokemon from getting damaged. Use Slowbro as a pivot that can consistently heal itself with Slack Off and Regenerator. If Slowbro gets hit with a very strong attack, switch it back out in order to keep it healthy. Utilize Regenerator throughout the battle by constantly switching out Slowbro to keep its HP high. Because of the aforementioned reason, Slowbro is great for soaking up moves like U-turn. Avoid Toxic users such as Porygon2 and Gastrodon, as being badly poisoned wears Slowbro down and hinders its ability to check physical attackers reliably. In some situations, using Thunder Wave twice in a row is recommended, when the opposing player may switch a check directly into Slowbro, in order to cripple the Pokemon that is sent out. Use Scald frequently in order to inflict burns and wear down bulky Pokemon such as Toxapex and Celesteela. Preserve Slowbro's Colbur Berry until it is necessary to check Dark-type Pokemon, most notably Mega Sharpedo and Bisharp, later in the game. Use Thunder Wave in order to cripple Pokemon that cannot otherwise be beaten through using Slack Off and Scald such as Mega Lopunny and Mega Sharpedo. Thunder Wave is also useful in situations where you would need to cripple faster Pokemon such as Mega Sharpedo and Mega Pidgeot, while fishing for burns with Scald would be more useful against physical attackers or bulky Pokemon that can be crippled or worn down by burn such as Garchomp and Celesteela. Be wary of Taunt users like Mega Gyarados looking to shut Slowbro down; use Scald on a predicted Taunt in order to fish for burns, crippling the opposing Pokemon.

Team Options

Choice Scarf Victini is a good partner for Slowbro, as it takes care of many of Slowbro's offensive checks such as Tapu Koko and Tapu Bulu. When using a Choice Band, Victini can break past Slowbro's defensive checks such as Chansey and Porygon2. Victini will often need to switch out sooner or later because of V-create and U-turn, and Slowbro is an excellent partner for Victini to pivot out to, being able to switch into Water- and Ground-type Pokemon such as Mega Swampert and Excadrill for Victini. Choice Scarf Latios is able to offensively check many of Slowbro's checks such as Hydreigon and Blacephalon. Similarly to Victini, Choice Specs Latios can also beat defensive Pokemon that Slowbro struggles against. Latios also checks Grass- and Electric-types that would otherwise threaten Slowbro. Latios and Latias pair well with Slowbro for their Defog support, being able to remove Toxic Spikes and other hazards, while Latias is also able to heal Slowbro with Healing Wish. Celebi supports Slowbro using its Grass typing, which allows it to switch into Electric- and Grass-type attacks for Slowbro. Celebi can also use U-turn to pivot into Slowbro and can absorb Toxic poison with Natural Cure. Mega Latias pairs well defensively with Slowbro because Slowbro's physical bulk protects Mega Latias from strong wallbreakers such as Excadrill and Mega Lopunny that may threaten Mega Latias before it sets up with Calm Mind. Mega Gallade can beat defensive Pokemon such as Chansey and Porygon2 for Slowbro. Slowbro can also use Thunder Wave to slow down opposing threats such as Greninja that could otherwise check Mega Gallade. Jirachi forms a solid defensive core with Slowbro, since it appreciates Slowbro's ability to switch into Fire-type attacks aimed at Jirachi, while Jirachi can switch into special attackers such as Latios and Mega Diancie that threaten Slowbro thanks to its Steel typing. Mew is a good partner for Slowbro because it beats Slowbro's defensive checks with Knock Off and Taunt and can also run Defog, which is especially good because it clears hazards such as Toxic Spikes that can threaten Slowbro's health. Offensive Mew sets also appreciate the speed control that comes from Slowbro's Thunder Wave, which can cripple fast threats and pave the way for Mew to sweep.

Calm Mind Mega (Psychic).description:
Moves

Calm Mind is Mega Slowbro's main form of setup, raising its Special Attack and Special Defense in order to sweep. Slack Off acts as Mega Slowbro's reliable recovery and works in tandem with Calm Mind in order to let it set up safety and heal off damage. Scald is Slowbro's most spammable attack and is useful for crippling physical attackers and wearing down Pokemon. Psychic allows Mega Slowbro to hit Poison-type Pokemon super effectively and is used over Psyshock in order to hit Toxapex harder.

Set Details

Maximum HP and Defense EVs with a Bold nature ensure that Mega Slowbro will be able to take physical hits comfortably after Mega Evolving, notably Choice Band Diggersby's Return, and safely boost with Calm Mind. Slowbro Mega Evolves through Slowbronite, increasing its Defense and Special Attack. Regenerator is the preferred ability before Mega Evolving because it allows Slowbro to serve as a defensive pivot. Shell Armor, Mega Slowbro's ability, protects Mega Slowbro from critical hits.

Usage Tips

Before Mega Evolution, utilize Slowbro as a defensive pivot that can heal itself with Slack Off and Regenerator. Be aware that Mega Slowbro loses Regenerator once it Mega Evolves. Thus, it is best to hold off on Mega Evolving and setting up until Mega Slowbro's checks and counters like Mantine and Tapu Koko have been removed. Mega Evolving Slowbro is also a good idea if the extra bulk is needed to check a certain threat that Slowbro wouldn't be able to otherwise such as Choice Band Diggersby or Dragonite. Take advantage of Pokemon Choice-locked into a move that does not threaten Mega Slowbro such as Victini's V-Create and Landorus-T's Earthquake in order to freely use Calm Mind. Try to remove entry hazards such as Toxic Spikes and Spikes before Slowbro comes in, as the former will leave Slowbro poisoned, putting a timer on it, and the latter will slowly wear it down when it switches in, hurting Slowbro's ability to switch into threats. Spikes aren't a huge threat to Slowbro until it has Mega Evolved, though, as then it cannot regenerate the chip damage caused by them as easily anymore. Steer Slowbro away from Toxic users like Porygon2, as being badly poisoned impedes its ability to set up and sweep. Similarly, in matchups such as Normal where Slowbro will be threatened by Toxic users, it is best to use it to bait burns or paralysis so that it cannot be affected by Toxic any longer. In matchups where Mega Slowbro does not have many setup opportunities, such as Fairy with Tapu Koko and Tapu Bulu, prioritize attacking and fishing for burns with Scald over trying to set up.

Team Options

Victini in particular is a good partner for Mega Slowbro, as its Choice Scarf set helps keep faster foes in check and beats Pokemon such as Tapu Koko, while its Choice Band set serves as an effective wallbreaker that can punch holes in Pokemon that Mega Slowbro struggles against such as Chansey, Mantine, and Mega Venusaur. Mega Slowbro is also able to switch into Pokemon like Excadrill and Diggersby that could potentially harm Victini in return. Latios pairs well with Mega Slowbro because it can Defog away entry hazards, mainly Toxic Spikes, and it can support Mega Slowbro through the power it packs with its offensive Life Orb and Soul Dew sets. Latias, like Latios, is also able to support Mega Slowbro by checking many Pokemon that threaten it, such as Choice Scarf Heracross and Hydreigon, while also giving Mega Slowbro more setup opportunities by healing it with Healing Wish. Additionally, using Latias and Latios along with Slowbro can confuse the opposing player as to which Mega Evolution you are actually using. Mew is a good partner for Mega Slowbro because it is able to deal with many of Mega Slowbro's defensive checks by using Taunt and Knock Off with its stallbreaker set and use Defog to remove hazards such as Toxic Spikes that may potentially damage Mega Slowbro. Jirachi can switch into special attackers such as Latios and Mega Diancie thanks to its high Special Defense and can also heal Mega Slowbro with Healing Wish; in return, Mega Slowbro is able to protect Jirachi from physical attackers such as Excadrill and Garchomp.

Calm Mind (Water).description:
Moves

Calm Mind makes Mega Slowbro more powerful while patching up its middling Special Defense. Slack Off gives it reliable recovery, which lets it effectively act as a defensive pivot or bulky sweeper without getting worn down. Scald is a STAB move that has a good chance to spread burns and further improves Mega Slowbro's bulk by burning physical attackers, making it very hard to break past. Psychic as Mega Slowbro's secondary STAB move allows it to hit Pokemon that resist Scald like Mega Venusaur and Toxapex. Psyshock may be used over Psychic to win Calm Mind wars and hit special walls, such as Chansey, significantly harder. However, Psyshock is less reliable against Toxapex, as most Toxapex are physically defensive.

Set Details

Maximum HP and Defense investment along with a Bold nature makes Mega Slowbro incredibly physical bulky, allowing Slowbro to switch in on Choice Band Diggersby to tank the hit and then Mega Evolve to tank the subsequent hit and prevent Diggersby from getting a clean KO. The spread also allows it to avoid a 2HKO from Tapu Bulu's Horn Leech. Slowbro has the ability Regenerator before Mega Evolving, letting it effectively act as a defensive pivot. Upon Mega Evolving, Mega Slowbro gains the ability Shell Armor, which allows it to safely use its setup moves.

Usage Tips

Avoid Mega Evolving Slowbro right away early-game, as it loses Regenerator upon Mega Evolving, which is incredibly useful for acting as a physical wall for Water teams. However, Slowbro should Mega Evolve as soon as possible against Normal teams to take on Choice Band Diggersby better. Early-game, Scald should be used often to spread burns and wear the opposing team down. Mega Slowbro has a mediocre Special Defense stat, so strong special wallbreakers like Mega Charizard Y, Tapu Koko, and Hydreigon need to be taken care of before it attempts to set up. Pokemon that carry Haze or phazing moves, such as Mantine, Swampert, and Empoleon, also need to be taken out before Mega Slowbro can attempt to set up. Status moves and entry hazards, such as Toxic and Toxic Spikes, should be avoided at all costs, as they make Mega Slowbro very easy to check by putting it on a timer. Against Water teams, Mega Slowbro should try to get burned by Scald, as this prevents the opposing team from using Toxic and crippling it, thus allowing it to set up effectively. Against Poison teams, Mega Slowbro should not switch into Toxic Spikes, as poison severely limits its ability to be a Calm Mind sweeper. Mega Slowbro can set up on passive Pokemon such as Toxapex, but one must scout for Toxic first to ensure safe setup.

Team Options

Toxapex has very good synergy with Mega Slowbro, as it provides a neutrality to Grass and forms a Regenerator core with Slowbro, which can be very hard for opposing teams to break. Toxapex can even check threats such as Mega Charizard Y and Volcarona, provide Toxic Spikes support for Mega Slowbro, and absorb Toxic Spikes. Swampert, Gastrodon, and Lanturn provide Mega Slowbro with a crucial Electric immunity, checking threats like Tapu Koko and Magnezone. Swampert also provides Stealth Rock support, which is useful for wearing down opposing teams and making types like Bug and Flying easier to deal with; Gastrodon has reliable recovery and good mixed bulk that allows it to better check Electric-type Pokemon for Mega Slowbro; and Lanturn can provide Heal Bell support, making it hard for opposing teams to wear down Mega Slowbro through Toxic. Mantine helps Mega Slowbro by checking special attackers such as Hydreigon and Volcarona. Additionally, it provides Defog support so that Mega Slowbro is not plagued by entry hazards like Toxic Spikes. Choice Scarf Greninja is a good teammate, as it can check fast threats such as Tapu Bulu and Tapu Koko as well as Dragon-types like Hydreigon and Latios. Keldeo breaks down walls such as Chansey, which are obstacles for Mega Slowbro if they carry Toxic. Keldeo also checks Dark-types like Hydreigon, while Mega Slowbro provides a defensive backbone for Keldeo by coming in on strong physical moves. Gyarados helps to check Grass-types such as Breloom and Tapu Bulu by utilizing its Flyinium Z set. Gyarados also acts as a secondary sweeper for Water teams and makes certain matchups, such as against Bug, a little easier. Sap Sipper Azumarill is a great teammate, as it not only provides a valuable Grass immunity to the team for checking threats such as Tapu Bulu and Breloom, but also acts as a check to Dragon-types like Hydreigon for Mega Slowbro. Azumarill can also take out walls such as Celesteela and Ferrothorn, with its Perish Song trapping set, which makes it easier for Mega Slowbro to set up. Suicune is a good teammate for Mega Slowbro, as it helps pressure Mega Slowbro's checks, making it difficult for a team to beat both.

Iron Defense (Water).description:
Moves

Calm Mind allows Mega Slowbro to patch up its lackluster Special Defense stat and tank special hits from threats like Latios and Greninja after a few Calm Mind boosts. Iron Defense allows Mega Slowbro to boost its gigantic Defense even further and shrug off strong setup sweepers such as Garchomp and Mega Pinsir, turning Mega Slowbro into an impenetrable force. Scald is the only STAB move on the set, as it offers good utility by having a very good chance to burn physical threats such as Tapu Bulu and Belly Drum Azumarill. Rest not only allows Mega Slowbro to fully regain its health but also makes Mega Slowbro unafraid of status-inducing moves such as Toxic.

Set Details

Maximum HP and Defense investment along with a Bold nature allows Mega Slowbro to be as physically bulky as possible and reliably check most physical attackers, including Diggersby. Regenerator as a pre-Mega ability allows Slowbro to be an effective defensive pivot for Water teams that is hard to wear down. Once it has Mega Evolved, it gains the ability Shell Armor, which gives it an easier time setting up.

Usage Tips

It is important to not Mega Evolve early-game, as this causes Mega Slowbro to lose out on Regenerator, which is very important for it to stay healthy during the match and act as a reliable wall for Water teams. Since Mega Slowbro has pretty lackluster Special Defense, it should not be switched in against strong special attackers such as Landorus, as it risks getting severely weakened. Mega Slowbro should attempt to use Calm Mind against physical attackers like Mega Lopunny and Mega Gallade as well as walls, as such Pokemon cannot do much damage to it in return and it can boost its Special Defense to endure special attackers on the opposing team. As Mega Slowbro relies on setup moves to pose a defensive threat, Taunt users such as stallbreaker Mew and Jellicent need to be removed before it can attempt to set up. Haze users such as Mantine and Toxapex also need to be removed, as these Pokemon can easily nullify all of Mega Slowbro's boosts and waste its PP. Additionally, Poison-types like Mega Venusaur and Toxapex need to be taken care of, as Mega Slowbro's only attacking move is Scald and both of these Pokemon resist the move. Mega Slowbro should use Rest to get rid of status conditions such as poison and set up on status inducers like Celesteela. Rest should also be used to keep Mega Slowbro healthy to allow it to better tank hits from special attackers once it starts setting up Calm Mind, while Iron Defense should be used to check physical setup sweepers and Z-Move users such as Gyarados, Bisharp, and Belly Drum Azumarill.

Team Options

Teammates that can cover Mega Slowbro's weakness to Electric such as Swampert and Gastrodon are appreciated. Both of these Pokemon can provide additional support for it, with Swampert using Stealth Rock to wear down Mega Slowbro's checks and counters and Gastrodon having reliable recovery and good mixed bulk to fare better against Electric teams. Toxapex provides a neutrality to Grass, which is important for checking threats such as Mega Venusaur. Additionally, Toxapex can provide Toxic Spikes support to wear down teams for Mega Slowbro and can also stop special set up sweepers such as Volcarona with Haze. Mantine can check strong special attackers such as Mega Charizard Y and Hydreigon as well as provide Defog support so that Mega Slowbro is not worn down by entry hazards such as Toxic Spikes, which may force it to use Rest. For stall teams, Alomomola is another good teammate that acts as a good mixed wall and can relieve pressure on Mega Slowbro to check physical attackers. It also forms a Regenerator core with Slowbro that is very hard to break past, provides Wish support to help with recovery, and checks threats such as Mega Venusaur by utilizing Mirror Coat. Sap Sipper Azumarill covers Water's weakness to Grass-type moves and checks Pokemon such as Breloom and Tapu Bulu, which can cripple or break past Mega Slowbro. It has an additional immunity to Dragon, allowing it to check Pokemon like Hydreigon. Teammates that can break the Mega Venusaur + Toxapex core such as Flyinium Z Gyarados and Groundium Z Greninja are also good teammates for Mega Slowbro. Keldeo is a good partner for Mega Slowbro, as it can take care of Water-immune Pokemon such as Mantine and Seismitoad with Hidden Power Electric and Secret Sword.

Defensive.description: Slowbro is a good choice as a bulky Water-type, since it's among the few with a reliable recovery move. The big choice to make is whether to use Mega Slowbro or regular Slowbro. Mega Slowbro is bulkier, and its access to Shell Armor makes it among the few Pokemon to be able to effectively use Iron Defense, while regular Slowbro can wear down physical attackers quicker with Rocky Helmet and can restore its health via switching out with Regenerator.

Trick Room Setter.description: Mega Slowbro's good Special Attack and pathetic Speed makes it a great choice for a Trick Room setter. Since setting up Trick Room is the most important aspect, Slack Off isn't always needed, though it's still useful if coverage isn't as important. While Regenerator is usually the better ability, Oblivious can be useful before Mega Evolving to set up Trick Room in the face of Taunt users.

1v1.overview: Mega Slowbro is one of the most consistent setup stall Pokemon in the 1v1 metagame. With naturally monstrous Defense, it can tank neutral attacks from the strongest physical attackers in the tier, such as Mega Charizard X, Flyinium Z-boosted Fly Dragonite, and Mega Lopunny, even without Defense investment. Thanks to this, Mega Slowbro can put as many EVs into Special Defense and HP as possible, which enables it to tank moves from powerful special attackers as well, such as specially offensive Dragonite and Choice Scarf Porygon Z, and follow up with recovery in the form of Slack Off or Rest, or use various setup moves such as Iron Defense, Calm Mind, and Amnesia in order to get out of KO range. Slowbro also has access to two very useful abilities for its role, those being Oblivious and Shell Armor, allowing it to be immune to the move Taunt, which normally shuts down all forms of stall, before Mega Evolving and avoid being hit by a critical hit after, making it more reliable against every Pokemon that can boost its offenses. Mega Slowbro is, unfortunately, one of the slowest Pokemon in the metagame, so it is only able to set up after it has already taken damage, leaving it susceptible to being knocked out by sufficiently powerful super effective attacks. Mega Slowbro is also weak to several common attacking moves, those being Grass-, Electric-, and Dark-type moves, so you'll need to watch out for moves such as Giga Drain, Thunderbolt, Dark Pulse, and their respective Z-Moves from Pokemon such as Mega Venusaur, Magnezone, and Hoopa-U.
1v1.comments:
Other Options

Foul Play is an interesting niche choice that beats a notable anti-Mega Slowbro set in Belly Drum Mega Charizard X. Considering the popularity of Mega Charizard X, this may be an interesting choice to have more of a guaranteed matchup against every variant of Mega Charizard X. However, in every other regard, Foul Play is severely inferior to Scald.

Checks and Counters

Super Effective Attackers: As Mega Slowbro is such an excellent stall Pokemon in the context of 1v1, with answers to Taunt, status conditions, most forms of stall, and critical hits, the most common threat against Mega Slowbro will be super effective attackers, and it will struggle against those that can exploit its Water / Psychic typing. These include prevalent Pokemon such as Mega Charizard Y, Magnezone, Z-Conversion Porygon-Z, Choice Specs Greninja, Aegislash, Choice Specs Genesect, Tapu Bulu, Gigavolt Havoc Zeraora, Bloom Doom Heatran, Kartana, and Hoopa-U. The only real relevant exception to this in 1v1 is the aforementioned Mega Gyarados, which, unfortunately, only has Crunch, which Mega Slowbro can tank using Iron Defense.

Very Powerful Attackers: There are a select few Pokemon in the metagame that are simply so powerful that they can overwhelm Mega Slowbro with neutral damage. These include Choice Specs or Normalium Z Porygon-Z, which can OHKO even a fully invested Mega Slowbro using Hyper Beam or Breakneck Blitz, or Belly Drum Mega Charizard X, which can very impressively 2HKO a +2 Defense Mega Slowbro with Outrage after a Belly Drum, unless Mega Slowbro runs Foul Play.

Encore Users: The cousin of Taunt, Encore, is, unfortunately, not blocked by Oblivious and will pose a serious problem to Mega Slowbro, as it will not be able to use anything except the move it has been locked into for the remainder of the battle. Some popular Encore users include Primarina, Mega Gardevoir, Mega Alakazam, and Whimsicott.

Other Rest Stallers: While Mega Slowbro can usually outlast other forms of stall by using the move Rest, retaining more PP while it is asleep, if its opponent also has Rest, Mega Slowbro may be in trouble.
