If Alolan Muk is carrying Pursuit, you can play more riskily and switch it directly in against Pokemon it wants to trap, such as Latios, in order to secure the KO. Try to keep entry hazards such as Stealth Rock away to avoid making Alolan Muk take unnecessary damage, as the lack of recovery means that damage will add up fairly quickly. Early-game, use Knock Off liberally to remove as many of the opposing team's items as possible. For example, against Fairy teams, removing the enemy Klefki's Light Clay is a top priority early on to limit the number of turns that Reflect and Light Screen will halve the damage you deal. While using Knock Off, Alolan Muk should also use Poison Jab frequently to spread poison. In this way, Alolan Muk can cripple walls like Porygon2 in two ways, both by removing a crucial item such as Eviolite and by poisoning them. Be careful when trying to poison walls that can burn Alolan Muk, such as Mega Sableye and Mantine, though, as it hates being burned. In addition to halving Alolan Muk's Attack, burns start the timer on how long Alolan Muk can act as a wall. Make sure to preserve Alolan Muk's health in matchups where it is needed to check a high priority threat. For example, against Bug teams, Rock Slide Alolan Muk is the most reliable check to Volcarona, as even a +2 Inferno Overdrive with Stealth Rock support can't OHKO Alolan Muk, so it is important to not let Alolan Muk take too much damage early on.

Team Options

Alolan Muk is a great teammate for almost all Dark teams, as it serves as a Fairy check for offensive teams and a very bulky special wall for more balanced teams. Entry hazard control is important for preserving Alolan Muk's HP, so Mega Sableye and physically defensive Mandibuzz are frequent partners for Alolan Muk, as Magic Bounce can prevent Stealth Rock from coming up and Mandibuzz can Defog hazards if they get past Mega Sableye. Together, the trio form a great defensive core as well, covering all weaknesses effectively. While Sand Stream will chip away at Alolan Muk, Tyranitar is still a good option for supporting Alolan Muk. Tyranitar can use Pursuit, letting Alolan Muk bring coverage moves instead, and it also has Stealth Rock to help punish the switches that Alolan Muk can easily force. With Levitate, Hydreigon makes for a more offensive teammate that can help beat Ground-types for Alolan Muk. Hydreigon also takes on physical walls and particularly Steel-types very effectively, so Alolan Muk may find it easier to drop Fire-type coverage for other options. Greninja is another strong offensive Ground check, as its Ice Beam threatens almost every Ground-type. Greninja also uses U-turn for pivoting into Alolan Muk easily and Gunk Shot to relieve some of the pressure on Alolan Muk to check Fairy-types. Weavile can be helpful for relieving pressure on Alolan Muk, as it sometimes runs Pursuit to enable Alolan Muk to choose other coverage moves and can offensively check most Ground-types such as Garchomp.

Specially Defensive.description:
Set Information

Crunch is Alolan Muk's Dark-type STAB move, which allows it to threaten one of the most dangerous Mega Evolutions in the tier in Mega Alakazam, as well as other Psychic-types like Starmie and Mew. Fire Blast is used to damage Melmetal effectively. Mega Drain take advantage of some of Alolan Muk's checks, namely Poliwrath and Rhydon, while also granting it recovery. Alolan Muk uses Toxic to set a timer on bulky foes such as Mew and Zapdos, which is especially useful because its accuracy is boosted through its Poison typing. Rest can be opted for over Toxic as a means of restoring its health, but this leaves Alolan Muk vulnerable to setup sweepers such as Calm Mind Mega Alakazam and Nasty Plot Mew; moreover, this move usually would require support from Eevee-S's Sparkly Swirl because of the time it takes for Alolan Muk to wake up. Facade can also be used in the last moveslot to deal extra damage when afflicted with a status condition and is especially beneficial against Will-O-Wisp Mew, despite it being worn down by a potential Toxic as well. A Sassy nature bolsters Alolan Muk's defensive capabilities without sacrificing any power while still letting it be faster than foes such as Rhydon and Melmetal.

Usage Tips

Alolan Muk should be kept as healthy as possible in order to threaten powerful special attackers such as Mega Alakazam, Gengar, and Starmie. If Alolan Muk is using Rest, it should avoid being taken advantage of by setup sweepers such as Calm Mind Mega Alakazam and Nasty Plot Mew. Alolan Muk should avoid powerful physical attackers such as Mega Beedrill and Dragonite because of its very poor physical bulk. It should also be cautious of Eevee-S, as its ability to burn it through Sizzly Slide and sap away at its health through Sappy Seed make it a nuisance to remove.

Team Options

Alolan Muk greatly appreciates Eevee-S's support, as it has the capability to heal its status conditions through Sparkly Swirl, burn some of its physical checks such as Dragonite and Mega Gyarados through Sizzly Slide, and even provide it with residual recovery by virtue of Sappy Seed. This especially holds true for Rest variants of Alolan Muk. Physically defensive foes such as Melmetal, Poliwrath, and Mega Venusaur can sponge powerful physical attacks for Alolan Muk and can share the burden of sponging other special attacks from foes such as Mega Alakazam and Gengar if need be. Alolan Muk appreciates Flying-types such as Dragonite and Zapdos, as they cover its weakness to Ground-type moves. Psychic-types such as Mew and Mega Alakazam can also be paired with Alolan Muk, as they can heavily threaten common Fighting-types such as Poliwrath. In return, Alolan Muk can threaten opposing Psychic-types for Mew and Mega Alakazam.

battlespotsingles.overview: Alolan Muk's good defensive typing of Poison / Dark, solid special bulk, and access to STAB Pursuit allow it to be a good special wall with Assault Vest that is capable of Pursuit trapping Pokemon such as Mega Gengar, Tapu Lele, and Latios and checking Greninja, Volcarona, and Serperior. Apart from Pursuit trapping, Alolan Muk provides its team with the utility of Knock Off and Poison Jab by removing the items of foes and spreading poison status. However, due to the fact that Alolan Muk is forced to use Assault Vest to effectively take hits from foes it switches into, it lacks recovery and is prone to getting worn down over the match. It also has a lone yet exploitable weakness to Ground, and combined with low Speed stat, Alolan Muk is very prone to getting revenge killed by many of the physical attackers in the tier, most of which run Earthquake. Lastly, although it has various coverage options such as Fire Punch, Rock Tomb, Shadow Sneak, Ice Punch, and Brick Break, Alolan Muk only has room for one of them, meaning common foes such as Landorus-T, Mega Salamence, Mega Mawile, Ferrothorn, and Mega Tyranitar can easily take advantage of Alolan Muk depending on what coverage move it opts for.
battlespotsingles.comments:
Other Options

Payback can be used to deal more damage to Pokemon that hold Z-Crystals, but it is less reliable overall and lacks the utility Knock Off provides. Gunk Shot is a stronger Poison-type STAB move, but its poor accuracy and lower chance of poisoning foes leave this option inferior to Poison Jab. Alolan Muk can choose various coverage moves; Fire Blast lets Alolan Muk 2HKO Ferrothorn without taking damage from Iron Barbs and guarantees the OHKO on Kartana while retaining the ability to 2HKO Mega Scizor, but it does pitiful damage to Celesteela and has a chance to miss. Brick Break hits Heatran and Tyranitar and also breaks screens and Aurora Veil, but it doesn't have much use otherwise. Ice Punch surprises Mega Salamence and Garchomp, but the former can set up on Alolan Muk after Intimidate anyway. Lum Berry is a plausible option to more reliably Pursuit trap Mega Gengar by healing from sleep or burn once. Recycle in tandem with Figy Berry, Curse, and Minimize can function with heavy team support, but Curse sets are outclassed by Snorlax, while strategies employing Minimize are inconsistent.

Checks and Counters

Ground-types: Ground-types such as Landorus-T, Garchomp, Swampert, and Excadrill take little damage from Poison Jab and can force out Alolan Muk, and therefore are some of the best offensive checks to Alolan Muk. However, most Ground-types do not like losing their items to Knock Off or getting poisoned, and Excadrill must be wary of Fire Punch.

Steel-types: Although all of them dislike losing their items to Knock Off unless they have Z-Crystals, Steel-types can switch into Alolan Muk with ease thanks to their generally high bulk and immunity to Poison Jab. While Celesteela, Ferrothorn, Kartana, and Mega Scizor must be wary of Fire-type moves, they can otherwise easily take advantage of Alolan Muk. Heatran can beat variants of Alolan Muk that carry Fire-type moves, but it does not like losing its item to Knock Off and dislikes the occasional Brick Break.

Strong Physical Attackers: Even when it is not hit super effectively, Alolan Muk is overwhelmed by a myriad of physical attackers in the tier, such as Mega Salamence, Mega Blaziken, Mega Charizard X, and Mega Kangaskhan, due to its mediocre Defense stat.

Physically Defensive Pokemon: In general, Alolan Muk struggles with foes that are marginally bulky and resist its moves. Tyranitar is a hard stop to any Alolan Muk variants without Brick Break and is only bothered by poison. Toxapex is impossible to surmount thanks to its phenomenal bulk, Regenerator, and immunity to poison, and it can threaten to burn Alolan Muk with Scald. Skarmory is not even 3HKOed by Fire Punch and only needs to worry about the rare Fire Blast and losing its item to Knock Off. Mega Venusaur doesn't mind Fire-type moves at all thanks to Thick Fat, and it can slowly wear down Alolan Muk with Leech Seed while shaking off any damage taken with Synthesis.

Burn: Not only does burn residually damage Alolan Muk, but it also neuters Alolan Muk's damage output, leaving it unable to Pursuit trap foes effectively. Therefore, Alolan Muk must play with caution against Scald users like Suicune and Toxapex and Will-O-Wisp users like Mega Gengar and Rotom formes.

Assault Vest.description:
Moves

Pursuit is capable of hitting foes hard if they attempt to switch out, and it allows Alolan Muk to guarantee removal of threats like Mega Gengar and Latios while netting significant damage against Tapu Lele. Knock Off is a stronger Dark-type STAB move that has utility of removing items and scouting for potential Z-Crystals and Mega Stones from certain foes. The move also ensures that the likes of Heatran and Celesteela are punished should they switch directly into Alolan Muk. Poison Jab is a consistent Poison-type STAB move that is used to deal with Fairy-types and notably OHKOes Tapu Lele, leaving it with a risky situation if it attempts to stay in predicting Pursuit. Factoring in Poison Touch, Poison Jab has a very high chance to poison a foe which is hazardous to Alolan Muk's potential checks. The last moveslot depends on what foes Alolan Muk desires to hit. Fire Punch 2HKOes Ferrothorn and Mega Scizor, has a chance to OHKO Kartana, and has general utility of hitting Steel-types super effectively. Rock Tomb lets Alolan Muk OHKO Volcarona and Mega Charizard Y and prevents Mega Salamence from freely setting up on Alolan Muk. Lastly, Shadow Sneak picks off weakened threats, especially Focus Sash users, and this move notably lets Alolan Muk finish off Tapu Koko, which has a chance to avoid the OHKO from Poison Jab.

Set Details

With 116 Attack EVs and an Adamant nature, Pursuit OHKOes Mega Gengar when it switches out, Poison Jab OHKOes Tapu Lele and 2HKOes Volcarona, and Knock Off almost always OHKOes maximum HP Aegislash in its Blade forme. Assault Vest in tandem with 140 HP EVs and 252 Special Defense EVs lets Alolan Muk avoid the 2HKO from Modest Choice Specs Tapu Lele, the 2HKO from +1 Volcarona after Stealth Rock, and the 3HKO from Life Orb Greninja. Minimizing Speed by using a Brave nature and 0 Speed IVs is an option that lets Alolan Muk underspeed Quiet Aegislash and OHKO it with Knock Off after it attacks and transforms into its Blade forme.

Usage Tips

Since Alolan Muk is capable of taking special hits well, it is a promising idea to switch it in on special attackers such as Mega Gengar, Tapu Lele, and Greninja. It can also switch into predicted uses of Toxic from passive walls such as Chansey. Once it comes in, Alolan Muk can KO or weaken Ghost- and Psychic-types with Pursuit as they are forced out, or it can proceed to hinder foes by removing their items with Knock Off or spreading poison with Poison Jab. Opponents are likely to switch in Steel-types, preferably the ones that can take advantage of or force out Alolan Muk, with an intention to prevent the spread of poison. Keep in mind that most common switch-ins to Alolan Muk can be punished with predictions and the coverage move Alolan Muk is carrying. Some Steel-types like Celesteela and Heatran are greatly hindered by a well-timed Knock Off on the switch, while Ferrothorn and Scizor will be harshly punished by Fire Punch. Lastly, be wary of foes that use Scald or Will-O-Wisp, as getting burned significantly hinders Alolan Muk's offensive capabilities, notably leaving it unable to effectively Pursuit trap a foe.

Team Options

Fighting-types make good partners for Alolan Muk; they can handle the Steel-types that annoy Alolan Muk, while Alolan Muk can dispose of Ghost- and Psychic-types, threaten Fairy-types, remove items from various physical walls like Celesteela, and spread poison. Mega Blaziken in particular appreciates Alolan Muk's ability to remove problematic Pokemon like Choice Scarf Latios and various Ghost-types, and Mega Blaziken can potentially stall out poisoned foes with Protect or Substitute to the point that it can KO them. Pokemon that can switch into Ground-type moves or handle physical attackers are good defensive partners for Alolan Muk. Landorus-T compresses both of these roles while threatening Steel-types with Earthquake. Rotom formes are good checks to Mega Salamence and Celesteela, and they can neuter physical attackers with Will-O-Wisp, giving Alolan Muk a better chance to take on them on. Serperior is a good offensive partner to Alolan Muk, as it appreciates Alolan Muk's ability to remove Mega Gengar and hinder Steel-types with Knock Off and Fire Punch, and in return it can take on Ground-types for Alolan Muk. Tapu Bulu summons Grassy Terrain, which weakens Earthquake and provides Alolan Muk with passive recovery. Defensive partners like Chansey, Skarmory, and Gliscor can pair well with Alolan Muk in defensive teams, as all of them appreciate removal of Mega Gengar. The latter two can also switch into Ground-type moves for Alolan Muk.

lc.overview: Possessing immense physical bulk and passable Speed and Attack, Shellder has the right traits to pull off a successful Shell Smash set. Being a pure Water-type is also beneficial for Shellder, not only giving it a great number of setup opportunities but also making it neutral or resistant to all priority attacks. Additionally, Skill Link gives Shellder an edge over most other Shell Smash users, as it allows Shellder to circumvent Focus Sash Abra without giving up an important coverage move. Skill Link has some interesting quirks in LC, making Icicle Spear and Rock Blast hit far harder than their already impressive 125 Base Power would imply. However, Shellder heavily relies on Shell Smash to become a threat and can hardly afford not to run the move.
lc.comments:
Other Options

Shellder has a few other options, though most are not worthwhile. Choice Scarf Shellder is one such example, but it lacks a niche due to Life Orb Staryu and Alolan Sandshrew being better fast Rapid Spin users. Choice Scarf Shellder may potentially catch a few Pokemon by surprise and revenge kill Pokemon behind Substitutes, but beyond this, its uses are limited. Staryu and Alolan Sandshrew also outclass a bulky Rapid Spin set, as both are able to KO Pumpkaboo attempting to spinblock, and, unlike them, Shellder struggles to switch into attacks. Shellder can use Rapid Spin as its fourth move on the Shell Smash set for role compression, but it necessitates a lot of support and is seldom worthwhile. Hidden Power Fighting can also be viable as the fourth attack, though it messes up Shellder's EV spread and leaves Shellder walled by some Mudbray sets with the only benefit being reliably KOing Pawniard and Magnemite. Hydro Pump is a decent option, KOing Mudbray if it switches into Rock Blast and doing more damage to Pawniard; however, it tends to miss at unideal times. Life Orb Shellder is the most viable other option at Shellder's disposal, though it requires Memento support to set up and its largest upsides are seldom useful unless Knock Off support cannot be afforded.

Checks and Counters

Slowpoke: Slowpoke survives any attack from even a boosted Shellder and stays healthy easily between Regenerator and Slack Off. Slowpoke is Shellder's largest issue, as even wearing it down is not enough thanks to Regenerator allowing for Slowpoke to switch in and heal at will.

Bulky Pokemon: Eviolite Spritzee proves to be an issue due to its massive bulk, but it cannot be hit by Knock Off lest a +2 Icicle Spear KO it. Similarly, Berry Juice Tirtouga and Chinchou can survive any one attack from +2 Shellder. Ferroseed is also able to defeat a boosted Shellder, though it needs to keep its HP high. Croagunk, while not especially bulky, is able to revenge kill with Vacuum Wave and can switch in on Liquidation or Rock Blast.

Choice Scarf Users with 18 Speed: 18 Speed Pokemon holding a Choice Scarf such as Gastly and Doduo are able to outspeed Shellder even after it has boosted, exploit its lowered defenses, and usually OHKO even from full health.

Intimidate: Shellder relies on being at +2 to secure KOs, making the likes of Snubbull and other Intimidate users problematic.

Steel-types: Liquidation is more than enough to handle a Magnemite set lacking Endure, but Endure + Recycle sets can be an issue. Similarly, Liquidation only KOes weakened Pawniard, so if kept healthy Pawniard is an adequate counter. Pawniard's Sucker Punch is threatening to Shellder as well, forcing weakened Shellder to try to avoid the priority attack. Honedge and Bronzor are bulky enough to also take little from Liquidation and therefore make good counters.

SMASHING.description:
Moves

Shell Smash makes Shellder super threatening, doubling both its Speed and its Attack. Icicle Spear and Rock Blast benefit from Skill Link, changing them from subpar attacks into Shellder's best offensive moves. Multi-hit attacks have some weird mechanics in LC, causing them to hit especially hard and be stronger than any of Shellder's STAB attacks. Moreover, Ice and Rock coverage is overall excellent, missing only Steel-types. Between just these two attacks, Shellder is truly an offensive threat and among the best sweepers in the tier. Liquidation is used to OHKO Mudbray and most Steel-types easily. Ice Shard can be run instead, primarily to KO Doduo and Diglett before they can use their strong priority options to revenge kill a weakened Shellder; however, Liquidation is generally better, as it makes Shellder far harder to wall.

Set Details

Skill Link is what makes Shellder so deadly, guaranteeing its multi-hit moves always hit five times, thus dealing the most possible damage. In LC, multi-hit moves are even more powerful than their Base Power would indicate thanks to the intricacies of the damage formula, giving Shellder amazing power. Shellder opts for an Impish nature over an Adamant one in favor of increasing its Defense to improve its survivability and setup capabilities, which are further bolstered by an Eviolite. The Attack investment without a boosting nature is more than adequate anyway, as +2 Icicle Spear and Rock Blast have the same damage rolls as they would with an Adamant nature. The Speed investment allows +2 Impish Shellder to outspeed 17 Speed Choice Scarf Pokemon such as Choice Scarf Mienfoo. A Jolly nature is also viable to allow Shellder to outspeed Scarf Doduo and Gastly after Shell Smash. The remaining EVs are invested into HP to give Shellder slightly better bulk.

Usage Tips

As with any sweeper, Shellder's checks need to be weakened before it can sweep. Some troubling Pokemon need to be scouted for, such as Chinchou and Tirtouga, as Berry Juice variants check Shellder while other variants do not. Otherwise, using Shellder is rather straightforward: set up on a physical attacker, avoid setting up on a status user, and proceed to sweep.

Team Options

Memento users, especially Cottonee and Diglett, pair well with Shellder, often giving it amazing setup chances and helping to keep it healthy enough to avoid being revenge killed. Diglett is also able to trap and weaken troubling Pokemon such as Chinchou and potentially Pawniard, while Cottonee is able to provide more utility through Knock Off support and act as a defensive pivot. Knock Off users are pretty good Pokemon to pair with Shellder too, as they remove Eviolites from the bulkiest Pokemon in the tier, allowing Shellder to blast through them. Vullaby is a great Knock Off user and is excellent at breaking down a number of checks it has in common with Shellder. Mienfoo and Timburr also pair well with Shellder, as they use Knock Off to remove Eviolites from some troubling Pokemon. More importantly, both are able to lure and exploit Croagunk and Snubbull, potentially removing one to make Shellder's sweep easier. Magnet Pull Magnemite is a decent partner that allows Shellder to drop Liquidation and run Ice Shard to prevent being revenge killed. Abra with Knock Off and Shadow Ball is a good wallbreaker for Shellder, as the set lures and beats Slowpoke and Honedge, two of the better, though uncommon, counters to Shellder. Lastly, Stealth Rock support is a necessity, making most reliable Stealth Rock users a good pairing. Hippopotas, Onix, and Pawniard are particularly good teammates due to helping fend off Electric-types and being the most reliable Stealth Rock users available.

monotype.overview:
Water

Cloyster is an amazing setup sweeper and late-game cleaner due to its access to Shell Smash, one of the best setup moves in the game. Cloyster's Skill Link ability in conjunction with moves like Icicle Spear and Rock Blast allows it to have very high-Base Power moves while also breaking potential Focus Sashes on Pokemon such as Breloom. A sky-high Defense stat allows Cloyster to set up Shell Smash against most physical attackers with ease, and a good offensive Water / Ice typing gives Cloyster opportunities to sweep many types, including Grass, Ground, Dragon, and Flying, once its checks have been taken care of. However, a lack of coverage moves forces Cloyster to rely on the less powerful Hydro Pump to hit Steel-types. Cloyster also has relatively low offensive stats, which means it needs to set up to be an offensive threat, and its very low special bulk makes it take lots of damage from even weak special attacks. This, combined with a poor defensive typing with only two resistances, means Cloyster can have a hard time finding appropriate setup opportunities. This causes it to be extremely reliant on a Focus Sash to help it set up, and this reliance on Focus Sash also causes Cloyster to be very vulnerable to priority, which can revenge kill it easily. A mediocre Speed stat causes Cloyster to be outsped by most offensive threats, some such as Choice Scarf Latios and Swift Swim Kingdra even after a Shell Smash. Finally, it can be hard to justify Cloyster a teamslot when it is outclassed in most situations by other late-game cleaners and setup sweepers such as Mega Sharpedo, Gyarados, and Azumarill.

Ice

Cloyster is one of the most threatening Ice-type sweepers due to its Water typing and access to Shell Smash, which allows it to sweep types such as Fire and Rock if given the chance to set up. A neutrality to both Fire- and Steel-type moves allows Cloyster to heavily influence these matchups with Rock Blast and Hydro Vortex, being able to set up on Pokemon such as Infernape locked into Flare Blitz and Excadrill with ease. Furthermore, Cloyster's good offensive ability in Skill Link allows it to make good use of moves like Icicle Spear and Rock Blast, enabling it to break through Focus Sash from Pokemon such as Breloom, Alakazam, and Araquanid. A gargantuan Defense stat means it can set up in front of many physical attackers such as Excadrill and Mega Swampert easily. However, an abysmal Special Defense leaves Cloyster vulnerable to any decently strong special hit and diminishes its ability to set up as easily. Even resisted special hits, such as Scald from Keldeo, will dent Cloyster. Low offensive stats mean it is further dependent on a Shell Smash boost to pose as an offensive threat, since it doesn't hit very hard unboosted. Cloyster's mediocre Speed stat makes it somewhat easy to revenge kill, since it cannot outspeed key threats such as Choice Scarf Latios, and due to its vulnerability to entry hazards and Shell Smash's defense-lowering effect, it's easy to chip it down, possibly leaving it vulnerable to opposing priority moves such as Dragonite's Extreme Speed and Breloom's Mach Punch.
monotype.comments:
Other Options

Water

White Herb mitigates the defense drops from Shell Smash, but the safety offered by Focus Sash is more helpful.

Ice

A Naughty nature can be used, but the loss in Speed isn't worth it, as Cloyster would be outsped by several Choice Scarf users such as Infernape, Blacephalon, and Terrakion. However, it does let Cloyster secure a 2HKO on Mega Swampert after very slight chip damage, as well as giving it more power before setting up Shell Smash, which it slightly lacks with a Naive nature. White Herb can be used to make Cloyster less vulnerable to priority and revenge killing; however, it sorely misses the one time nuke Waterium Z provides.

Checks and Counters

Water

Bulky Water-types: Pokemon such as Mega Slowbro, Tapu Fini, and Toxapex resist both of Cloyster's STAB moves, allowing them to easily take any hit. They are then able to status it, hit it hard, or remove its boosts, depending on the Pokemon.

Special Attackers: Due to Cloyster's pitiful Special Defense stat, fast special attackers like Alakazam and Porygon-Z are able to easily OHKO it if it has not yet set up. Cloyster cannot even switch into resisted special attacks, as they will still do large damage to it.

Priority: Cloyster's reliance on Focus Sash to set up means that it will usually be at 1 HP while sweeping, so fast priority such as from Weavile and Dragonite can easily revenge kill it. However, if Cloyster is using Ice Shard, it may be able to get one hit off against slower priority users before getting KOed.

Electric-types: Most Electric-types are very fast and have high offensive stats, allowing them to OHKO Cloyster before it has set up or even outspeeding it after it has set up. In particular, Alolan Raichu can outspeed Cloyster in Electric Terrain even after a Shell Smash and OHKO it with Thunderbolt. Magnezone can survive any hit from Cloyster and OHKO it in return, and Rotom-W can take any of Cloyster's attacks before pivoting out with Volt Switch.

Steel-types: Steel-types resist all of Cloyster's physical attacks, forcing it to rely on the weaker Hydro Pump to hit them. Bulky Steel-types such as Mega Scizor and Ferrothorn are able to easily take any of Cloyster's attacks even at +2 and can KO or outlast it.

Fighting-types: Even though most Fighting-types are physical, they are still able to deal massive damage to Cloyster, especially after a Shell Smash. While most of them are unable to tank hits from +2 Cloyster, Keldeo fears nothing from Cloyster and priority from Infernape or Breloom can pick Cloyster off.

Ice

Water-types: Water-types resist both of Cloyster's STAB moves and are mostly unaffected by Rock Blast, which can give free turns to several key threats to Ice teams such as Keldeo, which can launch a powerful attack, and Toxapex, which can freely set up Toxic Spikes.

Special Attackers: Due to its pathetic Special Defense stat, Cloyster will easily crumble to even relatively weak or resisted special attacks. While this is mitigated if Aurora Veil has been set up beforehand, it is still quite disappointing—for example, it won't even be able to take any attack from Choice Scarf Latios if it has taken Stealth Rock damage.

Faster Choice Scarf users: Any Choice Scarf user with base 110 Speed or higher will be able to outspeed Cloyster even after it has set up a Shell Smash, meaning Pokemon like Gengar, Greninja, and Latios can easily revenge kill it, especially after prior chip damage.

Entry Hazards: Cloyster absolutely hates having to take unnecessary damage, since it heavily relies on its natural bulk, further supported by Aurora Veil, to set up and endure priority attacks. This means the extra damage taken from entry hazards, Stealth Rock in particular, can mean the difference between sweeping a team and being taken out either while setting up or versus a faster foe.

Phazers and Haze Users: Pokemon such as Avalugg, Swampert, and Toxapex can stop a Cloyster sweep cold due to their ability to erase its stat boosts through Roar or Haze.

Physically Defensive Pokemon: Very physically bulky Pokemon such as Ferrothorn, Porygon2, and Quagsire are able to take Cloyster's attacks and retaliate, beating it one-on-one.

Status: Status moves are heavily detrimental to Cloyster, since it relies on all of its speed, power, and longevity, which paralysis, burns, and bad poison severely reduce.

Shell Smash Sweeper (Water).description:
Moves

Shell Smash is what allows Cloyster to sweep, raising all of its offensive stats by two stages while lowering its defensive stats. Icicle Spear is Cloyster's main STAB move, which has an effective 125 Base Power thanks to Skill Link. It can also break Focus Sashes on Pokemon that could stop Cloyster's sweep. Rock Blast is a good coverage move that is affected by Skill Link and helps against Bug, Ice, and Fire teams. Ice Shard is a priority move that can be used to revenge kill threats before setting up and also hits Choice Scarf Latios, which would otherwise outspeed and KO Cloyster even after a Shell Smash. It can also be used to outprioritize threats such as Diggersby that attempt to revenge kill Cloyster with their own priority attacks. Hydro Pump is a secondary STAB move that hits physically defensive Pokemon such as Forretress and Skarmory, especially those that resist Icicle Spear.

Set Details

Maximum Attack and Speed investment makes the most of Cloyster's sweeping potential, allowing it to outspeed most threats after a Shell Smash and making Icicle Spear and Rock Blast hit as hard as possible. A Jolly nature gives Cloyster even more Speed and should be used with Ice Shard; on the other hand, a Naive nature boosts Cloyster's Speed without decreasing the power of Hydro Pump. Skill Link makes Icicle Spear and Rock Blast always hit five times and gives them an effective 125 Base Power, allowing Cloyster to break through many threats. Focus Sash almost guarantees a safe setup opportunity for Cloyster by allowing it to survive at least one attack.

Usage Tips

Preserve Cloyster until near the end of the match, as it can be a great late-game cleaner once its checks have been weakened or removed. Since it is best to keep Cloyster at full HP to let it effectively set up Shell Smash, it is helpful to bring Cloyster in freely on a slow U-turn or Volt Switch from the likes of Pelipper or Lanturn or after an ally has been KOed. Similarly, entry hazards must be off the field before sending Cloyster in, especially as it is weak to Stealth Rock and the entry hazards will break its Focus Sash; it is very difficult to set up with Cloyster if its Focus Sash does not work. On the other hand, Cloyster can also sometimes utilize its massive Defense stat to switch into some physical attackers like Gyarados and Mimikyu and set up against them. Since Cloyster generally only has one chance to sweep, attempt to get rid of its checks and counters—in particular, bulky Water-types—before setting up. Similarly, priority users such as Dragonite and Weavile should also be removed before setting up, as they can revenge kill Cloyster when it's down to 1 HP. If Cloyster is running Ice Shard, it can also come in against weakened threats and revenge kill them.

Team Options

Tapu Fini and Mantine can use Defog to clear the entry hazards that can wear down Cloyster while also offering defensive utility; Mantine's Grass neutrality and amazing special bulk allow it to switch into many attacks that threaten Cloyster, while Tapu Fini's Misty Surge ability allows it to easily absorb status. Pelipper can set rain, which makes Hydro Pump hit much harder, while also sporting a Grass neutrality along with access to U-turn, which allows Cloyster to be brought in easily. In a similar vein, Rotom-W offers a slow Volt Switch that gives Cloyster free opportunities to switch in. It also has an Electric neutrality and can burn foes with Will-O-Wisp, slowly chipping at them. Lanturn also sports an Electric immunity thanks to Volt Absorb, can heal Cloyster of any status ailments with Heal Bell, and has access to Volt Switch to allow it to pivot into Cloyster easily. Entry hazard setters such as Swampert and Empoleon can set up Stealth Rock, which aids Cloyster's sweeping potential. Strong wallbreakers such as Greninja and Keldeo are able to weaken many foes and physical walls, allowing Cloyster to clean late-game. Z-Move users such as Azumarill, Manaphy, and Gyarados are great sweepers that can wear down shared checks with Cloyster.

Shell Smash Sweeper (Ice).description:
Moves

Shell Smash is an amazing setup move that enables Cloyster to sweep unprepared teams. Icicle Spear is Cloyster's main STAB attack, and coupled with Skill Link, it essentially reaches 125 Base Power. Hydro Pump, coupled with Waterium Z, enables Cloyster to bypass many of its would-be checks and counters such as Skarmory and Mega Scizor once it has set up. Regular Hydro Pump hits Steel-types for neutral damage, which otherwise would be able to wall Cloyster completely. Rock Blast is extremely useful to hit Fire-types that Hydro Pump can't hit super effectively such as Mega Charizard X and Torkoal, and it also comes in handy in the Bug and mirror Ice matchup, all of which are much harder without Cloyster. It can also hit Water-types that resist its STAB moves, but it doesn't hit particularly hard because of a lack of type advantage.

Set Details

Waterium Z enables Cloyster to use Hydro Vortex, which, with 144 Special Attack EVs, secures an OHKO on Mega Scizor at +2 after Stealth Rock. These EVs also ensure Cloyster OHKOes Skarmory with Hydro Pump when at +2. 252 Speed EVs and a Naive nature are necessary to avoid being outsped by common Choice Scarf users such as Terrakion and Infernape. The remaining EVs are poured into Attack to power up Icicle Spear and Rock Blast. Skill Link is the ability of choice due to it allowing Icicle Spear and Rock Blast to always hit five times, making them very reliable attacks.

Usage Tips

Due to its monstrous physical defense, Cloyster is able to easily set up on most non-super effective physical hits such as Infernape locked into Flare Blitz. Setting Aurora Veil with Alolan Ninetales helps Cloyster tremendously while setting up, allowing it to set up on even strong super effective moves like Horn Leech from Choice Scarf Tapu Bulu and on some weak special attackers it otherwise wouldn't be able to, such as Clefable. Make sure to clear Stealth Rock and other entry hazards when attempting a sweep with Cloyster; the chip damage taken from them can be extremely detrimental when trying to set up. This is especially important versus Pokemon that can hit Cloyster super effectively such as offensive Scizor and versus specially offensive Pokemon like Choice Scarf Keldeo, which OHKO it if any hazard is up. Weakening Water-types with Pokemon like Kyurem-B and Alolan Ninetales is necessary due to them resisting both of Cloyster's STAB attacks and taking little damage from Rock Blast, which allows Pokemon such as Slowbro and Toxapex to completely wall it. Ideally, you should save Cloyster for late-game once its checks and counters have been removed from the game, though it could be used to occasionally switch into a physical attack for its teammates, especially versus types like Flying, which don't tend to carry priority or fast Choice Scarf users. However, be extremely careful of switching Cloyster into attacks, since it may compromise its ability to set up later. Cloyster should not attempt to set up on Pokemon that can status it with moves like Scald, Will-O-Wisp, and Thunder Wave, such as Toxapex, Mega Sableye, and Klefki.

Team Options

Alolan Ninetales is an excellent partner for Cloyster, since it can set up Aurora Veil for it, which can help immensely while setting up, and check Fighting-type Pokemon, which can check Cloyster themselves. It can also use Encore on passive foes such as Celesteela to create setup opportunities and deal with bulky Water-types for Cloyster with Freeze-Dry. Kyurem-B is a terrifying wallbreaker for Ice teams that can pave the way for a Cloyster sweep due to its ability to heavily damage Pokemon like Toxapex and Mega Venusaur for it. Mamoswine and Piloswine can both set up Stealth Rock for Cloyster and its other teammates, which is a consistent way of dealing chip damage to Pokemon like Mega Venusaur. In addition, running Piloswine means Mamoswine is free to run a wallbreaking set, which can help break down Pokemon such as Porygon2 for Cloyster. Its access to Ice Shard can heavily damage Latios, which is a Choice Scarf user that can outpace Cloyster even at +2. Avalugg can use Rapid Spin to further support Cloyster when setting up, allowing it to stay at full health and helping it take decently strong super effective hits from the likes of Armaldo. Alolan Sandslash can run utility options; either Rapid Spin or Swords Dance are useful for Cloyster, since the former allows it to provide hazard removal support to its teammates and the latter lets it break through troublesome walls such as Toxapex with a boosted Earthquake. Rotom-F can provide useful Defog support and beat several Water- and Steel-types such as Toxapex and Scizor with its STAB Thunderbolt and Hidden Power Fire. Weavile is able to Pursuit trap troublesome Pokemon for Ice teams such as Victini and Latios with ease. Its access to priority in Ice Shard also allows it to pick off weakened foes such as Gengar, which Cloyster appreciates.

ubers.overview:
• Cloyster is one of the primary suicide leads in the tier thanks to its access to both Spikes and Toxic Spikes and Rapid Spin, making it suitable for certain offensive builds.
  • It also has a decent matchup against other dedicated leads such as Deoxys-S and Excadrill due to Skill Link-boosted Icicle Spear being a 125-Base Power move breaking their Focus Sash.
  • Cloyster tends to struggle against certain entry hazard control Pokemon such as Arceus-Water, which does not care about its Ice-type STAB Icicle Spear and can proceed to Defog away the hazards, and Mega Sableye, which can bounce back hazards, burn Cloyster with Will-O-Wisp and block its Rapid Spin. Also, Taunt users such as Mega Gengar and Yveltal prevent Cloyster from getting up hazards, although both of them have to be wary of Icicle Spear.
  • Cloyster has low special bulk, making it really weak to special attacks and attackers and thus a one-time use Pokemon.
ubers.comments:
Other Options

  • Explosion can be used over Rapid Spin for maintaining momentum and preventing Defog. It also prevents Cloyster from being setup bait for Necrozma-DM.
  • Ice Shard can also be used as an emergency check to Mega Salamence and Rayquaza, but Cloyster does not have a moveslot for it.
  • Spikes and Toxic Spikes can be run on the same set by forgoing Rapid Spin, but this is not advised, as Cloyster is usually the only form of hazard control for its team.
  • Lum Berry can be used over Focus Sash to help Cloyster deal with Mega Sableye and Smeargle.

Checks and Counters

Arceus-Water: Arceus-Water is a hard stop to Cloyster, as it does not mind taking even boosted Icicle Spears, always beats Cloyster with Toxic or the rare Will-O-Wisp, and can use Defog to get rid of Cloyster's entry hazards.

Support Arceus Formes: All support Arceus formes except Arceus-Ground and Arceus-Dragon act as Cloyster checks. They threaten Cloyster with Judgment and Toxic, can Defog away its hazards, and can take a +2 Icicle Spear if needed. Arceus-Dark can also burn Cloyster with Will-O-Wisp, rendering it useless.

Anti-Leads: Smeargle's higher Speed allows it to use Spore before Cloyster can move and proceed to set up its own hazards. Shuckle's natural bulk means that it can take two Icicle Spears, can Encore Cloyster into a move, and get its own hazards up. Mega Sableye does not care about Cloyster, as it can bounce back the hazards, take a boosted Icicle Spear, and burn Cloyster with Will-O-Wisp. It can also use Foul Play if Cloyster decides to set up on it. Both Choice Band Tyranitar and Dragon Dance Mega Tyranitar can OHKO Cloyster with the combination of Stone Edge and Sand Stream. Even though Mega Kangaskhan is very rare, it deserves a mention, as it can stop Cloyster from doing anything with the combination of Fake Out and Seismic Toss.

Special Attackers: Cloyster has terrible special bulk and gets 2HKOed by basically any neutral special move.

Bulky Water-types: Pokemon such as defensive Primal Kyogre and Toxapex take minimal damage even from a boosted Icicle Spear and can beat Cloyster.

Steel-types: Steel types such as Necrozma-DM, Mega Lucario, and Magearna resist Icicle Spear and can proceed to set up on Cloyster or beat it.

Entry Hazard Lead.description:
Moves

  • Spikes and Toxic Spikes help wear down the opponent's team, helping teammates to sweep. Toxic Spikes is less consistent, as it does not affect Steel-types such as Magearna, Ferrothorn, and Necrozma-DM. It also gets absorbed by Poison-types such as Mega Gengar and Toxapex but tends to be better against other offensive teams.
  • Shell Smash allows Cloyster to not be passive, boosting its Attack and Speed to let it outspeed the entire unboosted metagame with a Jolly nature and do heavy damage to Pokemon that do not resist STAB Icicle Spear.
  • STAB Icicle Spear paired with Skill Link always results in five hits, thus breaking Focus Sash and helping to weaken the opponent's team as much as possible.
  • Rapid Spin gives entry hazard control to the team, allowing teammates to be brought in safely.

Set Details

  • Maximum investment in Speed and Attack is used for maximum offensive presence. With a Jolly nature, +2 Cloyster outspeeds the entire unboosted metagame and notable Pokemon like +1 Adamant Mega Salamence, Deoxys-S, +2 standard Geomancy Xerneas, Choice Scarf Xerneas, and +2 standard Rock Polish Primal Groudon.
  • An Adamant nature can also be used, as Cloyster will have a high chance to OHKO standard Giratina and Necrozma-DW with +2 Icicle Spear, preventing the latter from blocking Rapid Spin.

Usage Tips

  • Since Cloyster is a dedicated lead, getting up entry hazards should be the main priority.
  • Try to preserve Focus Sash, as it can come in clutch later.
  • Use Shell Smash and Icicle Spear to pressure opposing hazard setters to prevent them from getting hazards up, to do as much damage as possible before going down, and to punish a predicted use of Defog or switch to a bulkier Pokemon.
  • Although weakening the opponent's team is great, spinning away hazards is more important.
  • Lead against Pokemon such as Deoxys-S and Excadrill, since Cloyster can beat them with Icicle Spear and spin their hazards away.
  • Avoid leading with Cloyster versus bad matchups such as against Mega Sableye, Smeargle, and support Arceus formes, especially Arceus-Water and Arceus-Dark, as some sets use Will-O-Wisp.
  • Getting only one layer of Toxic Spikes is more helpful versus offensive teams, since the games are quite fast paced and the constant 12% damage is preferred rather than the increasing damage over time with two layers, but against balance builds, two layers are better, as being badly poisoned is more threatening to defensive Pokemon.

Team Options

  • Cloyster is a dedicated entry hazard lead; hence, it only fits on hyper offensive builds.
  • Taunt users such as Mega Gengar, Mega Mewtwo Y, and Yveltal make excellent teammates for Cloyster, as they prevent the hazards from getting removed. They also help against Smeargle, although they can be crippled by Nuzzle.
  • Spinblockers such as Marshadow, Mega Gengar, Lunala, and Arceus-Ghost make great teammates for a similar reason. Lunala especially appreciates Cloyster's Rapid Spin support because of its Shadow Shield. Mega Gengar appreciates Toxic Spikes, since it can then run Hex more effectively.
  • Stealth Rock users such as Arceus-Fairy and Primal Groudon are helpful to Cloyster. Primal Groudon is especially useful, as it can pressure Pokemon Cloyster has trouble with such as support Arceus formes and Necrozma-DM.
  • Fairy-types such as Xerneas and Arceus-Fairy make decent teammates, as they can anti-lead against Mega Sableye and pressure Defoggers like Mega Salamence and Giratina. Arceus-Fairy is a great partner because it can also get Stealth Rock up. Xerneas appreciates the Spikes support, as it helps wear Pokemon like Necrozma-DM and Primal Groudon down.
  • Pokemon weak to hazards such as Mega Salamence, Yveltal, and Rayquaza appreciate Cloyster removing hazards for them.
  • Since Cloyster is decent at getting hazards up, strong wallbreakers and late-game cleaners such as Rock Polish Primal Groudon, Dragon Dance Mega Salamence, Double Dance Necrozma-DM, Dragon Dance Zygarde, Geomancy Xerneas, Marshadow, and Calm Mind Arceus-Flying are used alongside it, as they all appreciate their checks getting worn down.

ru.overview: Cloyster's unique access to Spikes, Shell Smash, Skill Link, and Icicle Spear allows it to act as a potentially fearsome wallbreaker or sweeper that can bypass Substitute and Sturdy as well as pressuring rival entry hazard setters such as Nidoqueen and Rhyperior while being able to set up hazards itself. Thanks to its enormous Defense and use of Focus Sash, Cloyster is almost guaranteed to set up either Shell Smash or one layer of Spikes. While those attributes sound incredibly appealing in RU's more offensive metagame, keep in mind that Cloyster lacks coverage to hit common Steel-types such as Registeel, Metagross, and Bronzong super effectively. Cloyster's Defense is amazing, but its Special Defense combined with its relatively low unboosted Speed usually leaves it threatened out by Pokemon like Roserade, Raikou, Gardevoir, and Mega Sceptile prior to boosting. Its bad defensive typing also leaves it vulnerable to all entry hazards, especially Stealth Rock, and Fighting-types like Machamp, Toxicroak, and Bewear. It also has to be cautious of Taunt from Pokemon such as Mandibuzz, Houndoom, and Vanilluxe, which stops it from setting up Spikes or boosting with Shell Smash, making it much less dangerous. Cloyster is also shut down by status conditions, cutting its sweep short. Even if Cloyster does set up, it is easily shut down by priority moves such as Bullet Punch from Machamp and Accelerock from Lycanroc-D. Cloyster faces a lot of competition for a spot on a team. As a physically offensive Water-type, it has to compete against Barbaracle and Golisopod because both of them have a stronger offensive presence before boosting and are better at pressuring Steel-types. As a Spikes setter, Roserade and Golisopod are arguably more appealing because Roserade is faster, applies immediate offensive pressure without having to set up, and has all the tools it needs to pressure entry hazard removers, while Cloyster usually has to resort to Explosion, and Golisopod does not have Cloyster's Fighting weakness, can pressure Steel-types with Liquidation, has priority in Aqua Jet and First Impression, and can pivot with Emergency Exit.
ru.comments:
Other Options

An all-out offensive set with Shell Smash / Icicle Spear / Hydro Pump / Explosion and Normalium Z makes Cloyster even more threatening late-game, especially when its checks and counters are softened or KOed. However, this set has some competition with Barbaracle; while Cloyster is better at luring Water-types, has a Ground neutrality, and can set up against physically offensive Pokemon, Barbaracle is the overall better option because of its more immediate offensive pressure and ability to deal super effective damage to Steel-types. Cloyster can also set up Toxic Spikes, since it can pressure Defoggers like Mandibuzz and Florges and beat Pokemon that can absorb them such as Nidoqueen and Drapion, but it is useless against Steel-types such as Metagross and Bronzong. Ice Shard is a good option to pressure Roserade, Timid Nidoqueen, and Virizion, but Cloyster can set up to beat these Pokemon anyway. Skill Link Rock Blast is an interesting option that can deal with Pokemon that resist Icicle Spear such as Arcanine, Ninetales, and Snorlax, but Explosion already does a considerable amount of damage to these Pokemon. Cloyster can also utilize Choice Scarf to provide role compression of a Spikes setter with speed control, as well as netting a surprise KO with Explosion against Pokemon like Raikou and Ninetales. However, it fails to outspeed other Choice Scarf Pokemon like Shaymin, and it is noticeably weaker without a boost from Shell Smash.

Checks and Counters

Steel-types: Cloyster has issues breaking Steel-types such as Metagross, Registeel, and Bronzong because it only runs Icicle Spear and Explosion.

Grass-types: Pokemon like Mega Sceptile, Roserade, Shaymin, and Virizion can apply immediate pressure against Cloyster and force it out of the battle. However, none of them want to come in when it sets up Shell Smash or uses Icicle Spear or even the rare Ice Shard.

Fighting-types: Cloyster's Ice typing leaves it vulnerable to Pokemon such as Machamp, Toxicroak, and Bewear before it can boost with Shell Smash. After it has boosted, these Pokemon need to be wary about switching directly into it.

Bulky Water-type Pokemon: Pokemon such as Milotic, Slowbro, and Mega Blastoise can easily take on Cloyster's Icicle Spear. However, none of them want to come in on Explosion, as it can severely dent or even OHKO them after a Shell Smash boost.

Special Attackers: Pokemon such as Raikou, Gardevoir, and Necrozma target Cloyster's weaker Special Defense stat to potentially knock it out, especially if Cloyster goes for Spikes instead of Shell Smash against them.

Priority Moves: After Cloyster has activated Focus Sash, it becomes vulnerable to priority moves such as Zygarde-10%'s Extreme Speed, Machamp's Bullet Punch, and Lycanroc-D's Accelerock.

Status Conditions: Toxic can stop Cloyster from setting up entry hazards or wallbreaking and breaks its Focus Sash, severely limiting what it can do. Cloyster getting burned or paralyzed makes it lose a lot of offensive presence.

Taunt: Because Cloyster is not very fast, it is very vulnerable to being shut down by Taunt users such as Vanilluxe, Houndoom, and Noivern. These Pokemon also easily beat Cloyster with their powerful special moves, especially if its Focus Sash has been broken prior. However, none of these Pokemon want to directly switch into any of Cloyster's moves, especially if it has boosted with Shell Smash.

Shell Smash.description:
Moves

Shell Smash can turn Cloyster into a potentially threatening offensive force, as it boosts Attack and Speed by two stages. Skill Link-boosted Icicle Spear is effectively a 125-Base Power STAB move that can break Raikou's Substitute and Donphan's Sturdy. Spikes helps Cloyster's teammates sweep thanks to the residual damage it provides. Explosion gives Cloyster a way of dealing with bulky Water-types that wall Icicle Spear such as Mega Blastoise, Milotic, and Golisopod. It also can be used to stop spinners such as Mega Blastoise, Forretress, and Adamant Tsareena from removing the Spikes it sets up. Rapid Spin can be used instead to remove entry hazards from Cloyster's side of the battlefield but makes it much more vulnerable to bulky Water-types.

Set Details

Maximum Attack and Speed investment is used so Cloyster can be as strong and fast as possible, especially after it boosts with Shell Smash. A Jolly nature allows Cloyster to outpace Guts Machamp and Bewear before it sets up Shell Smash. After it has used Shell Smash, Cloyster can outspeed common Choice Scarf Pokemon such as Shaymin. An Adamant nature can be used instead for extra power after boosting with Shell Smash, but this usually isn't recommended because Cloyster is in a crowded Speed tier when unboosted. Adamant Cloyster also fails to outpace Choice Scarf Shaymin and Flygon. Skill Link guarantees Icicle Spear will hit five times, turning it into an effective tool to break Focus Sash, Sturdy, and Substitute. A Focus Sash allows Cloyster to survive one powerful hit so it can set up Spikes or Shell Smash.

Usage Tips

Cloyster can safely set up Shell Smash thanks to its enormous Defense and Focus Sash so it can pressure entry hazard setters and Taunt users like Mandibuzz. It can wallbreak or set up Spikes early on as a lead, but it can also be preserved for later to clean up. Cloyster should be played aggressively and switch directly into opposing hazard setters such as Necrozma, Rhyperior, and Nidoqueen to preserve its Focus Sash as they set up their hazards and use its Focus Sash to either set up Spikes itself or use Shell Smash so it can deal as much damage as possible. If Cloyster has used its Focus Sash and the opponent brings in a Pokemon that resists Icicle Spear such as Milotic, Snorlax, or Mega Blastoise, then it can use Explosion to dent that Pokemon or even KO it. Explosion should also be used against a spinner like Mega Blastoise or Tsareena to stop them from removing the Spikes Cloyster sets up.

Team Options

Cloyster's ability to pressure entry hazard setters is appreciated by Pokemon that are vulnerable to Stealth Rock such as Arcanine, Noivern, and Salazzle. These Pokemon also help Cloyster beat Steel-type Pokemon that it cannot break. Necrozma, Gardevoir, and Slowbro can also be good partners, as they have better matchups against the common Machamp and other Fighting-type leads so Cloyster can set up Spikes later. Pokemon like Mandibuzz and Espeon can help deter entry hazards with Taunt and Magic Bounce to make it easier for Cloyster to sweep late-game. Mandibuzz can also use Taunt to stop Defoggers like Mantine and Florges from removing hazards. Mismagius and Alolan Marowak can spinblock for Cloyster, as it's important to keep Cloyster's Spikes up. These two also pressure common Steel-types such as Registeel, Metagross, and Bronzong. Stealth Rock setters like Necrozma, Rhyperior, and Nidoqueen can stack hazards with Cloyster. If Cloyster is running Rapid Spin, then partners like Ninetales, Salazzle, and Yanmega appreciate Cloyster's ability to remove hazards itself. If Cloyster is used early-game to set up Spikes, late-game setup sweepers and wallbreakers such as Zygarde-10%, Arcanine, Raikou, and Metagross will appreciate the Spikes support to help them net important KOs.

battlespotsingles.overview:
Cloyster makes its return from XY as one of the most infamous setup sweepers of Battle Spot Singles. High Base Power of multi-hit moves coupled with Skill Link makes Cloyster one of the most threatening sweepers in the metagame. While extremely predictable, Cloyster has still proven to be difficult to deal with, only stopped by a select few Pokemon. However, an atrocious Special Defense stat also makes tricky for Cloyster to set up either if it holding an intact Focus Sash. More often than not, Focus Sash will also be consumed in the setup, making Cloyster vulnerable to priority attacks.

Below are some sample sets. These sets are likely to be standard, but they will be expanded upon and updated as the metagame progresses.

Smash 'n' Sweep.description:
• Shell Smash boosts Cloyster's stats to a dangerous levels which can allow it to sweep unprepared teams.
  • Icicle Spear is the main STAB option, always hitting 5 times with Skill Link, allowing Cloyster to break through common Focus Sash Pokemon such as Garchomp and Tapu Koko, Pokemon carrying Substitute, and Mimikyu.
  • Rock Blast provides coverage against Fire- and Ice-types such as opposing Cloyster, Mega-Charizard X, Rotom-H, Blaziken, and Volcarona.
  • Ice Shard allows Cloyster to beat opposing priority users when at +2, including Mach Punch Breloom and Prankster Thundurus, while also providing general coverage when not boosted against Mega Salamence and Garchomp. However, Tapu Lele's Psychic Surge can be troublesome for Cloyster given the prevention of priority moves against grounded targets.
  • Waterium Z and Razor Shell in place of Ice Shard is an option to allow Cloyster to use Hydro Vortex, which can OHKO Heatran and Assault Vest Mamoswine without a boost, while also allowing +2 Cloyster to OHKO Aegislash and Mega Metagross after Stealth Rock damage.
  • Focus Sash guarantees Cloyster can use Shell Smash, which is essential in matchups against dedicated special attackers, as Cloyster's Special Defense is quite poor. Kings Rock works in conjunction with Icicle Spear and Rock Blast, granting a 41% chance to make the opponent flinch.
  • 252 Attack EVs ensure that Cloyster can hit to its full potential, while 252 Speed EVs are needed for Cloyster to outspeed Choice Scarf Tapu Lele. An Adamant nature is preferred, as +2 Speed from Shell Smash gives Cloyster enough Speed; however, a Jolly nature can still be used to ensure that +2 Cloyster is faster than Choice Scarf Garchomp and +1 Mega Charizard Y, which would otherwise OHKO it.
  • Even at +2, Cloyster struggles to break bulky Water-types and Porygon2, so be sure to carry Electric-type coverage somewhere and a means of dealing with Porygon2. Steel-types also prove to be problematic, so be sure to carry some coverage for these threats.

Choice Scarf.description: For full USUM 1v1 analyses, you can check out the USUM format page.

letsgoou.overview: Cloyster's viability is solely carried by Shell Smash, which lets it outspeed the entire unboosted metagame and double its offensive stats in a single turn. To complement this, it has strong STAB options that cover each other well and a Defense stat that lets it set up in front of many physical attackers, notably tanking any hit from Melmetal after Stealth Rock, as well as from Dragonite and Mega Aerodactyl. It also has Self-Destruct, which lets it sacrifice itself to OHKO or heavily damage Pokemon that could otherwise take it on like Alolan Muk and Mega Gyarados. Unfortunately, Cloyster's poor offensive movepool utilizes its lower Special Attack stat and leaves it unable to meaningfully damage Water-type Pokemon without using Self-Destruct, which can make handling it quite easy. Its abysmal special bulk limits its setup opportunities, and it faces competition from Omastar, which is vulnerable to revenge killing from the metagame's fastest Pokemon due to its poor Speed but is much more powerful and can even support its team with Stealth Rock.
letsgoou.comments:
Other Options

Cloyster's limited movepool does not offer it many options. Running Hydro Pump and Surf on the same set can offer both power and reliability, but dropping Self-Destruct is not recommended. Ice Shard is also an option, capable of picking off weakened Pokemon that outspeed Cloyster like Mega Beedrill, boosted Dragonite, and Mega Aerodactyl, but its low Base Power makes it a poor option for sweeping compared to Cloyster's standard attacking moves.

Checks and Counters

Water-types: Starmie, Poliwrath, Mega Gyarados, and the rare Mega Blastoise can deal with Cloyster well. Ice Beam and Hydro Pump will do very little to them, but boosted Self-Destruct will OHKO Starmie and do massive damage to the others, which cannot recover that lost health.

Specially Bulky Pokemon: Alolan Muk, Mew, Melmetal, Chansey and Snorlax can stomach a Hydro Pump, though Mew and Melmetal must be healthy and don't appreciate losing that much health. Alolan Muk, Chansey, and Snorlax are bulky enough to take more than one boosted Hydro Pump but must be careful of Self-Destruct.

Priority: When priority move users like Alolan Dugtrio's Sucker Punch are present, Cloyster should avoid being put into their KO range, as they will end Cloyster's sweep swiftly without it getting the chance to do damage. Also beware of the rare Pikachu-S, as it can take Cloyster out with some prior damage using its STAB priority.

Shell Smash.description:
Set Information

Shell Smash lets Cloyster outspeed fast Pokemon such as Mega Aerodactyl and Mega Alakazam and boost its damage output to KO Pokemon like Nidoqueen and Zapdos. Hydro Pump somewhat mitigates Cloyster's low Special Attack, while Surf is a somewhat weaker option that lets Cloyster accurately finish off Pokemon that resist Ice Beam where Hydro Pump is not necessary; it also deals reliable damage to Pokemon when needed and allows Cloyster to be a more consistent wincon. Ice Beam offers a 100% accurate STAB attack that prevents Grass-types and Dragonite from walling Cloyster. Self-Destruct takes advantage of the Attack boost from Shell Smash to blow past special walls like Alolan Muk, Snorlax, and Chansey as well as Water-types like Mega Gyarados, Starmie, and Poliwrath.

Usage Tips

Do not use Cloyster early on, as your opponent will be able to use their best or most convenient check and finish Cloyster off with minimal harm to their team. Cloyster performs much better later on, when its answers are limited and it can potentially use Self-Destruct on your opponent's counterplay and open the door for another Pokemon to win. When using Self-Destruct, be mindful of how much your opponent would be rewarded for predicting Self-Destruct and saving their check, as it might be worthwhile to predict this and simply use another attack. A key to using Cloyster is deciding whether it will be more effective to have Cloyster weaken walls such as Alolan Muk and Melmetal to support its fast, offensive teammates or to wallbreak with said teammates to enable a sweep with Cloyster. This is largely dependent on your matchup— if your opponent has multiple healthy checks to Cloyster, attempting to sweep with it is unadvised.

Team Options

Cloyster is a spectacular partner for Mega Alakazam, as all of Alakazam's defensive checks are commonly used to check a boosted Cloyster. Cloyster can put these Pokemon into KO range of Mega Alakazam's coverage with Hydro Pump, or outright remove them with Self-Destruct in the case of Snorlax and Alolan Muk. Cloyster can also capitalize on any wallbreaking that Mega Alakazam does to sweep later on. Starmie works well with Cloyster in a similar way, but it comes with more similar coverage and utility without taking a Mega slot. Pokemon that deal with the Water-types that stump Cloyster can be useful, and Zapdos matches up well against Mega Gyarados and Poliwrath. Nasty Plot Mew is also a great special attacker that can take advantage of Cloyster's ability to force damage on many of its best answers while also setting up freely on Poliwrath. Any Pokemon that appreciate the chunks of health Cloyster often rips out of Melmetal are options, most notably Mega Beedrill, Mega Aerodactyl, and Mega Gyarados. Mega Gyarados also pressures Water-types like Poliwrath.

lc.overview: Gastly is a fantastic Pokemon in the LC metagame thanks to its very good Speed stat, which allows it to offensively check tier titans such as fast Mienfoo and Snivy, and its top-tier Special Attack stat, which allows it to put enormous pressure on teams and reliably break down opposing walls. Its movepool leaves it with a plethora of coverage options that make it extremely difficult to switch into, and even includes reliable support moves such as Will-O-Wisp and Destiny Bond. Gastly's Ghost typing also comes with significant advantages, giving it an immunity to Fighting-type priority moves and allowing it to act as a risky spinblocker for hyper offensive teams. However, Gastly's poor defensive stats and weakness to the common Dark-type leave it prone to being taken out by anything it doesn't KO.
lc.comments:
Other Options

Gastly has access to several other coverage options such as Giga Drain which can be run on any set, but generally are only useful against specific Pokemon. Hidden Power Ground is especially notable, as it allows Gastly to lure in some of its typical checks, such as Alolan Grimer, Pawniard, and Stunky, and deal significant damage. Venoshock can be run on teams with a reliable method of poisoning the foe, such as Toxic Spikes, to give Gastly a move with much higher Base Power than Sludge Bomb. Taunt is an option with Berry Juice to prevent Gastly from being set up on by Pokemon it does not KO, but Gastly would usually rather either run a coverage move to hit these Pokemon or switch out. Ghostium Z can be used to boost the power of Shadow Ball, but Gastly sorely misses out on Life Orb's consistent power. Lastly, Knock Off can be used to lure in bulkier Pokemon and remove their items, but Gastly has all the wallbreaking potential it will generally need with just the standard sets.

Checks and Counters

Alolan Grimer and Stunky: Both Alolan Grimer and Stunky resist Gastly's STAB moves, have the bulk to handle any coverage move effectively, and remove Gastly from the battle with Pursuit. Hex variants are more difficult to trap, since Gastly can burn and escape from battle, but Stunky and Grimer will still be able to reliably counter it later in the battle.

Priority Moves: Gastly is very susceptible to priority, including Aqua Jet from Carvanha and Corphish and Sucker Punch from Pawniard and Croagunk.

Revenge Killers: Due to its enormous wallbreaking potential, the best way for offensive teams to handle Gastly is to revenge kill it. Pokemon with 19 Speed, such as Abra and Staryu, can outspeed and KO Gastly, as can Choice Scarf users such as Pawniard, which can trap Gastly with Pursuit. However, these Pokemon need to be wary of a surprise Choice Scarf Gastly, which will outspeed most other Choice Scarf Pokemon.

Specially Bulky Pokemon: Extremely specially bulky Pokemon are required to handle Gastly defensively. Munchlax, Lickitung, Ferroseed, and Lileep all tank any hit from Gastly, but still take significant damage in doing so. None of them like being poisoned, either (with the exception of Ferroseed), so switching into a Sludge Bomb can cripple them.

Bulletproof Users: Chespin and Jangmo-o get an honorable mention as Gastly counters, as they both have the ability Bulletproof, making them completely immune to both Shadow Ball and Sludge Bomb. However, both are generally useless otherwise and can become dead weight on teams. They also do not check the Hex set particularly well.

Life Orb.description:
Moves

Shadow Ball and Sludge Bomb are powerful STAB moves, especially when boosted by Life Orb, and can hit most of what doesn't resist them for solid damage. Gastly can choose to run either Hidden Power Fighting or Dazzling Gleam in the third moveslot to deal with Dark-types. Hidden Power Fighting hits Pawniard, which resists both of Gastly's STAB moves, for more damage, while Dazzling Gleam is more powerful against Vullaby. Psychic lets Gastly OHKO frailer variants of Eviolite Mienfoo more often than not, as well as consistently 2HKO Mareanie and OHKO Croagunk. Substitute allows Gastly to take advantage of the switches it forces, avoid stray status moves, and force Pawniard into mind games with Sucker Punch. Destiny Bond can be used instead to take advantage of Gastly's Speed to take out an opposing Pokemon when it is knocked out and still somewhat force Pawniard into mind games. Sucker Punch can be run as a surprise fourth move to take out opposing Gastly and Abra as well as severely weakened Pokemon that aim to revenge kill it, but Gastly's Attack stat is too low to make use of it otherwise.

Set Details

The EV spread on this set is simple, maximizing Gastly's Special Attack and Speed to allow it to hit as hard as possible and outspeed most of the metagame with a Timid nature, including Pokemon such as Mienfoo, Archen, and Drilbur, while Speed tying with Doduo. The remaining EVs go into Special Defense instead of HP to provide 19 HP, which minimizes both Life Orb recoil damage and the amount of HP it takes to make a Substitute. If Hidden Power Fighting isn't run, an EV spread of 36 Def / 196 SpA / 76 SpD / 196 Spe should be used instead. A Life Orb boosts Gastly's wallbreaking potential, assisted by Gastly's naturally high Special Attack stat.

Usage Tips

This Gastly set is fairly easy to use, working as a strong wallbreaker that uses its power and coverage to break down opposing teams. Gastly should avoid taking hits as much as it can, as it has low defenses. This means that generally Gastly should only be attacking when it can KO a Pokemon, which will be often due to its power. Scouting for opposing Choice Scarf users is important early in a match to ensure that Gastly isn't taken by surprise and revenge killed. Substitute should be used against opposing Sucker Punch users to force them into mind games until Gastly can get up a free Substitute and then attack. Be cautious when playing against Pursuit users, as they can come in and prevent Gastly from switching out.

Team Options

As with all wallbreakers, Gastly appreciates entry hazard support to break down opposing teams, with Omanyte, Pineco, and Dwebble all performing this role appropriately. Gastly can also spinblock for these Pokemon to support teammates that also take advantage of entry hazards. Fighting-types, such as Timburr, Croagunk, and Mienfoo, make fantastic partners due to their ability to use Knock Off to wear down defensive Pokemon, their ability to check bulky Normal- and Dark-types, and their potential to lure in Fairy-types that Gastly easily deals with. Offensive Ground-type Pokemon, including Drilbur, Mudbray, and Diglett, can take advantage of the Pokemon Gastly lures in, including Alolan Grimer, Pawniard, and Stunky. Other fast special attackers, including Elekid and Abra, put pressure on the same Pokemon that Gastly does, making them good partners to wear down these Pokemon to allow for a sweep. Pokemon that can give Gastly a free switch into the battle also make good partners, including slow pivots such as Mienfoo and U-turn Vullaby. Pursuit trappers, including Pawniard, Alolan Grimer, and Munchlax, work well due to their ability to eliminate Abra, which is a threat to this set.

Hex.description:
Moves

Hex becomes an extremely powerful STAB move for Gastly if the opponent has been inflicted with a status ailment. Will-O-Wisp allows Gastly to cripple physical attackers that come in hoping to check it and boosts Hex's power. Substitute allows Gastly to capitalize on the switches it forces, force Sucker Punch Pawniard into mind games, and avoid the occasional status move from the likes of Foongus. Sludge Bomb gives Gastly a Poison-type STAB move and allows it to function as a powerful Fairy-type check. Dazzling Gleam and Hidden Power Fighting are options to hit the various Dark-type Pokemon that Gastly lures in, but Hex will usually hit them harder after a burn than either of these moves. Disable in conjunction with Substitute allows Gastly to take on most of the tier's Fighting-types one-on-one by Disabling their Knock Off and switch out more easily against Pursuit users.

Set Details

Gastly is given a very diverse EV spread. 196 Speed EVs and a Timid nature allow Gastly to reach 18 Speed, making it one of the faster Will-O-Wisp users in the tier and allowing it to safely attack teams without taking hits. 116 Special Attack EVs boost Gastly's Special Attack to a level where it can threaten opposing teams with Hex. The remaining EVs give Gastly enough bulk to take a Pursuit or a Knock Off after it consumes Berry Juice from any Dark-type in the metagame, and provides a chance for Foongus's Giga Drain to not break its substitute. Berry Juice allows Gastly to regenerate its health once in a battle, giving it a certain measure of longevity and the ability to use Substitute more times.

Usage Tips

Gastly should nearly always avoid switching into attacks, as most defensive Pokemon can cripple it with status moves and offensive Pokemon easily take advantage of its poor defenses. Gastly should use Will-O-Wisp to spread burns as much as possible, especially to cripple Dark-type attackers that are switching in, which allows Gastly to switch out without being KOed by Pursuit if necessary. Gastly can then use Hex or its coverage moves to act as a powerful wallbreaker. Gastly usually does not want to take even burn-weakened attacks, so stay on the attack when you know Gastly will deal significant damage. Substitute should be used to ease prediction when Gastly will force a switch, against Pokemon reliant on status moves such as Foongus, and to activate Berry Juice if Gastly needs to be at full health to take a hit. If running Disable, Gastly can use Substitute against Pokemon that rely on Knock Off or Pursuit to deal with it, especially Fighting-type Pokemon that cannot hit Gastly without Knock Off, and then Disable to gain a free turn.

Team Options

Toxic Spikes works extremely well in conjunction with Hex Gastly, allowing it to fire off powerful Hexes without having to rely on Will-O-Wisp. Pokemon such as Mareanie, Skrelp, and Trubbish can set up Toxic Spikes effectively and check the Fighting-types that can hit Gastly with Knock Off. Other forms of entry hazards, which can be set by the likes of Omanyte and Dwebble, also help Gastly wear down opposing teams, and Gastly acts as a spinblocker to keep the hazards its teammates set up. Pokemon that can handle Knock Off users are essential if Gastly is not using Disable, which makes Fighting-types such as Mienfoo and Timburr good partners. These Pokemon can also handle specially bulky Pokemon such as Munchlax that counter Gastly. Mienfoo also makes a good slow pivot, which works well with Gastly because of its ability to bring Gastly in safely and gain momentum. Other slow pivots work well with Gastly, including Chinchou and U-turn Vullaby. Opposing Ghost- and Psychic-type Pokemon can check Gastly offensively, so Pursuit users, including Pawniard, Alolan Grimer, and Stunky, make good partners.

Lure.description:
Moves

Dazzling Gleam is an excellent coverage move for Gastly, hitting Fighting- and Dark-types quite hard. However, the main function of Dazzling Gleam on this set is to give Gastly access to Twinkle Tackle, a powerful Z-Move that OHKOes Mienfoo, certain Timburr sets, and Vullaby after Stealth Rock damage. Thunder can be used instead to give Gastly a good chance to beat Alolan Grimer switchins in addition to taking out Vullaby. Sludge Bomb and Shadow Ball are powerful STAB attacks with good coverage, especially against foes such as Snivy, Spritzee, and Pumpkaboo-XL. Substitute helps Gastly protect itself from a single move, lets it avoid Sucker Punch and status moves such as Foongus's Spore, and lets Gastly avoid having to predict a switch. Hidden Power Fighting can also be used to hit Pawniard, a Pokemon that otherwise walls Gastly.

Set Details

Fairium Z lets Gastly use Twinkle Tackle to surprise some of its checks, such as Vullaby, Mienfoo, and Timburr, and deal heavy damage. A Timid nature and 196 Speed EVs are used to maximize Gastly's Speed and let it outspeed Mienfoo, Snivy, and Cottonee. 196 Special Attack EVs let Gastly do a fair amount of damage. The rest of Gastly's EVs are put into its defenses to let it survive for as long as possible. Levitate gives Gastly an immunity to Ground-types moves, allowing it to switch in slightly easier against certain Pokemon such as Choice Scarf Mudbray and Hippopotas. If using Hidden Power Fighting, Gastly should use an EV spread of 40 Def / 200 SpA / 200 Spe to maximize Special Attack and Speed.

Usage Tips

To properly utilize Twinkle Tackle, it is a good idea to try and bait in threats Gastly can KO with it, namely Timburr, Mienfoo, and Vullaby. Before doing this, however, it is usually best to scout how your opponent will react to Gastly, as Twinkle Tackle can only be used once per battle. This usually consists of checking what usually switches into Gastly and what moves said Pokemon usually uses. It's best not to attack before using Twinkle Tackle, as this would reveal that Gastly lacks a Life Orb, leading your opponent to most likely believe it is either Choice Scarf or Fairium Z. This is especially important if the opponent has something Gastly can lure in. Don't be afraid to attack afterwards, however, as Gastly can still do a lot without the element of surprise. Due to Gastly's low bulk, it is generally good to not switch Gastly into unresisted attacks, and it's preferred to get Gastly in through a U-turn or Volt Switch or after one of its teammates has fallen. Substitute should be used on a predicted switch and against Sucker Punch users to safely protect Gastly. It can also be used to avoid status from certain Pokemon such as Spore Foongus. Be sure to always avoid being in against Pursuit trappers, such as Alolan Grimer. It is also best that Gastly is only used when it can ensure a KO on a foe, as it is too frail to take nearly any damage.

Team Options

Note that Twinkle Tackle Gastly should be used on teams that appreciate a lure to Timburr, Mienfoo, or Vullaby, as if teams don't need this, Life Orb Gastly would work better. Pokemon that appreciate the removal of Fighting-types and Vullaby, such as Scraggy and Carvanha, appreciate Gastly's ability to lure in and KO said threats. Abra in particular appreciates Twinkle Tackle's ability to remove Vullaby and severely weaken Alolan Grimer and Pawniard. Gastly greatly appreciates Stealth Rock support from setters such as Pawniard, Ferroseed, Onix, and Dwebble to help it break through more Pokemon, and in return, Gastly can block Rapid Spin for them. Fighting-types, namely Mienfoo and Timburr, are very useful to help Gastly beat Dark-types, Pawniard in particular, as well as many using Knock Off to cripple foes, and Gastly can deal with Fairy-types in return. Slow pivots, namely Mienfoo, Chinchou, and Vullaby, can help Gastly get onto the field without taking any damage from attacks.

Choice Scarf.description:
Moves

Shadow Ball and Sludge Bomb are solid STAB moves for Gastly, and Sludge Bomb comes with a chance to poison. Thunderbolt allows Gastly to hit Water-type Pokemon for super effective damage, most notably OHKOing Shellder and Omanyte, the latter after a Shell Smash boost. It also does significant damage to Vullaby, coming close to a KO after Stealth Rock damage. Dazzling Gleam allows Gastly to take out opposing Scraggy, which Gastly can deal with even after a Dragon Dance boost due to its Choice Scarf, and deal significant damage to Vullaby. Alternatively, Trick allows Gastly to lock an opposing Pokemon into a status or setup move, ideally giving a teammate a chance to set up.
