Quagsire is outclassed by other Electric immunities outside of stall teams, namely Swampert, which can set Stealth Rock, and Gastrodon with its fantastic special bulk, which can check big threats such as Choice Specs Tapu Koko and Kyurem-B for the team.
monotype.comments:
Other Options

Water

Rocky Helmet can be used over Leftovers in order to chip contact move users down, but Leftovers's passive recovery is generally preferred. In addition, Rocky Helmet should not be used with Protect because Protect provides more passive recovery as one of its main merits. Curse and Waterfall can be used over Toxic and Scald in order to let Quagsire serve as a slow wincon, making it ridiculously hard for all physical attackers outside of Grass-type Pokemon to beat.

Checks and Counters

Water

Grass-types: Grass-type Pokemon such as Tapu Bulu, Mega Venusaur, Breloom, and Celebi all knock Quagsire out with ease using their STAB Grass-type attacks.

Special Attackers: Due to its low special bulk, Quagsire struggles to take hits from common special attackers such as Keldeo, Latios, Mega Diancie, and Landorus.

Wallbreakers: Various wallbreakers such as Choice Band Dragonite and Choice Band Diggersby all threaten Quagsire with their strong attacks. However, physical wallbreakers need to be wary of being burnt by Scald.

Toxic: Being badly poisoned hinders Quagsire's ability to check physical setup sweepers consistently, as it is now forced to switch out to prevent itself from being worn down.

Taunt: Taunt users such as Gliscor, Hydreigon, and Mew are able to break through Quagsire by disabling its recovery and status moves and slowly wearing it down.

Unaware Wall (Water).description:
Moves

Scald has a chance to burn, which is particularly useful for crippling physical attackers such as Mega Gallade and Mega Scizor, allowing Quagsire to wall them more easily. Earthquake hits Electric-type Pokemon such as Tapu Koko, Magnezone, and Alolan Raichu for super effective damage. Protect is extremely good on stall Water for scouting attacks, racking up Toxic damage, and giving Quagsire more Leftovers recovery; it also helps keep Quagsire out of range of Mega Gallade's Close Combat and Mega Pinsir's Return. Recover is Quagsire's form of reliable recovery and keeps it healthy throughout a battle. Toxic puts opposing walls, such as Porygon2, Mantine, and Rotom-W, on timers. Counter can be used over Toxic in order to surprise physical wallbreakers such as Choice Band Dragonite that Quagsire usually would not be able to handle.

Set Details

Maximum Defense investment along with an Impish nature allows Quagsire to switch into and check physical attackers such as Landorus-T, Choice Band Zeraora, and Mega Scizor with ease. It also minimizes the chances of Mega Gallade and Mega Pinsir 2HKOing Quagsire. Leftovers provides Quagsire with passive recovery and prevents it from easily being worn down throughout the battle. Unaware allows Quagsire to check threatening setup sweepers such as Zeraora, Dragonite, Landorus-T, and Bisharp.

Usage Tips

Protect should be used to scout for attacks, which is especially useful against Choice-locked Pokemon such as Tapu Koko and Latios. It should also be used to regain health using Leftovers and rack up Toxic damage. Quagsire should be preserved in order to check setup sweepers that threaten your team, such as Dragonite, Azumarill, and Bisharp. Recover should be used constantly in order to keep Quagsire healthy so it can keep on switching into physical and Electric-type Pokemon. Quagsire should generally prioritize keeping itself healthy over spreading status. Try to avoid status conditions, particularly poison, as they hinders Quagsire's ability to check setup sweepers by putting it on a timer. With that being said, if Quagsire does happen to get afflicted with poison, try to look for opportunities to use Heal Bell with Lanturn in order to cure its status and keep it healthy. Try to use Toxic liberally in order to catch Quagsire's checks and counters such as Hydreigon and Breloom off guard in case they switch in. This makes it a lot easier to wear down said checks and counters over time through switching. Try to remove entry hazards using Defog before Quagsire is sent out, especially if Toxic Spikes and Spikes are set, as the former will make checking setup sweepers extremely hard, while the latter makes switching directly into Pokemon that Quagsire is supposed to check difficult. In the Electric matchup, Quagsire should try to scout which Pokemon is carrying Grass Knot in order to prevent itself from getting unnecessarily knocked out. As Quagsire can typically beat Alolan Raichu without Grass Knot, it is a good switch-in to a large portion of Electric-types, which is valuable in the matchup. Against teams with Choice Band Victini, try to keep Quagsire healthy, as Quagsire is one of the few Pokemon on stall Water teams that counters it.

Team Options

The entirety of stall Water teams appreciate Quagsire's ability to defensively check setup sweepers such as Zeraora, Azumarill, Bisharp, and Mega Scizor. Quagsire appreciates Toxapex as a blanket defensive check and is able to switch into Grass-type Pokemon such as Mega Venusaur and Breloom while also being able to set up and remove Toxic Spikes and use Haze to remove boosts from setup sweepers Quagsire can't check such as Tapu Bulu, which it can threaten with Sludge Bomb. Lanturn is a great secondary Electric immunity due to Volt Absorb and its high Special Defense, allowing it to switch into strong Electric-type special attackers that otherwise threaten Quagsire like Choice Specs Tapu Koko and Grass Knot Alolan Raichu. Quagsire also appreciates its Heal Bell support that cures status conditions that wear it down, such as poison. Azumarill is able to switch into, trap, and beat threatening Grass-type setup sweepers such as Swords Dance Breloom and Tapu Bulu because of its ability in Sap Sipper. Mantine's special bulk and Flying typing allow it to switch into and check special attackers that Quagsire struggles with such as Landorus, Mega Charizard Y, and Celebi. Quagsire also appreciates Mantine's ability to remove entry hazards that cripple it upon switching in, such as Spikes and Toxic Spikes, using Defog. Similar to Mantine, Empoleon's special bulk and Steel typing also allow it to switch into special attackers that threaten Quagsire such as Mega Venusaur and Latios while being able to remove entry hazards using Defog. It can also check Calm Mind Mega Latias with Roar for Quagsire. Alomomola can use its much higher base HP to pass huge Wishes to Quagsire to support it if it ever gets worn down. Alomomola can also check special attackers using Mirror Coat and use Knock Off to hamper recovery by removing Leftovers and scout potentially dangerous attacks using Protect for Quagsire. Mega Slowbro's phenomenal Defense stat allows it to check physical wallbreakers that Quagsire is unable to check such as Choice Band Dragonite and Diggersby. Slowking is able to switch into a variety of special attackers such as Latios and Keldeo for Quagsire. It is also able to check Kommo-o and Mew, setup sweepers that Quagsire cannot check, with Dragon Tail.

ru.overview: Espeon is a wallbreaker capable of punching holes into most balance builds, boasting great power when running Calm Mind or Choice Specs to overcome checks such as Bronzong and Mandibuzz. Nice coverage, a good Speed tier, a high Special Attack stat, and access to recovery in Morning Sun are some of the traits Espeon has to offer. Without a doubt, though, the flashiest aspect of Espeon comes from its ability Magic Bounce, which sends back any status moves and hazards to its user. However, Espeon's high Speed and Special Attack are obfuscated by its mediocre bulk, being only able to take very few special hits. Morning Sun also is a move with abysmal PP, which can be detrimental when Espeon attempts to set up. Despite having good ways to deal with Ghost- and Dark-types, it is still frail and very susceptible to Pursuit trapping. Due to not being able to switch into a lot of hits, Espeon usually needs pivoting to work properly.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Choice Scarf can turn Espeon into a revenge killer to setup sweepers like Barbaracle, Salazzle, and Mega Sceptile. Espeon can run a slower and bulkier Calm Mind set with a spread of 120 HP / 136 SpD / 252 Spe and a Timid nature, which allows it to set up on the likes of Registeel and Ninetales. However, this set lacks the immediate power Espeon has after one Calm Mind boost, and it's more geared towards beating bulkier teams without a Haze or Unaware user.

Checks and Counters

Steel-types: Bronzong can take at least one super effective hit and retaliate with Gyro Ball. Metagross and Escavalier can set up on Espeon when it lacks Hidden Power Fire and threaten it with their STAB attacks or Pursuit.

Dark-types: Umbreon can take virtually anything from Espeon and stall it out with Wish and Foul Play. Mandibuzz can usually take a hit and U-turn out to a faster threat or deal huge damage with Knock Off or Foul Play. Choice Scarf Drapion and Sneasel can Pursuit trap Espeon or take it out with Knock Off.

Specially Defensive Pokemon: Porygon2, Florges, Snorlax, Cresselia, and Registeel can deal with most hits from Choice Specs Espeon and proceed to beat it due to their resistances or recovery moves. However, they must be wary of Trick, as it may render them useless.

Faster Pokemon: The likes of Swellow, Noivern, Salazzle, Zygarde-10%, and Choice Scarf Tyrantrum can outspeed Espeon and take it down with their powerful STAB moves.

Priority Moves: Golisopod and Honchkrow can revenge kill Espeon from full with First Impression and Sucker Punch. After some chip damage, Toxicroak and Choice Band Zygarde-10% can do the same.

Calm Mind.description:
Moves

Calm Mind boosts Espeon's Special Attack and Special Defense to high levels against the likes of Florges, Roserade, and Dragalge, allowing it to take special neutral hits more easily and hit a lot harder. Psychic is Espeon's hardest-hitting STAB move, but Psyshock can be used to deal with the likes of Snorlax and other Pokemon with high Special Defense. Shadow Ball is the main coverage move on this set and allows Espeon to hit Bronzong, Metagross, and Cresselia super effectively. It also lets Espeon hit Steelix and Registeel neutrally. Morning Sun allows Espeon to stay healthy and keep setting up against the likes of Bronzong and Registeel. Alternatively, Zap Cannon is an one-time nuke when paired with Electrium Z that allows Espeon to break through some of its checks, outright OHKOing most Mandibuzz variants after Stealth Rock. It also offers good neutral coverage despite its shaky accuracy of 50%, allowing Espeon to blow up Water-types like Milotic and Mega Blastoise, deal with Pursuit trappers such as Drapion, and hit Registeel harder than Shadow Ball.

Set Details

Maximum investment in Special Attack and Speed with a Timid nature allows Espeon to hit hard and reach a great Speed tier, outspeeding the likes of Virizion, Ninetales, and Shaymin. Magic Bounce makes Espeon immune to Taunt and other status moves, allowing it to set up comfortably. Leftovers give Espeon some longevity to set up and recover off entry hazard damage. Electrium Z is essential if running Zap Cannon so Espeon is able to use Gigavolt Havoc. Colbur Berry can also be run to make Espeon less vulnerable against Knock Off and Pursuit users.

Usage Tips

Use Magic Bounce to your benefit by switching into possible status moves, such as Toxic and Thunder Wave, and into passive hazard users, such as Bronzong and Registeel, to reflect entry hazards and get setup opportunities. Make use of forced switches to use Calm Mind and deal with whatever comes in. After a Calm Mind boost, Espeon can even deal with the likes of Choice Scarf Gardevoir and Salazzle much more easily. When running Electrium Z, you can bluff Choice Specs and make switch-ins feel comfortable by taking a resisted or ineffective Psychic, just to start setting up or hit them with a super effective move. Note that not all Pursuit trappers can deal with Espeon; Drapion, Escavalier, and Metagross can all be dealt with via Gigavolt Havoc after some residual damage or a boost. However, faster Pursuit trappers such as Sneasel and Choice Scarf Drapion may stop Espeon dead in its tracks. Snorlax is the only Pursuit trapper that can always KO Espeon due to its great Special Defense.

Team Options

Espeon appreciates Pokemon that can take on Dark-types, especially Umbreon, as partners. Bewear, Florges, Virizion, and Machamp are great teammates that can take them on. Fairy-types such as Florges resist Dark- and Bug-type attacks and can give Wish support or set up on them. The likes of Sigilyph and Necrozma can form Calm Mind cores alongside Espeon to overcome each other's checks. Pursuit trapping is nice to take Metagross and Bronzong out of the way for Espeon. Drapion, Sneasel, and Escavalier can take them out and offer offensive presence or nice resistances. Pokemon with Knock Off are good partners to Espeon, since they can remove the passive recovery of Leftovers from the likes of Registeel, Forretress, and Diancie. Mandibuzz and Escavalier can provide this support as well as a good defensive presence. Offensive partners that can deal with Pokemon that resist Espeon's attacks such as Registeel and Steelix are good choices alongside Espeon. The likes of Mega Blastoise and Ninetales can take out those defensive Pokemon, while Espeon can break through Pokemon that resist their attacks such as Milotic, Noivern, and Rhyperior.

Choice Specs.description:
Moves

Shadow Ball is Espeon's main coverage move, enabling it to 2HKO Pokemon that resist Psychic such as Metagross, Cresselia, and Bronzong. Dazzling Gleam allows Espeon to 2HKO most Mandibuzz variants and take out the likes of Drapion and Pangoro and has a little chance of 2HKOing Umbreon. Trick allows Espeon to render defensive switch-ins like Umbreon, Registeel, and Bronzong almost useless, as they will be locked into one move. Hidden Power Fire allows Espeon to 2HKO Escavalier and damage other Steel-types.

Set Details

Full investment into Special Attack and Speed with Choice Specs is necessary to maximize Espeon's capabilities as a wallbreaker and give it immediate power. Magic Bounce protects Espeon from Thunder Wave's paralysis.

Usage Tips

Make sure Espeon will get in safely, be it with smart switching into status moves or with pivoting. Although Magic Bounce allows Espeon to bounce back entry hazards, you must measure very well when it's time to switch in, since Espeon can be wrecked by moves such as Bronzong's Gyro Ball. Choose wisely what move Espeon will get locked into; opposing Pokemon can take advantage of a Choice-locked Espeon, especially the likes of Escavalier, Snorlax, and Drapion, which can Pursuit trap it when it's locked into Psychic. Trick is a powerful tool that allows Espeon to limit the utility of many defensive switch-ins, so try to Trick Espeon's Choice Specs onto Pokemon like Bronzong, Registeel, and Cresselia.

Team Options

Slow pivoting from Pokemon such as Mandibuzz and Mega Ampharos pairs well with Espeon to bring it safely into the field. Gardevoir is a very nice pick alongside Espeon, and when equipped with a Choice Scarf, its cleaning potential becomes way greater after Espeon's wallbreaking job has been done. Roserade, Golisopod, and Mega Glalie all can support Espeon with Spikes, which makes most rolls positive for Espeon, while also packing a huge punch. Drapion, Escavalier, and Sneasel are good teammates that can remove Steel-types' items with Knock Off and Pursuit trap Pokemon that resist Espeon's attacks such as Bronzong. After Espeon gets trapped by the likes of Drapion and Sneasel, Pokemon such as Barbaracle, Zygarde-10%, and Salazzle can capitalize on their Choice-locked move to set up and sweep right after.

Dual Screens.description:
• With Stealth Rock growing in popularity in the tier, Dual Screen Espeon works as a fine answer to most Stealth Rock setters, such as Hippowdon, Swampert, Landorus-T, Garchomp, Mamoswine and Nihilego, protecting the field from the hazards thanks to Magic Bounce, while almost freely setting up Reflect and Light Screen for its team. Espeon also does a fine job versus passive Pokemon such as Toxapex, finding even more setup opportunities.
  • Its fast Yawn gives it an answer to opposing setups if needed, while Psychic does decent damage even without any evs investments.
  • The spread outspeeds adamant Mega Salamence and survives attacks such as Greninja’s Dark Pulse (has a 50% chance to survive even the Life Orb variant), Mega Gengar’s Hex, Choice Scarf Garchomp’s Outrage and adamant Choice Scarf Landorus-T’s Earthquake and U-Turn, before the screens.
  • This set is threatened by faster Pokemon that can take it out before it sets up, such as Electrium Z Tapu Koko and Offensive Mega Gengar’s Shadow Ball, leaving teams that rely on the screens without their main strategy.

Baton Pass Recipient.description:
• The combination of Magic Bounce, due to bouncing back moves such as Roar, Whirlwind or Toxic, and access to Stored Power, make Espeon a fantastic Baton Pass Recipient.
  • The spread outspeeds base 130 speed Pokemon at +1, while maximizing its bulk and physical defense as much as possible.
  • If using an Extreme Evoboost strategy, the speed can be raised to 92 EVs to outspeed +1 Jolly Mega Salamence after the Eeveeboost.
  • Kee Berry is the preferred item when Espeon is paired with Baton Pass users who don't pass many defensive boost, such as Normalium Z Umbreon. However, when receiving an Extreme Eevoboost or Iron Defense, items such as Sitrus Berry or Mago Berry are preferred.

Psychium Z.description:
• The main strength of this set is that it can hit fast, fairly hard and find set up opportunities in front of passive Pokemon such as Toxapex and Chansey thanks to Magic Bounce, and weaker special attackers such as Cresselia and Whimsicott due to the combination of Calm Mind and Morning Sun.
  • The spread allows Espeon to hit as hard as possible, and the Psychium Z gives it a fantastic nuke that can, for example, OHKO Mega Charizard X or have a 56% chance to OHKO Mega Salamence without boosts.
  • The EVs in Special Defense are there to survive certain attacks at +1, like Tapu Koko’s Z Thunderbolt in Electric Terrain and Offensive Mega Gengar’s Shadow Ball.
  • The speed EVs are to speed creep Pokemon that EV to outspeed Adamant Mega Salamence by 1.

anythinggoes.overview: Espeon is a staple on most Baton Pass teams because it is the only non-Mega Pokemon with both Baton Pass and Magic Bounce and the most effective Baton Pass receiver. Access to STAB-boosted Stored Power allows it to sweep teams effectively and efficiently, landing an OHKO on even the bulkiest Pokemon in the metagame with enough boosts, and a decent base Speed of 110 allows it to outspeed most of the metagame with a single Speed boost. However, Espeon should not be used on teams other than those utilizing Baton Pass; Mega Sableye would be a better option if only Magic Bounce is desired.
anythinggoes.comments:
Other Options

Espeon can be used on Extreme Evoboost teams, using Calm Mind over Dazzling Gleam and maximizing HP and Defense with a Timid nature. This is due to the nature of Extreme Evoboost teams essentially ensuring a +2 boost in everything besides accuracy and evasion, thus removing the need for Speed or Special Attack investment, as Espeon will OHKO and outspeed most threats anyway.

Checks and Counters

Mega Gengar: Mega Gengar can force Espeon out and threaten the rest of the team with Taunt, as it is usually the only team member with Magic Bounce. It also can trap Espeon with Shadow Tag and outspeed it, which results in Espeon being knocked out and possibly a loss if Espeon has no Speed or Special Defense boosts.

Yveltal: Yveltal forces Espeon to switch in to stop Taunt while threatening to OHKO it with Dark Pulse. Its dominance over Baton Pass teams can be slightly remedied by giving a Mental Herb to a team member with Substitute, providing Espeon with a safety net. Yveltal also can use Sucker Punch against Espeon, which can easily land an OHKO on Espeon if it doesn't have the proper Defense boosts.

Marshadow: Focus Sash Marshadow is deadly against Espeon, as it can steal all of its boosts with Spectral Thief. Even without Focus Sash, it can attack Espeon with a priority Shadow Sneak, which OHKOes with a Life Orb if Espeon lacks Defense boosts. If Marshadow's item has not been scouted and it is sent in against Espeon, it is usually safest to Baton Pass out to a Normal-type such as Smeargle.

Magearna: Magearna resists Stored Power and has high base Special Defense, requiring a great number of boosts, especially Special Attack, to knock it out. This, paired with its move Heart Swap, can let it steal a Espeon's boosts and allow it to reverse sweep. The presence of a Magearna on the opposing team can force a Baton Pass team to gather more boosts before going to Espeon to sweep, leaving it more vulnerable.

Ditto: Without regeneration from Ingrain and Aqua Ring or a Substitute to block Imposter, Ditto can switch into Espeon and copy all of its boosts to sweep.

Baton Pass Checks: Espeon requires significant boosts from teammates in order to be effective. Opposing Pokemon that can deter the team from gathering them include threats such as Haze Zygarde and Toxapex, Perish Song Arceus, forced switching, and Taunt, as well as those that simply hit the team incredibly hard, such as Deoxys-A, Mega Rayquaza, and Primal Kyogre.

Baton Pass Sweeper.description:
Moves

Baton Pass allows Espeon to switch in and out safely in combination with another Baton Pass user and to make use of Magic Bounce against status moves like Taunt and Roar or Whirlwind without losing stat boosts, as well as keeping stat boosts safe from Spectral Thief in case the opponent has a Focus Sash Marshadow. Stored Power is Espeon's main STAB move, which it can utilize to sweep due to its rapidly growing Base Power from all of Espeon's boosts. Dazzling Gleam is used to hit Dark-types such as Yveltal, Arceus-Dark, and Tyranitar due to their immunity to Stored Power. Substitute is useful as a safety net against priority moves while sweeping, and getting one up safely can be statistically inevitable with enough evasion boosts.

Set Details

8 HP EVs are used to allow Espeon to place four Substitutes without recovery. 208 Defense EVs are required to survive an Extreme Speed from Life Orb Adamant Arceus. 68 Special Attack EVs with a Modest nature are required to OHKO Mega Gengar with Stored Power after three boosts. These boosts will usually be in the form of Speed. The remaining EVs are invested into Speed in order to help Espeon outspeed the opposing Pokemon while sweeping without the need of excessive boosts, letting it outspeed the whole unboosted metagame except for Deoxys-S at +1. Magic Bounce is useful to bounce back various status moves, especially Taunt, Leech Seed, and Roar or Whirlwind before Ingrain is active. Shell Bell is useful to heal back damage taken from priority moves or Substitutes being hit through evasion, since Espeon will likely OHKO the foe. Leftovers may be preferable over Shell Bell if the team cannot provide enough regeneration from the likes of Aqua Ring to place more Substitutes with evasion boosts, as Shell Bell does not heal if Espeon does not attack.

Usage Tips

Espeon, as the only Magic Bounce user on most Baton Pass teams, will need to be switched in with Baton Pass to block Taunt from Yveltal or Mega Gengar. However, both of these threats can OHKO Espeon without significant Special Defense boosts, so switching it into them should be done with care. Apart from bouncing back key status moves such as Taunt and Leech Seed, however, Espeon should not be out until it is ready to sweep. Once enough boosts to sweep have been accumulated, setting up a Substitute to shield Espeon from one hit is recommended before switching it in, but it is not required. Against a Marshadow whose item has not been scouted, Espeon should Baton Pass out to Smeargle, as one Spectral Thief from a Focus Sash Marshadow can immediately turn a won game into a loss. A Substitute should be placed before attacking if Espeon has evasion boosts but inadequate Defense boosts, as evasion boosts mean that a Substitute should be able to be laid down without getting hit after a few tries. Substitute is also a good move to use when switching in Espeon to bounce back a status move with intent to switch out to another team member. Substitute allows Espeon to be hit and switch to the correct team member according to the situation.

Team Options

Espeon fits only on Baton Pass teams, as it lacks the ability to fulfill any other niche in the metagame. Scolipede is a powerful team member with access to Speed Boost, Baton Pass, and Iron Defense, allowing the team to farm Defense and Speed, giving Espeon the ability to outspeed opposing Pokemon while sweeping and have physical bulk to survive priority attacks from Arceus, Mega Rayquaza, and Marshadow. Smeargle is arguably the most popular Baton Passer due to having access to every move in the game along with Moody as an ability. Smeargle can put foes to sleep with Spore, use Ingrain to keep foes from phazing it, use Spectral Thief to steal back stats and hit Marshadow, and set up a Substitute to farm Moody boosts. Drifblim is the most viable evasion passer because of Minimize and Unburden along with its natural bulk. Evasion helps with setting up Substitutes when the Substitutes cannot survive any given move from the foe. Mr. Mime is invaluable against common methods of removing boosts. Soundproof allows it to switch into Perish Song and Roar, and its Fairy typing lets it switch into Dragon Tail. Taunt allows Mr. Mime to block opposing Taunts, Haze, and Heart Swap. Vaporeon can pass Aqua Ring for increased regeneration, which is useful while setting up Substitutes. It also has a defensively effective pure Water typing that allows it to get Defense boosts with Acid Armor more easily. Its natural bulk and low sSpeed also let it act as one of the most effective pivots on Baton Pass teams. Gliscor can farm evasion boosts with Double Team against Primal Kyogre, one of the most powerful threats to Baton Pass teams, because of its immunity to Thunder.

1v1.overview: Umbreon's great bulk allows it to take on both physical attackers like Zeraora, Landorus-T, and Mega Metagross and special attackers like Meloetta, Primarina, and non-Taunt Tapu Lele, and its Dark typing makes it immune to Prankster from Pokemon like Whimsicott. Umbreon also has great utility moves like Charm and Moonlight that enable it to take on Mega Gyarados, Mega Charizard X, and Choice Scarf Haxorus. Furthermore, Umbreon can pressure setup Pokemon such as Landorus-T with Foul Play and prevent Tapu Lele from setting up Calm Mind with Snarl. However, Umbreon has trouble facing bulky Pokemon such as Porygon2, Magearna, and Z-Move Togekiss, which are able to take its attacks and stall out of Moonlight's PP. It also suffers against common Leech Seed users such as Serperior, Jumpluff, and Mega Venusaur because of its inability to do major damage to them and its limited recovery with Moonlight. It further suffers against Taunt users such as Deoxys-S, Tapu Fini, and Kommo-o, as it cuts off Umbreon's recovery options and allows them to either stall it out or take it out with their super effective attacks.
1v1.comments:
Other Options

Umbreon has no other viable option.

Checks and Counters

Stall Pokemon: Umbreon struggles with walls such as Deoxys-S, Mega Slowbro, Porygon2, and Magearna due to their ability to outstall it and take any of its attacks.

Taunt: Pokemon that run Taunt such as Tapu Fini and Kommo-o can cut off Umbreon's recovery and take it out with their super effective attacks.

Leech Seed: Umbreon struggles with Pokemon that use Leech Seed like Serperior, Mega Venusaur, and Jumpluff because it is unable to do anything back to them and slowly gets stalled out of Moonlight PP.

Super Effective Attacks: Mega Mawile, Mega Gardevoir, and Sawk are all able to OHKO Umbreon with their super effective attacks before Umbreon can use Z-Charm or Snarl to lower their offensive stats.

Z-Charm.description:
Moves

Z-Charm makes Umbreon able to beat powerful physical attackers such as Mega Gyarados, Choice Scarf Haxorus, Choice Band Garchomp, and Choice Band Dragonite lacking Superpower. Foul Play enables Umbreon to beat physical attackers such as non-Substitute Landorus-T, Jirachi, and Mega Pinsir. Moonlight allows Umbreon to shake off damage after using Z-Charm on Choice Band Garchomp, Choice Scarf Haxorus, or Mega Charizard X or after using Snarl against Tapu Lele or Primarina. Snarl makes Umbreon able to beat Tapu Lele and Primarina due to the Special Attack drop. Toxic can be used over Snarl to take on walls like Porygon2 and non-Rest Slowbro.

Set Details

Fairum Z allows Umbreon to use Z-Charm, which allows it to beat Pokemon such as non-Superpower Choice Band Dragonite and Choice Band Garchomp. Inner Focus allows it to avoid flinches from Jirachi's Iron Head and Mega Gyarados's Waterfall. 252 HP EVs and 228 Defense EVs enable Umbreon to take attacks from Garchomp, Zeraora, and Landorus-T as well as two Outrages from non-Superpower Choice Band Dragonite. 28 Special Defense EVs with a Calm nature allow Umbreon to survive Normalium Z-boosted Hyper Beam from bulky Meloetta after Laser Focus as well as tank Moonblast from Primarina and non-Taunt Tapu Lele.

Usage Tips

Against Mega Metagross, do not use Z-Charm, because it can forgo Mega Evolving to avoid the Attack drop with Clear Body; instead, use Foul Play twice to beat it. Also, do not use Z-Charm against Victini, as Umbreon already OHKOes or 2HKOes Victini with Foul Play, and Victini can't do anything back. Umbreon is a good pick against both Mega Charizard X and Y, as Z-Charm + Foul Play will take care of Mega Charizard X while Snarl + Moonlight will allow Umbreon to stall out sun turns to beat Mega Charizard Y. It can also take on Jirachi due to Inner Focus, and use Foul Play to 2HKO it. For Meloetta, it is best to use Snarl turn 1; if it uses Calm Mind turn 2, use Snarl again, and if it used Laser Focus, use Moonlight turn 3 to be able to recover off Breakneck Blitz. Umbreon should avoid being sent out on most Leech Seed users, with the exception of Whimsicott, and walls such as Mega Venusaur, Serperior, Clefable, Registeel, and Mega Slowbro, as it cannot do enough damage to them to beat them and cannot do major damage back to them. Umbreon can win against Whimsicott only because its Dark typing allows it to avoid Prankster Leech Seed and Taunt.

Team Options

Pokemon that can take on Fighting-types like Kommo-o and Terrakion such as Tapu Fini and Mega Diancie make good partners for Umbreon. In return, Umbreon can take on Mega Metagross for them. Whimsicott and Mega Sableye are great counters to stall Deoxys-S, which Umbreon is unable to take care of. In return, Umbreon can take on Fairy-types like Tapu Lele and Primarina, Fire-types like Mega Charizard X and Mega Charizard Y, and Steel-types like Mega Metagross and Magnezone for Whimsicott. Flying-types like Togekiss and Flyinium Z Landorus-T can help against Grass-types such as Mega Venusaur and Serperior and Fighting-types that Umbreon can't beat like Kommo-o and Mega Gallade. In return, Umbreon can take on Naganadel and Mega Charizard Y for them. Steel-types such as Magnezone, Mega Metagross, and Mega Mawile are great to beat Fairy-type Pokemon that Umbreon has trouble beating such as Mega Diancie, Mega Gardevoir, and Tapu Fini; in return, Umbreon can take on Mega Charizard Y for them. Electric-type Pokemon that can beat Mega Slowbro like Magnezone and Zeraora make great partners for Umbreon. In return, Umbreon can take care of Ground-type Pokemon for them. Fire-types such as Mega Charizard X, Heatran, and Incineroar are great for taking on Steel-types like Registeel and Ferrothorn. Umbreon is able to take on Dragon-types like Haxorus and Garchomp in return.

uu.overview: Umbreon's high bulk and decent defensive typing allow it to check prominent threats in the metagame, such as Mega Sharpedo, Hydreigon, and Latias. Furthermore, access to Wish and Heal Bell makes Umbreon a great cleric. Toxic and Foul Play allow Umbreon to deter physical setup sweepers such as Scizor and Haxorus from setting up on it. However, Umbreon is easily exploitable by Toxic-immune Pokemon with Justified, such as Cobalion and Lucario. Furthermore, Taunt users, such as Crobat and Krookodile, completely shut Umbreon down by preventing it from healing itself or its teammates. Additionally, Umbreon's reliance on Wish + Protect to keep itself healthy can cause the loss of momentum, while reliance on Moonlight to keep itself healthy can be taken advantage of due to Moonlight's relatively low PP. Umbreon also suffers from the presence of pivots, such as Scizor, Mega Beedrill, and Infernape, that can threaten it out and gain momentum with U-turn. Umbreon also faces competition from Blissey as a special wall, with Blissey having higher HP, a defensive typing that grants it fewer weaknesses, and access to Soft-Boiled, Stealth Rock, and Natural Cure, and as a cleric from Sylveon, which has a better defensive typing and better offensive presence.
uu.comments:
Other Options

Normalium Z, in conjunction with Heal Bell, not only makes Umbreon immune to Trick but also gives it a one-time full recovery. However, Umbreon does not like giving up the passive recovery that Leftovers provides, because it loses the ability to better check key threats such as Mega Aerodactyl and Mega Sharpedo, and it also takes up a potential Z-Move from a teammate. A more physically defensive spread of 252 HP and Defense EVs with a Bold nature allows Umbreon to take on certain physical attackers such as Mega Sharpedo and Mamoswine better, but Umbreon's typing makes it still struggle against prominent physical attackers, such as Scizor and Cobalion.

Checks and Counters

Fighting-types: Fighting-types such as Terrakion and Infernape force Umbreon out and may even set up with Swords Dance or Nasty Plot. Lucario and Cobalion deserve a special mention thanks to their immunity to Toxic and their ability, Justified, that raises their Attack each time Umbreon tries to use Foul Play on them.

Bug-types: Bug-types such as Scizor and Mega Beedrill threaten out Umbreon with their powerful STAB moves. They also maintain momentum with U-turn after Umbreon switches out. Both of these dislike switching into Foul Play, though.

Fairy-types: Fairy-types, such as Mega Altaria and Primarina, threaten Umbreon out with their powerful STAB moves and resist Foul Play. They can also set up Dragon Dance or launch a powerful attack, respectively. Togekiss deserves a special mention due to being able to cure Toxic poison inflicted by Umbreon with Heal Bell and taking advantage of its passivity to set up Nasty Plot.

Toxic-immune Pokemon: Toxic-immune Pokemon such as Cobalion, Empoleon, and Gligar do not fear Toxic, take little damage from or can benefit from Foul Play, and can beat Umbreon one-on-one.

Taunt users: Taunt users such as Krookodile and Crobat take advantage of Umbreon by preventing it from healing. Furthermore, Krookodile can remove Umbreon's passive recovery.

Specially Defensive.description:
Moves

Foul Play is Umbreon's most reliable STAB move; it allows Umbreon to significantly damage physical attackers such as Scizor, Mamoswine, and Mega Beedrill. Heal Bell heals Umbreon's teammates and itself from status ailments, which also makes Umbreon a more reliable special wall. Toxic not only gives Umbreon an easier time beating setup sweepers, such as Latias, but also lets it badly poison common switch-ins, such as Terrakion and Infernape, and slowly wear them down. Wish allows Umbreon to recover its own health as well as heal its teammates up. Protect combines with Wish to give Umbreon an easier time healing itself up and also allows Umbreon to scout common Choice item users, such as Hydreigon and Infernape, and gain more recovery from Leftovers. Alternatively, Moonlight gives Umbreon a more reliable form of self-recovery; in combination with Wish, Umbreon can use Moonlight on a turn it would otherwise use Protect on and gain more health back. However, Moonlight's low PP means Umbreon can be stalled out rather easily.

Set Details

Maximum investment in HP and Special Defense, combined with a Calm nature, allows Umbreon to take on special attackers such as Latias, Hydreigon, and Nidoqueen as easily as possible. 4 Speed EVs allow Umbreon to outpace uninvested Scizor and hit it with a Foul Play before it gets to hit Umbreon with a super effective move. Synchronize allows Umbreon to punish certain Toxic users such as Rotom-H, Slowbro, and Swampert that attempt to badly poison it. Leftovers provides passive recovery, which helps Umbreon retain longevity.

Usage Tips

Switch in Umbreon on special attackers such as Latias, Hydreigon, and Nidoqueen and beat them via attacking with Foul Play when ever Umbreon is at a comfortable amount of HP; this is achieved by continuously using Wish in tandem with Protect or Moonlight. Hence, Umbreon needs to stay as healthy as possible throughout the match. Generally, you should use Wish either when Umbreon is low on HP or when a teammate should be healed up. Use Protect to scout for potential mixed special attackers with Fighting coverage, such as Superpower Hydreigon and Nidoking, and Choice-locked Pokemon like Latias and Volcanion. Be wary of using Protect against certain potentially Choice-locked Pokemon that may utilize setup moves, such as Scizor and Terrakion. In addition, be wary of switching in Umbreon on potential Trick users such as Togekiss and Latias. Umbreon could also be switched in on certain physical attackers, such as Mega Aerodactyl and Mega Sharpedo. Avoid spamming Foul Play against teams with Justified users such as Cobalion, Terrakion, and Lucario, as they can easily take advantage of it to boost their Attack. Despite its access to Toxic and Foul Play, Umbreon heavily struggles to beat certain setup sweepers such as Cobalion and Terrakion that beat it by virtue of their typings. Hence, it is wise to not stay in on them, as they use Umbreon as setup fodder. Do not stay in on Taunt users, such as Krookodile and Jellicent, because they can reliably shut down and beat Umbreon. Use Heal Bell when either Umbreon or its teammates are afflicted with a status ailment, such as Toxic, while keeping in mind Heal Bell's low PP.

Team Options

Umbreon fits well on balance and stall. Fairy-types, such as Mega Altaria and Togekiss, and Flying-types like Moltres and Crobat can handle Fighting-types such as Infernape and Cobalion. The aforementioned Fairy-types can also utilize Heal Bell so Umbreon can freely run Toxic, and the Flying-types appreciate Umbreon's Wish support because of their Stealth Rock weakness. Entry hazard removers such as Gligar and Tentacruel ensure that Umbreon won't have to take residual damage each time upon switching in. The latter pairs exceptionally well with Umbreon not only because it can take on certain physical attackers that scare Umbreon out, such as Cobalion and Scizor, but also because it removes Toxic Spikes by virtue of its Poison typing. Physically defensive Pokemon like Swampert and Mega Slowbro pair well with Umbreon thanks to their ability to handle the majority of physical attackers, such as Infernape and Cobalion. They are also capable of punishing common Taunt users like Krookodile with a potential Scald burn. Additionally, wallbreakers, such as Scizor, Volcanion, and Primarina, appreciate Umbreon's Wish support and also scare out setup sweepers that attempt to set up on Umbreon.

ru.overview: Umbreon is one of the premier clerics in RU thanks to its access to both Wish and Heal Bell, in addition to its incredible 95 / 110 / 130 bulk, which allows it to check a variety of threats such as Nidoqueen and Swellow. Furthermore, its access to Foul Play can be a detriment to the physical attackers that try to come in and use Umbreon for setup, so Pokemon like Tyrantrum and Escavalier have to be careful about taking STAB Foul Play, as it can 2HKO them. That being said, Pokemon like Swords Dance Bewear, Calm Mind Florges, and Curse Snorlax take very little from it and can use Umbreon as setup fodder. In addition, its weakness to Fighting is bothersome with Virizion and Pangoro being very threatening to Umbreon and defensive teams in general.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Moonlight on the cleric set instead of Protect is an option to not have Umbreon waste two turns by using Wish + Protect and instead just heal up. Taunt + Moonlight alongside Toxic can allow Umbreon to check and beat a number of Pokemon like Cresselia, Curse Snorlax, Slowbro, Milotic, and Porygon2. Screech is an option on the cleric set instead of Heal Bell to let it reliably beat Slowbro and Snorlax.

Checks and Counters

Fighting-types: Bewear, Toxicroak, Machamp, and Pangoro all don't take that much damage from Foul Play and can KO Umbreon with their STAB Fighting-type moves. Virizion has Justified to get an Attack boost from Foul Play and can set up with Swords Dance and KO Umbreon with Close Combat.

Bug-types: Bug-types such as Yanmega, Galvantula, Araquanid, Golisopod, and Escavalier all have super effective STAB attacks that can KO Umbreon, but the last two have to be wary of Foul Play, as it can do a lot of damage.

Fairy-types: Gardevoir packs a super effective Moonblast that can 2HKO Umbreon, but keep in mind that without Choice Specs or Life Orb, it only has a 7.4% chance to 2HKO. Florges with Calm Mind can also set up on Umbreon, but its Moonblast is very weak without boosts and fails to 2HKO specially defensive Umbreon. The same applies for Diancie.

Cleric.description:
Moves

Wish is the biggest reason to use Umbreon, as it lets it heal itself and teammates that need it, along with Protect, which guarantees that Umbreon gets recovery from Wish alongside passive recovery from Leftovers, gives the enemy an extra round of Toxic damage if they're poisoned, and scouts for moves and Choice-locked Pokemon. Heal Bell is a good option to get rid of harmful status for Umbreon and its team, but Toxic can be used over Heal Bell if it's not needed, as it can allow Umbreon to cripple bulky Pokemon such as Slowbro and Milotic, which it otherwise wouldn't be able to. Foul Play is the only way that Umbreon can do any meaningful damage, so it's chosen as the fourth move.

Set Details

Maximum HP and Special Defense investment is used to maximize Umbreon's special bulk and let it check threats such as Nidoqueen and Swellow. However, a physically defensive spread is a viable option to let Umbreon act as a better check to the likes of Honchkrow, Zygarde-10%, and Metagross. Leftovers is used for passive recovery and goes really well with Protect. Synchronize is the only ability worth using, as inflicting the same status to the foe is more helpful, and it also synergizes with Heal Bell.

Usage Tips

Use Umbreon to check threats such as Nidoqueen and Swellow throughout the game while utilizing Wish to heal Umbreon as well as pass it to other teammates that need it. However, be careful when using the Wish + Protect combination when healing Umbreon, as your opponent could easily see the Protect coming and take advantage of it by gaining momentum or setting up. Heal Bell only has 8 PP, so use it conservatively. For example, if you have a Pokemon that is burned but doesn't mind the Attack drop, saving Heal Bell for when other Pokemon get poisoned or burned might be better.

Team Options

Nidoqueen can set up Stealth Rock and Toxic Spikes and is also able to check the Fairy-, Fighting-, and Bug-type attacks and Pokemon that Umbreon's weak against while appreciating the Wish support and Umbreon's ability to switch into Psychic- and Ice-type attacks. Mantine is also a good teammate for the nice synergy that it provides, and it can also provide support with Defog. Diancie can pack Heal Bell to allow Umbreon to carry another move and benefits from the Wish support. In general, any bulky Pokemon that appreciates Wish or Heal Bell support, such as Mega Blastoise, Gigalith, Rhyperior, Bronzong, and Escavalier can be a nice option for a teammate.

ru.overview: Slowking has a niche as one of the only effective Assault Vest users in the tier, and coupled with its very good HP and Special Defense stats, it can act as an effective blanket check to special attackers. Some of the Pokemon it checks include Nidoqueen, Salazzle, Gardevoir, Noivern, Swellow, and Necrozma. It has a premier ability in Regenerator that allows it to check these Pokemon throughout the match. Its extensive movepool includes a plethora of coverage and utility options like Fire Blast, Ice Beam, and Dragon Tail. However, despite all its positives, it faces stiff competition for a slot on most teams from its Psychic-type counterparts such as Slowbro and Cresselia, which possess unique advantages including better natural physical bulk. It also has a crippling weakness to Pursuit and the ever-present Knock Off. Finally, Slowking struggles to take on the plethora of strong physical attackers in the tier, even ones without super effective coverage like Donphan, Zygarde-10%, and Bewear.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Slowking has a plethora of other options due to its expansive movepool, but it does still face competition from other bulky Water- and Psychic-types. A defensive Nasty Plot set can be used, as it boosts its Special Attack and is threatening faster than Slowbro and Cresselia. An offensive Trick Room set is an option to check special attackers while posing a bigger threat to offensive teams. Shadow Ball hits bulkier Psychic-types, such as Slowbro, Cresselia, and opposing Slowking, as well as Mismagius. Psychic or Psyshock are alternate STAB moves that can hit Toxicroak and Dragalge without waiting for Future Sight to hit, but typically Future Sight's power is appreciated. Calm Mind sets, meanwhile, face a lot more competition from these Psychic-types, but a mixed defensive Calm Mind set could be run to have an easier time setting up against special attackers.

Checks and Counters

Strong Physical Attackers: Slowking can take on most special attackers, but strong physical attackers such as Pangoro, Zygarde-10%, and Tyrantrum can severely dent or OHKO or Slowking with their attacks.

Special Walls: Bulky special walls such as Snorlax, Cresselia, Mantine, Bronzong, and Mandibuzz can take on Slowking without much trouble, as the best thing Slowking can do to them is burn them with Scald or hit them with Future Sight in Snorlax's case.

Dark-types: Pangoro, Drapion, Mandibuzz, and Sneasel all absorb the Future Sights that Slowking uses to wallbreak and can OHKO or 2HKO it with their STAB moves, but they should watch out for Scald.

Grass-types: Grass-types such as Shaymin, Roserade, Virizion, Tsareena and Mega Abomasnow can threaten Slowking with their super effective STAB moves and switch into Scald, but they should avoid Future Sight and Fire Blast.

Assault Vest.description:
Moves

Scald is Slowking's main STAB move, allowing it to check Fire-types and deny free switch-ins to physical attackers, such as Tsareena and Pangoro. Despite it not hitting immediately, Future Sight allows Slowking to limit future switches because it hits very hard. Fire Blast hits Grass-types such as Shaymin and Roserade as well as Steel-types such as Escavalier. Dragon Tail prevents Slowking from being setup fodder for Snorlax, Escavalier, and other bulky setup sweepers. It also works nicely with Future Sight because the foe will try to play around it by switching into a Dark- or Steel-type, which Dragon Tail will phaze out. Ice Beam is an option that allows Slowking to check Swellow, Dragalge, and Noivern more reliably.

Set Details

An Assault Vest bolsters Slowking's already great Special Defense, allowing it to act as a blanket check to special attackers. The main issue with running Assault Vest is that Slowking cannot run Slack Off, but Regenerator makes up for this and allows Slowking to check these attackers throughout the match. 252 HP EVs and 80 Special Defense EVs are used in order to take +2 Acid Downpour from Salazzle after Stealth Rock and check Swellow more reliably. The rest of the EVs are dumped into Special Attack, which, along with a Modest nature, allows Slowking to hit harder. Slowking can run many alternative EV spreads to check different threats. For example, it can run 136 Defense EVs to take Adamant Zygarde-10%'s Devastating Drake and Barbaracle's +2 Stone Edge, both after Stealth Rock. These are just two examples of alternative EV spreads; spreads with Speed investment to outspeed Bronzong or more Special Defense investment to be more forgiving against Salazzle are also possible.

Usage Tips

Pivot Slowking into Pokemon that it checks, such as Nidoqueen, Salazzle, and Sigilyph, so it can threaten the opposing team by using Future Sight or another STAB move. Remember that Regenerator is Slowking's only way of gaining back health, so it is even more important to pivot Slowking into Pokemon that it checks so it can recover health with its ability while avoiding losing it unnecessarily. Threaten physical attackers that try to switch into Slowking by going for Scald, which has a chance to burn and cripple them. Use Dragon Tail if you predict that the foe will attempt to set up. This is especially helpful against foes that cannot OHKO Slowking such as Snorlax, but you should be careful if the Pokemon in question is a strong physical attacker such as Dragon Dance Zygarde-10%. In conjunction with entry hazards, use Dragon Tail to wear down the opposing team quickly.

Team Options

Slowking has a hard time taking on powerful physical attackers, even ones that do not have powerful super effective coverage, such as Bewear and Tyrantrum. As a result, Pokemon that take on these threats, such as Metagross, Rhyperior, Bronzong, and Mandibuzz, make for great partners. Golisopod also takes on some of these attackers while setting up Spikes, which Slowking can exploit by using Dragon Tail, and also revenge killing Grass- and Dark-types with First Impression. Grass-types such as Shaymin and Roserade make for good teammates, as they take on the Grass- and Electric-types that threaten Slowking, like Raikou and Tsareena. They also appreciate Slowking taking on the Fire-types that threaten them. Similarly, Slowking appreciates teammates that can take on the Dark- and Ghost-types that threaten it. Examples of such Pokemon are Passimian, Florges, and Snorlax. U-turn and Volt Switch users such as Flygon, Mandibuzz, and Mega Ampharos can give Slowking more opportunities to switch in, thus maximizing the amount of health it gains back from Regenerator.

nu.overview: Slowking boasts excellent defensive typing, a great ability in Regenerator, and exceptional special bulk as well as good physical bulk, making it one of NU's most reliable defensive pivots, taking on Passimian, Delphox, and Mega Glalie reliably. Access to strong STAB moves, including Scald, Future Sight, and Psyshock, as well as good base 100 Special Attack means that Slowking is no slouch offensively either. This is accentuated by its wide variety of coverage move that include Fire Blast, Grass Knot, and Ice Beam, making Slowking difficult for anything but a dedicated wall to switch into. A wide utility movepool with Dragon Tail, Slack Off, Toxic, Nasty Plot, and Calm Mind means that Slowking can be customized for most teams. However, as its name suggests, Slowking is outrun by essentially every offensive Pokemon in NU as well as most walls, making it fairly easy to revenge kill. Additionally, Slowking is very vulnerable to Toxic, as any passive damage reduces the recovery it gets from Regenerator, hurting its ability to pivot.
nu.comments:
Other Options

A set of Block / Calm Mind / Scald / Rest can function as a potent trapper, eliminating Water-types such as Blastoise and Vaporeon as well as acting as a potent sweeper. An EV spread of 252 HP / 252 Def / 4 SpD with a Bold nature should be used with this set, as well as Normalium Z in order to give Slowking a Defense boost from Z-Block. An offensive Trick Room set of Nasty Plot / Trick Room / Scald / Psyshock with Psychium Z and an EV spread of 252 HP / 4 Def / 252 SpA with a Quiet nature can turn Slowking into a sweeper that can often beat offensive teams by itself; however, this set needs 2 turns of setup in order to sweep a lot of the time, limiting its effectiveness. Zap Cannon can be used on the Assault Vest set to potentially cripple Vaporeon and enemy Slowking; however, its low accuracy means it often does nothing, and Slowking often has to give up a more consistent option such as Grass Knot or Dragon Tail.

Checks and Counters

Grass-types: Dhelmise is one of Slowking's greatest enemies, OHKOing it with Power Whip while having the bulk to switch into any of its moves at least once. Special wallbreakers such as Alolan Exeggutor and Sceptile can muscle through even Assault Vest Slowking, although Sceptile needs it to be weakened in order to KO it with Leaf Storm.

Dark-types: Guzzlord is one of Slowking's greatest foes, taking little from Scald, Future Sight, or Fire Blast and threatening to heavily damage it with Dark Pulse or Knock Off, although it dislikes Dragon Tail. Incineroar, Pangoro, and Sneasel can easily KO the Assault Vest set with Darkest Lariat and Knock Off, although they fail to take out Colbur Berry sets as efficiently. Pursuit from Sneasel and Absol traps the Assault Vest set. Bulk Up Scrafty has the bulk to easily take almost any hit Slowking can throw at it and set up against it.

Toxic: Slowking is often reliant on Regenerator to heal itself, so a source of passive damage such as Toxic from Druddigon, Vaporeon, or Seismitoad can result in Slowking getting worn down rather quickly. All three of these Pokemon can often switch into Slowking freely use Toxic.

Electric-types: While Heliolisk and Rotom fail to OHKO Slowking, they can easily wear it down using Volt Switch, and neither is OHKOed by Slowking. Vikavolt can easily OHKO even Assault Vest Slowking with Savage Spin-Out, but it fears Fire Blast and cannot switch in easily. Heliolisk additionally takes no damage from Slowking's Scald, giving it many chances to switch in against it during a match.

Assault Vest.description:
Moves

Scald has good Base Power, has an incredibly useful burn chance, and hits common Pokemon like Rhydon and Incineroar, making it one of Slowking's most spammable moves. Future Sight lets Slowking support its team by setting up lose / lose situations for its foe when combined with a teammate such as Passimian, by removing Poison-types as a switchin to Passimian on the turn Future Sight hits. Alternatively, Psyshock is more reliable than Future Sight and 2HKOes Heliolisk while ignoring Comfey's Calm Mind boosts, preventing Slowking from being setup fodder for Comfey. Fire Blast hits Grass-types for very heavy damage, letting Slowking OHKO Sceptile after Stealth Rock, and provides good damage against Vikavolt and Heliolisk. Ice Beam can be used to hit Dragon-types such as Guzzlord and Alolan Exeggutor, OHKOing the latter, as well as heavily damaging Torterra, but it does not hit other Grass-types as hard as Fire Blast, lacking the ability to OHKO Sceptile. Dragon Tail lets Slowking prevent setup and force out a foe the turn Future Sight hits, potentially forcing in a target that can't take the move well. Grass Knot is Slowking's best way to hit Water-types, which otherwise wall this set.

Set Details

212 HP investment and an Assault Vest maximize Slowking's special bulk, letting it take attacks such as Sceptile's Leaf Storm. This investment is key to letting Slowking effectively check wallbreakers such as Magmortar and Sigilyph. 44 Speed EVs let Slowking outrun Palossand. 252 Special Attack EVs and a Modest nature increase Slowking's offensive presence significantly. Regenerator serves to keep Slowking healthy throughout a match by healing it when it switches out.

Usage Tips

Efficient usage of Regenerator is key to using this set correctly; try as much as possible to bring this set in against weak attacks such as Delphox's Flamethrower in order to heal Slowking. If the opponent has Pokemon weak to Future Sight such as Passimian and Weezing, try to use Future Sight and use Dragon Tail 2 turns later in order to try to force the Psychic-weak Pokemon in or to prevent your opponent from switching Psychic-resistant or -immune Pokemon in. Scald should also be used for this purpose if you predict the opponent to bring in an Incineroar on the turn Future Sight is due to hit. Scald is a very useful move early-game, as getting early burns on Pokemon such as Druddigon can help to wear them down, while burning potential switch-ins such as Sneasel can cripple them for the rest of the game. Dragon Tail can be helpful in an unsure situation, especially when Stealth Rock is up, as it can potentially weaken some of Slowking's answers. If Slowking is healthy, it can be used to scout almost any special hit in the game; it is often better for Slowking to take 70% from a Heliolisk's Thunderbolt than for a teammate to be KOed by Surf or Hyper Voice. Fire Blast or Ice Beam should be used if the opponent is predicted to bring in a Grass-type.

Team Options

Pokemon that want Poison- and Fighting-types KOed can make excellent usage of Slowking's Future Sight support. Passimian is an excellent example, as very few Pokemon in NU want to come in on its Close Combat on the turn Future Sight is due to hit. Comfey and Sceptile are excellent partners for similar reasons, being very difficult for opponents to deal with if their Poison-type gets KOed. Entry hazard support from Pokemon such as Rhydon, Garbodor, and Steelix is incredibly useful due to Slowking's Dragon Tail and ability to force switches. Pokemon such as Incineroar, Whimsicott, and Passimian help deal with Dark-types, and all appreciate Slowking's support, especially its ability to take on Poison- and Fighting-type Pokemon. Pokemon that can switch into Electric-types like Heliolisk such as Dhelmise, Rotom, and Togedemaru help to prevent Slowking from being worn down by them. Similarly, Grass-resistant Pokemon such as Braviary, Incineroar, and Garbodor take on threatening foes such as Sceptile and Dhelmise. While Slowking does resist Fighting, additional checks such as Rotom, Garbodor, and Weezing help to reduce the stress placed upon it.

Nasty Plot.description:
Moves

Nasty Plot lets Slowking beat Pokemon like Blastoise, Druddigon, and Silvally-Steel more reliably. Scald dissuades Dark-types like Incineroar, Pangoro, and Absol from directly switching into Slowking and is its best way of damaging Psychic-types like Delphox, Xatu, and Sigilyph. Future Sight is great for easing prediction and has very few safe switch-ins when boosted by Nasty Plot. Alternatively, Psyshock provides an immediate source of damage against Poison-types like Weezing and Garbodor as well as Heliolisk. Additionally, it is more reliable than Future Sight is after Shattered Psyche has been used. Slack Off increases Slowking's longevity and recover health lost to hard hits such as Choice Band Aerodactyl's Stone Edge and Medicham's Thunder Punch.

Set Details

44 Speed EVs let Slowking outspeed Palossand, while the remaining EVs with a Bold nature increase Slowking's physical bulk so it can better check Pokemon like Passimian, Aerodactyl, and Rhydon. Psychium Z gives Slowking access to Shattered Psyche, which, in conjunction with Nasty Plot, lets it break through Pokemon like Druddigon, Vaporeon, and Seismitoad more easily and allows it to bypass Future Sight's delay to immediately hit Heliolisk. Regenerator provides Slowking with additional recovery, letting it delay its use of Slack Off and scout Choice item users like Passimian and Aerodactyl more reliably.

Usage Tips

Slowking has phenomenal mixed bulk; as a result, it finds plenty of opportunities to switch in against Pokemon like Delphox, Passimian, and Rhydon and recover health with Slack Off, set up, or simply fire off an attack. It is also key to take advantage of Regenerator as much as possible by scouting Choice item Pokemon such as Passimian and Aerodactyl and switching into weak hits or non-attacking moves from the likes of Steelix and Xatu for free recovery. Due to how Future Sight works, it's a great way to ease prediction and make the opponent's plays more telegraphed. Make use of this by using Future Sight to force in Pokemon like Incineroar, opposing Slowking, and Pangoro and switching to the appropriate check, setting up with Nasty Plot, or using Scald. Timing the usage of Slowking's Shattered Psyche is very important to ensure the removal of bulky Water-types like Vaporeon, particularly when using Future Sight, which is less reliable at doing so. Although Scald is a very spammable move, be careful if the opponent has a Heliolisk, especially if using Future Sight instead of Psyshock, as it can switch into a predicted Scald to recover health.

Team Options

Slowking is a great fit on balanced and bulky offense teams due to what it offers both offensively and defensively. Slowking checks a wide variety of Pokemon due to its excellent mixed bulk and defensive typing, so Pokemon like Incineroar, Pangoro, and Steelix that appreciate having checks to Pokemon such as Aerodactyl, Passimian, and Delphox make for great teammates. Since Slowking can struggle with Heliolisk, especially when it lacks Shattered Psyche or Psyshock, it appreciates having teammates like Aerodactyl, Choice Scarf Passimian, and Dhelmise that can deal with it. Aerodactyl can also threaten Grass-types like Sceptile and Whimsicott, Passimian can deal with Dark-types like Incineroar and Pangoro, and Dhelmise provides entry hazard control. Slowking's ability to pressure specially defensive Pokemon like Druddigon, Seismitoad, and Vaporeon with Nasty Plot-boosted attacks is greatly appreciated by Pokemon like Magmortar and Heliolisk that share similar checks to it. Magmortar can also take out Grass-types, while Heliolisk helps with opposing Slowking.

Physically Defensive.description:
Moves

Scald has usable Base Power, an incredibly useful burn chance, and the ability to hit Pokemon such as Rhydon and Incineroar for super effective damage, making it one of Slowking's most spammable moves. Psyshock hits Poison-types such as Weezing and Garbodor and Fighting-types such as Passimian for heavy damage and prevents Heliolisk from freely switching into Slowking. Toxic provides a very valuable source of passive damage for Slowking, letting it easily wear down bulky Water-types such as Vaporeon, Seismitoad, and other Slowking as well as the likes of Druddigon and Comfey. Calm Mind is an option that turns Slowking into a useful late-game sweeper. Slack Off lets Slowking stay in against and beat Pokemon such as defensive Incineroar and Passimian. Future Sight can be run over Psyshock to further support Slowking's team and be used to great effect with Spikes support due to the switches it forces; however, the lack of an immediate Psychic-type attack can leave Slowking walled by Heliolisk.

Set Details

Near maximum physical bulk lets Slowking take attacks such as Passimian's U-turn and Mega Glalie's Double-Edge more easily. Regenerator helps Slowking pivot, letting it heal itself after switching out and easily sponge attacks such as Passimian's U-turn. A Colbur Berry minimizes the damage Slowking takes from Knock Off, letting it easily switch into and beat defensive Incineroar and Passimian as well as take on Pokemon such as Sneasel by making Pursuit far less threatening. Psychium Z should be primarily used with the Calm Mind set and gives Slowking a one-time nuke to break through Pokemon that would otherwise wall it, letting it OHKO Vaporeon at +3 Special Attack as well as providing a very strong initial hit if needed. This can also be used to provide an unexpectedly strong hit against Pokemon such as Garbodor.

Usage Tips

Efficient usage of Regenerator is key to using this set correctly; try as much as possible to bring this set in against weak attacks in order to heal Slowking. For example, bringing it into a Delphox's Flamethrower can often mean a net HP gain of 20%. Similarly, this lets Slowking easily come in on attacks such as Passimian's U-turn with minimal HP loss. As this set often aims to stay in longer than other Slowking sets, keeping Slowking free of Toxic can be very important. Try to scout for Toxic against walls that might carry it such as Steelix and Druddigon. Thanks to Regenerator, Slowking is often free to use its STAB attacks to damage the opponent's team or to use Toxic to potentially cripple an important threat, as it can heal up easily by switching out rather than needing to use Slack Off. Calm Mind should be used when the opponent no longer has efficient ways to break through a boosted Slowking; if using Calm Mind, be careful to prevent Slowking from being badly poisoned, and generally do not attempt to set up until all Toxic users are KOed. Thanks to its burn chance and good Base Power, Scald is often very difficult for the opponent to punish, making it a safe choice in unsure situations; however, be wary that it does not accidentally burn a Toxic target such as enemy Slowking or Blastoise.

Team Options

Fighting-weak Pokemon such as Incineroar, Steelix, and Heliolisk appreciate Slowking's ability to come in on almost any move from Passimian as well as beat other Fighting-types. Fairy-types such as Whimsicott and Comfey appreciate Slowking's ability to beat Poison-types and Steelix for them, and in return they can take on the Dark-types that trouble Slowking. Pokemon such as Pangoro, Whimsicott, and Passimian help deal with Dark-types and appreciate Slowking taking on Fighting-, Ground-, and Poison-types for them. Heliolisk switch-ins such as Dhelmise, Togedemaru, and Torterra are good teammates, as Slowking can often let Heliolisk in for free and does not appreciate taking Volt Switch. Grass-resistant Pokemon such as Weezing, Incineroar, and Garbodor take on foes that would either heavily damage or KO Slowking. Weezing and Garbodor can also set up Spikes, which can help wear down Sceptile and Heliolisk. Mega Audino can provide useful Heal Bell support, appreciates Slowking's ability to switch into Fighting-type attacks for it, and can function as part of a very potent Regenerator core with it. Mega Audino's sheer special bulk also means it can often take on special attackers such as Heliolisk, Rotom, and Guzzlord, all of which trouble Slowking.

pu.overview: This is completely outclassed by special attackers such as Aurorus, Victreebel, and Drampa.

Choice Specs.description: Unown only has two options: using Hidden Power and swapping out. Well, there is actually a third option: utilizing another special attacker over Unown. Victreebel and Drampa are notable, as they provide useful defensive utility to teams and actually have longevity, allowing them to consistently perform their roles. Unown suffers from terrible stats and only having access to Hidden Power, making it a complete waste of a team slot.

pu.overview: Due to the fact that the one thing that would make Wobbuffet usable, Shadow Tag, is banned, it's no surprise that it is completely useless in the PU tier. Wobbuffet has a shallow and predictable movepool, and it can't directly attack the opponent. This means that Wobbuffet is complete setup bait, can easily be chipped down by status conditions, and, above all else, is completely invalidated by its foe switching out. Many other walls, like Regirock and Jellicent, do a much better job at dealing with strong attackers because they can actually attack the opponent and have better utility options like Stealth Rock and Will-O-Wisp.

Bulky Death Fodder.description: This set attempts to take hits from and eliminate strong all-out attackers like Choice Scarf Primeape, Skuntank, Jellicent, and Victreebel thanks to its good bulk in conjunction with Mirror Coat or Counter. However, the foe can simply switch out, rendering Wobbuffet useless because it can't do anything unless the foe uses an attack. The best Wobbuffet can do is hope that it can knock something out with Destiny Bond, but even then, Wobbuffet can't use Destiny Bond two turns in a row, allowing the opponent to play around it easily by just switching on the turn Wobbuffet uses it. Taunt and Toxic also eliminate that option outright.

ubers.overview:
• Instead of using Shadow Tag to trap and revenge kill or PP stall a foe like Mega Gengar, Gothitelle, and Gothorita do, Wobbuffet takes advantage of its superior bulk to retaliate against certain threats after stomaching a heavy hit or leave a foe in an exploitable state by locking it into a move with Encore.
  • Wobbuffet's bulk is also noteworthy for being able to ensure that Geomancy Xerneas will be dealt with before it proceeds to annihilate offensive teams, as it survives any boosted attack from full health to retaliate with Mirror Coat or lock Xerneas into any status move it carries.
  • Access to Encore also serves as one of the crucial elements to Wobbuffet's viability, as Wobbuffet won't be easily taken advantage of by its checks the same way as Gothitelle and Gothorita, which can be left completely helpless against certain foes. This means Wobbuffet will not be left useless even if weakened and be able to prevent setup or potentially even reverse momentum by locking a foe into a setup move.
  • Due to its tiny movepool, horrendous defensive typing, and lack of recovery moves, Wobbuffet's effectiveness is quite limited as a bulky trapper. Wobbuffet is almost impossible to viably fit in teams other than offense, an archetype that prefers Wobbuffet's ability to generate setup opportunities and check out-of-control foes in emergency over its longevity.
ubers.comments:
Other Options

  • A physically defensive EV spread can be used to take hits from Extreme Killer and physical Primal Groudon better, but worsening Wobbuffet's matchup against Geomancy Xerneas and support Arceus formes is generally not worth it.
  • Wiki Berry heals half of Wobbuffet's HP when its HP decreases below 25%, but this is much harder to safely activate. However, extra recovery allow Wobbuffet to avoid 2HKOs from stronger attacks such as maximum Attack Primal Groudon's Precipice Blades and, after Stealth Rock damage, Water-type moves from offensive Primal Kyogre variants and Double-Edge from Adamant Mega Salamence.
  • Leftovers can be considered, as it provides Wobbuffet with passive recovery, gives it some resilience against passive damage, and notably allows it to survive +2 Moonblast from Xerneas after Stealth Rock and Leftovers recovery.

Checks and Counters

Ghost-types: Wobbuffet is offensively threatened by and has no way to effectively neutralize Ghost-types, as they cannot be trapped by Shadow Tag. Marshadow in particular can be troublesome, as it is immune to Counter and some variants can even set up Bulk Up on a forced switch or weaken Wobbuffet with Pursuit.

Zygarde: Zygarde has many ways to avoid getting hindered by Wobbuffet's trapping. Almost every offensive variant has Substitute, and a Zygarde behind Substitute can attack Wobbuffet without worrying about Counter once, forcing Wobbuffet to predict between locking Zygarde into Dragon Dance using Encore or using Counter to at least break the Substitute for teammates. Variants with Dragon Tail are less concerned about Encore, and others holding Groundium Z can still use Tectonic Rage while Encore-locked.

Dark-types: Yveltal, Arceus-Dark, and the rare Darkrai can hit Wobbuffet super effectively with their STAB moves without fearing retaliation thanks to their immunity to Mirror Coat.

Z-Move Users: Other Z-Move users like Necrozma-DM, Ultra Necrozma, Swords Dance Arceus-Ground, and Naganadel can set up on Wobbuffet and still attack a switch-in with a Z-Move through Encore, meaning they cannot be completely neutralized.

Taunt Users: Taunt users like Mewtwo can prevent Wobbuffet from locking them into a move using Encore and set up on it without fear.

Mixed Attackers: Powerful mixed attackers like Primal Groudon and Primal Kyogre can make predictions more difficult when Wobbuffet has to choose between using Counter and Mirror Coat. Wobbuffet can avoid some 2HKOs against mixed attackers with Sitrus Berry intact, however.

Trapper.description:
Moves

  • Trapped foes afflicted by Encore will be easily taken advantage of by Wobbuffet's teammates. Using Encore when Wobbuffet is no longer needed also prevents it from being set up on.
  • Counter and Mirror Coat prevent Wobbuffet from being completely passive, returning doubled damage if Wobbuffet made a correct prediction. An attacking foe locked into Encore can be taken out by Wobbuffet itself if the attack isn't strong enough to take out Wobbuffet in a few hits. Note that Counter will not affect Ghost-types nor will Mirror Coat hit Dark-types.
  • Though Wobbuffet is very slow, it can effectively utilize Destiny Bond to take down a threat after getting weakened. Due to Destiny Bond lasting until Wobbufet’s next turn, an opponent will likely have to spend two turns deciding between trading KOs or setting up and risking getting locked by Encore.
  • While Safeguard may not seem like the most sensible utility move due to Wobbuffet's slow Speed leaving it vulnerable to most status ailment users, it can be used to prevent a foe locked into status moves like Toxic or Thunder Wave from statusing incoming teammates.

Set Details

  • Maximum HP and Special Defense investment with a Calm nature allows Wobbuffet to survive any attack from +2 Xerneas and minimize the chance it falls to +2 Moonblast after taking Stealth Rock damage. Specially defensive investment also helps with Wobbuffet's ability to stomach Judgment from support Arceus formes that it typically attempts to take advantage of.
  • Custap Berry gives +1 priority to Wobbuffet's move when its health is 1/4 or below, allowing Wobbuffet to use effectively Destiny Bond and take down a foe.
  • Sitrus Berry heals a quarter of Wobbuffet's HP when its HP decreases below 50%, enabling it to take another hit against support Primal Groudon after Precipice Blades or Overheat and avoid other potential 2HKOs. Sitrus Berry also enables Wobbuffet to check mixed Rock Polish Primal Groudon from full health, as it can avoid a 2HKO from Fire Blast or Precipice Blades with Sitrus Berry recovery, lock Primal Groudon into a move, and KO back the next turn using Counter or Mirror Coat.

Usage Tips

  • Wobbuffet aims to punish bulky Pokemon that its team struggles to bypass. While it does not necessarily cripple trapped foes by weakening them with Counter and Mirror Coat, it can benefit its team more by giving free switches with Encore.
  • This means Wobbuffet can switch into or, if possible, double switch into support Arceus formes or relatively passive Pokemon like defensive Necrozma-DM to easily survive a hit and lock them with Encore. This will either force them to keep attacking Wobbuffet with the same move or lock them into status moves like Stealth Rock, Defog, Recover, and Toxic. Attacks can be handled with Counter or Mirror Coat, and status moves make them fodder for Wobbuffet's teammates.
  • Double switching into passive Pokemon can preserve Wobbuffet's health so that it may have another chance to trap and temporarily neutralize a foe later in the game.
  • Wobbuffet is likely going to be hit by status moves like Toxic while locking a foe into Encore, so Safeguard should be used afterwards to prevent its teammate from getting crippled.
  • A healthy Wobbuffet can also take more aggressive approach to lock stronger foes into Encore. However, it is quite dangerous to recklessly create a confrontation with powerful and unpredictable foes like Primal Groudon that have varying ways to 2HKO Wobbuffet. Xerneas, which Wobbuffet avoids a 2HKO from, should be faced with caution as well. If Geomancy Xerneas hits Wobbuffet with Moonblast on switch, it can force a risky mind game between using Mirror Coat on the next Moonblast or punishing Geomancy with Encore. Get a safe switch in against these Pokemon if possible.
  • A lead Pokemon will likely be taken down by a Pokemon that Wobbuffet will proceed to trap next, and this means there will be an opportunity to acquire some information about opposing lead Pokemon depending on the moves they carry or the damage they do to the lead Pokemon.
  • Against offensive teams, Wobbuffet will struggle to be able to trap multiple foes. Identify which offensive Pokemon will be threatening to Wobbuffet's team. Wobbuffet may have to be left healthy if the team is not able to adequately deal with Geomancy Xerneas and Rock Polish Primal Groudon, but if its team has enough ways to pressure the opposing team, it can be used to allow its team to immediately become threatening after it cripples a foe with Encore and either cause serious damage early-game or secure a win against weakened teams that attempt a comeback by using setup moves or removing entry hazards.
  • Do not worry much about Wobbuffet's longevity. While excessive layers of entry hazards can mess with Wobbuffet's ability to effectively trap foes, Wobbuffet will typically trade itself for the momentum or ideal setup conditions it generates for the team. Use Wobbuffet as sacrifice fodder if it is no longer needed, and if it is one-on-one situation against a foe after getting weakened, use Encore before going down so that a foe it is facing won't get to set up on Wobbuffet without getting punished.

Team Options

  • There are multiple ways for Wobbuffet's team to draw in Pokemon like support Arceus formes, which Wobbuffet can turn into setup fodder for teammates. Offensive teams that typically employ Wobbuffet can have a dedicated lead like Cloyster or Deoxys-S to set entry hazards or powerful yet commonly prepared-for threats like Primal Groudon and Xerneas to draw in passive foes. Note that letting foes remove entry hazards in exchange of Wobbuffet turning them into setup fodders is not an ideal decision in cases where there are bulkier foes that need entry hazards to be effectively taken out.
  • A number of setup sweepers can run rampant with Wobbuffet giving them a free turn to set up unharmed. Pokemon like Rayquaza, Mega Blaziken, and Naganadel, which can be devastating after a turn of setup but are typically too frail to successfully set up and remain healthy enough to survive a priority move, can have the perfect setup condition they desire. Rayquaza is also helpful for being one of the very few Pokemon that can take advantage of Primal Groudon locked into one its STAB moves and providing its team with extra security against sweepers with Extreme Speed. Lunala can check out some out-of-control sweepers in a pinch with Shadow Shield intact, and it can potentially set up Calm Mind while keeping its Shadow Shield with the free turn Wobbuffet generates for it.
  • Marshadow should be strongly considered in Wobbuffet's team.
