  • Blissey is one of the most reliable special walls in the tier that handles essentially all special attackers that Skarmory struggles against, with the exceptions of Yveltal and Mewtwo. In return, Skarmory checks the majority of the physical attackers that take advantage of Blissey, especially the likes of Substitute variants of Mega Salamence and Arceus assuming they aren't the last Pokemon. Chansey can be used instead if a more durable special wall is desired, but this leaves Skarmory's team more vulnerable against Shadow Tag users, which isn't too ideal.
  • A number of common offensive threats appreciate Skarmory's Spikes support, as the entry hazard helps wear down their checks. Spikes support is extremely helpful, if not mandatory, for setup sweepers like Dragon Dance variants of Zygarde-C, Mega Salamence, and Rayquaza to successfully bypass their conventional checks like support Arceus formes. Zygarde-C in particular can take advantage of Spikes to facilitate its sweep by wearing down foes with Dragon Tail and Spikes on the field. As other threats like Xerneas and Calm Mind Arceus formes tend to draw in their checks, and as most of them are vulnerable to Spikes, Skarmory can be a considerable teammate for them as well.
  • Various support Arceus formes pair with Skarmory. Arceus-Ground, Arceus-Water, and Arceus-Dragon all check Primal Groudon and provide Defog support. They also check offensive Zygarde-C, a threat that Skarmory cannot handle due to Thousand Arrows. Arceus-Ground in particular is a great check to Mega Lucario and can pick off Necrozma-DM in an event where Skarmory is KOed by boosted Searing Sunraze Smash. Arceus-Water and Arceus-Dragon are also good checks to Ho-Oh.
  • Lugia is a good blanket check to Primal Groudon, Zygarde-C, and Mega Lucario. It can use Ice Beam to take care of Substitute variants of Zygarde-C and Mega Salamence if they are the last Pokemon left and cannot be phazed by Whirlwind. Lugia can also take advantage of Skarmory's Spikes support to wear down foes with Whirlwind.
  • Ho-Oh and Toxapex are good checks to Mega Lucario as well. Ho-Oh checks Xerneas and spreads burn with Sacred Fire to make physical attackers almost useless against Skarmory, while Toxapex also spreads burn with Scald and provides Toxic Spikes support. Toxapex in particular can be helpful against the last foe behind Substitute, as it can prevent their setup with Haze.
  • Giratina takes on most physical attackers that can overwhelm Skarmory such as Primal Groudon, Mega Lucario, and Ho-Oh. It also stands as a solid Defog user that can handle Primal Groudon.
  • Mega Sableye shuts down passive walls that are immune or resilient to Toxic, such as Ferrothorn, Celesteela, Chansey, and defensive variants of Necrozma-DM. It also can take a more offensive approach to check Extreme Killer Arceus. Magic Bounce allows Skarmory's team to have the upper hand in hazard control.
  • Defensive variants of Primal Kyogre provide a Fire-type immunity to the team with Primordial Sea and deal with support Arceus formes well thanks to massive special bulk and Rest. Defensive Kyogre sets can also use Scald to cripple physical attackers. In return, Skarmory puts Primal Kyogre's checks on timer with Toxic and wears down Primal Groudon and Ferrothorn with Spikes. Skarmory can also switch into Toxic for offensive variants of Primal Kyogre.

ou.overview: Skarmory is a solid physical wall, with its great typing allowing it to check dangerous threats such as Kartana, Excadrill, Garchomp, and Mega Scizor. Its good bulk alongside the combination of Whirlwind and Counter deters their attempts to set up and break past Skarmory while also letting it act as a stopgap to other sweepers such as Dragon Dance variants of Mega Tyranitar and Kommo-o. It is also one of the tier's best users of Spikes, gaining entry on the aforementioned Pokemon alongside the likes of Landorus-T, Gliscor, and Chansey. However, its poor special bulk means that, despite its typing, it cannot check the likes of Mega Alakazam and Tapu Lele and gives foes such as Heatran and Rotom-Wash free switch-ins to set up Stealth Rock or clear Skarmory's Spikes with Defog. Moreover, Counter variants of Skarmory lack a way to reliably deal damage, leaving it completely shut down by Taunt users like Serperior, Tornadus-T, and Mega Gyarados. While Skarmory can use Brave Bird or Toxic to alleviate its damage issue, this leaves it with only Whirlwind against the aforementioned physical attackers, giving them opportunties to break it especially with Z-Moves.
ou.comments:
Other Options

Iron Head is an option in the fourth moveslot on stall teams with Mega Sableye to threaten Fairy-types like Tapu Lele and Mega Diancie, especially the latter given its ability to consistently set up Stealth Rock against Mega Sableye and block both of their utility moves with Magic Bounce. Otherwise, Brave Bird is generally preferred as a damage-dealing move, and Skarmory's other utility options are already hard to pass up on. Specially defensive sets appear to have promise as a more robust switch-in to the likes of Mega Alakazam, but Skarmory's Special Defense is lacking even when invested, being outclassed by Celesteela in this regard, and the loss of physical bulk is significant against Pokemon that Skarmory intends to check.

Checks and Counters

Special Attackers: Skarmory's low Special Defense means almost every special attacker can threaten it with heavy damage, including Tapu Koko, Ash-Greninja, and Heatran; even resisted attacks like Tapu Lele's and Mega Alakazam's Psychic and Magearna's Fleur Cannon heavily dent it. Despite Skarmory's advantageous typing against Clefable, Serperior, and Tornadus-T, they often carry Fire-type coverage in Flamethrower, Hidden Power Fire, and Heat Wave to bypass it.

Strong Physical Attackers and Those with Super Effective Options: Although Skarmory has excellent Defense, attackers like Mega Charizard X and Kyurem-B can target its weaknesses with Flare Blitz and Fusion Bolt. It is unable to withstand attacks from extremely strong wallbreakers like Mega Medicham, Swords Dance Mega Mawile, and Choice Band Hoopa-U. After slight chip damage, Pokemon it checks like Kartana and Garchomp can use Fightinium Z and Rockium Z, respectively, after Swords Dance to KO it.

Taunt: Skarmory lacking Brave Bird is completely shut down by Taunt from the likes of Serperior, Tornadus-T, and Mega Gyarados; the latter is particularly dangerous, as it can use Dragon Dance and bypass Sturdy + Counter attempts with Mold Breaker. Even Skarmory variants with Brave Bird are heavily irritated by Taunt, leaving it unable to heal with Roost or use Spikes.

Magnezone: Skarmory lacking Shed Shell is completely unable to stop Magnezone from trapping and removing it if it switches in, only being able to survive additional turns with Sturdy and Whirlwind.

Physically Defensive.description:
Moves

Roost is crucial to allow Skarmory to sustain itself in front of the attackers it is tasked with checking. Spikes capitalizes on Skarmory's ability to handle common Pokemon like Landorus-T, Choice item Kartana, and Mega Scizor to wear down foes. Whirlwind synergizes naturally with Spikes, accruing passive damage and forcing out Pokemon that attempt to threaten Skarmory. It also allows Skarmory to phaze setup sweepers like Swords Dance Gliscor, Tapu Bulu, and Mega Scizor. Counter is by far Skarmory's best fourth option, OHKOing boosted attackers like Garchomp and Kartana that would be inclined to attack it to avoid being neutralized by Whirlwind. Without it, Skarmory is much less effective against boosted threats, since phazing with Whirlwind can only go so far before Skarmory is overwhelmed. Alternatively, Toxic cripples common switch-ins, such as the Mega Charizard formes, Mega Latias, and Zapdos. Brave Bird provides an instant form of damage, most notably heavily damaging Taunt Serperior, which otherwise shuts down Skarmory; it also hits the likes of Tornadus-T and Mega Alakazam hard. Finally, on certain structures that appreciate Skarmory's defensive qualities and access to Spikes but can be potentially vulnerable to entry hazards themselves such as hard stall teams, Skarmory can run Defog as its final move, using its own immunity to Spikes to remove multiple layers of entry hazards on its side.

Set Details

The given EV spread maximizes Skarmory's physical bulk; an Impish nature should be used if Skarmory is running Brave Bird to avoid losing power, whereas a Bold nature and 0 Attack IVs should be used otherwise to minimize damage from Foul Play and confusion. Rocky Helmet punishes contact moves such as Landorus-T's and Mega Scizor's U-turn, Mega Lopunny's High Jump Kick, and Mega Swampert's Waterfall. Shed Shell is a niche option on stall teams, which often require all its defensive pieces intact, to prevent Skarmory from being trapped by Magnezone. However, Pokemon that Skarmory checks like Kartana and Mega Scizor commonly carry Knock Off, making Rocky Helmet generally preferred. Sturdy allows Skarmory to survive a hit in a pinch and retaliate with one of its utility options, most notably Counter.

Usage Tips

Generally, using Skarmory is simple: switch into physical attackers and avoid special attackers, as almost all of the latter threaten it with heavy damage. Pokemon that do not threaten Skarmory whatsoever, like Choice-locked Kartana, Mega Scizor, and Landorus-T, should be its cue to set up Spikes provided it is healthy enough. It can also come in on Ferrothorn and opposing Skarmory, and mirror their Spikes with its own, and set up on other defensive Pokemon like Chansey and Clefable; however, unscouted variants of these foes can retaliate with Thunder Wave, or Flamethrower in the latter's case, potentially crippling Skarmory. Skarmory should be kept healthy if it is required to check the likes of Kartana and Garchomp, as even slight chip damage can put it in range of +2 All-Out Pummeling and +2 Continental Crush, respectively. Rocky Helmet can be incredibly helpful to punish attacks like Mega Swampert's rain-boosted Waterfall and Mega Tyranitar's Fire Punch, preventing them from otherwise fishing for flinches and burns, and it also stops Excadrill from using Rapid Spin freely against it. In the worst case, Rocky Helmet can leave chip damage on the likes of Kartana and Weavile as it is removed by Knock Off. The second layer of Spikes is generally less valuable unless Skarmory can also safely set up the third layer, which it can against teams without entry hazard removal. Instead, Skarmory should heal or use a utility move, such as Whirlwind to accrue more chip damage or Toxic to catch the likes of Tapu Koko and Zapdos on the switch. Skarmory lacking Shed Shell should be wary of Magnezone, which threatens to trap and remove it. While Skarmory will inevitably faint, since using Roost to offset damage it takes will give Magnezone a free opportunity to switch in, it can generate momentum beforehand by using Whirlwind and double switching before sacrificing itself in exchange for Spikes. If Skarmory lacks Counter, be prepared for a setup sweeper with longevity like Swords Dance Gliscor or Mega Scizor when it becomes the last Pokemon and Skarmory is unable to delay its sweep with Whirlwind.

Team Options

Skarmory fits best on defensive teams ranging from balance to full stall, which appreciate its defensive attributes and Spikes wearing down offensive threats. Chansey and Toxapex form a fantastic core with it, taking on a myriad of special attackers including Mega Alakazam, Tapu Koko, Mega Charizard Y, and Ash-Greninja while providing Stealth Rock and Toxic Spikes to pair with Spikes. In return, Skarmory checks dangerous physical attackers like Kartana, Mega Swampert, and Garchomp that scare them out. Other defensive Steel-types like Heatran and Magearna make up for Skarmory's low Special Defense, checking the likes of Magearna and Tapu Lele. Excadrill is a Steel-type able to check Magearna and Tapu Koko for Skarmory and crucially provides Rapid Spin, being able to remove entry hazards for Skarmory's teammates without clearing its Spikes. However, running Skarmory and Excadrill stacks Steel-types that are unable to check Tapu Lele and Mega Alakazam, thus necessitating a teammate like Cresselia or specially defensive Slowbro. Skarmory's Spikes enable a variety of bulky wincons, such as Swords Dance Gliscor, Calm Mind variants of Mega Latias, Reuniclus, and Clefable, which appreciate the chip damage on their checks such as Slowbro, Mega Scizor, and Magearna. In return, these Pokemon take pressure off Skarmory early- or mid-game, such as Mega Latias's ability to check Kartana and Reuniclus answering Mega Medicham. They are resilient against entry hazards, thus minimizing the need for Defog support and keeping Skarmory's Spikes up.

Physical Wall.description: Skarmory's access to Roost and great Defense make it a significant option to consider over Celesteela for stall teams. It also has a much wider variety of support options to consider over Celesteela, such as Stealth Rock, Whirlwind, and Taunt. However, Skarmory's specially defensive capabilities are pitiful compared to Celesteela's, so teaming it up with strong special walls such as Chansey is a must.

Flyinium Z.description: For full USUM 1v1 analyses, you can check out the USUM format page.

lc.overview: Houndour is one of LC's premier wallbreakers with a STAB combination resisted only by the frail Carvanha, opposing Houndour, and the largely unviable Deino. As a result, only a handful of Pokemon are able to switch into Houndour and even less can manage to more than once. STAB Sucker Punch helps Houndour fend off quicker foes as well, helping to augment its only okay Speed. Houndour's typing is quite lackluster defensively, however, as not only is Houndour weak to the ever-common Fighting-, Water-, and Ground-types in the tier, but it is also frail. This means Houndour is frequently forced out if it cannot KO what is in front of it, which is particularly bad because Houndour is weak to Stealth Rock. It also suffers from being weak to Mach Punch, Aqua Jet, and Vacuum Wave, all quite common priority moves.
lc.comments:
Other Options

A fully physical set might seem appealing for a stronger Sucker Punch, yet it is unviable due to Fire Fang being far too weak to pick up key OHKOs and 2HKOs. Z-Sunny Day sets with Firium Z are technically viable options but are better done by the faster and bulkier Ponyta. Similarly, Nasty Plot sets can completely sweep slower teams, but it is pretty bad outside that specific matchup and seldom worthwhile. It is also rather hard to safely set up a Nasty Plot due to Houndour's middling bulk. Beat Up is a cool alternative to Snarl, but at least 3 of your Pokemon need to be alive, and the benefit is largely nonexistent. Crunch can be somewhat viable in an effort to lure and KO Munchlax on the Life Orb set, but it is otherwise worse than Dark Pulse and requires more EVs to be invested in Attack. Early Bird is a viable alternative ability that's useful for switching into Spores and Sleep Powder, but it relies on getting early wakes to excel. Using Early Bird also has the downside of losing to opposing Flash Fire Houndour and no longer being powered up by Pumpkaboo and Ponyta's Fire-type attacks.

Checks and Counters

Super Effective Priority: Houndour is frail enough to be KOed from full HP by Timburr's Mach Punch or Carvanha's Aqua Jet, and Houndour has little counterplay against this, often forcing it out. These priority users struggle to switch in, however.

Bulky Pokemon: Specially defensive Pokemon that resist one of Houndour's STAB options can switch in, though only on the resisted attack. Specially defensive Berry Juice Pokemon are able to counter once, with the exception of Munchlax which persistently counters, but it must beware potentially switching into Life Orb Flame Charge and then finished off with one of Houndour's STAB moves. Other common bulky Pokemon that can check Houndour include Mareanie, Mudbray, and Spritzee, although the latter can't hit back for much damage.

Revenge Killers: Due to Houndour's only okay Speed, a good number of Pokemon are able to revenge kill it, assuming they are at full health. For example, defensive Staryu is able to switch into Life Orb Houndour and KO back, though only one time unless it can successfully use Recover. Choice Scarf Mienfoo is a reliable check to Houndour as well due to it resisting Sucker Punch, though it cannot switch in. Choice Scarf Chinchou can also check Houndour rather well but only if it is outside of Sucker Punch KO range.

Life Orb.description:
Moves

Fire Blast is Houndour's most powerful attack, 2HKOing everything that does not resist Fire. Its raw power makes it preferable over Flamethrower, which often fails to secure the same 2HKOs and OHKOs. Dark Pulse is a far more reliable STAB move and Houndour's best option for a special Dark-type STAB move; Dark Pulse 2HKOs certain Pokemon that resist Fire such as Staryu, Slowpoke, and usually even Ponyta as well, and it is very spammable. Sucker Punch helps Houndour handle faster Pokemon seeking to abuse its mediocre Speed and abysmal defenses to revenge kill it. Flame Charge allows Houndour to trouble teams lacking super effective priority and again helps offset Houndour's average Speed and helps it outspeed Doduo, Gastly, and most Choice Scarf users. Pursuit is another option to give Houndour more defensive utility, reliably trapping spinblockers for Staryu and Drilbur.

Set Details

Life Orb is the item of choice to make Houndour hit incredibly hard while retaining the flexibility of switching moves. HP IVs are lowered to 9 in order to allow Houndour to hit 19 HP and take less Life Orb recoil. Flash Fire allows Houndour to potentially take advantage of opposing offensive Fire-types, such as Ponyta packing Flame Charge as its fourth move. Flash Fire also makes opposing Pumpkaboo hesitant about using Will-O-Wisp, potentially punishing the play. The EV spread aims to make Houndour hit hard and fast, hence the heavy investment into Speed and Special Attack. A Naive nature is used so Houndour can check Pawniard better by outspeeding it and taking less from Sucker Punch while keeping both its Attack and Special Attack as high as possible.

Usage Tips

Houndour best switches in after one of its teammates has been KOed or via a slow U-turn or Volt Switch. Generally, Houndour should avoid switching in on most Pokemon. Some exceptions can be made to Pumpkaboo, Pawniard, and Ponyta, as Houndour is able to check these Pokemon by the virtue of its Dark / Fire typing and access to Flash Fire, yet Houndour can still only switch in once or twice. Outside of these three Pokemon, Houndour should almost never be switched into play. Additionally, Houndour should only be brought into play when it is capable of KOing the opposing Pokemon. Typically, Houndour aims to take advantage of passive Pokemon, such as Pumpkaboo, Foongus, or Ferroseed, to fire off its powerful attacks or get off a Flame Charge to outspeed the opponent's team. If Pursuit is being used, Houndour should switch directly into Pumpkaboo in order to threaten it with Fire Blast and Pursuit trap it.

Team Options

Houndour appreciates entry hazard removal from the likes of Staryu or Drilbur, as otherwise it struggles to be nearly as effective when Stealth Rock is up. Pursuit variants of Houndour can trap spinblockers for Staryu and Drilbur too, allowing them to better perform their role. Knock Off users are great teammates as well, softening up teams by removing Eviolites and making Houndour that much harder to handle. Dark-types in general appreciate Houndour's raw power and ability to remove their shared checks, making Pawniard, Vullaby, and Scraggy decent partners for Houndour. Fighting-type checks such as Snubbull, Foongus, and Cottonee are almost mandatory due to Houndour's weakness to Mach Punch and Vacuum Wave. The latter two options are especially great as they function as a check to Water-types, which also force out Houndour. Offensive Water-types enjoy Houndour's ability to completely break down opposing bulky Water- and Grass-types, opening the game up for themselves frequently. Similarly, Snivy makes a great partner due to deterring Sticky Web, checking Water-types, and forming a very deadly wallbreaking core. Snivy handles the Ground- and Water-types Houndour struggles with, while Houndour is able to check the Steel- and Grass-types which trouble Snivy. Additionally, Snivy's Glare can help Houndour against quicker teams by slowing them down. Slow pivots with U-turn, such as Mienfoo, or Volt Switch, such as Chinchou, help to switch away from the faster Pokemon that threaten Houndour out, giving Houndour opportunities to come back in safely to fire off its powerful attacks.

Choice Scarf.description:
Moves

Fire Blast hits hard and is Houndour's most powerful attack. Dark Pulse is good for cleaning up teams late-game and revenge killing neutral targets due to its accuracy. Pursuit allows Houndour to trap Abra, Gastly, and Pumpkaboo, which are irksome threats to many teams. Destiny Bond is an emergency button for when a sweeper gets out of hand. Destiny Bond is especially useful when Houndour is paired with another Dark-type, as it can often remove a shared counter. Snarl hits Gastly and Abra behind Substitute, making Houndour a more reliable check to them, although it isn't very powerful.

Set Details

Maximum Speed investment makes Houndour able to check Choice Scarf Pawniard and Speed tie with Jolly Choice Scarf Mienfoo. The Speed investment coupled with a Choice Scarf turns Houndour into a great revenge killer, outspeeding most setup sweepers such as Scraggy at +1. Maximum Special Attack investment makes Houndour as powerful as possible, maximizing how effectively it can revenge kill Pokemon or sweep teams late-game. A Naive nature plus 36 Defense EVs allows Houndour to check Life Orb Pawniard while not weakening its Pursuit. The leftover EVs are invested into Special Defense, as their placement in Attack does not affect Pursuit's rolls, and it can help offset the Special Defense lost from a Naive nature. Flash Fire can be utilized to switch into Will-O-Wisp and Fire-types in general.

Usage Tips

Choice Scarf Houndour is a great revenge killer and is usually best used as such. Houndour should avoid switching into attacks, as it is woefully frail. However, it can clean late-game when opposing priority users are removed and teams are aptly weakened with well-placed Knock Offs and hazards. Due to Houndour's naturally high Special Attack and Speed with a Choice Scarf, it is still hard to switch into. Destiny Bond allows Houndour to remove a would-be check or stop a setup sweeper dead in its tracks, though it can be a little predictable.

Team Options

Entry hazard setters makes Choice Scarf Houndour especially hard to handle due to its high Speed and powerful STAB moves; with hazards on the field, even Pokemon that resist its attacks can only switch in once. Foongus, Cottonee, and Snubbull help maintain momentum, checking the threatening Fighting-types that easily switch into a Houndour Choice-locked into Dark Pulse. The former two also help handle the Water-types that switch into Fire Blast handily. Snivy is a more offensive Water-type counter that appreciates Houndour's ability to trap Gastly and Abra. The duo can wallbreak for one another as well due to sharing similar checks, making them a rather threatening pair. Staryu helps keep hazards off the field, allowing Houndour to check Pokemon throughout the match, while Houndour can trap spinblockers for Staryu. Dark-types as a whole, especially Vullaby, Pawniard, and Scraggy, appreciate Choice Scarf Houndour's ability to cripple checks with powerful STAB attacks or Destiny Bond, and they are good at using Knock Off on key bulky Pokemon such as Mienfoo. Slow pivots with access to Volt Switch, namely Chinchou, or U-turn, such as Mienfoo and the aforementioned Vullaby, are able to generally sponge attacks from Pokemon that Houndour lures in.

uu.overview: The notable Special Attack and Speed boosts Houndoom receives upon Mega Evolution make it a respectable sweeper in the UU metagame. Its movepool complements its massive Special Attack stat and strong offensive typing perfectly, containing high-Base Power STAB moves, a great boosting move in Nasty Plot, and other intriguing options such as Sludge Bomb, Taunt, and Destiny Bond. With its high Speed, Mega Houndoom outspeeds much of the unboosted tier, notably including Pokemon like Cobalion, Latias, and Gengar. However, while its Dark / Fire typing is solid offensively, it leaves Mega Houndoom weak to the tier's common Water-, Fighting-, and Ground-type attacks. Mega Houndoom also finds itself vulnerable to all entry hazards, including a notable weakness to Stealth Rock, which in combination with its average bulk does not leave Mega Houndoom with many opportunities to fulfill its role. It also has some rough one-on-one matchups with top-tier Pokemon like Hydreigon and Mega Aerodactyl, putting more pressure on the rest of the team to shore up those recurring weaknesses.
uu.comments:
Other Options

Mega Houndoom has a wide variety of options for its flexible fourth moveslot, though they are generally less effective than the options listed above. Destiny Bond lets Mega Houndoom sacrifice itself in order to take slower Pokemon down with it, but it is fairly situational. Flame Charge gives Mega Houndoom +1 Speed, though it possesses low Base Power and there are few opportunities to viably pull it off. Hidden Power Electric punishes Mantine while maintaining respectable damage against Primarina, but again, other options are generally much better. Sunny Day in combination with Solar Beam lets Mega Houndoom take advantage of its Solar Power ability and act as a monstrous wallbreaker, but the recoil and lack of setup opportunities often make it less useful than a simple Nasty Plot boost.

Checks and Counters

Hydreigon: Hydreigon fears little from any of Mega Houndoom's common attacking moves and can proceed to throw out free attacks of its own.

Special Walls: Even with Taunt, Mega Houndoom struggles to break through sturdier special walls like Blissey, Mantine, and Snorlax due to its initial damage output against them.

Faster Pokemon: Fast Pokemon like Mega Beedrill, Choice Scarf Infernape, and Choice Scarf Krookodile all outspeed Mega Houndoom and can deal heavy damage to it.

Fairy-types: Though they must fear Sludge Bomb, Fire-resistant Fairy-types like Primarina and Mega Altaria can heavily pressure Taunt variants of Mega Houndoom.

Rock-types: Nihilego and Mega Aerodactyl shrug off any of Mega Houndoom's unboosted attacking moves and can KO it in return.

Bulky Water-types: Suicune, Empoleon, and Swampert can all stomach Mega Houndoom's neutral hits and deal huge damage with their STAB moves.

Priority: Mega Houndoom is easily picked off by priority moves like Infernape's Mach Punch and Crawdaunt's Aqua Jet.

Nasty Plot.description:
Moves

Nasty Plot raises Mega Houndoom's Special Attack two stages, immediately making it a threatening sweeper. Fire Blast provides Mega Houndoom with a high-Base Power STAB move, though it does possess a chance to miss. Dark Pulse is a more consistent STAB option, hitting much of the tier for solid damage and having a decent chance to cause foes to flinch. Sludge Bomb allows Mega Houndoom to threaten troublesome Fairy-types like Mega Altaria and Primarina, which effectively wall its two STAB moves.

Set Details

252 Special Attack EVs allow Mega Houndoom to hit as hard as possible. Maximum Speed investment with a Timid nature lets Mega Houndoom outspeed common threats like Cobalion, Latias, and Gengar. Houndoominite is necessary for Houndoom to Mega Evolve. Flash Fire is the preferred ability prior to Mega Evolution, as it makes it possible for Houndoom to take advantage of Choice-locked Fire-types like Infernape and Volcanion.

Usage Tips

Bring Mega Houndoom in mid- or late-game to either throw out strong attacks or sweep. Use Nasty Plot only when it is safe to do so and when its checks have been weakened to the point where Mega Houndoom can break through. Due to its middling bulk and weakness to entry hazards, try to bring Mega Houndoom when it is safe to do so, such as through U-turn or double switches. If necessary, Mega Houndoom can revenge kill threats like Scizor and Latias. Use Taunt against special walls when expecting recovery moves, whittling them and hindering their effectiveness later on.

Team Options

Mega Houndoom fits best on bulky offense teams that appreciate its revenge killing and sweeping capabilities. Physical wallbreakers like Heracross are essential alongside Mega Houndoom, as it struggles to break through more specially inclined walls like Blissey. U-turn and Volt Switch users such as Scizor, Crobat, and Rotom-C can bring Mega Houndoom in safely, giving it more opportunities to throw out powerful attacks or set up and sweep. Grass-types like Celebi and Rotom-C punish the bulky Water-types that Mega Houndoom may struggle to break through. On the other hand, bulky Water-types such as Tentacruel, Empoleon, and Swampert can help shore up some of Mega Houndoom's weaknesses, making them solid defensive partners. Due to its weakness to Stealth Rock, Mega Houndoom pairs nicely with entry hazard removers like Latias and the aforementioned Tentacruel and Empoleon. Entry hazard setters such as Klefki and Nihilego aid Mega Houndoom in wearing Blissey down, coupled with Mega Houndoom's Taunt.

ru.overview: Houndoom's typing gives it a powerful secondary Dark-type STAB move that much of the tier struggles against, lets it counter Pokemon like Ninetales, Necrozma, and Sigilyph in conjunction with its ability, helps it act as an offensive check to a plethora of Psychic-, Ghost-, and Fire-types, and gives it a good matchup against priority users like Toxicroak and Abomasnow. Houndoom has a great Speed tier, outpacing threats like Roserade, Toxicroak, and Gardevoir. A decent support movepool gives Houndoom options like Taunt that let it completely obliterate stall, shutting down staples such as Pyukumuku and Cresselia. However, Houndoom's bulk, particularly physically, leaves much to be desired and limits its setup opportunities. A glaring weakness to every entry hazard in the game, especially Stealth Rock, further limits its ability to set up and makes it difficult to check Ghost-, Psychic-, and Fire-types. Dark Pulse's low Base Power leaves Houndoom very reliant on its Z-Move against Water-types such as Milotic, meaning it'll be helpless against them if another Pokemon can successfully lure its Z-Move. Other Fire-types such as Salazzle and Ninetales are usually more consistent picks due to their amazing Speed and much better damage output, respectively.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Substitute lets Houndoom threaten slower teams that rely on their Choice Scarf user to force out setup sweepers.

Checks and Counters

Rock-types: Faster Rock-types such as Lycanroc-D, Gigalith, and Tyrantrum beat Houndoom with their super effective STAB attacks. Gigalith can even stomach a boosted Black Hole Eclipse, so it does not need to worry when switching in.

Choice Scarf Users and Faster Pokemon: Choice Scarf users like Passimian as well as faster threats like Virizion force out Houndoom with their super effective STAB attacks.

Water-types: Water-types threaten Houndoom, especially after it has used its Z-Move, and others like specially defensive Milotic outright beat it.

Specially Defensive Walls: Defensive threats like specially defensive Milotic, Diancie, Goodra, and Snorlax can take hits from Houndoom and KO it in return. Although some walls can be threatened by Houndoom's Z-Move, after it has been used, they have no trouble walling it.

Nasty Plot.description:
Moves

Nasty Plot lets Houndoom boost its Special Attack to scary levels. Dark Pulse is Houndoom's strongest, most reliable STAB attack that can be boosted by Darkinium Z for a one-time nuke. Fire Blast is Houndoom's secondary STAB attack that hits harder at the cost of accuracy. Taunt lets Houndoom get around Pokemon like Toxic Mandibuzz and lets it decimate stall staples like Pyukumuku. It is also fantastic for stopping Pokemon like Porygon2 from healing.

Set Details

Maximum Speed EVs along with a Timid nature let Houndoom outpace Pokemon like Roserade. Darkinium Z lets Houndoom break through defensive counterplay like Milotic after boosting. Flash Fire gives Houndoom some defensive utility, letting it hard counter Ninetales.

Usage Tips

Understand that many Fire-, Psychic-, and Ghost-types are free setup for Houndoom, so use this to your advantage by positioning Houndoom against Pokemon like Ninetales and Sigilyph. Keep in mind that using unboosted Dark Pulse and sometimes Fire Blast is a great middle-ground play that can discourage offensive early-game plays like hard switching to revenge killers, notably Tyrantrum and Virizion. Chip down defensive threats such as specially defensive Milotic and clear entry hazards from your side of the field so as to give Houndoom an easier time at breaking the opposing team. If given the opportunity, eliminate revenge killers that threaten Houndoom. Use Taunt against stall to prevent Pokemon like Toxic Pyukumuku and Toxic Cresselia from crippling Houndoom. Similarly, prevent walls like Porygon2 and Mantine from healing by using Taunt on them.

Team Options

Slow pivots like U-turn Noivern, Volt Switch Raikou or Mega Ampharos can bring Houndoom in freely, giving it more setup opportunities. Roserade provides Spikes, which is fantastic for softening walls, and can take on a few specific checks to Houndoom, notably Mega Blastoise and specially defensive Milotic. If using Houndoom on a balance team, make sure to pack answers to common Pokemon that force it out. For example, Registeel can take on opposing Choice Scarf Tyrantrum and provide Stealth Rock, and Mandibuzz can answer Zygarde-10% and Virizion. Pair Houndoom with entry hazard removers like Mega Blastoise so that when it comes in to set up it won't drop to a weak attack. Be wary of stacking heavy weakness when teambuilding with Houndoom. For example, it's very easy to stack a Ground weakness when using a core like Houndoom + Toxicroak, so make sure to patch up the team later on with a sturdy answer to Ground-types, notably physically defensive Mandibuzz or Tsareena.

Choice Scarf.description:
Moves

Hidden Power Ice is able to OHKO Zygarde-10% and Noivern, the latter after Stealth Rock damage, which can otherwise take a hit and KO Houndoom one-on-one. Destiny Bond allows Houndoom to take out foes that could otherwise soak up its attacks like Goodra and Snorlax, but keep in mind that it can't be used in rapid succession. Overheat serves as a powerful STAB move that achieves KOs against Pokemon that Fire Blast misses out on such as Virizion and Raikou while boasting generally higher power and slightly better accuracy. However, note that the Special Attack drop upon use makes it difficult to spam repeatedly. Toxic cripples defensive switch-ins like Milotic and Mantine, putting them on a timer. Hidden Power Grass is a viable alternative to Hidden Power Ice that takes out Rhyperior and Seismitoad at the expense of missing out on Hidden Power Ice targets like Zygarde-10% and Noivern.

Set Details

12 Defense EVs allow Houndoom to always survive Choice Band Zygarde-10%'s Extreme Speed after Stealth Rock damage. The remaining EVs are tailored to maximizing both Houndoom's damage output and Speed, and a Timid nature ensures that it outpaces Pokemon like Choice Scarf Toxicroak and +1 Adamant Flygon. A Modest nature is a viable option with its ability to more reliably 2HKO Arcanine and OHKO Mismagius, but it leaves Houndoom unable to outspeed the Pokemon previously mentioned. Flash Fire grants Houndoom an immunity to Fire-type attacks, allowing it to better take on Pokemon like Ninetales.

Usage Tips

Choice Scarf Houndoom operates as a revenge killer as well as a late-game cleaner once checks such as Milotic and Florges are disposed of. Utilizing its Speed tier and decently powerful attacks, Houndoom can revenge kill generally fast Pokemon such as Mega Sceptile and Choice Scarf Tyrantrum. Choosing to not reveal Houndoom's item also allows it to surprise and take out foes like Virizion and Zygarde-10% one-on-one, which could otherwise outspeed and OHKO it. Houndoom can make use of Flash Fire to pivot into Pokemon like Ninetales and Choice-locked Salazzle, which pose no threat to Houndoom and give it a chance to freely fire off a move. While it can switch into weaker attacks like Mega Abomasnow's Ice Shard, Houndoom generally wants to be brought in through slow pivots, as its poor bulk limits its chances of directly switching into most Pokemon. Finally, while Houndoom's fourth moveslot options are effective for dealing with its checks or breaking past certain Pokemon, it is ill-advised to use these moves recklessly, as being Choice-locked into any one of these moves can be highly exploitable by setup sweepers and wallbreakers alike.

Team Options

Powerful wallbreakers such as Choice Band Zygarde-10%, Mega Ampharos, and Machamp help break down Pokemon that Houndoom struggles against like Diancie, Mandibuzz, and Porygon2 while also being generally strong Pokemon that can weaken teams to aid Houndoom in cleaning late-game. The likes of Zygarde-10% and Raikou also appreciate Houndoom's ability to break past Grass- and Ice-types like Shaymin and Sneasel. Entry hazard setters such as Metagross and Rhyperior can chip down the opposing team, giving Houndoom more leeway when attempting to revenge kill or clean. Metagross also possesses the firepower to dismantle many of Houndoom's checks, including Florges, Gigalith, and Mantine if running Thunder Punch, while providing both momentum and wallbreaking potential with Explosion. Entry hazard removal from Pokemon like Mega Blastoise, Tsareena, and Florges allows Houndoom to enter play more often, and Tsareena can provide additional pivoting capabilities through U-turn. Choice Scarf Houndoom fails to outspeed particularly fast Pokemon like Choice Scarf Flygon and +1 Shaymin, so Pokemon like Tangela and Goodra can be switched in to sponge attacks that would otherwise power through it.

ru.overview: Kingdra's niche in RU is carved by its ability to break past Pokemon such as Cresselia and Umbreon thanks to Sniper, Focus Energy, and Scope Lens. A reasonable Speed stat allows Kingdra to outpace metagame staples such as Nidoqueen, Mega Blastoise, and Necrozma, and it can take advantage of its typing to use Pokemon like Milotic and Bronzong as setup fodder. However, Kingdra's mediocre bulk can make it difficult to set up both Focus Energy and Substitute or Agility, especially if the opponent plays wisely enough to pressure it throughout the game.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Choice Specs Swift Swim Kingdra can be used on rain teams, but weather generally isn’t a good playstyle in RU. A cleaner set that utilizes a set of Draco Meteor / Hydro Pump / Rain Dance / Ice Beam and Life Orb / Dragonium Z can be used as well. However, Kingdra's power is very underwhelming, so it's usually better off running Focus Energy and Agility to retain a good match up against offensive teams while still having some use against bulky teams.

Checks and Counters

Offensive Pressure: Choice Scarf users such as Shaymin, Roserade, and Gardevoir can revenge kill Kingdra. Other Pokemon like Noivern, Swellow, and Yanmega outpace and revenge kill Kingdra thanks to having moves that bypass Substitute such as Boomburst and Bug Buzz.

Specially Defensive Pokemon: Speically defensive Pokemon like Florges, Snorlax, and Cresselia can stomach a hit from Kingdra and retaliate with their own attacks.

CritDra.description:
Moves

Focus Energy allows Kingdra to boost its critical hit rate. Draco Meteor is Kingdra's strongest STAB attack and synergizes well with Focus Energy and Scope Lens because critical hits ignore Draco Meteor's Special Attack drops. Hydro Pump lets Kingdra hit Fairy- and Steel-types that would otherwise wall it like Gardevoir and Registeel and OHKO Pokemon that can survive a Draco Meteor like Rhyperior. Surf is an alternative option that is more accurate than Hydro Pump but does not OHKO Pokemon like Gardevoir. Substitute lets Kingdra threaten defensive teams that might try to beat it with more passive means such as Toxic. Running Agility over Substitute allows Kingdra to improve its matchup against offensive teams, and is particularly useful if Kingdra is being run on double screens teams.

Set Details

Scope Lens used in conjunction with Focus Energy allows Kingdra to achieve a critical hit every time it attacks. Sniper greatly increases the power of Kingdra's critical hits. A Timid nature and 252 EVs invested in Speed let Kingdra outpace Pokemon such as Mega Blastoise and Necrozma. 252 EVs invested in Special Attack maximize Kingdra's wallbreaking potential.

Usage Tips

Use Substitute on predicted status moves from Pokemon like Milotic in order to gain setup opportunities. Play sensibly against Choice-locked Pokemon that could potentially give you free setup opportunities. For example, if a Choice Scarf Salazzle is locked into Fire Blast, Kingdra can force a switch or easily take the 4x resisted attack and set up Focus Energy or a Substitute. When utilizing Substitute, play wisely to get Kingdra positioned against Pokemon it can freely set up a Substitute against, such as Milotic and Araquanid. Many Choice Scarf users like Roserade threaten Kingdra’s attempts to sweep, so make sure to scout for potential Choice Scarf users and handle all of them before attempting a sweep.

Team Options

Pokemon like Salazzle, Nidoqueen, and Metagross deal with Fairy-types that Kingdra can't get around like Florges, making them great teammates. Likewise, Dragon-types like Flygon and Zygarde-10% prevent Kingdra from setting up, so Pokemon such as Mega Glalie are also good teammates. Entry hazard setters like Roserade, Nidoqueen, Steelix, Mega Glalie, and Rhyperior are great teammates; the chip damage that hazards provide helps Kingdra KO Pokemon like Umbreon and Florges. Pokemon like Nidoqueen, Vanilluxe, and Salazzle, which struggle with special walls like Cresselia, work great in tandem with Kingdra, as they can help each other wear down their checks and counters. Checks to Yanmega and Swellow such as Snorlax and Registeel are important teammates for Kingdra, since both can bypass Kingdra's Substitute using Bug Buzz or Boomburst. If running Substitute, Kingdra can improve its matchup against offensive teams by partnering with a Sticky Web user like Galvantula or Ribombee.

ou.overview: Kingdra's decent Speed stat in combination with Swift Swim allows it to outspeed the entire unboosted metagame, as well as most Choice Scarf users, when in the rain. This combined with a decent Special Attack stat makes it a top Swift Swim user in the metagame. Kingdra's access to a powerful secondary STAB move in Draco Meteor is a blessing, giving it the means to pressure or KO Pokemon that annoy rain teams such as Mega Venusaur and Mega Latias. Kingdra's Dragon / Water typing is also useful for checking Ash-Greninja as it is a rain attacker that isn't prone to Water Shuriken. Unfortunately, bulky Water- and Grass-types such as Toxapex, Ferrothorn, and Assault Vest Tangrowth are some of the most common defensive Pokemon in OU, meaning that Kingdra will have trouble sweeping most teams. Kingdra is also heavily dependent on rain in order to be effective, as it is relatively weak and slow for an offensive Pokemon outside of it.
ou.comments:
Other Options

Toxic can be used to cripple common switch-ins to Kingdra such as Tangrowth, Mantine, Gastrodon, and Alomomola. Kingdra can opt to run Hidden Power Electric to hit Mantine.

Checks and Counters

Bulky Grass-types: Ferrothorn, Amoonguss, and Assault Vest Tangrowth all resist Kingdra's main STAB move, avoiding the 2HKO from rain-boosted Hydro Pump. However, Ferrothorn lacks reliable recovery, and Amoonguss and Tangrowth must be wary of switching in to Ice Beam.

Bulky Water-types: Toxapex, Mantine, Tapu Fini, and Gastrodon are tough Pokemon for Kingdra to take down. Toxapex, Gastrodon, and Mantine boast good special bulk and reliable recovery, while Tapu Fini resists Water and is immune to Kingdra's Draco Meteor.

Chansey: Chansey's incredible special bulk in combination with reliable recovery allows it to consistently deal with Kingdra, easily avoiding the 2HKO from even rain-boosted Hydro Pump.

Revenge Killers: Priority users such as Mega Mawile and Mega Pinsir can all pick off Kingdra if it has been weakened a bit. Choice Scarf Tapu Koko and Greninja are so fast that they can outspeed Kingdra even under the rain. Mega Alakazam can trace Kingdra's Swift Swim ability to outspeed it and deal heavy damage with Psychic or Dazzling Gleam.

Alternative Weather Setters: Pokemon such as Tyranitar, Mega Charizard Y, and Alolan Ninetales are able to hamper Kingdra by changing the weather condition. Tyranitar will summon sand, boosting its Special Defense and allowing it to tank Hydro Pump. Mega Charizard Y will summon sun, forcing Kingdra out. Lastly, Alolan-Ninetales will summon hail, which will allow it to outspeed Kingdra, threatening to OHKO it with Freeze-Dry.

Choice Specs.description:
Moves

Hydro Pump is Kingdra's main STAB move of choice. Boosted by rain and boasting high power, Hydro Pump is a powerful move that will 2HKO, if not OHKO, most of the metagame, bar Chansey and specially defensive resists. Surf is slightly weaker, trading that power for 100% accuracy, making it a reliable option when trying to clean late-game. Draco Meteor is a powerful secondary STAB move that can deal heavy damage to common Water-resistant Pokemon such as Toxapex and Mega Venusaur. Ice Beam is used to nail Grass-types such as Tapu Bulu and Tangrowth. Hidden Power Grass may also be used to remove Gastrodon, but has little use otherwise.

Set Details

Swift Swim is what enables Kingdra to be a threatening sweeper, doubling its Speed when in the rain. Maximum Special Attack investment combined with a Modest nature and Choice Specs enables Kingdra to hit as hard as possible, while maximum Speed investment allows Kingdra to outspeed everything up to and including base 110 Choice Scarf users such as Gengar and Latios when factoring in Swift Swim.

Usage Tips

One of the biggest things to keep in mind when using Kingdra is that one cannot afford to play passively. Taking full advantage of the 8 turns of rain provided by Pelipper is one of the first things that one should aim to do. Once the rain is set, aim to bring Kingdra onto the field as quickly as possible and start firing off attacks. Kingdra's decent defensive typing and serviceable bulk can help in instances such as switching into Pokemon such as Heatran or Greninja. It is also worth noting that if the opponent has a full on counter measure, such as Toxapex, Chansey, or Gastrodon, it is a smart idea to double switch out of Kingdra into another Pokemon that can pressure it.

Team Options

Pelipper is the obvious first choice and a mandatory partner when you consider that Kingdra requires rain support in order to take advantage of its Swift Swim ability. Pelipper also happens to provide momentum via U-turn, which can be useful to bring Kingdra in safely. Pelipper can even utilize its Choice Specs set to pressure Kingdra's counters such as Toxapex, Ferrothorn, and even Knock Off Chansey's Eviolite. Tapu Koko is a good partner for its ability to pressure Toxapex, wearing down defensive Grass-types such as Ferrothorn and Mega Venusaur, and boost Kingdra's Hidden Power Electric. Defensively, Ferrothorn is a great teammate because of how its Fire-type weakness is reduced under rain, and it can support Kingdra with moves such as Stealth Rock, Spikes, and Knock Off. Mega Scizor is an option too because it can provide momentum with U-turn and Defog away Toxic Spikes for Kingdra and its teammates. Lastly, Tapu Lele can be a nice partner with its Psychic Surge ability, preventing Pokemon from revenge killing Kingdra with priority moves. Tapu Lele takes advantage of many Pokemon Kingdra loses to such as Toxapex and Amoonguss and it can utilize items such as Fightinium Z to lure in Ferrothorn.

monotype.overview:
Water

Kingdra's access to Swift Swim and a strong STAB move in Hydro Pump makes it one of the best wallbreakers and sweepers under rain, heavily denting most Pokemon in combination with its STAB Draco Meteor. Although this STAB combination is resisted by many Pokemon, Kingdra's access to Ice Beam helps out in letting it hit threats like Tapu Bulu and Cradily. Kingdra has pretty decent bulk and a neutrality to Electric- and Grass-type attacks, which helps given the fact that it needs to continuously switch in throughout a match. While Kingdra can outspeed the entire unboosted metagame in rain, its Speed is underwhelming outside of it. Additionally, without rain boosting its Water-type STAB moves, Kingdra's Special Attack is unimpressive. Therefore, it requires specific team support that limits Kingdra to rain teams.
monotype.comments:
Other Options

Water

Kingdra doesn't have any viable options outside of the main set.

Checks and Counters

Water

Chansey: Chansey completely walls Kingdra and can KO it with Seismic Toss or cripple it with status.

Walls: Specially defensive Pokemon like Cradily, Ferrothorn, and Assault Vest Araquanid can switch into Kingdra and whittle it down or take it out with Toxic, Leech Seed, and Mirror Coat, respectively. Mega Venusaur is notable for being able to switch into Hydro Pump and Ice Beam, thanks to Thick Fat, and beat Kingdra one-on-one. It can't switch into Draco Meteor or Hydro Pump in rain after Stealth Rock damage, however.

Defensive Water-types: Most defensive Water-types, such as Toxapex and Mantine, resist Hydro Pump and can comfortably switch into Draco Meteor. Certain Water-types that are immune to or resist Dragon, like Tapu Fini and Empoleon, are great switch-ins as well.

Residual Damage: Since Kingdra needs to come into play often, letting it accumulate too much chip damage can lead to it being picked off through priority moves.

Trace: Trace users like Mega Alakazam and Gardevoir can copy Swift Swim, outspeed Kingdra, and KO it easily.

Paralysis: Paralysis halves Kingdra's Speed, which means it can no longer sweep.

Alolan Raichu: Under Electric Terrain, Alolan Raichu can easily outspeed Kingdra and KO it with a boosted Thunderbolt.

Rain Sweeper (Water).description:
Moves

Hydro Pump is an insanely strong STAB move under rain that lets Kingdra 2HKO most Pokemon, including those that resist it, such as Rotom-W, Latios, and Slowbro. Draco Meteor lets Kingdra muscle past Pokemon that don't take much from Hydro Pump, such as Mega Venusaur and Lanturn. Ice Beam gives Kingdra a reliable tool against Dragon teams, notably hitting Mega Altaria, while also letting it hit certain Grass-type threats, like Tapu Bulu and Cradily, hard. While Hydro Pump is used to wallbreak, Surf lets Kingdra clean up weakened teams reliably thanks to its higher accuracy and PP. Alternatively, Scald can be used to try to cripple common switch-ins, like Ferrothorn, at the cost of a little power.

Set Details

Maximum investment is made in Speed, which, alongside Swift Swim, lets Kingdra outspeed the entire unboosted metagame under rain. 252 EVs are put into Special Attack with a Modest nature to let Kingdra hit as hard as possible. Choice Specs patches up Kingdra's average Special Attack and lets it wallbreak more easily under rain. 4 EVs are placed in Special Defense to prevent Download users, like Porygon2 and Porygon-Z, from getting a Special Attack boost.

Usage Tips

Kingdra should primarily be used in rain. Bring it in as often as possible early-game to wallbreak with a strong rain- and Choice Specs-boosted Hydro Pump. Under rain, Hydro Pump is strong enough to 2HKO even targets that resist it and normally don't take much damage, like Mega Venusaur after Stealth Rock damage. Therefore, try to keep the rain turns in mind to make the most use out of them. Kingdra can often be used to take out its own checks early-game and clean up with Surf or Scald later on. That being said, don't let it take too much chip damage from status or entry hazards, since it needs to switch in regularly. Therefore, try to bring it into play through Pelipper's slow U-turn or Politoed's Eject Button. Definitely keep Kingdra away from paralysis, as it prevents it from doing either of its jobs: sweeping and wallbreaking. While a paralyzed Kingdra can outspeed certain slower walls in the rain, it can't wallbreak efficiently between Hydro Pump's shaky accuracy and the chance to be fully paralyzed. For the most part, Kingdra shouldn't be used outside of rain, since its Special Attack and Speed are nothing to write home about. However, Choice Specs-boosted Draco Meteor is still pretty strong and can still be used to wallbreak without rain. Should Draco Meteor be used in rain, be wary that using it forces Kingdra to switch out and waste rain turns due to the Special Attack drop.

Team Options

Since Kingdra absolutely requires rain support, rain setters like Pelipper and Politoed are great partners. Pelipper is notable for being able to check Grass-types like Mega Venusaur. Both of these Pokemon can also bring Kingdra into play safely through U-turn and Eject Button, respectively. Wallbreakers like Tail Glow Manaphy, Azumarill, Supersonic Skystrike Gyarados, and Keldeo can take care of checks to Kingdra, like Chansey, letting Kingdra clean up easily. Greninja's access to Protean and a fantastic movepool lets it customize its moveset to beat checks to Kingdra. For example, Greninja can take care of Mega Venusaur with Extrasensory and Mantine with Hidden Power Electric. Cleaners like Mega Sharpedo, Mega Swampert, and Kabutops appreciate Kingdra's wallbreaking abilities. Swampert and Seismitoad provide Electric immunities and can also set Stealth Rock, which makes wallbreaking easier. Toxapex can wear down the opposing team with Toxic Spikes while also acting as a reliable pivot into priority moves for Kingdra. Lanturn's ability Volt Absorb lets it act as a fantastic check to Alolan Raichu. Lanturn can also cure any status condition with Heal Bell and bring Kingdra in safely through Volt Switch.

vgc2018.overview:
• Kingdra is one of the best rain sweepers available thanks to its good offensive typing and access to spread Muddy Water, both of which also help to distinguish itself from Ludicolo.

  • Kingdra's solid Water / Dragon typing also leaves it with few weaknesses, though its mediocre bulk makes it vulnerable to strong neutral hits.

  • Ordinarily uncommon support options, such as Disable and Quash, give Kingdra the flexibility to support its team when necessary.

  • Kingdra's STAB moves are resisted by common threats, most notably Tapu Fini and Ferrothorn.

  • Kingdra is highly reliant on rain due to its middling Speed and lackluster damage output outside of rain, which causes a loss of momentum if the opponent activates other weather or gains a Speed advantage from Tailwind or Trick Room.

Rain Sweeper.description:
• Muddy Water is a powerful STAB spread move under rain that also has a decent chance to lower the accuracy of its targets. Generally, this move will be spammed until a foe is put into KO range of another move.

  • Draco Meteor serves as a secondary STAB move to hit Water-resistant foes and beat Dragon-types, such as opposing Kingdra and Mega Salamence.

  • Ice Beam can be used to KO Dragon- and Grass-types without worrying about Misty Terrain or the Special Attack drop from Draco Meteor, although running this leaves Kingdra walled by bulky Water-types.

  • Hydro Pump is valuable as a strong single-target STAB attack, finishing off targets that Muddy Water can't KO and letting Kingdra bypass Wide Guard Celesteela and Aegislash, which otherwise wall it.

  • Rain Dance allows Kingdra to set up independently, improving momentum by making it unnecessary to switch your weather setter in and out to maintain field presence.

  • Protect can be used to shield Kingdra while its partner removes a threat, punishes double targets, and scouts a foe’s actions.

  • The given EV spread and nature allow Kingdra to hit as hard and as fast as possible, with the four Special Defense EVs ensuring Download users like Porygon2 don't receive a Special Attack boost.

  • Waterium Z enables the use of Hydro Vortex, which is notable in providing a perfectly accurate Water-type move as much as in providing a strong one. Alternatively, Life Orb gives Kingdra a more consistent damage boost.

  • If your opponent doesn't have weather setters, such as Tyranitar and Mega Charizard Y, Kingdra makes a perfect lead to punch holes early in the opposing team. If they have a setter, consider removing it before sending out Kingdra.

  • Partners with the Drizzle ability are required to activate Swift Swim. Pelipper grants Tailwind and the ability to hit Grass-types, while Politoed offers Helping Hand support and more bulk.

  • Since Kingdra relies heavily on its Speed advantage, running Taunt on at least one teammate to stop Tailwind and Trick Room is recommended.

  • Running Pokemon with strong Fire- and Electric-type moves, such as Incineroar and Tapu Koko, respectively, is encouraged to avoid Ferrothorn and Celesteela late-game, as they largely wall Kingdra's attacks.

  • Mega Gengar is a good teammate, as it's able to use Shadow Tag to trap and remove Grass-types, bulky Water-types, and opposing weather setters, making it easier for Kingdra to sweep.

doublesou.overview: Kingdra is a powerful rain sweeper that applies immediate offensive pressure to its foes. It outspeeds the entire unboosted metagame when Swift Swim is activated, and its Water-type attacks hit most targets for heavy damage when boosted by rain. Draco Meteor generally allows Kingdra to nuke targets that resist its Water coverage, although strong Fairy-types like Tapu Fini and Tapu Bulu wall Kingdra completely. One of Kingdra's main drawbacks is the middling accuracy of its STAB attacks Muddy Water, Hydro Pump, and Draco Meteor, which are all prone to missing at inopportune moments. It should also be noted that, outside of its STAB moves, Kingdra's offensive coverage is quite underwhelming due to its middling Special Attack stat. Defensively, Kingdra's Water / Dragon typing leaves it with few weaknesses overall but with a crippling weakness to strong Fairy-types, which are omnipresent in the metagame. Finally, it should be noted that Kingdra relies on its high Speed to maintain a commanding position, and it quickly loses its momentum if the opponent activates an opposing weather or a form of speed control like Tailwind or Trick Room.
doublesou.comments:
Other Options

With Choice Specs, Kingdra deals a significant damage to even bulky or resistant targets; for example, it OHKOes 4 HP / 252 SpD Kartana with Hydro Pump in rain. Rain Dance is an option that allows Kingdra to maintain its rain advantage, especially against opponents planning to switch in an opposing weather setter.

Checks and Counters

Fairy-types: Bulky Fairy-types like Tapu Fini completely wall Kingdra's STAB coverage and threaten back with STAB-boosted Moonblasts or Grassy Terrain-boosted Wood Hammers. Tapu Lele and Tapu Koko also threaten Kingdra with strong Fairy- and Electric-type attacks, respectively, but inside of rain, Kingdra can threaten to outspeed and KO them first with strong Water-type attacks.

Grass-types: Bulky Grass-types such as Tapu Bulu and Amoonguss are capable of absorbing Kingdra's STAB coverage and hitting back either with strong Grass-type moves or with status moves such as Spore.

Water-types: Bulky Water-types such as Volcanion, Milotic, and Araquanid have enough bulk and the right typing to absorb Kingdra's STAB attacks. Tapu Fini can then hit back with a STAB-boosted Moonblast, while Milotic can simply use Recover to negate the damage. Milotic also gains a sharp Special Attack boost if its accuracy is lowered by Muddy Water. Araquanid can block Kingdra's Muddy Water with Wide Guard for as long as it stays on the field.

Opposing Weather: Kingdra quickly becomes dead weight outside of rain, since it relies on its Swift Swim Speed boost to maintain its offensive pressure. Therefore, opposing weather setters like Mega Charizard Y and Tyranitar can be problematic for Kingdra.

Tailwind and Trick Room: Tailwind and Trick Room either negate or reverse Kingdra's Swift Swim Speed boost. Prominent Trick Room setters such as Porygon2 and Bronzong are also generally bulky enough to survive one attack from Kingdra, although a well-timed Hydro Vortex inside of rain is generally able to OHKO them before they set Trick Room. A Zapdos carrying Misty Seed or Psychic Seed is a particularly thorny Tailwind setter for Kingdra to deal with, as it has enough bulk to withstand all of Kingdra's attacks outside of Hydro Vortex. However, Zapdos almost never carries Protect, so Kingdra is pretty safe to use up its Hydro Vortex on an opposing Zapdos.

Rain Attacker.description:
Moves

Muddy Water is a powerful spread STAB move that also has a 30% chance to drop the accuracy of each target it hits. Hydro Pump is a single-target STAB attack that can snipe out targets that are just outside of Muddy Water's KO range. It also bypasses Wide Guard Araquanid to hit its ally. Draco Meteor hits hard against most targets that resist Water-type attacks and destroys opposing Dragon-types like Kommo-o, Mega Salamence, Zygarde. Beware of Misty Terrain, though, as it halves the power of Draco Meteor against grounded targets. Ice Beam is another option that lets Kingdra snipe out opposing Dragon-types without dropping its Special Attack stat or worrying about Misty Terrain. However, running this leaves Kingdra helpless against bulky Water-types like Milotic, Suicune, and Araquanid. Protect keeps Kingdra safe while its partners deal with any possible threats.

Set Details

Kingdra's spread isn't complicated. Maximum investments in Special Attack and Speed let it hit as hard and fast as possible under rain. A Modest nature is preferred for maximum power, since the extra Speed granted by a Timid nature isn't generally useful. It is worth noting, however, that a Timid nature on Kingdra is required to outspeed Dragon Dance-boosted Mega Salamence in the rain. Waterium Z grants Kingdra one opportunity to turn Hydro Pump into Hydro Vortex, a move that bypasses Kingdra's otherwise shoddy accuracy and hits all but the bulkiest of targets for heavy damage. Life Orb is an alternative item that can be used for more consistent damage output. Swift Swim doubles Kingdra's Speed when rain is activated.

Usage Tips

If the opponent isn't carrying an opposing weather setter, Kingdra and its respective rain setter make for excellent leads that apply immediate offensive pressure, but if they are, consider playing Kingdra more conservatively, opting to take out the opponent's weather setter first if possible. Kingdra quickly becomes dead weight once Swift Swim deactivates, so it is best saved for a point in the match where rain can't be disrupted. If you're able to clear out Kingdra's checks and counters beforehand, it also makes for an excellent late-game cleaner, outspeeding and picking off weakened foes with strong spread damage. When in play, Kingdra's main goal is to spam Muddy Water and consistently chip away at the opponent's team. Hydro Pump can also be used to snipe down targets that are just outside of Muddy Water's KO range. Use Draco Meteor with caution, as Kingdra quickly loses momentum once its Special Attack drops to -2. Also keep in mind that Misty Terrain halves Draco Meteor's power against grounded targets like Zygarde. If using Waterium Z, be mindful that Hydro Vortex is a one-time nuke; avoid using it on a turn where the opponent is likely to Protect or switch into a Water-resistant Pokemon. Finally, Kingdra's bulk is average at best, and Life Orb sets in particular are prone to getting worn down quickly, so avoid pivoting Kingdra in on opposing attacks if you can.

Team Options

Kingdra is a dedicated rain attacker, so it goes without saying that running either Politoed or Pelipper as a rain setter is mandatory. Politoed offers higher overall bulk and has access to Helping Hand, which further amplifies Kingdra's attacks. Pelipper has access to Tailwind, a second form of speed control that reduces Kingdra's dependency on Swift Swim being activated. On hyper offensive teams, Kingdra pairs notably well with Tapu Lele and Psychic Terrain attackers such as Deoxys-A and Mega Metagross. Psychic Terrain blocking priority attacks reinforces Kingdra's commanding Speed tier inside of rain. Deoxys-A and Mega Metagross apply immense offensive pressure to targets that resist Kingdra's STAB moves, such as Tapu Fini and Milotic. Likewise, these Psychic-types appreciate Kingdra's ability to clear out bulky Steel-types such as Heatran and Aegislash. On more balance-oriented teams, bulky Steel-types such as Ferrothorn and Aegislash make for excellent partners, as they can pivot in on the strong Fairy- and Dragon-type attacks that Kingdra hates. Tapu Koko and Thunder Punch Mega Metagross are great options for beating Tapu Fini and Araquanid, which are prominent checks to rain teams. Kingdra relies on Swift Swim to maintain a commanding position, so partners that can deal with opposing weather setters and speed control techniques are always a good idea. Running Taunt on at least one partner helps to shut down opposing Tailwind and Trick Room users. Opposing speed control can also be countered with your own, so consider running Tailwind users like Zapdos and Pelipper or Icy Wind users such as Politoed.

Waterium Z.description: Kingdra is a dangerous cleaner under the rain thanks to Swift Swim making it extremely fast. Hydro Pump-based Hydro Vortex will deal massive damage to any Pokemon that doesn't resist it, making it a great way to break through weakened walls. However, Kingdra will have big problems if Mega Charizard Y sets up Drought, making it rather useless if Pelipper or Politoed has been KOed. Other weather changers such as Hippowdon, Tyranitar, and the rare Alolan Ninetales are also very problematic.

Choice Specs.description: This Kingdra focuses on more consistent power at the cost of switching moves. Since Choice Specs is a restrictive item, it's best to leave this Kingdra for late-game sweeps while the rain is up.

lc.overview: Despite its access to useful moves such as Knock Off and Ice Shard, Phanpy is unviable in the Little Cup metagame because it is directly outclassed by Mudbray, due to its better overall stats and ability in Stamina. Phanpy is weak and slow, and its Special Defense is horrible, which is something Abra, Snivy, and Omanyte can exploit.

Utility.description: Phanpy provides utility through Stealth Rock, which is useful against the likes of Ponyta and Doduo, and Knock Off, which is useful because most Pokemon in Little Cup hold Eviolite. Despite Phanpy's access to Ice Shard as a form of priority, it is horrifically weak. Mudbray outclasses Phanpy as a Ground-type Stealth Rock setter due to its better stats and ability, and Sandshrew is a Ground-type Knock Off user that outclasses Phanpy thanks to its better bulk and access to Rapid Spin.

ru.overview: With its solid typing and great Attack and Defense, Donphan is a reliable tank in RarelyUsed that can check top threats in the tier such as Zygarde-10%, Noivern, and Tyrantrum. Donphan is also unique in that it has access to Rapid Spin to clear away entry hazards and Ice Shard as a priority move to pick off weakened threats such as Zygarde-10%, Roserade, and Noivern. Despite these solid traits, Donphan's biggest issue is that it is easy to wear down with weak attacks and status conditions thanks to a lack of reliable recovery. This is especially bad considering Donphan has to repeatedly switch into Pokemon it is supposed to check and entry hazards to clear them away, breaking its Sturdy ability every time. Donphan may have a high Attack, but it has issues breaking common defensive Pokemon such as Slowbro, Mandibuzz, and Mantine. Donphan's low Speed and Special Defense are easily exploited by Pokemon that can hit it with super effective attacks such as Mega Blastoise, Roserade, and Milotic. While Donphan's typing and bulk allows it to check Rock-, Ground-, and Steel-types, it still receives tough competition from other entry hazard removers such as Mega Blastoise, Mandibuzz, and Mantine thanks to either stronger offensive presences with Mega Blastoise or better resistances and recovery with Mandibuzz and Mantine. It also has competition as an offensive Ground-type from the likes of Zygarde-10% and Rhyperior. Zygarde-10% is much faster and has a better STAB move with Thousand Arrows, while Rhyperior has a higher Attack and better typing both offensively and defensively.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Toxic can be used so Donphan has a better match up against physically defensive Pokemon such as Milotic without Refresh and Mandibuzz. Choice Band is a decent option that gives Donphan more immediate power. Donphan also has interesting coverage options such as Gunk Shot and Seed Bomb to hit targets that other Ground-types cannot. However, this set is largely outclassed by Rhyperior thanks to its higher Attack, better coverage options, and stronger defensive presence thanks to its Solid Rock ability taking super effective hits that Donphan cannot. Stone Edge can be used on the main set to hit Flying-type Pokemon such as Noivern, Honchkrow, and Mandibuzz for super effective damage, but the utility provided by Ice Shard and Knock Off are much more useful. A defensive set can be appealing thanks to Donphan's solid bulk. However, this set is lackluster because Donphan lacks reliable recovery and sacrifices its power.

Checks and Counters

Residual Damage: As Donphan lacks a reliable way to recover its HP, it is easily worn down by entry hazards and status conditions such as poison from Toxic. Burns from Will-O-Wisp not only chip away at Donphan's HP, but they also halve its Attack, making it lose a lot of offensive pressure against the foe. Poison from Toxic puts Donphan on a timer, and the residual damage stacks up.

Physically Defensive Pokemon: While Donphan has great raw power, it still fails to dent Pokemon with high Defense stats such as Milotic, Mandibuzz, and Tangela because all of these Pokemon can shrug off a hit from Donphan and recover their HP. Golisopod resists all of Donphan's attacks and retaliates back with Liquidation. Cloyster also survives any attack Donphan uses on it and sets up Shell Smash against it.

Special Attackers: Pokemon such as Mega Blastoise, Gardevoir, and Espeon target Donphan's much weaker Special Defense stat, forcing it out of battle.

Water- and Grass-type Pokemon: Water-type Pokemon such as Slowbro, Barbaracle, and Milotic threaten out Donphan with their powerful STAB moves. Similarly, Grass-type Pokemon such as Virizion and Shaymin resist Earthquake and also threaten to KO Donphan. However, most of the Water-type Pokemon and Roserade do not want to switch into Donphan's Earthquake, and weakened Grass-types do not want to stay in on Donphan's Ice Shard or even the rare Gunk Shot.

Offensive Spinner.description:
Moves

Rapid Spin is the most important move in this set because it removes entry hazards such as Stealth Rock and Spikes for its team. Earthquake is Donphan's most powerful STAB move that deals with Pokemon such as Metagross, Arcanine, and Tyrantrum. Knock Off further supports Donphan's team by crippling Pokemon reliant on their items such as Bronzong, Porygon2, and Registeel. It is also great against Ghost-type Pokemon such as Mismagius that try to switch in on Rapid Spin. Ice Shard is crucial so that Donphan can check weakened offensive threats such as Roserade, Virizion, and Noivern. The move is also a guaranteed OHKO against Zygarde-10% after Stealth Rock. Gunk Shot can be utilized to gain momentum against any Grass-type Pokemon that tries to switch into Donphan such as Shaymin and Virizion, as well as to damage Gardevoir and Florges more. Stealth Rock can be utilized if Donphan’s team lacks a dedicated user of the move.

Set Details

The listed EV set allows Donphan to be as strong and sturdy as possible. Leftovers gives Donphan a little extra health back every turn so that it has an easier time checking Pokemon such as Zygarde-10%, Tyrantrum, and Toxicroak, allowing Donphan to Rapid Spin more often by restoring its Sturdy if it comes in on Stealth Rock.

Usage Tips

Donphan is a Rapid Spinner designed to tank hits from physically attacking Pokemon such as Zygarde-10%, Tyrantrum, and Toxicroak, so it needs to be as healthy as possible throughout the match. This is especially true if the opponent still has an entry hazard setter and if Donphan has a teammate that needs hazard control. Donphan can easily come in on Stealth Rock users that do not threaten it very much, such as Metagross, Registeel, or Tank Rhyperior. It can also come into battle with a slow U-turn or Volt Switch if a teammate has fainted or from an aggressive double switch. From there, Donphan can threaten the opponent out with a powerful Earthquake or revenge kill with Ice Shard if the foe is weakened enough. If the opponent has a Ghost-type Pokemon such as Mismagius or Alolan Marowak and switches them in on Donphan expecting it to go for Rapid Spin, then it is advised to go for Knock Off, as the move does massive damage to these Pokemon, putting Mismagius within Ice Shard KO range and heavily crippling Alolan Marowak. Do not let Donphan take any status conditions, as poison from Toxic severely limits its longevity and the number of times it can switch in on Pokemon it is supposed to check. Being burned from Will-O-Wisp, meanwhile, makes Donphan lose offensive pressure.

Team Options

Donphan appreciates support from clerics such as Umbreon or Vaporeon or Healing Wish users such as Shaymin and Gardevoir, as Donphan itself lacks a reliable form of recovery. Pokemon such as Ninetales, Noivern, Salazzle, and Swellow appreciate Donphan's ability to clear entry hazards away and threaten Stealth Rock users. These Pokemon also appreciate Donphan's ability to threaten out Zygarde-10%. Teammates that can absorb Water-type attacks aimed at Donphan such as Virizion, Toxicroak, Mantine, and Seismitoad are needed. On that note, partners like Roserade, Shaymin, and Raikou can also keep Water-type Pokemon in check. Donphan also needs partners that can take Grass-type attacks such as Ninetales, Metagross, or Registeel. Metagross and Registeel also provide entry hazards for Donphan's team. Donphan, in return, can check Ground-types for Metagross and Registeel. Spikes setters such as Roserade and Golisopod love that Donphan can remove entry hazards without removing their own Spikes. Slow pivots such as Mega Ampharos, Mandibuzz, or Forretress can help bring Donphan safely into battle. Specially defensive Pokemon such as Snorlax, Florges, and Goodra can help take attacks that target Donphan's weaker Special Defense.

1v1.overview: Donphan is an excellent physical bulky offensive presence in the 1v1 metagame with powerful moves, good offensive stats, decent bulk, and an invaluable ability in Sturdy. Donphan's wide movepool with access to Ground- and Rock-type moves allows it to hit the entire tier for at least neutral damage, if not super effective. With Ice Shard, Donphan has a consistent priority move to finish off faster Pokemon. However, it faces stiff competition from other Rockium Z Sturdy users such as Crustle, Carracosta, and Golem. It also struggles with bulky offensive Pokemon such as Mega Gyarados. With no way of boosting its stats reliably, Donphan is vulnerable to setup stallers or even just naturally bulky Pokemon, such as Chansey and Porygon2.
1v1.comments:
Other Options

Groundium Z can be replaced with Rockium Z for guaranteed accuracy and a harder-hitting Rock-type move, but the power of STAB Tectonic Rage is sorely missed. On the main Groundium Z set, Head Smash and Counter can be replaced with Endeavor and Substitute to potentially lure Pokemon such as Mega Gyarados and Kommo-o. Using Endeavor immediately can be effective to bait attackers to which Donphan cannot normally retaliate. However, if they do not attack turn one, use Substitute repeatedly until Donphan is at 1 HP followed by Endeavor and Ice Shard to defeat any Pokemon that does not carry a priority move. This gives Donphan the potential to outplay Pokemon that it would normally not stand a chance against.

Checks and Counters

Pokemon that Ignore Sturdy: Mold Breaker users, such as Mega Gyarados and Magnet Rise Excadrill, can break through Donphan's Sturdy. Necrozma can also OHKO Donphan thanks to Photon Geyser ignoring opposing abilities. Pokemon with Skill Link, like Cloyster and Mega Heracross, can also aptly deal with Donphan.

Physically Bulky Pokemon: Pokemon such as Landorus-T and Zygarde are naturally bulky, so despite having a 4x weakness to Ice Shard, they are still able to defeat standard Donphan. Pokemon like Magearna and Tapu Lele can boost their defenses to defeat Donphan, however, they must be wary of lure sets.

Ground-immune Pokemon: Pokemon that can utilize Magnet Rise, such as Aegislash and Excadrill, are usually good checks to Donphan. Air Balloon users, such as Heatran, usually handle Donphan well too. However, these can be lured in and defeated using Choice Band-boosted Superpower, excluding Aegislash. Some Flying-type Pokemon, such as Celesteela, are also able to easily tank any of Donphan's attacks and defeat it.

Priority Users: Special Dragonite with Extreme Speed can safely beat Donphan. Primarina can defeat standard Donphan with Aqua Jet; however, it can be lured and taken out with Choice Band-boosted Gunk Shot.

Stall Pokemon: As Donphan is unable to raise its offenses, Pokemon such as Mega Sableye are able to set up without worry and whittle Donphan down with Will-O-Wisp, while others like Mega Venusaur and Mega Slowbro can PP stall Donphan or beat it with their STAB moves.

Water- and Grass-type Pokemon: Pokemon such as Tapu Bulu and Tapu Fini have a type advantage over Donphan, although they must watch out for Choice Band-boosted Gunk Shot.

Groundium Z.description:
Moves

Earthquake is Donphan's strongest STAB move and, when combined with Groundium Z, allows it to OHKO most hyper offensive Pokemon that do not resist it, such as Kartana and Mega Lopunny. Ice Shard allows Donphan to pick off any weakened Pokemon that Tectonic Rage fails to OHKO. Its +1 priority also allows it to gain the upper hand against some faster foes like Jumpluff and Garchomp. Head Smash lets Donphan hit Flying-types for super effective damage. It is also Donphan's most powerful attack against Pokemon that resist Earthquake; however, the recoil negates Donphan's Sturdy. Stone Edge can be used instead to preserve Donphan's Sturdy at the cost of power. Counter is used to defeat most physical Pokemon, mainly Choice item users such as Haxorus, Sawk, and Landorus-T. Bulldoze is another option to slow down foes, in particular Magearna. Rock Tomb can also be used to beat slow Mega Charizard X and Y.

Set Details
