These two are often paired with Mega Metagross on bulky offense teams due to the excellent defensive backbone this trio forms without becoming too passive. Gliscor can just as easily be used on stall teams with the likes of Chansey and Skarmory as well, though this specially defensive set is most commonly used on bulky offense teams. Bulky Normal-types such as Porygon2 and Snorlax also appreciate Gliscor's Fighting-type resistance and can also shrug off most common Water- and Ice-type moves due to their high Special Defense.

Fast Substitute.description:
Moves

Earthquake is a powerful STAB move even without investment, allowing Gliscor to chunk away at foes without relying on stalling the foe. Substitute makes Gliscor very annoying to deal with for teams that lack a proper countermeasure, since the combination of Substitute, Protect, and Poison Heal allow it to reliably stall out any foe it can hit with Toxic. Protect also generally allows Gliscor to safely stall out a turn for recovery or Toxic damage, though powerful setup sweepers can take advantage of predictable Protects. Guillotine allows Gliscor to try to instantly remove a passive foe that can't reliably break its Substitute and punish switches to an otherwise reliable check. It can also be used to try and fish for a surprise KO against a dangerous foe if Gliscor is safely behind a Substitute. Toxic is a lower-risk alternative to Guillotine that allows Gliscor to stall foes more self-sufficiently, though this comes at the cost of being walled by defensive foes that are immune to Toxic such as Mega Venusaur, Ferrothorn, and Celesteela, which makes it harder to stallbreak.

Set Details

The given EV spread with a Jolly nature makes Gliscor as fast as possible, allowing it to Substitute stall as many foes as possible while also optimizing Poison Heal recovery. The remaining EVs are placed into Special Defense to give Gliscor some extra bulk against a stray Hidden Power Ice, though these EVs can also be placed elsewhere if extra power, physical bulk, or speed is desired. Toxic Orb and Poison Heal are also necessary, as Gliscor needs these in order to effectively stall out foes.

Usage Tips

This Gliscor is often used on stall teams in order to stallbreak other annoying passive threats, such as Celesteela and Mega Venusaur. This means Gliscor will ideally be brought against other slow and passive teams in order to take advantage of its Speed to Substitute stall or fish for Guillotine hits. If a team is filled with many powerful wallbreakers or Pokemon that can bypass Substitute via multi-hit or sound moves, Gliscor is typically best left on the bench. However, Gliscor can still be effective against more offensive teams if you can bring it in against a passive foe or something that it forces out, such as Landorus-T or Hippowdon. If Gliscor can get a free turn to use Substitute, faster foes can also struggle to break Gliscor as it tries to land a Toxic or Guillotine and stall out on appropriate turns. Keep in mind that this Gliscor set is not very bulky overall, so being proactive with Protect and Substitute is important. If Gliscor can't safely heal enough damage in between Substitute turns and attempting to break through a foe, try to find an opportunity to safely switch out with enough HP in case it needs to come back in later.

Team Options

Toxapex is a primary consideration for Gliscor's teammates, since the two of them can comfortably switch into most of each other's weaknesses, though other bulky Water-types such as Tapu Fini are similarly effective for this role. Normal-types such as Snorlax, Chansey, and Porygon2 also benefit from having a teammate that can safely switch into Fighting-type attacks and are bulky enough to handle Water- and Ice-type attacks aimed at Gliscor. Steel-types such as Mega Metagross and Skarmory also handle Ice-type moves aimed at Gliscor and pair well with the aforementioned Water-type as well. This Gliscor set fits particularly well on stall teams that may be lacking in tools to break through opposing stall teams or similarly bulky teams, which may be forced to risk losing something to Guillotine if they're too passive. However, this Gliscor can still function outside of stall teams as long as it has bulky teammates to fall back on to make up for the lack of bulk on this set.

uu.overview: Mamoswine is a premier wallbreaker in UnderUsed thanks to its huge Attack stat and an excellent STAB combination, which offers nearly perfect coverage. It also has access to STAB Ice Shard, which can patch up its paltry Speed while picking off several top threats, such as Latias, Mega Altaria, and Mega Aerodactyl, when weakened. Moreover, Mamoswine can support its team with options such as Knock Off and Stealth Rock, increasing its overall utility. Unfortunately, despite hitting extremely hard, Mamoswine has a hard time actually coming into play due to its terrible defensive typing, which lacks useful resistances and gives it several common weaknesses, such as to Fighting and Water. Its poor defensive utility is further compounded by its unremarkable bulk and weakness to common priority moves like Bullet Punch and Aqua Jet, which compromises its ability to pressure slower threats in Scizor and Crawdaunt. Lastly, Mamoswine struggles with a below average Speed tier for an offensive Pokemon, which can leave it vulnerable to several of the tier's powerful faster threats, including Infernape, Cobalion, and Starmie.
uu.comments:
Other Options

Freeze-Dry is also an option in the fourth slot, luring in and 2HKOing bulky Water-types like Swampert and Alomomola. However, with adequate chip damage, both of these Pokemon can already be 2HKOed by Earthquake, while the need to run a Naughty or Naive nature further compromises Mamoswine's defensive capabilities. Mamoswine can viably function as a suicide lead, running a set with Stealth Rock, Focus Sash, Oblivious to evade Taunt, and Ice Shard + Endeavor for picking off at least one foe before fainting. However, it faces competition from other suicide leads like Azelf and Terrakion and isn't nearly as useful a set as Life Orb. Toxic can be used in the fourth slot to cripple Mamoswine's defensive switch-ins but usually doesn't provide as useful of overall utility as Stealth Rock or Knock Off. Finally, Protect is an option for scouting Choice Band Scizor's Bullet Punch or attacks from other Choice-locked Pokemon like Infernape and Volcanion, though it also often struggles to provide better utility than either Knock Off or Stealth Rock.

Checks and Counters

Defensive Water-types: Defensive Water-types like Alomomola, Slowbro and its Mega Evolution, and bulkier Suicune variants can often avoid the 2HKO from Earthquake while threatening Mamoswine with a super effective STAB Scald.

Fighting-types: Though they can't switch in, the likes of Infernape, Cobalion, and Terrakion are all faster than Mamoswine and can tank an Ice Shard, which allows them to KO Mamoswine with super effective STAB attacks.

Offensive Pressure: Due to Mamoswine's low Speed and terrible defensive typing, faster Pokemon capable of hitting it hard can pose a large threat. Examples include Terrakion, Starmie, and Kyurem, though all should be wary of switching into Mamoswine directly. Rotom-Heat is particularly troublesome, as it is only hit hard by Knock Off and Stone Edge due to its typing and ability, and it can pick Mamoswine off with STAB Overheat.

Super Effective Priority: Mamoswine's typing leaves it weak to several forms of super effective priority that are run in UU, including Scizor's Bullet Punch, Crawdaunt's Aqua Jet, and Lucario's Vacuum Wave. However, only offensive variants of the former can KO Mamoswine from full HP, meaning that both Infernape and Crawdaunt will require some chip damage to pick it off with priority moves.

Residual Damage: Mamoswine's middling bulk, poor defensive typing, and Life Orb recoil leave it open to being easily chipped down by forms of residual damage, which include entry hazards, U-turn pivoting from foes, and status ailments like poison.

Life Orb.description:
Moves

Ice Shard takes advantage of the tier's several faster Pokemon that are weak to Ice, letting Mamoswine revenge kill foes such as Crobat, Latias, Hydreigon, and Celebi after some chip damage. Earthquake is Mamoswine's most powerful STAB attack, 2HKOing the majority of switch-ins while forcing out defensive threats like Klefki and Mega Aggron. Icicle Crash applies pressure to several defensive Pokemon that could tank an Earthquake and damage Mamoswine in return, including Amoonguss and Hippowdon. It also hits Levitate users and Flying-types like Hydreigon, Latias, and bulkier variants of Togekiss, which would traditionally be used as Ground-type checks. Knock Off 2HKOes Rotom-Heat in addition to burdening foes with the removal of their items. Stealth Rock is an entry hazard that can be set as Mamoswine forces switches; however, it should only be run on Mamoswine if no other member of its team has room for the move as it greatly appreciates running a better coverage option instead. Stone Edge is an option that can OHKO Rotom-Heat and Moltres, which can both otherwise come in once and pressure Mamoswine with either powerful attacks or status. It often comes at the cost of utility or better coverage, however.

Set Details

Full investment in Attack with an Adamant nature maximizes Mamoswine's power, allowing it to more easily secure OHKOs on foes such as Primarina and Amoonguss and 2HKOs on the likes of Mega Aggron and Slowbro. Full investment in Speed makes it as fast as possible with a neutral nature, outrunning the majority of the metagame's defensive threats. A Jolly nature is also an option, allowing Mamoswine to outrun Timid Volcanion and Speed tie with Togekiss, Mega Altaria, and Chandelure at the cost of some power. Life Orb increases Mamoswine's overall damage output, notably allowing it to secure the 2HKO on Suicune with Earthquake. Thick Fat is the preferred ability, decreasing the damage Mamoswine takes from Fire- and Ice-type attacks that Electric-types like Mega Manectric often use to power through other Ground-types.

Usage Tips

Mamoswine's best use is on offensive teams as an early-game wallbreaker that can pave way for teammates to clean up later on. Ice Shard should be utilized to threaten to revenge kill the tier's several faster Pokemon that are weak to it, such as Latias, Togekiss, and Mega Aerodactyl. If the opposing team is weakened enough, Mamoswine can also try using it to clean up late-game. The decision of whether to use Icicle Crash or Earthquake to wallbreak can be tough at times, though against teams with Ground-immune Pokemon, which are often weak to Ice, Icicle Crash is often smarter to use early on. Earthquake is best to use once Ground-resistant and -immune foes are removed or weakened due to its better neutral coverage. Mamoswine forces several switches as it wallbreaks and as such should take advantage of said switches to fire off powerful STAB attacks, hit various switch-ins that tank its STAB attacks, like Rotom-Heat, with Knock Off, or set Stealth Rock if utilizing the move. Because its typing doesn't provide it with many switch-in opportunities, it's best to bring Mamoswine in via pivot support or after a teammate has fainted. However, it can come into play in a few specific scenarios, such as against passive defensive Pokemon like Klefki, Hippowdon, and Blissey and against Electric-types like Mega Manectric if it predicts carefully. Lastly, Mamoswine should capitalize on its strong matchup against defensive teams by using Knock Off to chip foes early-game, then weakening them further later on.

Team Options

Due to its huge offensive presence and struggle to defensively contribute to teams, Mamoswine is most comfortably fitted on offensively inclined builds. It is appreciated by setup sweepers, like Terrakion, Mega Altaria, and Doublade, thanks to its ability to weaken opposing teams for them to more easily do their job late-game. Cleaners such as Mega Sharpedo and Scizor also appreciate Mamoswine's support for this reason. Pokemon capable of providing pivot support, like Scizor, Mega Manectric, and Rotom-Heat, are capable of safely bringing Mamoswine into play. Mamoswine also appreciates teammates capable of supporting it with entry hazards, such as Cobalion and Nihilego, as chip damage allows it to more easily muscle past the likes of Alomomola and Mega Slowbro on its own. Stealth Rock support can also allow Mamoswine to more comfortably run Knock Off, its preferred coverage option. Klefki and Froslass are particularly helpful partners, as they can provide Spikes support for Mamoswine to take advantage of in addition Klefki being able to patch up its poor Speed with Thunder Wave. Adequate methods of checking faster foes, such as Choice Scarf Krookodile and Mega Aerodactyl, can help patch up Mamoswine's susceptibility to being revenge killed due to its poor Speed. Fighting-type checks like Latias, Mimikyu, and Primarina can come in on the several Fighting-types that force Mamoswine out, such as Infernape, Cobalion, and Terrakion. Lastly, due to Mamoswine's susceptibility to being worn down, it enjoys the support of Pokemon capable of removing entry hazards, such as Mega Blastoise, Starmie, and Hydreigon.

ou.overview: Mamoswine's primary role in OU is as a wallbreaker due to its high Attack stat and fantastic Ice- and Ground-type STAB combination that is very difficult to deal with defensively. It also has good utility due to its priority Ice Shard, threatening prevalent Pokemon such as Landorus-T and Garchomp. Access to Stealth Rock and its Ground typing are some of the main traits that help it fit onto teams, as both are invaluable. However, Mamoswine suffers competition from other Stealth Rock setters and Ground-type wallbreakers such as Landorus-T and Garchomp due to its mediocre Speed stat and subpar defenses, leaving it vulnerable to a lot of offensive Pokemon. Inability to reliably beat common priority users like Ash-Greninja and Mega Scizor further worsens Mamoswine's Speed issues. Overall, Mamoswine is a decent Pokemon but requires more team support than the most common Ground-types in the tier.
ou.comments:
Other Options

Superpower can hit Ferrothorn, but that's about it. Substitute can be used to ease prediction, but the utility Stealth Rock and Knock Off provide isn't worth dropping most of the time.

Checks and Counters

Steel-types: Mega Scizor is the biggest threat to Mamoswine due to its ability to tank multiple Earthquakes and use Roost to heal off the damage while threatening Mamoswine with Bullet Punch. Celesteela and Skarmory also eat Mamoswine's attacks pretty well but don't check it as well offensively and can be taken down with boosts from Metronome and timely Icicle Crash flinch. Ferrothorn can take any two attacks from Mamoswine if it's not fully specially defensive but does not have reliable recovery and cannot switch in repeatedly.

Water-types: Offensive Water-types such as Ash-Greninja and Manaphy threaten to OHKO Mamoswine with super effective STAB moves. More defensive Water-types such as Rotom-Wash, Mega Slowbro, and Alomomola can switch into Mamoswine relatively well and threaten it out.

Faster Pokemon: Pokemon such as Kartana, Tapu Lele, and Volcarona all naturally outspeed Mamoswine and threaten to OHKO it.

Fighting-types: The likes of Mega Medicham, Mega Lopunny, and Mega Gallade, while being unable to switch directly in on Mamoswine, naturally outpace it and can OHKO Mamoswine with their super effective STAB moves. These Pokemon also can get revenge killed via Ice Shard when weakened enough. Mega Heracross's typing and bulk set it apart from other Fighting-types and let it switch in on Mamoswine's Earthquake pretty comfortably.

Physical Attacker.description:
Moves

Ice Shard helps Mamoswine check Pokemon such as Garchomp and Landorus-T as well as pick off other weakened threats. Mamoswine makes a good use of Stealth Rock, since its great STAB coverage enables it to find many opportunities to set it up against Pokemon it threatens out. Knock Off, on the other hand, cripples Mamoswine's answers like Celesteela and defensive Rotom-Wash by removing their items for the rest of the battle.

Set Details

An Adamant nature is the preferred option, since Jolly doesn't allow Mamoswine to outspeed anything notable and lowers its firepower. Thick Fat is the ability of choice to reduce the damage Mamoswine takes from Fire- and Ice-type moves. Metronome is used to bypass would-be-checks such as Celesteela and Mega Scizor over time.

Usage Tips

Mamoswine should be used as a wallbreaker to threaten defensive backbones that cannot stomach powerful Ice- and Ground-type attacks. Icicle Crash is often the primary option, because nothing is immune to it and Ice-type attacks are generally very difficult to switch into. In general, one should weigh the risk and reward scenario presented to them and select their move based on that; Earthquake might not lose you too much against a team whose Ground switch-in is Landorus-T. Mamoswine can also be used to check faster threats such as Garchomp with Ice Shard; you can use this opportunity to predict a switch and go for more powerful STAB attacks as well. Mamoswine shouldn't be directly switched in very often, as it has relatively poor defenses, but it can be used in some cases to block Volt Switch from Pokemon such as Magearna and Tapu Koko if you predict correctly.

Team Options

Due to its great offensive presence and relative frailty, Mamoswine fits best on offensive teams that can give it proper support. VoltTurn pivots like Rotom-Wash, Tapu Koko, and Magnezone can bring Mamoswine in on bulky Grass-types, which these three tend to lure in, for free so Mamoswine can force them out and take advantage of it The likes of Tapu Fini and Tangrowth take on offensive Water-types, mainly Ash-Greninja, for Mamoswine; the latter also checks Kartana. Ash-Greninja appreciates Mamoswine's ability to threaten most of its defensive stops like Toxapex and Tangrowth while also creating a hazard stacking core with Mamoswine.

monotype.overview:
Ground

Mamoswine functions as a powerful physical wallbreaker thanks to its incredible Attack stat, as well as its unique and nearly unresisted STAB combination. Notably, Mamoswine is the only viable Ground-type with access to a STAB boosted priority move in Ice Shard. This assists Ground teams by granting them the ability to revenge kill faster, weakened foes such as Mega Lopunny and Choice Scarf Tapu Bulu. Mamoswine also is incredibly useful for sweeping Dragon and Flying teams late-game, as both types struggle to switch into Mamoswine's Ice-type STAB moves. Because of Thick Fat, Mamoswine can offensively check foes with Ice-type coverage such as Alolan Ninetales for Ground teams. However, Mamoswine's typing is defensively terrible and leaves it susceptible to various types such as Steel and Water. Additionally, foes with type coverage such as Close Combat Zeraora can OHKO Mamoswine. Also, while powerful, Mamoswine has a predictable moveset that can be played around if pressured correctly. Despite Mamoswine being a powerful wallbreaker, physically defensive walls such as Skarmory and Mega Slowbro can tank its attacks and can recover their health.

Ice

Mamoswine is a staple pick for Ice teams due to its ability to effectively fill multiple roles, including a Stealth Rock user, Choice Scarf revenge killer, and wallbreaker. Its high Attack stat and Ground typing allow it to check many Fire- and Steel-type threats such as Torkoal, Heatran, and Magnezone. Its Ground typing also grants it a neutrality to Stealth Rock, which can allow it to switch in more often. Its solid offensive presence makes it one of the best Stealth Rock users for Ice teams. With the ability Thick Fat, Mamoswine can offer a Fire neutrality for Ice teams, and with Oblivious, suicide lead sets can negate Taunt users to freely set up Stealth Rock. Access to priority in Ice Shard allows it to pick off weakened threats. Mamoswine has a wide range of coverage attacks, including Stone Edge, Superpower, and Knock Off, which allow it hit Flying-, Normal-, and Psychic-types such as Mantine, Chansey, and Slowbro, respectively. With Endeavor and Ice Shard along with a Focus Sash, Mamoswine is capable of blanket checking important threats such as Mega Scizor, Choice-locked Keldeo, and Volcarona. With a Choice Scarf, Mamoswine can operate as an effective revenge killer capable of checking threats such as Mega Charizard Y, Tapu Koko, and Nihilego. Unfortunately, Mamoswine is susceptible to being walled by Pokemon such as Skarmory and Mega Slowbro. Its mediocre Speed stat makes it incredibly easy to revenge kill. Its Ice / Ground typing leaves it weak to common priority moves such as Aqua Jet, Mach Punch, and Bullet Punch. Even with a Choice Scarf, Mamoswine finds itself outsped by common Choice Scarf Pokemon like Victini, Terrakion, and Heracross.
monotype.comments:
Other Options

Ground

A Life Orb can be utilized over Choice Band, as it allows Mamoswine to freely switch moves. Additionally, it is recommended to use Knock Off over Superpower on such a set in order to remain as powerful as possible. However, the loss in power means Mamoswine misses out on some notable 2HKOs, namely on Celesteela and Ferrothorn. It also forces Mamoswine to take recoil after using a move, which is especially detrimental against Flying teams, where it needs to be healthy in order to break them down. A Choice Scarf can be used over Choice Band to threaten faster foes such as Choice Scarf Tapu Bulu and Choice Scarf Magnezone, but this comes at the cost of the power attained from a Choice Band.

Ice

Ice Shard can be used on Choice Scarf sets as a means of revenge killing priority users like Breloom as well as faster Choice Scarf Pokemon like Latios, Hydreigon, and Landorus-T. However, the coverage offered by Superpower and Knock Off is much more valuable. Rock Slide can be run over Stone Edge on Choice Scarf sets for more consistency, but it can't always 2HKO Mantine and Armaldo. Stone Edge can be run on wallbreaking sets as a means of hitting Water-types like Pelipper and Araquanid. However, Knock Off and Superpower are generally better coverage options. Stealth Rock can be used on the wallbreaking set to take advantage of how Mamoswine can force switches. However, without Superpower, Mamoswine won't be able to threaten Air Balloon Heatran.

Checks and Counters

Ground

Rotom-Wash: Rotom-Wash is the single best counter to Mamoswine. It resists Mamoswine's Ice-type STAB moves, is immune to its Ground-type STAB moves, and can burn it through Will-O-Wisp or outright KO it with Hydro Pump.

Water-types: Water-types such as Greninja and Suicune can threaten Mamoswine with their STAB moves or a potential Scald burn. They also resist Mamoswine's Ice-type STAB moves.

Fighting-types: Fighting-types such as Buzzwole and Mega Gallade can threaten to KO Mamoswine with their STAB moves.

Burns: Burns severely hinder Mamoswine by halving its Attack stat and softening its damage output.

Physically Defensive Walls: Mega Slowbro and Skarmory are a few examples of physically defensive walls that can take Mamoswine's attacks and recover any damage taken.

Ice

Fighting-types: Fighting-types like Terrakion, Heracross, and Keldeo outspeed Mamoswine and threaten to KO it with their Fighting-type STAB moves.

Water-types: Water-types such as Greninja, Mega Sharpedo, and Manaphy outspeed Mamoswine and threaten it with their Water-type STAB moves.

Fast Steel-types: Choice Scarf Steel-types like Excadrill and Jirachi are capable of outspeeding and KOing Mamoswine. However, neither of them can take an Earthquake.

Priority: Priority users such as Mega Scizor and Azumarill can KO Mamoswine with their STAB priority attacks after setting up. Mega Scizor can even sustain itself with Roost, allowing it to set up with even more ease.

Physically Defensive Walls: Physically defensive walls like Skarmory, Mega Venusaur, and Mega Slowbro all easily survive any of Mamoswine's attacks, can restore the damage taken, and slowly wear it down.

Revenge Killers: Mega Alakazam, Choice Scarf Meloetta, and Choice Scarf Gengar are all capable of outspeeding and KOing Mamoswine with Focus Blast.

Multi-hit Moves: Multi-hit moves from Breloom and Mega Heracross are capable of breaking past Mamoswine's Focus Sash and KOing it. However, if Breloom is weakened enough, it will be KOed by Ice Shard.

Choice Band (Ground).description:
Moves

Icicle Crash is Mamoswine's best Ice-type STAB move that reliably damages bulky Flying-types such as Zapdos and Mantine, and it also has a chance to make the foe flinch. Earthquake is used to hit Steel-types such as Jirachi and Metagross. Ice Shard is a priority move that allows Mamoswine to check setup sweepers such as Landorus-T and Mega Latias. It can also be used to revenge kill weakened foes, especially those faster than Mamoswine such as Mega Lopunny and Choice Scarf Tapu Bulu. Superpower is a good coverage move against Normal- and Steel-types such as Porygon2 and Air Balloon Heatran. Alternatively, Knock Off helps against physically defensive walls such as Porygon2 and Slowbro by hampering their defenses and recovery, respectively, as well as providing coverage against Ghost- and Psychic-types.

Set Details

Maximum Attack investment paired with a Choice Band makes Mamoswine a threatening physical wallbreaker. Maximum Speed investment with a Jolly nature allows Mamoswine to outspeed some of its offensive checks, such as Breloom and Tapu Bulu without Choice Scarf. Thick Fat helps against Fire-types such as Heatran and Victini by weakening their Fire-type STAB moves and allowing Mamoswine to revenge kill them. An Adamant nature can be used as a means of attaining extra power, but this comes at the cost of extra Speed attained from a Jolly nature, as it no longer outspeeds Jolly Breloom and Tapu Bulu.

Usage Tips

Keep Mamoswine as healthy as possible against Flying teams, as it can reliably damage Pokemon such as Celesteela and Gliscor without having to rely on Gravity Landorus. It also is crucial against Dragon teams thanks to its priority Ice Shard to revenge kill faster Dragon-types such as Kommo-o and Latios, while Icicle Crash can OHKO or 2HKO all of them. Because Mamoswine is holding a Choice Band, it must be careful of what move it chooses to lock itself into, as it should try to predict what the foe will do. Use Mamoswine to offensively check foes with Ice-type coverage such as Greninja and Thundurus-T, as Thick Fat helps to lessen the damage. However, be cautious of other options from these foes, as they may predict Mamoswine switching in and deal severe damage to it. Knock Off can be used early-game against Eviolite users such as Chansey and Porygon2 to allow teammates such as Excadrill and Landorus to deal heavier damage to them. Additionally, removing the foe's items will decrease their overall usefulness. Mamoswine must be careful of using Superpower, as the drops in its Attack and Defense stats can make it setup bait for foes such as Volcarona and Swords Dance Mega Scizor. Avoid burns as much as possible, as they severely compromise Mamoswine's ability to break teams.

Team Options

Landorus holds incredible wallbreaking power on Ground teams thanks to its Life Orb and Sheer Force combination, being able to break physically defensive foes such as Porygon2 and Slowbro for Mamoswine. Additionally, Landorus aids Mamoswine by providing Gravity support to let it spam Earthquake to take care of checks such as Celesteela, Rotom-Wash, and Skarmory while also being able to use its coverage moves such as Focus Blast and Sludge Wave to threaten some of Mamoswine's checks such as Porygon2 and Choice Scarf Tapu Bulu. Gastrodon and Seismitoad are the two viable Ground-types that compensate for Mamoswine's Water-type weakness by providing an immunity, though they serve different purposes. Gastrodon's access to Recover and good bulk make it a fabulous defensive check to foes such as Greninja and Suicune. Seismitoad, however, doesn't have reliable recovery but makes up for it by outspeeding and KOing Azumarill after a Belly Drum boost, which would otherwise pose a threat to Ground teams. Hippowdon's solid physical bulk, Slack Off recovery, and access to Whirlwind are used to handle physical setup sweepers such as Bisharp and Mega Scizor for Mamoswine. The sand that Hippowdon provides also chips away at foes and puts them in range of being KOed by Mamoswine. Sand Rush Excadrill works in tandem with Hippowdon by becoming a powerful revenge killer under sand and checks fast threats to Mamoswine such as Mega Lopunny, Choice Scarf Tapu Bulu, and Zeraora, while it's also able to clear away entry hazards with Rapid Spin. Garchomp's typing is useful, as it provides a neutrality to Grass- and Water- type moves from Pokemon such as Mega Venusaur and Mantine for Mamoswine and uses its solid Speed tier and Swords Dance boosts to break them down. Alternatively, Mega Garchomp becomes immensely powerful and assists Mamoswine by using its mixed coverage to break down physical walls such as Celesteela and Skarmory with Fire Blast and also checks Azumarill after a Belly Drum boost. Mega Steelix assists Mamoswine by checking physical attackers such as Mega Pinsir, Tapu Bulu thanks to its incredible defenses, and even survives Adamant Azumarill's +6 Aqua Jet to KO it in return with Heavy Slam. Mega Steelix and Mamoswine also create a solid core that effectively breaks down Dragon teams.

Entry Hazard Lead (Ice).description:
Moves

Stealth Rock is used to make foes take Rock-type damage whenever they switch in, which is especially helpful against Fire- and Bug-types. Earthquake is used to hit Fire-, Steel-, and Poison-types such as Torkoal, Magnezone, and Nihilego. Endeavor is used to bring foes down to 1 HP when Mamoswine's Focus Sash is activated. Ice Shard is used for revenge killing Pokemon after Mamoswine has weakened them with Endeavor.

Set Details

Maximum investment in Attack and Speed is used to make Mamoswine as fast and powerful as possible. A Jolly nature allows Mamoswine to outspeed Jolly Breloom and Bisharp. A Focus Sash is used to guarantee that Mamoswine survives any hit and can safely put up Stealth Rock, as well as reducing the opposing Pokemon's HP to 1 with Endeavor. 0 IVs in HP are used in order to have as few HP as possible, allowing Mamoswine to use Endeavor more effectively even when it hasn't been attacked. The ability Oblivious is used to get past Taunt users that prevent Mamoswine from getting up Stealth Rock like Deoxys-S.

Usage Tips

Mamoswine should be led with most of the time in order to get up Stealth Rock as quickly as possible. However, you do have to be careful when leading against entry hazard removers like Torkoal and Armaldo. If there's a threat that Mamoswine needs its Focus Sash to handle, make sure to preserve it by switching it out. Keep hazards off the field as much as possible, since they can break Mamoswine's Focus Sash. If hazards can't be prevented, try switching Mamoswine in as the opponent goes for Stealth Rock in order to keep Mamoswine's Focus Sash intact. It's a good idea to bring in a weakened Mamoswine against a slower threat such as Celesteela in order to chip away at it with Endeavor. Avoid burns and poison as much as possible, since both break Mamoswine's Focus Sash and burns also cripple it by halving its Attack. After getting up Stealth Rock, it's a good idea to preserve Mamoswine, since it'll still be able to check Pokemon such as Heatran and Magnezone.

Team Options

Everything on Ice appreciates Mamoswine's Stealth Rock and ability to blanket check various threats, including Volcarona and Mega Scizor, with Endeavor and Ice Shard. Kyurem-B can break through walls such as Skarmory, Celesteela, and Mega Venusaur, which Mamoswine can't do good damage against. Kyurem-B also offers helpful Grass and Water resistances, which Mamoswine greatly appreciates. Alolan Ninetales can check Water- and Fighting-types that give Mamoswine trouble like Swampert, Keldeo, and Terrakion. In return, Mamoswine checks Fire-types like Alolan Marowak and Heatran as well as Steel-types like Magnezone and Bisharp. Cloyster is a powerful setup sweeper that appreciates Mamoswine's Stealth Rock enabling it to break through Sturdy Pokemon like Skarmory and Forretress. Lapras offers a helpful Water immunity with Water Absorb as well as a Steel neutrality for Mamoswine. It also serves as a helpful check to Mega Scizor and Azumarill with Hidden Power Fire and Freeze-Dry, respectively, and it can use Mamoswine's Stealth Rock to guarantee an OHKO on Rotom-Wash with Choice Specs Freeze-Dry. Avalugg can remove hazards with Rapid Spin to preserve Mamoswine's Focus Sash and switch into threats like Jirachi, Heracross, and Terrakion. In return, Mamoswine complements Avalugg's phazing with Stealth Rock. Alolan Sandslash is an effective cleaner that can remove hazards with Rapid Spin to preserve Mamoswine's Focus Sash. It's also capable of checking threats such as non-Choice Scarf Terrakion and Hasty Victini after Stealth Rock damage. Weavile can Pursuit trap Psychic- and Ghost-types like Victini, Jirachi, and Gengar while also removing items with Knock Off and using Mamoswine's Stealth Rock to guarantee KOs against Mega Charizard Y and Heatran.

Choice Scarf (Ice).description:
Moves

Earthquake is a basic Ground-type STAB move used to hit Fire-, Steel-, Poison-, and Rock-types such as Torkoal, Magnezone, Nihilego, and Mega Diancie. Icicle Crash is an Ice-type STAB attack used to hit Ground-types like Landorus and Garchomp. Stone Edge is important for hitting Fire- and Flying-types like Volcarona, Mega Charizard Y, and Mantine. Superpower lets Mamoswine hit Steel-types that aren't threatened by Earthquake, such as Ferrothorn and Air Balloon Heatran, as well as Normal-types like Chansey and Porygon2. Knock Off can be used to remove items, specifically Chansey's and Porygon2's Eviolites.

Set Details

Maximum investment in Attack and Speed is used to make Mamoswine as fast and strong as possible. A Jolly nature is important for outspeeding Choice Scarf Tapu Bulu and Tapu Koko as well as Speed tying with Choice Scarf Togekiss. A Choice Scarf is used to allow Mamoswine to outspeed numerous threats such as Volcarona, Mega Charizard Y, and Mega Pinsir. Thick Fat is the preferred ability to take neutral damage from Fire-type attacks.

Usage Tips

While the set is most effective late-game when its checks and counters have been removed, Mamoswine can still be brought in early-game on a resisted hit in order to potentially revenge kill something like Mega Charizard Y. Be careful about what move Mamoswine locks itself into, or it'll risk becoming setup bait. If Superpower is being used, make sure to switch out immediately after using it, as Mamoswine is incredibly susceptible to being revenged killed afterward. Avoid burns as much as possible, since they will wear Mamoswine down while also halving its Attack stat.

Team Options

Mamoswine filling a Choice Scarf role allows Kyurem-B to freely run a wallbreaking set, allowing it to break past some of Mamoswine's defensive checks such as Skarmory, Mega Venusaur, and Celesteela. Alolan Ninetales is capable of checking bulky Pokemon such as Mega Sableye, Mega Slowbro, and Swampert for Mamoswine as well as setting up Aurora Veil to give Mamoswine some extra bulk. In return, Mamoswine can check Volcarona and Mega Charizard Y. Avalugg can switch into Choice Scarf Pokemon that threaten to KO Mamoswine such as Jirachi, Heracross, and Infernape. Avalugg can also remove entry hazards with Rapid Spin to make sure Mamoswine stays healthy. Cloyster is a powerful setup sweeper that appreciates Mamoswine's Knock Off softening Chansey and Porygon2. Lapras offers a helpful Water immunity with Water Absorb as well as a Steel neutrality while also checking priority users like Mega Scizor and Azumarill with Hidden Power Fire and Freeze-Dry. In return, Mamoswine can switch into Electric-type attacks and check Electric-types like Tapu Koko and Magnezone. Weavile can Pursuit trap Psychic- and Ghost-types like Victini, Jirachi, and Gengar while also checking priority users like Breloom. In return, Mamoswine can check Toxapex and Torkoal, both of which wall Weavile. Piloswine can set up Stealth Rock for Mamoswine, allowing it to sweep teams more effectively. It also is capable of phazing out setup sweepers with Roar and can switch into faster Choice Scarf Pokemon like Hydreigon and Nihilego.

Wallbreaker (Ice).description:
Moves

Earthquake is Mamoswine's best Ground-type STAB move and used to hit Fire-, Poison-, Steel-, and Rock-types like Torkoal, Toxapex, Heatran, and Nihilego. Icicle Crash is its strongest Ice-type STAB move and used to hit Flying- and Ground-types like Zapdos and Hippowdon. Ice Shard is a STAB priority move used to revenge kill faster threats like Latios, Salamence, and Landorus. Knock Off allows Mamoswine to hit Water-types like Slowbro and Jellicent as well as remove Chansey's and Porygon2's Eviolites. Superpower can be used to hit Normal-types like Chansey and Porygon2 as well as Air Balloon Heatran.

Set Details

Maximum investment in Attack and Speed is used to make Mamoswine as fast and strong as possible. An Adamant nature can be used to further increase its wallbreaking potential. A Jolly nature can be used in order to outspeed Heatran as well as Jolly Breloom and Bisharp. Life Orb can be used to further increase Mamoswine's power while giving it the freedom to switch moves. Choice Band is another option to give Mamoswine an even larger power increase at the cost of being locked into a single move. Thick Fat is the ability used to take neutral damage from Fire-type attacks.

Usage Tips

Try sending out Mamoswine early-game to break through bulky Pokemon like Toxapex and Chansey in order to make it easier for sweepers like Kyurem-B and Cloyster to win late-game. It's also a good idea to send it in against weakened threats to revenge kill them with Ice Shard. If an Adamant nature is used, it's helpful to try to bluff a Jolly nature in order to force out Pokemon like Heatran and Tapu Bulu. If Choice Band is being used, be careful about what move you lock Mamoswine into, or it risks becoming setup bait. If Life Orb is being used, make sure to keep entry hazards off the field, since they'll be quickly wearing Mamoswine down alongside the Life Orb recoil. Avoid burns as much as possible, since they will hinder Mamoswine's wallbreaking potential.

Team Options

Choice Scarf Kyurem-B appreciates Mamoswine's wallbreaking giving it the chance to sweep late-game. It also checks fast threats like Mega Alakazam, Mega Charizard Y, and Keldeo. Alolan Ninetales can allow Mamoswine to switch into attacks more easily thanks to Aurora Veil while also checking Fighting-types like Keldeo and Terrakion. In return, Mamoswine can beat Steel-types like Heatran and Magnezone. Avalugg can remove entry hazards for Mamoswine with Rapid Spin while also switching into threatening physical attackers like Excadrill and Heracross. In return, Mamoswine can beat Fire-types like Torkoal, Volcanion, and Alolan Marowak. Piloswine can set up Stealth Rock, allowing Mamoswine to wallbreak more effectively, while also switching into Nihilego and Heatran and checking Mega Charizard Y and Volcarona. Cloyster is a powerful sweeper that appreciates Mamoswine softening Chansey and Porygon2 with Knock Off. Mamoswine also removes some of Cloyster's counters like Toxapex and Empoleon. Lapras can switch into and beat Water-types like Slowbro and Pelipper for Mamoswine while also checking Mega Scizor with Hidden Power Fire. In return, Mamoswine switches into Electric-type attacks and can check Magnezone and Zapdos. Alolan Sandslash appreciates Mamoswine's wallbreaking allowing it to sweep late-game and can remove entry hazards with Rapid Spin. Weavile can Pursuit trap Psychic- and Ghost-types that threaten to KO Mamoswine like Victini and Gengar. In return, Mamoswine can break past some of Weavile's checks such as Toxapex and Torkoal.

battlespotsingles.overview:
• Mamoswine stands out in the Battle Spot Singles metagame for its ability to check many relevant threats such as Mega Salamence and Landorus-T, which are both 4x weak to its Ice-type STAB moves.
  • Its Ground typing allows it to take on Tapu Koko with its Assault Vest set and it differentiates itself from other Assault Vest users thanks to its access to Fissure making it difficult to switch into.
  • Mamoswine also boasts an incredibly potent STAB combination in Ice and Ground, making it very hard to take on.
  • Despite its impressive offensive prowess, Mamoswine is putty in the hands of bulky Water- and Flying-types like Tapu Fini, Suicune, Pelipper, and Celesteela, which can all switch in on it and threaten it out with their respective STAB moves.
battlespotsingles.comments:
Other Options

  • Both Life Orb and Choice Band bolster Mamoswine's power, aiding it in securing an OHKO with Earthquake versus Aegislash and making it much harder to switch into.
  • Lum Berry is especially useful when dealing with Ghost-types, protecting Mamoswine from being burned by the likes of Mega Gengar and Mimikyu.
  • A physically defensive set can be run with Rocky Helmet in order to discourage contact attackers such as Mega Salamence and Mega Kangaskhan, which dislike taking recoil damage.
  • Freeze-Dry is 4x super effective against Gyarados and Pelipper, allowing Mamoswine to catch them both off guard on a predicted switch in, but it should never be used directly against either since Mamoswine is threatened by their Water-type STAB moves and Gyarados is able to reduce the amount of damage taken by Mega Evolving. Additionally, Freeze-Dry lacks the power of Mamoswine's other moves, making it a rather ineffective lure if not paired with a damage-boosting item like Life Orb.
  • Groundium Z can turn Fissure or Earthquake into a 180-Base Power physical nuke capable of inflicting serious damage against unsuspecting foes and safely eliminating Porygon2 once it's fallen under 50% HP.
  • Toxic possesses some merit as a safer alternative to wear down Porygon2.
  • Choice Scarf coupled with a Jolly nature allows Mamoswine to outspeed typically faster Pokemon such as Mega Gengar and Tapu Koko, allowing it to KO them with an Earthquake before they can attack.

Checks and Counters

Floating Pokemon: Anything that is immune to Earthquake and isn't weak to Ice-type attacks will usually wall Mamoswine. Commone examples include Celesteela, Cresselia, Rotom-Wash, Skarmory, and Gyarados.

Bulky Water-types: Tapu Fini can come in on Mamoswine and threaten it with a powerful Hydro Vortex as well as take an Earthquake regardless of its defensive investment, allowing it to take out Mamoswine even if it's holding a Focus Sash. Similarly, Pelipper can switch into Mamoswine and take out offensive variants with a single rain-boosted Scald, and defensive Gyarados can also cause Mamoswine problems by being able to easily sponge attacks with its Intimidate ability and deal massive damage in return with a STAB Waterfall. Both make such excellent answers for their immunity to Ground-type moves, guaranteeing their safety won't be compromised by a timely Fissure. While not strictly a bulky Water-type, Cloyster's natural physical bulk and secondary Ice typing mean that Mamoswine can't pick it off with a combination of Earthquake and Ice Shard from high HP, allowing it to Shell Smash against it without fear and OHKO Mamoswine with a +2 Icicle Spear.

Buzzwole: Buzzwole resists Earthquake and shrugs off Mamoswine's Ice-type attacks only to bring Mamoswine down to its Focus Sash or possibly KO it with a STAB Superpower. However, since Buzzwole is grounded, it must be wary of a potential Fissure.

Faster Offensive Steel-types: Mamoswine fears Kartana like the plague. It's able to KO Mamoswine with either of its STAB moves and its Steel typing decreases its susceptibility to Ice Shard; however, it dislikes taking an Earthquake. Mega Metagross and Mega Lucario are also able to outright KO Mamoswine once its Focus Sash has been broken, but neither should switch directly into it for fear of being hit by a super effective Earthquake.

Mega Scizor: Mega Scizor deserves a special mention; unlike other Steel-types, it's able to use Mamoswine as setup fodder, safely setting up a Swords Dance before plowing through the rest of Mamoswine's team.

Mega Venusaur: Thanks to its own Thick Fat, Mega Venusaur can take on anything Mamoswine dishes out except for Fissure, and threaten massive damage with Giga Drain.

Focus Sash.description:
Moves

  • Stealth Rock gradually wears down foes and breaks Focus Sashes, easing up play versus Pokemon like Tapu Koko and Cloyster.
  • Earthquake is Mamoswine's main STAB move, dealing super effective damage to Steel- and Poison-types such as Aegislash, Mega Gengar, and Nihilego.
  • Ice Shard gives Mamoswine priority against Pokemon that would outspeed it otherwise, helping it take on Dragon-types such as Garchomp and Mega Salamence or even scoring a revenge KO on a weakened foe.
  • Icicle Spear is an alternative form of damage output that, while slightly less consistent than Earthquake, enables Mamoswine to break through opposing Focus Sashes as well as Mimikyu's Disguise.
  • Fissure is an alternative option to Icicle Spear, providing a guaranteed OHKO against bulkier Pokemon Mamoswine would otherwise struggle with (provided that it hits).
  • Roar can also be used over Icicle Spear to phaze setup sweepers such as Mega Scizor, preventing Mamoswine from being complete setup fodder and racking up Stealth Rock damage in the process.

Set Details

  • Maximum Attack investment with an Adamant nature allows Mamoswine to hit as hard as possible, while maximum investment in Speed helps it outpace as many threats as possible.
  • Focus Sash allows Mamoswine to take at least one hit and set up Stealth Rock.
  • Thick Fat lets Mamoswine tank Ice-type attacks, and handle weaker Fire-type moves.

Usage Tips

  • Lead with Mamoswine in order to set up Stealth Rock as early as possible, wearing down foes with chip damage and breaking Focus Sashes along the way.
  • Focus Sash can also help Mamoswine combat Pokemon it cannot outspeed outright, serving as an effective safety net.
  • If need be, attempt to preserve Mamoswine's Focus Sash in order to combat a powerful threat on the opponent's team.
  • Make use of Mamoswine's Ground typing in order to switch in on predicted Electric-type moves from Tapu Koko or a Sludge Wave from Nihilego and threaten to KO back with a STAB Earthquake.
  • Threaten to revenge kill Dragon-types like Garchomp, Naganadel, and Mega Salamence with a STAB Ice Shard after they've sustained a bit of damage. Ice Shard is also capable of picking off Hydreigon from below 50% HP.

Team Options

  • Setup sweepers benefit from the chip damage provided by Stealth Rock, making them excellent teammates for Mamoswine. Gyarados in particular does a good job of covering Mamoswine's weaknesses before Mega Evolving and Mamoswine in turn protects it from Electric-type moves. Furthermore, if possessing Substitute, Gyarados is able to easily set up versus Celesteela, paving the way to a potential sweep.
  • Tapu Koko is a fantastic partner, being able to check many of the Pokemon that give Mamoswine trouble such as Tapu Fini, Pelipper, Celesteela, and Buzzwole.
  • Celesteela covers many of Mamoswine's weaknesses and forces switches, often racking up Stealth Rock damage.
  • Both Heatran and Volcarona help to mitigate Mamoswine's vulnerability to certain Steel-types such as Celesteela and Scizor.
  • Mega Salamence switches in and sets up on Mega Scizor, one of Mamoswine's best answers, alleviating what would otherwise be a massive headache.

Assault Vest.description:
Moves

  • Earthquake is Mamoswine's strongest STAB move with consistent damage.
  • Ice Shard compensates for this set's lack of Speed investment and deals a sizeable chunk of damage to opposing Dragon-types such as Garchomp and Mega Salamence.
  • Icicle Spear breaks through Focus Sashes as well as Mimikyu's Disguise, giving Mamoswine the upper hand on Garchomp and the aforementioned Mimikyu.
  • Fissure allows Mamoswine to remove bulkier Pokemon such as Porygon2 and makes switching in checks to Mamoswine such as Tapu Fini and Buzzwole much riskier.

Set Details

  • 44 EVs in HP minimize all forms of residual damage, extending Mamoswine's longevity as much as possible.
  • 212 EVs in Attack with an Adamant nature allow Mamoswine to maintain a noticeable offensive presence.
  • Maximum Special Defense investment compounds nicely with Assault Vest in order to optimize Mamoswine's special bulk.

Usage Tips

  • Use Mamoswine's Assault Vest-boosted bulk in order to switch into Pokemon such as Tapu Koko and Nihilego with ease.
  • Mamoswine's improved bulk can also aid it in switching into neutral hits from Pokemon like Alolan Ninetales, Porygon2, and Mega Gengar; however, it must be wary of burns from bulky variants of Mega Gengar.
  • Attempt to use Fissure in order to remove common Mamoswine switch-ins, most notably Porygon2.
  • Use Ice Shard to revenge kill Dragon-types such as Garchomp, Mega Salamence, and even weakened Hydreigon.

Team Options

  • Flying-types like Celesteela and Gyarados benefit from Mamoswine's ability to take on Tapu Koko.
  • Tapu Koko itself is able to take on Water- and Flying-types as well as Buzzwole, which all bother Mamoswine.
  • Fire-types like Arcanine and Silvally as well as Alolan Marowak (though it must be wary of Dark-type coverage) can contest threatening Steel-types such as Mega Scizor and Celesteela with their STAB moves.
  • Mega Salamence is able to switch into Mega Scizor and easily set up, taking a lot of pressure off Mamoswine, while Mamoswine removes the Porygon2 that can trouble Salamence.
  • With its Magnet Pull ability, Magnezone is also able to trap and KO Steel-types that bother Mamoswine, making it a potentially valuable asset.
  • Tapu Fini appreciates Mamoswine's ability to switch into Tapu Koko and is able to take on Buzzwole, Gyarados, and possibly Celesteela with the combination of Nature's Madness and Hydro Vortex.

Groundium Z.description: For full USUM 1v1 analyses, you can check out the USUM format page.

ou.overview: While it's true that after Z-Conversion Porygon-Z becomes a threatening sweeper, its overreliance on stat boosts from the aforementioned move, inability to get a second chance at sweeping, and reliance on a lot of support hold it back from being viable in the metagame. Furthermore, Porygon-Z's low stats, except Special Attack, mean that it's hard to find setup opportunities due to low defenses and lack of resistances, so Porygon-Z is outclassed by better setup sweepers like Magearna. Even after setup, Porygon-Z is still relatively easy to revenge kill with common forces like Choice Scarf Landorus-T and Ash-Greninja because Porygon-Z doesn't have priority to hit these revenge killers.

Z-Conversion.description: This set attempts to use Z-Conversion at the right time and then sweep. STAB Thunderbolt after setup absolutely destroys Toxapex. Ice Beam gives Porygon-Z the best coverage possible alongside Thunderbolt. Recover is useful, as it allows Porygon-Z to set up Z-Conversion more freely on Pokemon like Celesteela and Assault Vest Magearna, leaving it less prone to being revenge killed. Porygon-Z isn't worth using, though, as it struggles to break past common defensive or just bulky Pokemon like Ferrothorn and Tyranitar, and the metagame has more consistent setup sweepers requiring less support like Magearna and Mega Mawile due to their better movesets and typings.

monotype.overview:
Normal

Porygon-Z is one of the best stat boosters available to Normal thanks to Z-Conversion giving it +1 in all stats; it can prove to be an amazing sweeper when utilized late-game. Z-Conversion allows Porygon-Z to change its typing, which can prove invaluable in certain matchups. Notably, turning into Ghost provides an important Fighting immunity. This is complemented by great Special Attack and coverage moves, most notably BoltBeam, allowing it to hit a large majority of Pokemon at least neutrally. BoltBeam coverage enables Porygon-Z to blast through the Flying matchup, cleanly sweeping through entire Flying-type teams after a Z-Conversion. Adaptability further enhances Porygon-Z's ability to act as a sweeper after setting up by boosting its Shadow Ball's power even further. It also has access to Recover, which gives it sustain after receiving its stat boosts, granting it longevity throughout the battle. However, Porygon-Z generally relies on its stat boosting to be threatening in a battle, and its only mediocre bulk and Speed leave it vulnerable to faster attackers such as Landorus and Keldeo, therefore limiting its ability to set up and sweep. Its mediocre Speed also leaves it susceptible to powerful Choice Scarf Pokemon such as Greninja and Victini even after Z-Conversion. Porygon-Z also relies on its teammates to weaken foes and eliminate its checks prior to setting up in order to sweep teams. While gaining +1 in all stats can be game changing, Porygon-Z can only do so once, so choosing the right time to do so is crucial in a battle. On balance-oriented teams, Porygon-Z has a hard time fitting onto a team, as it typically competes for the same slot as the amazing physical wallbreaker Diggersby.
monotype.comments:
Other Options

Normal

Utilizing Thunderbolt in the first slot enables Porygon-Z to changes its typing to Electric following Z-Conversion, which is helpful in preventing Porygon-Z from being paralyzed as well as helping immensely in the Steel matchup. However, it loses out on the important Fighting immunity that the Ghost typing grants and becomes unable to take advantage of Shadow Ball's general lack of Pokemon that resist it. This set should also utilize Hidden Power Fire over Shadow Ball to help take down troublesome Steel-types such as Excadrill after prior chip damage. Nasty Plot could be utilized to bolster Porygon-Z's Special Attack to tremendous levels, allowing it to blast through even most of its common defensive checks. However, without Z-Conversion, Porygon-Z lacks the Speed necessary to handle its common offensive checks.

Checks and Counters

Normal

Specially Defensive Walls: Specially defensive walls such as Chansey and Alolan Muk are able to absorb attacks from a boosted Porygon-Z and whittle it down with status while taking little damage from its attacks.

Dark-types: Dark-types such as Tyranitar and Bisharp resist Porygon-Z's primary attack in Shadow Ball and prevent it from utilizing Z-Conversion effectively. They also threaten Porygon-Z after it sets up due to resisting Shadow Ball and being able to hit back hard with Dark-type STAB moves.

Revenge Killers: Porygon-Z's awkward Speed tier leaves it vulnerable to most common Choice Scarf Pokemon such as Victini and Blacephalon, which can revenge kill it even after a Z-Conversion boost.

Haze and Phazing Moves: Pokemon that threaten to remove Porygon-Z's stat boosts with Haze, such as Toxapex, or moves like Whirlwind and Roar, such as Swampert, effectively nullify Porygon-Z's sweeping ability, as it can only set up once.

Paralysis: Paralysis completely inhibits Porygon-Z's ability to sweep opposing teams due to the drop in Speed, which makes it unable to outspeed most offensive Pokemon.

Z-Conversion Sweeper (Normal).description:
Moves

Shadow Ball becomes Porygon-Z's most spammable move after utilizing Z-Conversion thanks to Adaptability and being able to hit the vast majority of types neutrally. Conversion is utilized in combination with Normalium Z to boost all of Porygon-Z's stats by 1 and change its typing to its first-in-slot move. Thunderbolt is a fantastic coverage move, being able to super effectively threaten Flying- and Water-types such as Mantine and Celesteela. Recover grants Porygon-Z a means of reliable recovery, which grants Porygon-Z longevity throughout the battle, minimizing its reliance on avoiding chip damage. Alternatively, Ice Beam is amazing in combination with Thunderbolt to threaten a large number of Pokemon, most notably Ground- and Dragon-types such as Diggersby, Garchomp, and Dragonite.

Set Details

252 Special Attack and Speed EVs with a Timid nature maximize Porygon-Z's offensive presence and Speed, allowing it to outspeed threats such as Mega Altaria and Gyarados as well as common Choice Scarf Pokemon like Excadrill when at +1. Normalium Z enables Porygon-Z to use Z-Conversion, which boosts all of its stats by 1 and changes its typing to Ghost. Adaptability maximizes Porygon-Z's STAB attack damage, boosting Shadow Ball after Porygon-Z uses Z-Conversion.

Usage Tips

Porygon-Z works best as a late-game sweeper after its faster checks, such as Choice Scarf Blacephalon and Sand Rush Excadrill, have been eliminated. Weaken Porygon-Z's defensive checks such as Toxapex and Tyranitar prior to setting up so it can easily clean through the remaining team. Take advantage of Ghost's immunity to Fighting to mitigate the threat of offensive Fighting-types such as Keldeo and Terrakion after Porygon-Z changes its type through Z-Conversion. Porygon-Z has mediocre bulk, so it should avoid switching into attacks. In the same vein, because Porygon-Z can only set up once, it should look for opportune times to set up its Z-Conversion to not be overly weakened or KOed on its setup turn. Take advantage of Porygon-Z's ability to force switches by using Recover to heal up any lost health while its checks are still healthy, prior to using Z-Conversion to prolong Porygon-Z's life throughout the battle. Recover should also be utilized after it gains its stat boosts in order to heal back chip damage that defensive Pokemon deal out in an effort to wear Porygon-Z down. Utilizing Recover correctly will also help bring Porygon-Z out of range of common priority users' attacks such as Bullet Punch from Scizor. Do not set up against Pokemon that commonly run Haze or phazing moves, such as Mantine and Hippowdon, as setting up on them can lead to the stat boosts being removed, wasting Porygon-Z's Z-Move. Porygon-Z should be wary of status effects and entry hazards, as they all wear it down, leaving it vulnerable to faster revenge killers and minimizing its ability to set up effectively. Paralysis prevents Porygon-Z from effectively performing its job as a late-game sweeper, as it relies on outspeeding threats to eliminate them.

Team Options

Chansey supports Porygon-Z by utilizing both Thunder Wave and Stealth Rock. Thunder Wave helps slow down opposing Pokemon such as Keldeo and Terrakion, which gives Porygon-Z more opportunities to set up and the ability to outspeed its common checks, and Stealth Rock chips down opposing Pokemon and enables Porygon-Z to more easily sweep through weakened foes late-game. Porygon2 forms an amazing defensive core with Chansey and supports Porygon-Z thanks to Toxic, further whittling down opposing Pokemon into KO range from Porygon-Z late-game. Staraptor removes entry hazards from the field for Porygon-Z and lowers opposing Pokemon's Attack stats with Intimidate, allowing it to act as a physical wall. It also can act as a pivot with U-turn to bring Porygon-Z in safely to begin its sweep. Ditto helps check opposing setup sweepers and faster offensive Pokemon for Porygon-Z, granting it more opportunities to sweep late-game. Mega Lopunny and Diggersby are both offensive powerhouses that can help take down common special walls and Dark-types that check Porygon-Z such as Alolan Muk, Chansey, and Bisharp. Smeargle sets Sticky Web for Porygon-Z, which on more offensively oriented teams allows Porygon-Z to effectively outspeed all grounded Pokemon after a Z-Conversion boost. Additionally, Smeargle can spread both sleep and paralysis between Spore and Nuzzle, giving Porygon-Z more opportunities to set up safely.

battlespotsingles.overview:
Porygon-Z is a threatening setup sweeper due to its near exclusive access to Z-Conversion, boosting all stats by +1. It has a good ability in Adaptability, boosting the power of moves the same type as it. Combined with a good movepool, passable Speed, and high Special Attack, Porygon-Z can dominate if left unchecked. However, even at +1, its defenses are rather lackluster, leaving it threatened by most sweepers. Its Speed tier also isn't very good for boosting, leaving it outsped by Choice Scarf users such as Tapu Lele, Greninja, and Garchomp as well as faster Pokemon such as Naive Pheromosa. Z-Conversion additionally allows Porygon-Z only one opportunity to set up, resulting in a sweeper that isn't very flexible and rendered nearly useless against something that walls it when it sets up.

Below are some sample sets. These sets are likely to be standard, but they will be expanded upon and updated as the metagame progresses.

Z-Conversion Ghost.description:
• Shadow Ball is used in the first moveslot, giving Porygon-Z a largely unresisted STAB move that at +1 with Adaptability is capable of obliterating Ghost- and Psychic-types while being less vulnerable to being revenge killed by Choice Scarf Garchomp than other Z-Conversion sets. However, this set gets decimated by Mimikyu and is more vulnerable to being sniped by Shadow Sneak and Sucker Punch.
  • Ice Beam provides excellent coverage, hitting Ground- and Dragon-types super effectively such as Landorus-T, Garchomp and Mega Salamence.
  • Conversion is mandatory on this set, as it boosts Porygon-Z's stats by +1 when used as a Z-Move.
  • Maximum Speed and a Timid nature allow Porygon-Z to be as fast as possible after Z-Conversion, notably outspeeding Mega Gengar, Jolly Mega Salamence, and Tapu Koko, while maximum Special Attack lets Porygon-Z hit as hard as possible.
  • A Modest nature, however, secures OHKOs that Porygon-Z misses out on, such as Hippowdon with Ice Beam. However, it misses out on outspeeding neutral nature Choice Scarf users, such as Modest Tapu Lele and Adamant Landorus-T.
  • Adaptability doubles the power of Shadow Ball, allowing Porygon-Z to OHKO Aegislash and almost always OHKO Cresselia.
  • Download, however, can be used to potentially gain a second Special Attack boost, powering up all of its moves. It is much riskier though, as gaining an Attack boost could make Porygon-Z's sweep less consistent.
  • Porygon-Z is best used late-game, after its checks have been eliminated. It is also weaker to phazing and Haze, which threaten to remove its boosts as Z-Conversion can only be used once.
  • Tapu Lele can mitigate Ghost-type Porygon-Z's weakness to Sucker Punch and Shadow Sneak while dealing with Dark-types thanks to its Fairy-type STAB moves.
  • Ghost-type Porygon-Z despises facing opposing Mimikyu, so dedicated checks to it are necessary.
  • As Porygon-Z struggles against most Choice Scarf users, Pokemon that can deal with them make great teammates.
  • Porygon-Z also has difficulty against special walls, so wallbreakers are greatly appreciated.
  • Pokemon that can set up Stealth Rock can provide Porygon-Z an easier opportunity to sweep, weakening foes while breaking Sturdy and Focus Sash.

Z-Conversion Electric.description:
• With Thunderbolt in the first moveslot, Porygon-Z becomes an Electric-type, granting it a powerful STAB move that can be boosted by Tapu Koko's Electric Terrain while allowing it to better take advantage of its defense boosts due to having only one weakness in Ground. It is able to easily blast through most Water-types and Celesteela, is immune to paralysis, and has little to fear from priority. However, Porygon-Z would then be more vulnerable to fast Choice Scarf Ground-types such as Garchomp and Landorus-T along with those that carry Focus Sash, as they can easily revenge kill it.
  • Ice Beam deals with Ground- and Dragon-types that Thunderbolt cannot touch, such as Garchomp, Landorus-T, and Hippowdon.
  • Shadow Ball is a great move to round out Porygon-Z's coverage, especially given the prevalence of Ghost- and Psychic-types in Battle Spot Singles along with few Pokemon resisting it. It also prevents Porygon-Z from being walled by the rare Alolan Marowak, which is immune to Thunderbolt and resists Ice Beam.
  • Conversion allows Porygon-Z to boost its stats by +1 when used as a Z-Move while also changing it into an Electric-type.
  • Maximum Speed allows Porygon-Z be as fast as possible at +1, while maximum Special Attack allows it to hit as hard as possible.
  • A Timid nature allows Porygon-Z to be faster than Adamant Choice Scarf Landorus-T, while Modest allows it to OHKO defensive Hippowdon with a +1 Ice Beam.
  • Adaptability is its most reliable ability, doubling the power of Thunderbolt.
  • Download has the capability to power up all of Porygon-Z's moves, though it makes it more vulnerable to Haze and Unaware than Adaptability.
  • Porygon-Z is best used late-game after its checks and Pokemon that can remove its stat boosts are removed, allowing it to comfortably set up with Z-Conversion.
  • As with most variants of Z-Conversion Porygon-Z, wallbreakers can remove special walls such as Chansey and Celesteela, while Stealth Rock setters can help break Focus Sashes and wear down opposing Pokemon to aid Porygon-Z's sweep.
  • Electric-type Porygon-Z is horribly weak to Choice Scarf Ground-types. As such, Pokemon with the ability to deal with them are absolutely necessary. Such partners include Ice Shard users such as Mamoswine and Weavile and faster Choice Scarf users with super effective coverage, such as Pheromosa and Choice Scarf Greninja.

Z-Hyper Beam.description:
• When holding Normalium Z, Z-Hyper Beam becomes a powerful STAB nuke that bypasses Hyper Beam's recharge turn. Even after its use as a Z-Move, Hyper Beam is still very threatening.
  • Nasty Plot augments Porygon-Z's Special Attack, granting it the power to break down bulky foes.
  • Ice Beam hits Ground-, Dragon-, Grass-, and most Flying-types super effectively.
  • Thunderbolt complements Ice Beam very well, dealing with Water- and Flying-types that resist Ice Beam.
  • Maximum Special Attack lets Porygon-Z deal as much damage to opponents as possible with Breakneck Blitz. 252 Speed EVs plus a Timid nature are absolutely necessary, as without Z-Conversion, Porygon-Z has no way to boost its Speed.
  • Adaptability further powers up Porygon-Z's STAB move.
  • Download allows Porygon-Z to use its coverage moves more effectively without the need to set up with Nasty Plot. However, it risks the chance of not gaining a Special Attack boost, and Porygon-Z deals less damage against Unaware users.
  • While it can be used as a sweeper late-game thanks to Nasty Plot, this Porygon-Z works well early- to mid-game, breaking through walls thanks to the aforementioned Nasty Plot and Hyper Beam.
  • Even though Porygon-Z's Breakneck Blitz is capable of breaking through many Normal-resistant foes, it still appreciates Pokemon that can deal with extremely bulky Steel-types such as Celesteela and Aegislash.
  • Setup sweepers such as Volcarona and Mega Salamence make great partners for Porygon-Z, as it can break through walls for its teammates to destroy opposing teams.

1v1.overview: Porygon-Z is an extremely strong special attacker due to its high Special Attack and Adaptability, capable of OHKOing many key threats in 1v1 such as Zygarde, Landorus-T, and Mega Charizard X. This is also aided by its access to an extremely powerful Hyper Beam; its ability to OHKO most Pokemon eliminates the main drawback of a recharge turn. A mono-Normal typing means that Porygon-Z only has one weakness, but Fighting-types such as Mega Lopunny, Sawk, and Mega Blaziken are dominant forces in the 1v1 metagame, and it also has no resistances and only one immunity, resulting in it having a lack of defensive value. Lastly, because Porygon-Z primarily relies on its Normal-type STAB moves, it is often walled by Normal-resistant and -immune Pokemon such as Magearna and Mega Tyranitar.
1v1.comments:
Other Options

Choice Specs can be used instead of Choice Scarf to increase Porygon-Z's damage output and allow it to OHKO Dragonite with Blizzard, but Z-Conversion secures the same +1 boost without locking Porygon-Z into a move. Z-Conversion Porygon-Z can run both Nasty Plot and Recover, forgoing Shadow Ball or Hyper Beam, but this set is walled by Steel-, Rock-, and Ghost-types.

Checks and Counters

Steel-types: Steel-types resist Hyper Beam and Ice Beam and can often tank Hidden Power Fire due to their bulk. Mega Aggron, Magearna, and Celesteela are big threats to Porygon-Z because they can often check or even wall it depending on its set.

Rock-types: Rock-types such as Nihilego and Mega Tyranitar resist Hyper Beam and Breakneck Blitz and can often OHKO Porygon-Z back with their STAB moves. Mega Tyranitar also resists Shadow Ball, meaning Z-Conversion sets cannot break past it.

Ghost-types: Due to their immunity to Normal, Aegislash and Mega Gengar are only damaged by Shadow Ball, which requires a turn of setup for it to become a STAB option. This means that they can easily wall and shut down Porygon-Z.

Specially Defensive Pokemon: Chansey and Mega Venusaur can all take one of Porygon-Z's attacks and either recover HP or inflict it with status. It cannot effectively break them due to Hyper Beam's recharge turn. However, they can all be overwhelmed by Nasty Plot sets.

Z-Conversion.description:
Moves

Shadow Ball hits most Pokemon neutrally and heavily damages Ghost- and Psychic-types; after a Conversion boost and Adaptability, it can OHKO a majority of the metagame such as Aegislash and Mega Slowbro. Recover enables Porygon-Z to remain healthy throughout a match so it can break bulkier foes and Sturdy users like Donphan and Golem more easily. Nasty Plot is an alternative that boosts Porygon-Z's Special Attack further so it can beat specially bulky Pokemon such as Chansey and Mega Venusaur. This can also be run instead of Hyper Beam, but Porygon-Z loses out on the raw power that it offers. Hyper Beam is Porygon-Z's strongest STAB move, capable of OHKOing a majority of the metagame due to its high Base Power when boosted by Adaptability. It can also be turned into a 200-Base Power Breakneck Blitz if the boosts from Z-Conversion aren't required. Conversion changes Porygon-Z's typing to that of its first move in Shadow Ball, providing it with resistances to Bug and Poison and two useful immunities in Normal and Fighting as well as a strong STAB move. When powered up with Normalium Z, it grants Porygon-Z a +1 boost to all its stats. Uproar can be run as an alternative to Recover in order to beat Substitute users such as Jumpluff more reliably, but losing out on the longevity of Recover makes beating bulkier Pokemon harder.

Set Details

216 Speed EVs combined with a Timid nature allow Porygon-Z to outspeed Sawk and Mega Metagross as well as slower variants of Mega Charizard X. 212 Defense EVs enable Porygon-Z to survive Mega Charizard X's Flare Blitz or Outrage as well as Mega Gyarados's Waterfall. Adaptability boosts Porygon-Z's Normal-type STAB moves and Ghost-type moves after it has used Z-Conversion, making Hyper Beam even harder to combat and Shadow Ball difficult for neutral targets to take. Normalium Z can be used for a strong Normal-type attack or to grant Porygon-Z a +1 boost to all its stats with Z-Conversion.

Usage Tips

Breakneck Blitz is notable in the absurd amounts of power it offers, alongside a follow up Hyper Beam; Porygon-Z can be sent out against bulkier Pokemon like Mega Slowbro and Primarina and proceed to OHKO or heavily damage with Breakneck Blitz. You should avoid bringing it in against a Sturdy user if it isn't running Recover, as Porygon-Z cannot break Sturdy without taking a hit, and its frailty makes this difficult. Setting up with Z-Conversion is optimal against bulkier Pokemon that Porygon-Z cannot OHKO so it can utilize its boosted Special Attack to net a KO as well as its increased defenses to take hits from them more easily. It can also stall them out with Recover. Be wary of Z-Conversion; while Porygon-Z's new Ghost typing offers resistances, it also offers a weakness to Ghost- and Dark-type moves from Pokemon such as Mega Gengar and Mega Gyarados, which a Normal-typed Porygon-Z can take more easily.

Team Options

Porygon-Z cannot adequately damage Steel-types if it's unable to set up Z-Conversion due to their resistance to Breakneck Blitz, so Ground-types such as Landorus-T and Zygarde-C and Fire-types such as Mega Charizard X and Mega Charizard Y make good partners due to their ability to reliably win these matchups. Answers to special walls are appreciated, as Porygon-Z cannot beat Chansey. As such, physical wallbreakers such as Mega Charizard X and Mega Metagross make good partners. Before a Speed boost and without a Choice Scarf, Porygon-Z has an average Speed tier, which faster threats such as Mega Charizard Y can take advantage of to OHKO it before it can attack; pairing it with faster teammates such as Mega Metagross and Mega Lopunny or bulkier Pokemon that can take a hit help deal with this. Porygon-Z is a relatively frail Pokemon and cannot take many hits; thus, bulkier partners such as Magearna and Mega Venusaur are appreciated.

Choice Scarf.description:
Moves

Hyper Beam is Porygon-Z's strongest STAB move, capable of OHKOing a majority of the metagame due to its high Base Power when boosted by Adaptability. Uproar is a secondary STAB option that doesn't have a recharge turn and as such is more reliable; it can break bulkier foes, notably non-Ghost-type Rest users like Mega Slowbro, as well as bypass Substitutes. Ice Beam enables Porygon-Z to hit Ground-types such as Landorus-T and Zygarde-C for the most damage, preventing them from setting up on a free turn granted by recharge, and Trick shuts down defensive Pokemon such as Chansey by locking them into one move and removing their defensive items. Hidden Power Fire can be run to damage Steel-types, but 1v1's main Steel-type threats, mainly Magearna and Mega Aggron, do not take enough damage from it and can OHKO or heavily damage Porygon-Z in return. It can OHKO Genesect and Durant as well as beat Ferrothorn, however. Dark Pulse can be run for coverage against Ghost-types, like Mega Gengar, with Dark Pulse offering a chance to cause foes to flinch.

Set Details

252 Special Attack EVs in combination with a Modest nature maximize Porygon-Z's offensive capabilities and make it the most threatening it can be. A Choice Scarf and 252 Speed EVs enable Porygon-Z to outspeed most of the unboosted metagame and severely damage most of it before it can attack. Adaptability boosts Porygon-Z's Normal-type STAB moves, making Hyper Beam even harder to combat.

Usage Tips

Porygon-Z should not be sent out if the opponent has a Pokemon that walls it such as Magearna or Celesteela, as it struggles to win those matchups. You should also avoid bringing it in against a Sturdy user, as the recharge turn that Hyper Beam has can grant them setup opportunities or a free chance to KO Porygon-Z. Avoid bringing it out in front of passive Z-Move users such as Pyukumuku or Mega Evolutions such as Mega Slowbro, as they are immune to Trick, and will stall out Porygon-Z's attacks. Bulkier offensive Pokemon such as Mega Gyarados cannot be OHKOed by Hyper Beam, so using Uproar to avoid the recharge turn and KO it over two turns is more beneficial.

Team Options

Porygon-Z cannot adequately damage Rock- and Steel-types due to their resistance to Hyper Beam, so Ground-types such as Landorus-T and Zygarde-C make good partners due to their ability to reliably win these matchups. Ghost-types wall Porygon-Z and can KO it, so other Ghost-types like Aegislash and Dark-types like Mega Gyarados are good partners to deal with these Pokemon. Answers to special walls are appreciated, as Porygon-Z cannot beat Chansey without relying on Trick to remove its Eviolite and recovery. As such, physical wallbreakers such as Mega Charizard X and Terrakion make good partners. Porygon-Z is a relatively frail Pokemon and cannot take many hits; thus, bulkier partners such as Magearna and Mega Venusaur are appreciated.

pu.overview: Access to Magnet Pull gives Probopass a slight niche in PU, as thanks to this ability, it can remove several bulky Steel-types from the match, such as Aggron, Metang, and Alolan Sandslash. 4x resistances to Normal and Flying are quite useful, as they allow Probopass to, for example, switch in on a Choice Band Stoutland locked into Return and an Oricorio-E's Hurricane. Probopass has a surprisingly customizable movepool, with very useful utility and coverage options such as Taunt to cripple slower walls, Earth Power for Steel-types, and Volt Switch for pivoting working very well with it. Defensively speaking, though, its 4x weaknesses to Fighting and Ground severely hamper its viability, as both types are very common in the metagame in the forms of Pokemon such as Golurk, Torterra, and Gurdurr. It also can be hit very hard by coverage moves of these types used by Pokemon that Probopass otherwise would check, such as Kangaskhan, Stoutland, and Aurorus. Probopass has no reliable recovery, making it prone to getting worn down fast against opposing teams. Even when fully invested, Probopass is often embarrassingly weak against a lot of neutral targets. However, its biggest issue is simply that trapping Steel-types is not an especially valuable niche in PU.
pu.comments:
Other Options

Toxic is an option to catch Gastrodon on the switch, which otherwise completely stops Probopass in its tracks. It can be used to cripple Pokemon such as Musharna as well, which is particularly useful because Synchronize cannot affect Probopass. However, Probopass's four-moveslot syndrome means that Toxic has a hard time being fit, as Probopass's moves are all very important to its success. A more defensive set with Sturdy is usable, but for the most part it's outclassed by Regirock, which has better offensive presence and a better typing. It also lacks Probopass's main niche as a trapper. Pain Split gives Probopass a form, albeit an unreliable one, of recovery. It fits more on bulkier sets, but such sets are less practical in general and as mentioned before Pain Split is a very unreliable way of recovery that can easily be played around.

Checks and Counters

Ground-types: Air Balloon can somewhat help Probopass's poor matchup against Ground-types, but Leftovers variants are easily KOed by strong Earthquakes from Pokemon such as Golurk, Mudsdale, and Torterra. In addition, it needs the right coverage move to deal a decent amount of damage to these Pokemon, which is somewhat hampered by Probopass's four-moveslot syndrome.

Fighting-types: Probopass's 4x weakness to Fighting coupled with a lack of firepower against them leads to it being countered by the likes of Primeape, Gurdurr, and Hitmonchan, which can revenge kill it, set up on it, or easily remove its entry hazards, respectively.

Water-types: Pokemon such as Lanturn, Ludicolo, Jellicent, and Gastrodon can easily switch into Probopass and hit back with Scald or similar moves. Lanturn and Gastrodon are also immune to Volt Switch.

Offensive Stealth Rock.description:
Moves

Flash Cannon is Probopass's STAB move of choice, allowing it to hit Pokemon such as Aurorus and Clefairy for super effective damage.
