Rotom-Wash can also burn switch-ins like Ferrothorn, Mega Latios, Mega Latias, and Tapu Bulu with Will-O-Wisp, punishing them without having to switch out. Will-O-Wisp is also great to reduce prediction, since most Pokemon that can switch into Hydro Pump or Volt Switch hate being burned. It can even run Waterium Z on its defensive set to OHKO Pokemon like Heatran and Gliscor or run a more offensive set with Electrium Z that lures in and takes out bulky targets that would otherwise pivot into it, like Toxapex, Tapu Fini, and Manaphy. However, Rotom-Wash lacks reliable recovery, so it can sometimes struggle to pivot into what it needs to in the long run, especially if Wiki Berry Rotom-Wash gets hit by Knock Off from Pokemon it's meant to check, mainly Tornadus-T. Rotom-Wash is also vulnerable to Toxic from the Pokemon it's meant to switch into, namely Heatran and Gliscor. Lastly, while its bulk is good, it isn't good enough to comfortably answer very strong wallbreakers like Tapu Lele, Mega Mawile, and Mega Medicham.
ou.comments:
Other Options

A Choice Scarf variant provides some added Speed and can cripple passive foes with Trick as well as generate momentum with Volt Switch; however, sacrificing its defensive utility is usually not worth the trade-off. An offensive set with Hydro Pump / Volt Switch / Hidden Power Fire / Defog, Waterium Z, and an EV spread of 200 HP / 252 SpA / 56 Spe is an alternative for more offensively oriented teams. Thunder Wave is an option to cripple Clefable, Heatran, and Reuniclus as well as immediately neuter offensive threats like Mega Charizard X and Volcarona.

Checks and Counters

Grass-types: Grass-type Pokemon resist both of Rotom-Wash's STAB attacks and can threaten it out with super effective attacks. While Kartana and Tapu Bulu fear a burn upon switching in, they can still effectively scare out Rotom-Wash. Ferrothorn and Tangrowth can come in on Rotom-Wash freely but can be worn down with the combination of Will-O-Wisp and Volt Switch.

Dragon-types: Kyurem-B is a terrifyingly powerful Pokemon that resists both of Rotom-Wash's STAB moves and only partially fears a burn, which can be played around by Substitute variants, as well as threaten Rotom-Wash with Earth Power thanks to Teravolt. Mega Latios similarly fears nothing from Rotom-Wash and threatens it with a 2HKO from Psychic. Garchomp similarly does not appreciate being burned, but it is capable of threatening Rotom-Wash with a +2 Continental Crush.

Pokemon That Can Bypass Levitate: Despite having access to Levitate, there are still Ground-types that can threaten Rotom-Wash. Particularly, Rotom-Wash has to watch out for Landorus-T's Smack Down or Gravity and Mold Breaker Earthquake from Excadrill and Mega Gyarados, as all are able to circumvent Levitate.

Residual Damage: Rotom-Wash's mediocre recovery means it is very susceptible to chip damage from various sources, such as Toxic from Heatran, U-turn from Tornadus-T and Landorus-T, and Stealth Rock. Keep this in mind as you try to keep Rotom-Wash healthy to check what it is needed for. Gastrodon is particularly noteworthy, as it is immune to Volt Switch and Hydro Pump and can cripple Rotom-Wash with Toxic.

Specially Defensive Pokemon: Pokemon with high special bulk like Chansey, Reuniclus, and Clefable can freely switch into Rotom-Wash, although they all fear the threat of Volt Switch. Natural Cure and Magic Guard allow the aforementioned Pokemon to shrug off burns, and both Calm Mind Clefable and Reuniclus can use Rotom-Wash as setup fodder.

Defensive.description:
Set Description

Rotom-Wash is a good Defogger thanks to its good matchup against common entry hazard setters like Landorus-T, Heatran, Mega Tyranitar, Gliscor, and Greninja and ability to keep up momentum with Volt Switch. Besides providing recovery, Pain Split can punish healthy switch-ins due to Rotom-Wash's low base HP stat, especially Chansey, which is one of the most common switch-ins to Rotom-Wash on stall teams. Will-O-Wisp cripples some of its switch-ins like Tangrowth, Ferrothorn, Kyurem-B, Tapu Bulu, and Assault Vest Magearna. Toxic can be used over Defog, Pain Split, or Will-O-Wisp to more heavily cripple switch-ins that aren't as fazed by burn, like Tangrowth, Gastrodon, Serperior, Kommo-o, and Mega Latias. However, it doesn't do anything to Steel-types that check it like Ferrothorn and Magearna.

Rotom-Wash can run a fully physically defensive or specially defensive set, depending on what threats its team needs it to check more. A physically defensive spread lets it better check the Ground-types of the tier, most notably Swords Dance Gliscor, as well as miscellaneous threats like Hawlucha, Mega Pinsir, and Mega Scizor. It also avoids the OHKO from Mega Mawile's Play Rough and Mega Medicham's High Jump Kick. Meanwhile, a specially defensive spread lets it more efficiently pivot into Battle Bond Greninja, Mega Alakazam, Tapu Koko, and offensive Heatran. Wiki Berry is an alternative to Pain Split that doesn't cost a turn to use, helping Rotom-Wash preserve momentum, pivot wallbreakers in, and switch into attacks like Greninja's Dark Pulse even when worn down, which is especially good on offensive teams. It also saves the moveslot needed for Pain Split. Waterium Z, on the other hand, lets Rotom-Wash OHKO Pokemon it otherwise couldn't like Gliscor, Heatran, Mega Medicham, and Tapu Koko while heavily damaging others like Tapu Lele, offensive Magearna, and Garchomp.

Team Options

Tornadus-T can check Grass-types like Kartana, Serperior, and Tapu Bulu, run Defog so Rotom-Wash has an extra moveslot, and switch into Mega Medicham while also forming a VoltTurn core with Rotom-Wash. Rotom-Wash pivots into Ice-type moves from Weavile and Mega Latias while also answering Heatran in return. Mega Scizor can similarly check Grass-types and form a VoltTurn core with Rotom-Wash while also checking strong Psychic-types like Mega Alakazam, Mega Latios, and Mega Latias, with Rotom-Wash answering Heatran and Tornadus-T and using Defog to aid Mega Scizor's longevity. Heatran can answer Grass-types like Kartana and Serperior, handle Fairy-types like Tapu Lele and Magearna, and spread residual damage with Stealth Rock alongside Magma Storm and Toxic. Rotom-Wash can answer opposing Heatran, Ground-types like Gliscor and Landorus-T, and Water-types like Mega Swampert and Greninja in return while pivoting Heatran in safely on some of its targets, like Magearna and Ferrothorn, to preserve its health. Ferrothorn can be a sturdier Water-resistant Pokemon and Grass-type check while spreading residual damage with entry hazards and using Knock Off, removing Leftovers to make Rotom-Wash's Volt Switch damage stick, while Rotom-Wash checks Heatran and Tornadus-T. Assault Vest Magearna has amazing synergy with the physically defensive set, taking strong special attacks from Pokemon like Mega Alakazam, Mega Diancie, Mega Latios, Tapu Lele, and opposing offensive Magearna while enjoying Rotom-Wash taking on Fire- and Ground-types. It also appreciates Rotom-Wash keeping entry hazards off the field to make up for its lack of recovery. The two form a solid backbone for offensive teams against Ash-Greninja, since Magearna can take Dark Pulse, while Rotom-Wash can take Hydro Pump and clear the Spikes it sets. Ground-types like Gliscor and Landorus-T enjoy Rotom-Wash taking Water- and Ice-type attacks for them, with Gliscor able to act as a strong wincon with Swords Dance and absorb status from Heatran, while Landorus-T sets up Stealth Rock and forms a good VoltTurn core with it. Pursuit trappers like Mega Tyranitar and Weavile can trap checks like Mega Latios, Reuniclus, and Mega Latias, with Mega Tyranitar able to set up Stealth Rock, and Weavile using Knock Off to remove bulky targets' Leftovers so Rotom-Wash's Volt Switch damage sticks. Both appreciate it pivoting them in safely with Volt Switch and taking strong Water-type attacks for them. Volcarona appreciates Rotom-Wash keeping entry hazards off the field and answering Heatran and Water-types, and it takes advantage of Volt Switch pivoting to more easily set up Quiver Dance on Pokemon like Kartana, Tapu Bulu, and Mega Latias lacking Thunder Wave.

Offensive.description:
Moves

Volt Switch helps Rotom-Wash maintain offensive momentum, limiting free switches in from Pokemon such as Chansey, Ferrothorn, Tapu Bulu, and Mega Latias. Thunder is Rotom-Wash's strongest Electric-type STAB attack and when paired with Electrium Z can heavily damage unsuspecting targets, including Toxapex, Clefable, Zapdos, and Magearna. Pain Split helps Rotom-Wash last longer so it can be more effective. Moreover, it can be especially helpful against bulkier teams, allowing Rotom-Wash to constantly pressure Pokemon such as Chansey and overall not be as easy to wear down.

Set Details

216 Speed EVs in tandem with a Timid nature allow Rotom-Wash to always outspeed Gyarados and Heatran. 184 Special Attack EVs ensure an OHKO on Celesteela and Toxapex with Electrium Z-boosted Thunder after Stealth Rock, a 2HKO on offensive Garchomp with Hydro Pump after Stealth Rock, and an OHKO on Weavile with Electrium Z-boosted Thunder. Waterium Z is also a viable option over Electrium Z for a better nuke against the likes of Garchomp, specially defensive Heatran, Tapu Koko, and Mega Tyranitar. By doing so, it is usually better to run Will-O-Wisp over Thunder, as without the Z-Crystal, Thunder is not as reliable.

Usage Tips

It is important to not carelessly waste Rotom-Wash's Z-Move. You should be patient with using the Z-Move by making sure your opponent won't anticipate and scout for it. Try to aggressively switch Rotom-Wash in on a predicted switch from a Pokemon such as Toxapex or Magearna and surprise it with its Z-Move. Lots of balance and stall teams tend to rely on a single Pokemon such as Mega Latias or a defensive Grass-type like Tangrowth to check Rotom-Wash, so focus on removing it by bringing in a counter with Volt Switch. The main attraction of this set is the great utility Rotom-Wash offers with the combination of applying constant pressure with Volt Switch and Pain Split. Setting up entry hazards and pivoting to strong wallbreakers enhances Rotom-Wash's ability to break apart teams. Keep in mind that Rotom-Wash will have trouble consistently checking Pokemon such as Heatran, Tornadus-T, and Gyarados. Be careful with hard switching it in often, as Rotom-Wash is frail and prone to being worn down, especially when Stealth Rock is up.

Team Options

Mega Scizor can switch into Grass-types that force Rotom-Wash out and form a potent VoltTurn core alongside it. Scizor draws in Heatran, Toxapex, and Celesteela, all of which Rotom-Wash can take advantage of. Additional Fire- and Flying-type checks are crucial alongside this set, as Rotom-Wash is not a reliable switch-in to the likes of Heatran, Hawlucha, and Tornadus-T. Calm Mind sweepers such as Clefable and Mega Latias are good teammates for Rotom-Wash, as it can remove surefire checks like Heatran and Toxapex, allowing them to set up and sweep a lot more easily. Clefable in particular can also aid in setting up Stealth Rock, which helps Rotom-Wash even more by getting more chip damage on switch-ins alongside Volt Switch. Rotom-Wash appreciates entry hazards to have a better chance at pressuring teams. Ferrothorn and Greninja are great partners, as they can reliably set up Spikes to help Rotom-Wash's Volt Switch be more impactful.

Electrium Z.description: For full USUM 1v1 analyses, you can check out the USUM format page.

monotype.overview:
Electric

Rotom-Wash is one of the best defensive options for Electric thanks to its decent mixed bulk, fantastic pivoting abilities with slow Volt Switches, and immunity to Ground-type moves. Its Electric / Water typing, in conjunction with Levitate, lets it wall numerous threats to Electric, such as Mamoswine and Mega Swampert. STAB Hydro Pump also gives a way for Rotom-Wash to threaten numerous Ground-types that bother Electric teams, such as Hippowdon and Sand Rush Excadrill. Access to Will-O-Wisp lets Rotom-Wash cripple various physical threats, such as Dragonite and Curse Alolan Muk, while its nice special bulk allows it to withstand strong hits from dangerous foes like Volcarona and Hydreigon. Rotom-Wash can also use Pain Split or Defog for semi-reliable recovery and additional utility to clear entry hazards and screens. Although Rotom-Wash's low Speed stat is useful for safely bringing a teammate on the field with Volt Switch, it also comes at the cost of being outsped by numerous threats like Tapu Bulu. Finally, Rotom-Wash has no reliable way to recover its HP, which means it can't recklessly pivot around and can get easily worn down.

Water

Rotom-Wash's great mixed bulk and ability Levitate makes it one of the very few Ground switch-ins that Water has access to, helping to take on wallbreakers that pressure Water teams such as Choice Band Excadrill and Swords Dance Garchomp. Unlike Mantine, one of Water's other Ground-immune Pokemon, Rotom-Wash has Volt Switch, giving it a way to keep up momentum and have offensive utility, and it lacks a weakness to Rock that Pelipper and Mantine both have, allowing it to handle EdgeQuake coverage easily. With Volt Switch, Rotom-Wash can be a strong option for offensive Water teams that still want to cover strong Ground-types. Rotom-Wash also has other rare defensive utilities in both Defog and Will-O-Wisp, enabling it to fulfill multiple roles for the team at once. In addition to taking on Ground-types, Rotom-Wash's Electric typing lets it only take neutral damage from and check Electric-types such as Choice Band Thundurus. However, in spite of being a defensive Pokemon, Rotom-Wash has no reliable recovery options and must use Pain Split if it needs recovery, meaning it can be worn down quite quickly in its role as a defensive pivot. To make its lack of reliable recovery worse, its mixed bulk isn't enough to stop strong wallbreakers like Diggersby or Z-Move users like Garchomp. Rotom-Wash also faces strong competition from Mantine, a more traditional Ground-immune wall with superior special bulk as well as access to Defog and recovery in Roost. More defensive teams will normally not favor Volt Switch's pivoting potential over the longevity of Mantine.
monotype.comments:
Other Options

Electric

A physically defensive spread can be used instead to pivot into physical attackers and survive hits from stronger Pokemon like Choice Band Dragonite and Diggersby. However, such variants are left completely open to most special attackers, while a specially defensive Rotom-Wash can threaten physical attackers with Will-O-Wisp. Toxic can be used over one of the utility options to lure and cripple defensive answers, such as Gastrodon and Seismitoad, as well as setup sweepers like Mega Charizard X. Unfortunately, giving up on two moves between Will-O-Wisp, Pain Split, and Defog would make Rotom-Wash much less useful for Electric teams, as the two former moves are unique to Rotom-Wash while Toxic can be better used by a teammate like Zapdos.

Water

Rotom-Wash can run a specially defensive spread in order to have a better matchup against Landorus and other Electric-types, but it will be less capable of handling most Ground-types such as Garchomp and Excadrill, making it a much more niche spread. Thunder Wave can be used over Defog as another double status set choice to make it even better against offensive Pokemon, but Volt Switch and Will-O-Wisp cover most offensive Pokemon already, making it hard to usually justify using over other utility options.

Checks and Counters

Electric

Grass-types: Grass-type Pokemon, such as Mega Venusaur and Celebi, comfortably switch into Rotom-Wash's STAB moves and can hit it back super effectively. On the other hand, physical Grass-types like Tapu Bulu and Breloom are threatened by Rotom-Wash's Will-O-Wisp, so they can't reliably switch into it.

Gastrodon and Seismitoad: Both of these Pokemon completely counter Rotom-Wash, as they are immune to its STAB moves and don't really care about being burned.

Dragon-types: Rotom-Wash struggles against the numerous Dragon-types in the metagame due to their typing and natural bulk. For example, Kyurem-B and Latios easily switch into Rotom-Wash's moves before dealing a great amount of damage to it, while Mega Latias and Mega Charizard X can set up on it and sweep the team.

Physical Wallbreakers: Powerful attackers like Choice Band Diggersby and Zeraora can OHKO Rotom-Wash, but they must be careful as to not get burned by Will-O-Wisp.

Mold Breaker and Teravolt Users: Due to their respective abilities, Excadrill and Kyurem-B ignore Rotom-Wash's Levitate and can threaten it with a Ground-type move.

Stallbreakers: Taunt users such as Hydreigon and Mew can prevent Rotom-Wash from using Defog or Will-O-Wisp to clear entry hazards and screens or cripple physical attackers. Those Pokemon also take minimal damage from Rotom-Wash's STAB moves.

Residual Damage: Rotom-Wash's lack of reliable recovery makes it very susceptible to Toxic and Stealth Rock. Having its Leftovers recovery canceled out by burn or sand damage can also be very detrimental for Rotom-Wash's longevity.

Walls: Since it lacks power and doesn't usually carry Toxic, certain walls like Zapdos and Normal's Eviolite core aren't threatened by Rotom-Wash at all. However, letting Rotom-Wash use Volt Switch too often to pivot out to a teammate could lead to fruitful results for the Electric team.

Water

Grass-types: Grass-types such as Mega Venusaur are normally unconcerned with most of what Rotom-Wash can do to them and can hit it super effectively. However, physical Grass-types, such as Breloom and Tapu Bulu, cannot switch into Rotom-Wash for fear of Will-O-Wisp.

Wallbreakers: Because it lacks reliable recovery and Pain Split is especially bad against less bulky offensive Pokemon, Rotom-Wash is handled by most wallbreakers such as Choice Specs Keldeo, Choice Band Diggersby, and Mega Heracross even if they are normally threatened by its moves.

Defensive Pokemon: Without Toxic, Rotom-Wash struggles to pressure defensive Pokemon such as Chansey at all, as it often lacks power, crippling status, and recovery, allowing them to switch in. They should be careful of frequently letting Rotom-Wash pivot out to a teammate, though.

Certain Electric-immune Pokemon: Pokemon such as Seismitoad, Gastrodon, and Lanturn that are unafraid of anything Rotom-Wash does can still switch in freely and prevent Rotom-Wash from pivoting out.

Poison: Poison and Toxic poison cripple Rotom-Wash, which already lacks longevity. As a result, Pokemon that occasionally carry ways to poison Rotom-Wash, such as Mantine and Celesteela, are hard for Rotom-Wash to pivot around before their moveset is scouted.

Specially Defensive (Electric).description:
Moves

Volt Switch allows Rotom-Wash to gain momentum by pivoting out into a teammate safely thanks to its low Speed stat. Hydro Pump is Rotom-Wash's way to deal with Ground-types like Hippowdon and Sand Rush Excadrill and is its strongest STAB move. Will-O-Wisp cripples physical attackers like Dragonite and Alolan Muk that Rotom-Wash couldn't seriously hurt otherwise. Pain Split allows Rotom-Wash to regain some HP, letting it tank more attacks from the opposing team, and enables Rotom-Wash to take advantage of defensive Pokemon such as Chansey by regaining most of its HP after each use thanks to Rotom-Wash's low HP stat. Defog is a nice alternative over Pain Split to clear entry hazards and screens and works well on Rotom-Wash thanks to its neutrality to Stealth Rock and immunity to Spikes and Toxic Spikes.

Set Details

The suggested EV spread and nature let Rotom-Wash be as specially defensive as possible while also enabling it to outspeed Jolly Azumarill and -1 Choice Band Victini. Leftovers is Rotom-Wash's preferred item, as it offers better longevity over the course of a long-lasting game. Wiki Berry, on the other hand, gives Rotom-Wash a single burst of healing, which can be pretty useful if Defog is used over Pain Split, as Rotom-Wash wouldn't have access to any kind of recovery otherwise. It can also recover some damage from strong moves like Hydreigon's Devastating Drake. Levitate is Rotom-Wash's only ability and grants it a much-needed immunity to Ground-type moves, Spikes, and Toxic Spikes.

Usage Tips

Rotom-Wash is one of the few defensive Pokemon on Electric, so it must be preserved throughout the game if threatening special attackers like Heatran are still alive. In fact, Rotom-Wash is best used when switched into weak moves or resisted hits before pivoting to a teammate with a slow Volt Switch to gain momentum as the opposing Pokemon switches out. Rotom-Wash can burn incoming physical attackers that threaten Electric teams and take little damage from its STAB moves, such as Dragonite and Tapu Bulu, making them much easier for Electric to deal with. In specific matchups, Rotom-Wash can be played differently. For example, against rain teams, Rotom-Wash walls both Seismitoad and Mega Swampert, so it can be switched into them without much to worry about. Against Ground teams with Landorus, it is essential that Rotom-Wash face Landorus before it can use Gravity so that it can KO it with Hydro Pump. If not, Rotom-Wash will be outsped and OHKOed by almost any Ground-type STAB move. Also, against Bug teams, Rotom-Wash must be kept healthy in order to check threats to Electric like Volcarona, since Volcarona won't 2HKO Rotom-Wash when unboosted or OHKO it when at +1. When facing defensive Pokemon, it is usually best for Rotom-Wash to Volt Switch out to a teammate that can better handle them, since most of them are too bulky to be seriously harmed by its STAB moves, and they're generally not threatened by Will-O-Wisp as much as Toxic. If Rotom-Wash is carrying Defog, don't pivot too much on enemy moves, as Rotom-Wash lacks Pain Split for recovery and Electric depends on it to clear entry hazards and screens. Finally, as a defensive Pokemon, Rotom-Wash must avoid Toxic and Knock Off as much as possible, as that would jeopardize its longevity and deny it passive recovery. If Wiki Berry is used over Leftovers, it is imperative for Rotom-Wash to not be hit by Knock Off, since that would leave it without any form of recovery whatsoever.

Team Options

Every Electric team member appreciates Rotom-Wash's ability to slowly pivot with Volt Switch and bring them safely onto the field. Physically defensive Zapdos perfectly complements Rotom-Wash, as they cover almost all of each other's weaknesses. Furthermore, Rotom-Wash and Zapdos form a reliable defensive backbone that virtually all Electric teams rely on, thanks to their utility options, recovery, and great bulk. For example, Zapdos can reliably check Tapu Bulu for Rotom-Wash, and in return, Rotom-Wash supports Zapdos by switching into Mamoswine's STAB moves. Also, either Zapdos or Rotom-Wash can run Defog to free up a slot for Pain Split on Rotom-Wash or for Toxic on Zapdos. Tapu Koko takes on problematic Dragon-types like Kyurem-B and Kommo-o with Dazzling Gleam. Additionally, if Tapu Koko carries Grass Knot, it can take on Seismitoad and Gastrodon, both of which completely counter Rotom-Wash. In return, Rotom-Wash can switch into Ground-type moves aimed at Tapu Koko and bring it safely on the field with its slow Volt Switch. Alolan Golem and Magnezone are both useful teammates that are able to trap threatening Steel-types like Excadrill and Ferrothorn for Rotom-Wash, with the former also being able to set up Stealth Rock. Rotom-Wash can even use Volt Switch to bring either trapper against Ferrothorn to reliably KO it. Zeraora is a valued partner that handily beats Normal teams and Tapu Bulu, which give a lot of problems to Rotom-Wash. In return, Rotom-Wash acts as a great defensive pivot for Zeraora, which is often forced to switch out after locking into a move. Alolan Raichu can KO Mega Venusaur, while Rotom-Wash can burn Alolan Muk, which is typically paired with Mega Venusaur on Poison. Thundurus is another physical attacker that helps Rotom-Wash take down Mega Venusaur and Normal teams. In exchange, Rotom-Wash can tank Ice-type moves aimed at Thundurus, such as Ice Shard from Mamoswine, and safely bring Thundurus on the field with its slow Volt Switch.

Defensive Pivot (Water).description:
Moves

Volt Switch allows Rotom-Wash to take advantage of its low Speed to pivot a teammate into play safely and keep up momentum. Hydro Pump is Rotom-Wash's most powerful STAB attack and gives it offensive presence. Importantly, Hydro Pump hits Ground-type Pokemon for super effective damage, preventing most of them from blocking Volt Switch. Defog removes entry hazards from the field and makes sure that Toxic Spikes cannot cripple Rotom-Wash's teammates. Will-O-Wisp is the preferred status move for Rotom-Wash, as it allows Rotom-Wash to cripple physical attackers and setup sweepers that try to boost. On teams that are especially reliant on Rotom-Wash's Defog, Pain Split can be used instead of Will-O-Wisp to make it a more reliable switch-in to physical attackers and capable of taking more attacks as it pivots out. Pain Split can also be used if the team doesn't need Rotom-Wash's Defog support. Toxic is another option that can be used with Will-O-Wisp if Defog is unneeded to cripple specific defensive checks in Seismitoad, Porygon2, and Zapdos, along with many other walls.

Set Details

The EV spread and Bold nature maximize Rotom-Wash's physical bulk while minimizing Stealth Rock damage and ensuring it outspeeds Jolly Azumarill and defensive Landorus-T. Other EV spreads with more Speed, such as 248 HP / 40 Def / 220 Spe, can be used to allow Rotom-Wash to outspeed Pokemon such as Diggersby and Breloom; however, the lost Defense will make it more difficult for Rotom-Wash to check these Pokemon. Leftovers is useful for improving Rotom-Wash's longevity over a long game. Iapapa Berry can be used instead to gain a one-time burst of healing, which can come in handy against attacks like Breloom's Bullet Seed if Rotom-Wash needs to burn it. Levitate is Rotom-Wash's only ability, granting it a valuable immunity to Ground-type attacks, Spikes, and Toxic Spikes.

Usage Tips

Rotom-Wash should primarily be used to switch into attacks for its teammates before pivoting out again with Volt Switch. While Ground-types can block Rotom-Wash's Volt Switch, the threat of Hydro Pump and Will-O-Wisp can typically keep most of them from switching in or staying in against it. However, because Gastrodon and Seismitoad are immune to Hydro Pump, they are big threats to Rotom-Wash and it should typically double switch out when you expect them to come in. Rotom-Wash still needs to be careful around other Electric-immune Pokemon such as Thundurus-T, as they can freely switch into Volt Switch and threaten to use a Volt Switch of their own. However, be careful with letting Rotom-Wash take more powerful hits when it switches in, as its lack of reliable recovery prevents it from being a switch-in to wallbreakers. Whenever the opponent has set entry hazards, try to bring Rotom-Wash into play to remove them. If possible, try to switch it in as Stealth Rock is being set, as Rotom-Wash hates taking even minor residual damage. For the same reason, be sure to avoid letting Rotom-Wash get poisoned or badly poisoned, as it will be much easier to wear down. Because Leftovers helps counteract the chip damage it inevitably will take, avoid Knock Off users. Alolan Muk is a particularly dangerous Knock Off user, as its Poison Touch ability can allow it to poison Rotom-Wash and simultaneously remove Leftovers. If it's running Toxic itself, Rotom-Wash should typically hide it to surprise walls that do not expect to get crippled. It can also be used to put setup sweepers on a timer if Will-O-Wisp is incapable of stopping them. Otherwise, Rotom-Wash should usually avoid contesting other defensive Pokemon, as it cannot afford to take a status move and has no reliable recovery. That being said, Pain Split should be used mainly against other defensive Pokemon, as Rotom-Wash's low base HP makes it especially good at healing against them.

Team Options

Thanks to Levitate, Rotom-Wash makes a fantastic teammate for Water teams that are typically threatened by the strong Ground-type attackers in Excadrill and Landorus-T but prefer to have the offensive presence that other defensive Ground checks lack. Choice Scarf Greninja with U-turn can form a strong VoltTurn core with Rotom-Wash and also runs Gunk Shot, making it a good check to Grass-types. In addition to this, Greninja can revenge kill many of the powerful attackers that Rotom-Wash cannot check defensively, such as Choice Band Dragonite and Diggersby. Wallbreakers such as Mega Sharpedo and Choice Specs Keldeo are good options to receive Volt Switch's free switch, as they can break many of the walls that try to stop Rotom-Wash. Setup sweepers such as Gyarados and Mega Slowbro are also very capable of taking advantage of the momentum that Volt Switch provides, as Rotom-Wash can bring them onto the field against Pokemon they can set up on. Gyarados is especially notable for being able to beat Mega Venusaur and other Grass-types that Rotom-Wash cannot deal with. Good switch-ins to Grass-types are often needed because Rotom-Wash will often pivot out of them; Toxapex, Empoleon, and Sap Sipper Azumarill are especially great teammates for this purpose. Toxapex and Empoleon are notable for setting Toxic Spikes and Stealth Rock, respectively, which can help cripple and chip at Pokemon as they are forced out by Rotom-Wash. In addition to its unique Grass immunity, Sap Sipper Azumarill can Perish trap the walls that Rotom-Wash can't handle, such as Chansey. On more defensive teams, Alomomola's use of huge Wishes and Regenerator makes it another good defensive pivot option that helps keep Rotom-Wash very healthy.

vgc2018.overview:
• Rotom-Wash, once one of the top dogs of VGC in years prior, has rather fallen from grace. The introduction of Z-Moves and Island Guardians have made Rotom-Wash's already somewhat mediocre bulk more noticeable, and Tapu Fini's Misty Terrain has made Rotom-Wash's support moveset less useful.

  • However, Rotom-Wash still has a great typing with only one weakness, Grass, and a myriad of resistances; its ability also grants it an immunity to Ground.

  • Rotom-Wash is no slouch offensively either; Water and Electric coverage backed by 105 Special Attack hits many popular Pokemon for super effective damage.

  • Rotom-Wash faces stiff competition as a bulky Water-type with Tapu Fini, and as an Electric-type with Zapdos, both of which are overall better at their jobs. This can make it difficult to justify the use of Rotom-Wash on a team.

  • Rotom-Wash’s only Water-type move is Hydro Pump, which relies on an iffy 80% accuracy to hit.

Offensive Support.description:
• Hydro Pump is essential to all Rotom-Wash movesets, as it is Rotom-Wash's only Water-type move.

  • Thunderbolt is a reliable Electric-type STAB move with decent power.

  • Will-O-Wisp is great for crippling the many physical attackers in this metagame, but the introduction of Tapu Fini and its Misty Surge ability has made this unreliable.

  • Electroweb is a great option for speed control, offering accuracy and efficacy under Misty Terrain over Thunder Wave.

  • Protect is always very useful in VGC, as it allows stalling through weather and terrains, as well as capitalizing on double targets by allowing Rotom-Wash’s partner to take out a threat while it defends itself.

  • Wiki Berry greatly extends Rotom-Wash’s longevity by providing a one-time HP boost. Alternatively, Sitrus Berry could be used for its far greater window of activation.

  • Waterium Z is great for upping Rotom-Wash’s offensive presence with a powerful and 100% accurate Water-type STAB move.

  • The defensive nature and EVs let Rotom-Wash survive a multitude of powerful attacks, including Jolly Mega Metagross' Zen Headbutt in Psychic Terrain, an Adamant Mega Kangaskhan's Double Edge, -1 Adamant Kartana's Leaf Blade, and -1 Adamant Tapu Bulu's Horn Leech. It also ensures that Rotom-Wash avoids a 2HKO by Jolly Tyranitar's Rock Slide with sandstorm damage, an OHKO by Timid Mega Charizard Y’s Solar Beam in sun, and a 2HKO by 252 Atk Incineroar Darkest Lariat. The rest is dumped in Special Attack, with the one point leftover put in Speed.

  • If running Electroweb, an alternate spread is 252 HP / 44 Def / 52 SpA / 60 SpD / 100 Spe with a Modest nature. This outspeeds base 110s after they're hit with Electroweb and 2HKOes both 252 HP / 100 SpD Assault Vest Incineroar and 252 HP Milotic, at the cost of fainting to Mega Charizard Y’s Solar Beam. The rest is dumped in Special Defense.

  • Rotom-Wash is very flexible when it comes to EVs; adjust them to suit your team.

  • Assault Vest is another viable item, especially since Tapu Fini was introduced. For Assault Vest Rotom-Wash, a set of Electroweb, Hydro Pump, Thunderbolt, and Volt Switch is recommended.

  • Reflect is a good alternative to Will-O-Wisp, if your team is really struggling with Tapu Fini.

  • Ally Switch can be used in place of Protect, as Rotom-Wash has an incredibly useful typing that allows it to utilize Ally Switch well. It also has the potential to catch your opponents off guard, as Ally Switch is relatively uncommon.

  • Use Rotom-Wash as a straightforward pivot. Switch it in on resisted attacks and start attacking, or force the opponent to switch through its typing.

  • Many Pokemon pair well with Rotom-Wash. Landorus-T is a great partner, as Rotom-Wash handily removes Flying- and Water-types and is immune to its Earthquake. Steel-types like Metagross and Ferrothorn also appreciate Rotom-Wash, as it handles Fire- and Ground-types easily. Fire-types can deal with Rotom-Wash’s only weakness, Grass, and appreciate the annihilation of Water-, Ground-, and Rock-types.

  • When running Will-O-Wisp an Island Guardian on your team other than Tapu Fini is necessary to remove Misty Terrain, which denies Rotom-Wash’s ability to burn.

battlespotsingles.overview:
Rotom-Wash has an incredible typing that, when paired with Levitate, only makes it weak to Grass-type attacks. It's one of the best users of Volt Switch in the game, and it has plenty of versatility to use it in different ways, such as on defensive sets, offensive sets, Choice Specs sets, and Choice Scarf sets. However, Rotom-Wash's mediocre stats force it to focus on being either offensive or defensive, never being able to be both at the same time.

Below are some sample sets. These sets are likely to be standard, but they will be expanded upon and updated as the metagame progresses.

Bulky.description:
• Hydro Pump is Rotom-Wash's main STAB move, while Volt Switch allows it to escape the clutches of its foes, especially since most Ground-types don't want to risk getting hit by Hydro Pump.
  • Will-O-Wisp is great for crippling physical attackers such as Garchomp and Mega Salamence.
  • Thunderbolt is a good Electric-type attack for when you don't want to switch out.
  • With the given EV spread, a Sitrus Berry, and a Bold nature, Rotom-Wash has an easier time against physical attackers such as Mega Salamence and Mamoswine. A Wiki Berry is a riskier alternative, giving Rotom-Wash 50% recovery at 25% health.
  • A more offensive spread is feasible, dealing much more damage with Hydro Pump and Volt Switch. You can use this with Waterium Z to always hit Hydro Pump at least once. Hydro Vortex even has a 56% chance of OHKOing Garchomp. Note that going the more offensive route gives Mega Salamence a good chance of 2HKOing Rotom-Wash with a boosted Double-Edge.
  • Don't be too reckless with Rotom-Wash switch-ins, as even defensive variants take a serious amount of damage from boosted physical attackers such as Garchomp. Switch into threats that can't deal much damage to it such as Mamoswine and Celesteela.
  • You'll need a check to Grass-types such as Ferrothorn, Mega Venusaur, and Tapu Bulu, which are all big threats to Rotom-Wash. While less common, special attacking Dragon-types such as Hydreigon and Latias also have little to fear from Rotom-Wash.

Choice Specs.description:
• With a Choice Specs, Hydro Pump deals much more damage than usual, OHKOing Tapu Koko and 2HKOing Aegislash, Mega Charizard X, and even Porygon2 90% of the time.
  • Volt Switch is important for maintaining momentum against the opponent's switch-ins.
  • Trick allows Rotom-Wash to cripple defensive Pokemon such as Ferrothorn and Chansey.
  • Hidden Power Ice is Rotom-Wash's only way of 2HKOing Tapu Bulu, while Thunderbolt is useful if you want to use an Electric-type attack without switching out, and it OHKOes physically defensive Celesteela, unlike Volt Switch.
  • The given EV spread and nature maximize Rotom-Wash's power and bulk, but a Timid nature with 220 Speed EVs to outspeed Jolly Mega Gyarados before it boosts is also possible.
  • Grass-types are a huge problem for Rotom-Wash, such as Ferrothorn, Mega Venusaur, and Tapu Bulu, so make sure to prepare for these threats.

Choice Scarf.description:
Moves

  • Volt Switch works well with Choice Scarf, often letting Rotom-Wash throw out an attack and switch out without getting hit.
  • Hydro Pump is the standard STAB attack that deals much more damage than Volt Switch.
  • Trick gives Rotom-Wash a weapon against bulky Pokemon such as Tapu Bulu and Ferrothorn.
  • Hidden Power Ice deals serious damage to Garchomp and Mega Salamence, but Will-O-Wisp works great against physical attackers once Choice Scarf has been Tricked. Thunderbolt lets Rotom-Wash stay in, which is helpful against the likes of Celesteela and revenge killing weakened Mega Charizard Y.
  • A Timid nature ensures Choice Scarf Rotom-Wash outspeeds Pheromosa and a Mega Gyarados that has used Dragon Dance once.
  • Grass-types are a huge problem, especially Tapu Bulu, which Rotom-Wash can no longer 2HKO. Mega Venusaur is an even bigger problem, since it's immune to Trick. All teams that use Rotom-Wash must find ways to check them.

pu.overview: Rotom-Frost is a solid offensive threat by virtue of its decent stats, diverse utility movepool, and potent STAB combination that targets the majority of the tier neutrally or super effectively. Most notably, Rotom-Frost makes for an effective user of Defog, as it bears a fantastic matchup against common entry hazard setters such as Mudsdale and Qwilfish. Rotom-Frost's Speed tier is also of value, as it puts it above prominent Pokemon such as Stoutland and Skuntank, making it highly threatening against bulky offense teams without proper switch-ins. Rotom-Frost can also run a decent Choice Scarf set that can revenge kill a multitude of Pokemon while still utilizing its good selection of utility moves. Unfortunately, the Pokemon that do outspeed Rotom-Frost, such as Lycanroc, Primeape, and Simisear, are all considerable threats, as they possess super effective STAB moves against it. Additionally, while Levitate grants Rotom-Frost an immunity to Spikes and Toxic Spikes, a weakness to Stealth Rock combined with its low HP and inconsistent forms of recovery harms its viability as a Defog user, limiting what it can come in on if Stealth Rock is up. Lastly, though Rotom-Frost can pivot out of most unfavorable matchups with Volt Switch, it struggles to break past most specially bulky Pokemon such as Type: Null, Clefairy, and Audino. Lanturn notably serves as a complete stop to Rotom-Frost due to its resistance to Blizzard and ability to punish Volt Switch with Volt Absorb.
pu.comments:
Other Options

Electrium Z is a viable alternative to Icium Z that turns Thunderbolt into Gigavolt Havoc, breaking through Pokemon like Aurorus and Alolan Sandslash with much more ease. Substitute can be used in conjunction with Pain Split to avoid status and pressure bulkier teams, as it allows Rotom-Frost to safely recover health off of the likes of Audino and Lanturn, but having to give up Defog takes away Rotom-Frost's major niche. Hidden Power Fighting targets Aurorus and Alolan Sandslash similarly to Electrium Z, but it has very few targets otherwise. Toxic cripples switch-ins such as Audino and Lanturn by putting them on a timer, but it provides little other use and is difficult to fit into sets.

Checks and Counters

Specially Bulky Pokemon: Dedicated special walls like Audino, Lanturn, and Type: Null take pitiful amounts of damage from Rotom-Frost's attacks, though they must be cautious of Trick from the Choice Scarf set. Lanturn in particular acts as a hard counter to Rotom-Frost, since it possesses a resistance to Blizzard and an immunity to its Electric-type moves. Assault Vest Hitmonchan and Eelektross can't take repeated hits, and the former must be cautious of Will-O-Wisp, but they can soak up any one hit from full health and retaliate with Drain Punch and Flamethrower, respectively. Hitmonchan can remove entry hazards, while Eelektross can use Volt Switch to generate momentum in the event that Rotom-Frost is forced out. Calm Mind Clefairy can also use Rotom-Frost as setup fodder, though it doesn't like taking Subzero Slammer damage beforehand.

Revenge Killers: Rotom-Frost sets lacking Choice Scarf fail to outpace the likes of Primeape, Lycanroc, and Simisear, which can all obliterate it with their super effective STAB moves. The latter two can potentially use their respective setup moves if they manage to force Rotom-Frost out.

Residual Damage: Due to Rotom-Frost's inconsistent forms of recovery, low HP, and weakness to Stealth Rock, it's prone to getting worn down when attempting to remove Stealth Rock with Defog.

Offensive Defog.description:
Moves

Thunderbolt works as an alternative Electric-type STAB move that doesn't force Rotom-Frost to switch out and has increased damage output against the likes of Jellicent and Articuno. Will-O-Wisp cripples switch-ins to Rotom-Frost such as Assault Vest Crabominable and Hitmonchan by causing residual damage and severely weakening their attacks. Pain Split compensates for Rotom-Frost's lack of reliable recovery by healing off damage against switch-ins with high HP stats like Audino and Lanturn.

Set Details

Icium Z converts Blizzard into Subzero Slammer, dealing high damage to targets like Stoutland and Gurdurr while boasting perfect accuracy. Alternatively, Iapapa Berry acts as one-time health recovery outside of Pain Split when at low health and can be activated through Stealth Rock and residual damage. Note that sets using Iapapa Berry should run the 4 remaining EVs in HP to activate the item after three rounds of Stealth Rock damage.

Usage Tips

Rotom-Frost finds ample opportunities to revenge kill Pokemon like Jellicent and Oricorio-G or remove entry hazards throughout most of a match. Rotom-Frost can pivot into moves like Mudsdale's Earthquake, as well as into weaker entry hazard setters such as Qwilfish, in order to fire off a powerful attack or remove entry hazards upon a forced switch. Avoid reckless switching if Stealth Rock is on the field, as Rotom-Frost can easily by worn down by it despite its role as a Defogger. However, Iapapa Berry variants of Rotom-Frost can periodically switch into Stealth Rock in order to activate their item and heal themselves. Volt Switch should be used generously to pivot out of Pokemon that check Rotom-Frost like Audino and Clefairy, dealing a slight amount of damage and providing momentum, which gives Rotom-Frost's team the upper hand. Rotom-Frost's utility moves can be used effectively against Pokemon that may attempt to pivot into it; Assault Vest Crabominable and Hitmonchan are greatly crippled by Will-O-Wisp, whereas Rotom-Frost can gain health off of Pokemon like Lanturn and Audino through Pain Split. Icium Z is best utilized to severely weaken or even OHKO bulkier Pokemon that Blizzard misses out on, like Eelektross and Stoutland. It's also helpful in situations where Blizzard's poor accuracy can potentially jeopardize Rotom-Frost's ability to take out foes such as Golurk and Drampa.

Team Options

Rotom-Frost can form an excellent offensive core with physical wallbreakers and setup sweepers such as Stoutland, Choice Band Skuntank, and Lycanroc, as it highly appreciates their ability to break past Clefairy and Audino and can dispatch the likes of Mudsdale and Tangela in return. Stoutland and Skuntank are notably able to chip Lanturn with Pursuit. Gurdurr can also remove the items of Pokemon like Clefairy and Lanturn with Knock Off while being a reliable switch-in to threats to Rotom-Frost such as Lycanroc and Hitmonchan. Pokemon like Primeape and Scyther can be paired with Rotom-Frost to create a VoltTurn core, increasing the amount of momentum its team has, and they can be brought in more often due to Rotom-Frost's ability to remove entry hazards. Rotom-Frost can also break down Jellicent and Oricorio-E to support these Pokemon. Other Pokemon like Alolan Persian and Type: Null similarly operate as pivots, but they can more safely bring Rotom-Frost into play due to the former's stat reductions and the latter's low Speed. Alolan Persian's Z-Parting Shot can also bring Rotom-Frost up to full health, while Type: Null can lure in Pokemon for Rotom-Frost to take advantage of such as Carracosta and Oricorio-G. Although somewhat counterintuitive with Defog, entry hazard setters such as Qwilfish and Omastar are capable of wearing down bulky switch-ins to Rotom-Frost like Audino and Lanturn while putting Pokemon like Stoutland and Abomasnow in range of Subzero Slammer. Secondary entry hazard removers such as Hitmonchan and Kabutops appreciate Rotom-Frost's ability to break down Pokemon like Jellicent and Tangela while compensating for its inability to use Defog in the face of threats like Simisear and Lycanroc.

Choice Scarf.description:
Moves

Trick is able to cripple specially defensive Pokemon such as Audino, Lanturn, and Type: Null that might switch in on Rotom-Frost when it doesn't require the added Speed provided by the item. Defog can let Rotom-Frost remove entry hazards in an emergency, though the option isn't very reliable, since Rotom-Frost is weak to Stealth Rock and would rather not be locked in a status move most of the time.

Set Details

Choice Scarf allows Rotom-Frost to outspeed Pokemon like Oricorio-E, non-Choice Scarf Dodrio, and Silvally-Fairy, granting it its ability to check a big portion of the tier and function as a reliable revenge killer. A Timid nature allows Rotom-Frost to outspeed +2 Modest Omastar as well as other Choice Scarf users like Skuntank and Kabutops.

Usage Tips

Choice Scarf Rotom-Frost should try to function as a revenge killer and check to many Pokemon such as Oricorio-G, Kabutops, and Alolan Persian thanks to its unresisted coverage and formidable Speed. If the opposing team lacks a solid counter such as Lanturn or Audino, this set can be utilized early-game to soften up foes for a late-game cleaner. Rotom-Frost is even able to break through some less bulky specially defensive Pokemon such as Eelektross thanks to its high Special Attack and BoltBeam coverage. Since Rotom-Frost is able to threaten Ground-types such as Mudsdale and Golurk, predict well on when to use Blizzard and when to use Volt Switch; once you successfully predict a Ground-type switch-in by using Blizzard or those Pokemon have been removed by other teammates, Rotom-Frost will be able to use its Electric-type STAB moves freely. Bluffing a non-Choice Scarf set can turn Rotom-Frost into an even more threatening revenge killer late-game if the opposing team doesn't have a faster Choice Scarf user like Primeape or a priority user such as Gurdurr. Utilizing Trick wh​en Rotom-Frost doesn't re​quire the added Speed is a valuable way of crippling expected switch-ins such as Lanturn, Assault Vest Crabominable, and Cryogonal.

Team Options

Fighting-type answers such as Oricorio-E, Victreebel, and Tangela are able to check or counter Pokemon such as Gurdurr and Choice Scarf Primeape, effectively threatening some of the most common revenge killers for Choice Scarf Rotom-Frost. In return, Rotom-Frost cripples their checks like Cryogonal and Lanturn with Trick. Other pivots such as Alolan Persian, Eelektross, and Primeape can form a VoltTurn core with Rotom-Frost to help maintain momentum and bring in offensive threats. Pokemon such as Stoutland, Lycanroc, and Kangaskhan are able to threaten slower special walls such as Audino and Lanturn, even being able to Pursuit trap them in the case of Stoutland. In return, Rotom-Frost is able to threaten physical walls such as Mudsdale and Tangela, as well as being able to bring these Pokemon in safely through Volt Switch. Entry hazard setters like Mudsdale and Qwilfish are able to support Rotom-Frost by effectively wearing down Pokemon such as Eelektross and Crabominable with Stealth Rock, Spikes, and Toxic. They're also able to counter or threaten Choice Scarf Primeape, while Rotom-Frost checks Pokemon such as Victreebel and Jellicent. Due to its Stealth Rock weakness, more reliable hazard removes such as Skuntank, Alolan Sandslash, and Silvally-Fairy are valuable partners for Rotom-Frost. Skuntank and Alolan Sandslash appreciate Rotom-Frost's ability to check Ground-types, while Silvally-Fairy is also able to create a VoltTurn core with Parting Shot and check Fighting-types such as Primeape and Gurdurr.​

monotype.overview:
Ice

Rotom-Frost is a solid option for Ice teams thanks to its ability to cripple physical attackers like Mega Scizor and Jirachi with Will-O-Wisp. Its dual typing lets it switch into Steel-type attacks from Choice Scarf Excadrill and Jirachi and burn them. Access to Volt Switch allows Rotom-Frost to keep momentum and switch to an offensive teammate like Kyurem-B, Alolan Sandslash, or Mamoswine. Additionally, it fills the role of an entry hazard remover for Ice teams with Defog, which is especially important to a type generally weak to Stealth Rock. It also takes pressure off other hazard-removing teammates like Alolan Sandslash and Avalugg. However, its HP isn't high enough to keep it safe from wallbreakers like Diggersby and Victini. Its best form of recovery is Pain Split, which is largely dependent on the opponent's HP, making it an inconsistent means of recovering health. Rotom-Frost's Stealth Rock weakness and mediocre recovery also result in it being worn down very quickly when it switches in, hindering its effectiveness as an entry hazard remover. Lastly, its nonexistent offensive presence leaves it unable to do anything to offensive Pokemon like Latios and Nidoking.
monotype.comments:
Other Options

Ice

Choice Scarf can be used to make Rotom-Frost a fast pivot capable of revenge killing Mega Aerodactyl and Keldeo. However, without defensive investment, it fails to survive a +2 Bullet Punch from Mega Scizor. Toxic is able to slowly wear down opposing walls such as Porygon2 and Swampert, but Will-O-Wisp is more valuable to cripple physical setup sweepers like Mega Scizor, Bisharp, and Mega Gallade. Without Will-O-Wisp, Rotom-Frost's team would require a separate Mega Scizor check such as Lapras or Walrein.

Checks and Counters

Ice

Super Effective Attacks: Victini, Mega Diancie, and Mega Gallade are all capable of OHKOing Rotom-Frost with their super effective STAB moves.

Ground-types: Despite being immune to Ground-type attacks with Levitate, Rotom-Frost does not usually carry an attacking move that can hit Ground-types, leaving it unable to do much of anything against Ground-types like Swampert, Gastrodon, and Nidoking.

Wallbreakers: Diggersby and Landorus are able to take advantage of Rotom-Frost's mediocre bulk and OHKO it.

Specially Defensive Pokemon: Chansey, Zapdos, and Cradily can easily survive any of Rotom-Frost's attacks and wear it down with Toxic.

Residual Damage: Rotom-Frost's underwhelming recovery in Pain Split combined with its Stealth Rock weakness leaves it worn down very quickly.

Bulky Pivot (Ice).description:
Moves

Volt Switch is Rotom-Frost's main attacking move and is used to pivot out and generate momentum for offensive teammates like Kyurem-B and Weavile. Will-O-Wisp is important for crippling physical attackers like Mega Scizor and Excadrill. Pain Split allows Rotom-Frost to stay healthy throughout the match and weakens foes by reducing their HP. Defog is a good option for removing entry hazards such as Stealth Rock that threaten Ice teams. Hidden Power Fire can also be used to defeat Steel-types like Mega Scizor and Ferrothorn.

Set Details

252 EVs in HP are used to make Rotom-Frost as generally bulky as possible. The Speed investment is used to outspeed Jolly Breloom and Jolly Bisharp and burn them, mitigating their priority attacks. The remaining EVs are put into Defense with a Bold nature to augment Rotom-Frost's physical bulk. Leftovers is the preferred item, giving Rotom-Frost passive recovery and letting it survive longer. Levitate is useful for switching into Ground-type attacks and either restoring health with Pain Split or crippling the opposing Pokemon with Will-O-Wisp.

Usage Tips

Despite Rotom-Frost's role as a physical tank, it's best not to switch it in against wallbreakers such as Diggersby and Hydreigon, since its defensive stats are only decent. Preserve Rotom-Frost's health so it can check physically offensive Pokemon like Mega Scizor and Jirachi with Will-O-Wisp, as well as use Defog more often. Try switching Rotom-Frost in on the turn the opponent sets up Stealth Rock in order to mitigate unnecessary damage, especially against Stealth Rock setters that Rotom-Frost can beat if carrying Hidden Power Fire, such as Jirachi, Skarmory, and Ferrothorn. Predict when special walls like Chansey and Zapdos will try to switch into Rotom-Frost and use Volt Switch to gain the necessary momentum for an offensive teammate. Similarly, try to predict when an offensive Pokemon like Latios or Victini tries to switch in so that you can bring in Weavile to trap them with Pursuit. If using Defog, make sure to use it very often to prevent Stealth Rock and Toxic Spikes from affecting Rotom-Frost's teammates. Avoid status conditions like Toxic, since they can wear down Rotom-Frost faster than it can recover health with Pain Split.

Team Options

Every Pokemon on Ice teams appreciates Rotom-Frost's ability to check Steel-types like Mega Scizor, Ferrothorn, and Excadrill. Kyurem-B can beat defensive Pokemon like Mega Venusaur and Zapdos that Rotom-Frost can't do much of anything against, as well as check Ground-types like Diggersby and Nidoking that are immune to Volt Switch. Alolan Ninetales can set up Aurora Veil for Rotom-Frost, allowing it to switch in more safely against Mega Scizor and Excadrill. It can also check Fighting-types like Keldeo and Buzzwole. Alolan Sandslash is a fast sweeper under hail that appreciates the momentum Rotom-Frost provides for it with Volt Switch. It also becomes free to run Swords Dance with Rotom-Frost filling the role of a hazard remover and can set up against foes Rotom-Frost burns. Mamoswine can revenge kill Rotom-Frost's checks such as Garchomp and Landorus, as well as Steel-types that Rotom-Frost can't do much damage against like Heatran and Magnezone. Avalugg is a defensive entry hazard remover that can switch into physical attackers like Heracross and Infernape that Rotom-Frost can't take many hits from. Piloswine can switch into Rock-type attacks from Nihilego and Mega Diancie for Rotom-Frost thanks to its secondary Ground typing. It can also wear down opposing defensive Pokemon like Porygon2 with Toxic. Weavile can trap Psychic-types like Victini and Latios with Pursuit and appreciates Rotom-Frost's Volt Switch bringing it in safely. Cloyster can take advantage of burned physical attackers to set up and sweep with Shell Smash.

pu.overview: Rotom-Fan has a niche because of its good defensive Electric / Flying typing, which gives it the ability to check common threats such as Oricorio-G, Gurdurr, Scyther, and Swanna. Its movepool, which includes moves such as Will-O-Wisp and Defog, gives it some more utility as a defensive Pokemon. Although it's one of the few relevant hazard removers that are immune to both Spikes and Toxic Spikes, its weakness to Stealth Rock and lack of reliable recovery hinder its ability to switch in, which interferes with its role as a Defogger. In addition, it's pressured by common hazard setters like Regirock and Focus Sash Omastar. Weaknesses to prevalent Rock- and Ice-type moves further undermine its ability to check standard Fighting-types like Primeape and Hitmonchan. Furthermore, Oricorio-E is another notable adversary; despite Oricorio-E's slightly lower bulk, Taunt is its main selling point over Rotom-Fan, permitting Oricorio-E to shut down defensive hazard setters such as Mudsdale – something Rotom-Fan cannot do. On the offensive side, it is likewise overshadowed by Oricorio-E due to the latter's access to Hurricane, Roost, Taunt, Calm Mind, as well as Defog. As an offensive pivot, it is outclassed by Eelektross and Rotom-Frost, which have more coverage options that can be used to threaten counters. As a result of its numerous flaws, Rotom-Fan is often considered to be an unconventional Electric-type pick in general, but it finds a small place in the tier with its typing and defensive capability. It also faces competition from Lanturn, as Lanturn has an immunity to Electric-type moves and a resistance to Ice-type moves, greater special bulk, and access to Heal Bell. It should be kept in mind that having both Will-O-Wisp and Defog on the same moveset is Rotom-S's only niche over the previously mentioned Pokemon and is, for the most part, the only reason to use it.
pu.comments:
Other Options

An alternate EV spread of 248 HP / 192 Def / 68 SpD permits Rotom-Fan to avoid the 2HKO from Primeape's Stone Edge and Hitmonchan's Ice Punch after Leftovers recovery. Rest + Chesto Berry is a possible recovery option, but it can only effectively be used once, subsequently forfeiting its item slot; since Rotom-Fan does not have the room for Sleep Talk, it is not suggested either, since a sleeping Rotom-Fan cannot serve its primary role of being a Defogger. Rocky Helmet is another option for an item but it is generally inferior to Leftovers or Iapapa Berry, which supplement Rotom-Fan's recovery. It can get a little chip damage on physical attackers like Kangaskhan but eliminates its recovery altogether unless Pain Split is used. Specially defensive Rotom-Fan can be used, but is largely outshined by Lanturn in this role. Choice Scarf is a possible but unrecommended set that is overshadowed by other Electric-types such as Rotom-Frost, which has a better STAB combination. An offensive Defog set can be utilized, but it is outclassed by Oricorio-E, which can use a much stronger Flying-type STAB move in Hurricane, has reliable recovery in Roost, and has higher Speed. Swanna is another Fighting-type check and Defogger that overshadows Rotom-Fan in speed and offensive prowess. Substitute + Pain Split is yet another option Rotom-Fan can run. Toxic and Thunder Wave can be run too, as they enable Rotom-Fan to cripple its checks. However, Substitute, Toxic, and/or Thunder Wave are usually less useful and would mean that Rotom-Fan would have to replace a much more valuable utility move.

Checks and Counters

Electric-types: Lanturn is Rotom-Fan's greatest downfall. It not only prevents Rotom-Fan from pivoting, but it actually heals itself through Volt Absorb and takes advantage of Rotom-Fan's inability to deal significant damage to it. In general, offensive Electric-types take of advantage Rotom-Fan; examples include Rotom-Frost, Alolan Raichu, and Eelektross. The most Rotom-Fan can do is pivot against them as they come in.

Specially Defensive Pokemon: Walls such as Clefairy and Audino can comfortably take all of Rotom-Fan's attacks and retaliate with Toxic or provide clerical support for their team. Clefairy can also spam Stealth Rock or set up with Calm Mind.

Ice-types: Powerful Ice-type wallbreakers such as Abomasnow, Cryogonal, and Aurorus will obliterate all Rotom-Fan sets. On the other hand, Rotom-Fan can threaten the former with STAB Air Slash.

Rock-types: Regirock can use Toxic on Rotom-Fan and proceed to set up Stealth Rock in spite of Rotom-Fan's numerous attempts to remove them, stalling Rotom-Fan until it succumbs to poison. Faster Rock-types like Lycanroc and Kabutops will either OHKO or easily 2HKO Rotom-Fan.

Defensive Pivot.description:
Moves

Volt Switch is the preferred STAB Electric-type attack, as it enables Rotom-Fan to generate momentum for the team. Will-O-Wisp can be used to burn common physical attackers such as Golurk and Primeape, reducing the damage of their moves and neutralizing them. It can also be used to pressure Rotom-Fan's checks such as Mudsdale. Defog allows Rotom-Fan to remove any hazards. Thus, it expands Rotom-Fan's role as a defensive pivot. Though unreliable, Pain Split can heal Rotom-Fan while damaging the foe simultaneously. Because of Rotom-Fan's naturally low HP stat, this move can be fairly good. It can be used offensively as well, severely denting its counters and possibly even putting them in knockout range.

Set Details

48 Speed EVs allow Rotom-Fan to outspeed Jolly Aggron and maximum invested neutral-natured base 60s such as Abomasnow and Pawniard. Iapapa Berry gives Rotom-Fan a one-time heal of 50% of its maximum health, which will activate after Rotom-Fan switches into Stealth Rock three times. Alternatively, Leftovers is a passive form of recovery that lets Rotom-Fan avoid the 2HKO from Primeape's Stone Edge and Hitmonchan's Ice Punch but is otherwise negligible.

Usage Tips

Rotom-Fan should be brought in early-game, as it can cripple common entry hazard setters such as Regirock with Will-O-Wisp as well as clear any entry hazards with Defog. Its tendency to be worn down easily throughout the match signifies the need to remove entry hazards as soon as possible so it is healthy enough to check Gurdurr, Primeape, and Scyther. Later in the match, Rotom-Fan should be brought in on slower Pokemon such as Audino or on resisted Grass-, Fighting-, or Flying-type moves to eliminate any remaining entry hazards. This may include, but is not limited to, Choice-locked Primeape's Close Combat and Swanna's Hurricane. Being immune to the Toxic Spikes, Rotom-Fan should be brought in directly on Qwilfish to quickly remove the aforementioned hazard before a teammate can be afflicted by poison. Although it has a great Defense stat, Rotom-Fan's appalling HP stat prevents it from taking more powerful physical hits such as Stoutland's Return and Zangoose's Facade. Therefore, be sure to switch it in only on weak to moderate physical attacks. Since Electric-types like Alolan Raichu tend to wall Rotom-Fan's attacking moves, predict this by going for a status move or pivot out, unless the foe has Lightning Rod or Volt Absorb. After it inevitably gets worn down from repeated attacks, Rotom-Fan should go for Pain Split, as it will recover a lot of health, especially against Pokemon with high HP stats such as Skuntank and Audino. When facing faster Taunt users such as Qwilfish or Defiant users such as Primeape, instead of going for Defog, predict and respond with a STAB move.

Team Options

In general, Fighting-types such as Hitmonchan are valuable teammates to Rotom-Fan because of their good type synergy with it. While Rotom-Fan can easily take a Supersonic Skystrike from Oricorio-G, Gurdurr and Primeape can deal with the common Ice-types that are the bane of Rotom-Fan's existence, with Primeape being able to form a solid VoltTurn core with Rotom-Fan. Other pivots like Silvally-Fairy can coincide with Rotom-Fan to gain momentum for the team. They also help with breaking specially defensive walls such as Lanturn. Clefairy and other specially defensive walls can take on the strong special attackers that would otherwise beat Rotom-Fan, like Drampa. Wish support from clerics such as Audino helps with Rotom-Fan's lackluster recovery. In return, Rotom-Fan can check the Fighting-types that threaten Audino, such as Hitmonchan, Primeape, and Gurdurr. Pokemon such as Aurorus, Jynx, and Omastar that can tear apart Rotom-Fan's checks and counters appreciate the removal of entry hazards and benefit greatly from Rotom-Fan's Defog. As such, Rotom-Fan would fit better on more balanced or offensive teams that value Defog support but can moreover harness its pivotal capabilities.

zu.overview: Rotom-Fan carves a niche for itself among many pivots and support Pokemon in the metagame due to its typing, stats, and fantastic support movepool. It further separates itself from other pivots and Defoggers because of its ability to soft check numerous top threats such Swanna, Combusken, Leafeon, and Pinsir. Similarly, Rotom-Fan is a great Choice Scarf user because of its ability to check various threats, pivot on forced switches, and threaten switch-ins with Will-O-Wisp or Trick. Moreover, utility moves in Trick and Will-O-Wisp make up for Rotom-Fan's relatively weak offensive coverage and middling Speed compared to Choice Scarf Electivire. However, Rotom-Fan's weakness to Stealth Rock significantly hinders its ability to pivot. Moreover, a lack of reliable recovery and vulnerability to residual damage limit its ability to repeatedly switch into Pokemon it checks. While its STAB attacks offer decent coverage, Choice Scarf Rotom-Fan is still easy to wall and usually has to rely on Trick or Will-O-Wisp to cripple switch-ins, which leaves Rotom-Fan unable to revenge kill faster threats or makes it easy to take advantage of. Also, Rotom-Fan's typing leaves it unable to directly switch into popular entry hazard setters such as Golem and Bronzor.
zu.comments:
Other Options

Leftovers with a bulkier spread of 252 HP / 208 Def / 48 Spe and a Bold nature is an option on the defensive pivot set. The Speed EVs ensure Rotom-Fan outspeeds Adamant Pawniard, and the HP and Defense EVs make it a better switch-in for physical attackers such as Z-Mirror Move Swanna and Swords Dance Leafeon. However, the loss of Speed is not ideal, as it forces Rotom-Fan to trade damage against Pokemon it would otherwise outspeed and threaten such as Swords Dance Bibarel, Monferno, and Swords Dance Pinsir. On this set, Protect is an option in the third move slot that allows Rotom-Fan to generate additional turns of Leftovers recovery and scout out Choice Scarf users such as Electivire and Silvally. Flyinium Z is an option over Wiki Berry if your team lacks a Z-Move user that makes Rotom-Fan a better Knock Off switch-in and consequently a better check to Leafeon, Pawniard, and Kecleon, and it also allows Rotom-Fan to OHKO most Grass-types with Supersonic Skystrike. However, without a form of recovery from Wiki Berry, Rotom-Fan becomes much more reliant on Pain Split and more susceptible to chip damage. Hidden Power Ground over Will-O-Wisp on the Choice Scarf set can help Rotom-Fan nail would-be switch-ins such as Electivire, Raichu, and Golem, but Hidden Power Ground is a very exploitable move and usually inferior to the utility Will-O-Wisp brings.

Checks and Counters

Electric-types: Electivire, Raichu, and Silvally-Electric all switch into Rotom-Fan easily and threaten it out. In particular, Electivire and Raichu block Volt Switch thanks to Motor Drive and Lighting Rod, respectively, but they must watch out for Will-O-Wisp and being worn down by Air Slash.

Ground-types: Ground-types such as Golem, Sandslash, Silvally-Ground, and Marowak block Volt Switch and cause Rotom-Fan to lose momentum as a result. While these Pokemon check the Choice Scarf set, Rotom-Fan threatens to cripple them with Will-O-Wisp.

Faster Pokemon: Faster Choice Scarf users such as Electivire, Silvally, Simipour, and Rapidash threaten to OHKO Choice Scarf Rotom-Fan after it is weakened. Similarly, offensive Pokemon such as Choice Band Basculin, Silvally-Dragon, and Simisear outspeed defensive Rotom-Fan and can OHKO it after some chip damage, though they need to consider knocking Rotom-Fan down into Wiki Berry range.

Bulky Pokemon: Walls such as Bronzor, Lickilicky, and Dusclops easily switch into Rotom-Fan and only fear Trick. Other bulky Pokemon such as Muk, Beheeyem, and Assault Vest Bouffalant comfortably take on Rotom-Fan, but they cannot block Volt Switch, and the latter two fear Trick. Rest variants of Silvally-Dark and Silvally-Poison used on stall teams can also switch into Rotom-Fan and do not fear Trick, but they cannot block Volt Switch.

Defensive Pivot.description:
Set Description

Will-O-Wisp allows Rotom-Fan to burn slower physical attackers such as Pawniard and Marowak and prevents Electivire and Golem from switching in freely. Pain Split can be used over Will-O-Wisp to give Rotom-Fan somewhat reliable recovery so it can pivot around and check threats such as Pinsir, Simisage, and Poliwrath.

Set Details

Maximum Speed and HP investment and a Timid nature are necessary so Rotom-Fan can check Pokemon such as Pinsir, Monferno, and Servine. Wiki Berry is preferred over Leftovers because Rotom-Fan benefits more from the one-time recovery than it does from residual recovery and can use its Stealth Rock weakness to activate Wiki Berry.

Usage Tips

Rotom-Fan should cripple switch-ins with Will-O-Wisp and wear down Ground-types such as Silvally-Ground and Camerupt with Air Slash. This helps it use Volt Switch more freely, as typical Volt Switch switch-ins fear burn or do not want to be worn down. Rotom-Fan should be wary of what it uses Defog against. For example, Rotom-Fan loses to entry hazard setters such as offensive Golem and Bronzor, but it can threaten out defensive Torterra, Mareanie, and Mawile. If entry hazards are present, Rotom-Fan should use Defog against Pokemon it forces out such as Leafeon, Pawniard, and Machoke; be wary of a Knock Off from these three, though, as staying in can jeopardize Rotom-Fan's recovery later on by removing its Wiki Berry. This also means that Rotom-Fan should be mindful of its HP, as certain attacks such as Ice Punch from Electivire can 2HKO it without activating Wiki Berry. Similarly, Rotom-Fan can sometimes use its Stealth Rock weakness to knock itself down to 25% health or less to activate Wiki Berry, which helps it check Pokemon such as Swanna, Combusken, and Simisage in a pinch.

Team Options

Rotom-Fan fits best on balance and bulky teams that appreciate a pivot and soft check to Grass-, Water-, and Fighting-types such as Leafeon, Simipour, and Silvally-Fighting. As such, Rotom-Fan pairs well with Pokemon such as Poliwrath, Combusken, and Komala. Wallbreakers such as Swords Dance Torterra and Choice Specs Beheeyem appreciate Rotom-Fan's ability to pivot with Volt Switch against defensive Pokemon they take advantage of such as Lickilicky and Curse Muk. In addition, Rotom-Fan checks Flying- and Grass-types such as Swanna, Toucannon, and Exeggutor for Torterra and checks Bug- and Dark-types such as Pinsir, Ninjask, and Pawniard for Beheeyem. On more defensive teams, Rotom-Fan forms a good defensive backbone alongside bulky Pokemon such as Komala, defensive Golem, defensive Torterra, and Gourgeist-XL. In particular, Komala provides Wish support and creates a VoltTurn core with Rotom-Fan, defensive Golem checks Electric-types, and both defensive Torterra and Gourgeist-XL check Rock- and Ground-types. Setup Pokemon such as Nasty Plot Simipour, Substitute Swords Dance Bouffalant, and Swords Dance Leafeon appreciate Rotom-Fan's ability to clear entry hazards.

Choice Scarf.description:
Set Description

Thunderbolt gives Rotom-Fan a strong Electric-type STAB attack and makes it more of a revenge killer, but Will-O-Wisp is generally preferred because it punishes typical switch-ins such as Electivire and Golem and gives Rotom-Fan utility as a Choice Scarf user. Trick enables Rotom-Fan to cripple counters such as Bronzor, Dusclops, and Lickilicky. It also helps it cripple slower setup sweepers such as Nasty Plot Beheeyem and Bulk Up Vigoroth.

Set Details

Maximum Speed and Special Attack investment with a Timid nature enables Rotom-Fan to revenge kill foes such as Floatzel, Simisage, and Combusken.

Usage Tips

Rotom-Fan's main focus should be to pivot with Volt Switch, but it also needs to anticipate Pokemon such as Silvally-Ground, Sandslash, Electivire, and Raichu switching in and blocking Volt Switch. Will-O-Wisp immediately cripples physical attackers and Ground-types, while Air Slash wears down switch-ins immediately and 2HKOes the aforementioned Ground-types if they are weakened enough. However, being locked into Will-O-Wisp invites in offensive Pokemon such as Combusken, Komala, and Silvally-Dragon, which forces Rotom-Fan out and loses momentum in the process. Similarly, being locked into Air Slash invites in Flying-type switch-ins such as Bronzor and Silvally-Electric, so be mindful of what Rotom-Fan locks itself into. Once faster threats are removed and Rotom-Fan no longer needs to act as a revenge killer, Trick should be used to cripple switch-ins such as defensive Golem, Lickilicky, and Bronzor that Rotom-Fan cannot hurt otherwise. If Rotom-Fan needs its Choice Scarf for faster threats, avoid using Trick to cripple those Pokemon and double switch to a teammate instead. Against more defensive teams where Rotom-Fan's Speed is less valuable, Trick should be used early on to cripple bulky Pokemon such as Wish Komala, Altaria, and Dusclops.

Team Options

Choice Scarf Rotom-Fan is an excellent pivot and check to offensive Pokemon such as Simisage, Pinsir, and Swanna, so Pokemon that appreciate them being revenge killed such as Torterra, Beheeyem, and Combusken make for good partners. These Pokemon can also wallbreak and pave way for a late-game cleanup for Rotom-Fan. Grass-, Water-, and Ground-types pair well with Rotom-Fan, as they check Ground- and Electric-types, which helps Rotom-Fan use Volt Switch freely. Grass- and Water-types such as Exeggutor, Torterra, Simipour, and Floatzel beat common Ground-types, while Pokemon such as Golem, Marowak, and Silvally-Ground pair well with Rotom-Fan because they can check Electric-types such as Electivire, Raichu, and Silvally-Electric. Rotom-Fan is slower than common Choice Scarf users such as Electivire and Silvally and loses its ability to revenge kill faster Pokemon such as Simipour and Leafeon after using Trick. Because of this, pair Rotom-Fan with Pokemon such as Golem, Choice Band Furfrou, and Kadabra that can check those Pokemon. Entry hazard removers such as Sandslash, Silvally-Fighting, and Silvally-Water help keep Rotom-Fan healthy and able to pivot around by removing Stealth Rock. The latter two also form a VoltTurn core alongside Rotom-Fan.

uu.overview: Rotom-Mow possesses an interesting niche in UU as a fast offensive pivot with a good matchup against some of the top threats in the tier like Primarina, Togekiss, and Mega Slowbro. Its secondary Grass typing and access to Leaf Storm make it extremely difficult to bring in a Ground-type Pokemon to block its Volt Switch, allowing it to gain momentum for its team quite easily. In addition to its useful STAB combination, it also has a handful of useful support moves such as Thunder Wave, Will-O-Wisp, and Defog in its arsenal. Its access to Defog in particular also allows it to become a solid remover of entry hazards with a good matchup against common setters like Klefki, Hippowdon, and Empoleon. Additionally, Rotom-Mow's ability Levitate gives it a useful immunity to Ground-type moves. On the other hand, its typing gives it a poor matchup against many other significant threats in UU, most notably Dragon-type Pokemon like Hydreigon, Latias, and Mega Altaria. In addition to this, Rotom-Mow is held back by its somewhat average Special Attack that can pale in comparison to some of UU's more prominent special attackers like Mega Manectric and Hydreigon. Its Speed stat is only slightly above average as well, which means that it will almost always be forced out by faster offensive threats like Infernape, Latias, and Mega Beedrill. Its defensive prowess is also somewhat lackluster compared to Rotom-Heat's, and its base HP of 50 combined with weaknesses to Bug and Ice as well as its inability to face common Dragon-type Pokemon means that Rotom-Mow often won't bring much to a team defensively. Lastly, Rotom-Mow also lacks any powerful coverage to help it break through its normal checks. Conventional special walls like Blissey, Amoonguss, and Alolan Muk will almost always be able to beat it in a one-on-one scenario.
uu.comments:
Other Options

Rotom-Mow can use Thunder Wave or Will-O-Wisp in its fourth moveslot to leave a crippling status condition on threats to it such as Alolan Muk and Mega Altaria. It can also attempt to use a Choice Scarf to become a decent revenge killer but is often better off acting as an offensive Defogger with Grassium Z or Iapapa Berry. Choice Specs is another viable option so Rotom-Mow can act as a strong wallbreaker and pivot that can be very threatening with its high-Base Power STAB move in Leaf Storm; however, Rotom-Mow often prefers being able to switch between attacking moves so it can threaten more of the tier offensively as well as being able to use Defog without being forced out. Hidden Power Ice can catch Mega Sceptile that attempt to check Rotom-Mow and dent switch-ins like Latias and Mega Altaria. Rotom-Mow can also attempt to use lure sets like Dream Eater with Psychium Z and Signal Beam with Buginium Z. The former is used to surprise Chesnaught and Amoonguss, which can allow a teammate like Calm Mind Suicune to sweep more easily, and the latter is used to surprise Hydreigon and Latias.

Checks and Counters

Dragon-types: Due to Rotom-Mow's STAB combination and lack of powerful coverage moves, it struggles to break through Dragon-types like Mega Altaria, Latias, and Hydreigon. Mega Sceptile in particular is 4x resistant to Leaf Storm and immune to Electric-type moves thanks to its ability Lighting Rod.

Grass-types: Most of UU's Grass-type Pokemon do not mind facing off with Rotom-Mow, as they can take advantage of it fairly easily. Mega Sceptile is immune to its Electric-type STAB moves thanks to Lightning Rod while also being 4x resistant to Leaf Storm due to its typing. Amoonguss can shrug off any of Rotom-Mow's hits besides the extremely rare Shattered Psyche from Dream Eater thanks to Regenerator constantly restoring a third of its HP. Celebi threatens to get free Nasty Plot boosts when facing off with Rotom-Mow as well. However, they all must be mindful of Rotom-Mow being commonly paired with Pursuit trappers.

Special Walls: Rotom-Mow's middling Special Attack and lack of coverage outside of Hidden Power means that conventional special walls often give it trouble. Blissey, Amoonguss, and Alolan Muk will all be able to stop Rotom-Mow in a one-on-one scenario, though Blissey and Amoonguss should be wary of Trick.

Residual Damage: While Rotom-Mow can switch in on weak Scald users such as Swampert and Suicune and passive Ground-types like Hippowdon, it should be wary of taking damage from status conditions like burn and poison as well as residual damage from sand and Stealth Rock, which can all wear it down very quickly.

Faster Pokemon: While Rotom-Mow's defensive prowess is decent, it often will still take a large amount of damage from any Pokemon that outpaces it.
