Primal Kyogre: Primal Kyogre resists Judgment and Ice Beam and can threaten to 2HKO Arceus-Water back with Thunder. Even without Thunder, Primal Kyogre can break through Arceus-Water with the combination of Calm Mind and Origin Pulse if it's faster or completely wall Arceus-Water with Rest and Toxic. However, Arceus-Water can use its resistances to Water- and Ice-type moves to switch into Primal Kyogre before pivoting out to a more appropriate check such as Primal Groudon.

Powerful Special Attackers: Arceus-Water is mainly invested in Defense and relies on its typing to take on special attackers. Powerful special attackers that can hit it neutrally, such as Geomancy Xerneas, Calm Mind Lunala, and Calm Mind Arceus formes, can often 2HKO Arceus-Water and potentially set up on it.

Support.description:
Moves

Recover is mandatory to keep Arceus-Water healthy, while Toxic is very a important move to punish bulky Pokemon such as Primal Kyogre, Primal Groudon, and support Arceus formes, which aren't really threatened by any other move. Ice Beam is primarily an offensive move, hitting many offensive Pokemon such as Mega Rayquaza, Yveltal, and Zygarde-C for super effective damage. However, Will-O-Wisp is a very viable option and can be used over Ice Beam to neutralize physical attackers such as Mega Rayquaza, Necrozma-DM, Marshadow, and Extreme Killer Arceus, making them easy to take on for the rest of the team. Judgment is an aggressive way to hit Steel-types, mainly offensive Necrozma-DM, and it also 2HKOes Ho-Oh and Mega Gengar, which both check Arceus-Water otherwise. Arceus-Water is a decent user of Stealth Rock thanks to the good role compression it provides and its ability to beat Defog Arceus-Ground, a trait that is relatively rare in common Stealth Rock setters. Defog can be considered instead of Judgment to remove entry hazards. However, in addition to the fact that Steel-types like specially defensive Necrozma-DM and Ferrothorn are completely free to switch back in to set entry hazards, Arceus-Water struggles to consistently remove Stealth Rock against Primal Groudon even with a type advantage versus it due to the popularity of Toxic on the latter, making Defog a subpar option.

Set Details

16 Speed EVs allow Arceus-Water to outspeed neutral-natured base 90 Speed Pokemon, notably Primal Groudon and Primal Kyogre. 252 HP and 240 Defense EVs maximize Arceus-Water's physical bulk, allowing it to survive powerful moves such as +2 Searing Sunraze Smash from Necrozma-DM and +1 Soul-Stealing 7-Star Strike from Marshadow and giving it a good chance to survive +1 Dragon Ascent from Life Orb Mega Rayquaza. Alternatively, a spread of 252 HP / 160 Def / 96 Spe with a Timid nature allows Arceus-Water to outspeed Adamant Mega Rayquaza and anything below.

Usage Tips

Thanks to heavy defensive investment, this set can switch into many physical attackers like offensive Necrozma-DM, Primal Groudon, Zygarde-C, and Marshadow and punish them with the appropriate coverage or status move. Arceus-Water should use Toxic against bulky foes such as Primal Groudon as soon as possible to punish them over the match, while Recover should be used often to ensure that Arceus-Water can still check common Pokemon like offensive Necrozma-DM, Marshadow, and Primal Groudon. Use Ice Beam and Judgment only against foes they hit super effectively or, in Judgment's case, against Steel-types that lack both recovery and Toxic. Otherwise, it is often better to use Toxic or switch out to an appropriate teammate. If running Will-O-Wisp, keep in mind that your opponent can scout for it by pivoting to Pokemon like Calm Mind Arceus formes, which Arceus-Water will lose the ability to threaten with Toxic, before sending in a Pokemon that dislikes Will-O-Wisp like offensive Necrozma-DM. In general, avoid unnecessarily revealing Will-O-Wisp. If running Stealth Rock, setting it on Pokemon forced out by Arceus-Water, like support Arceus-Ground, is ideal. Finally, Defog variants of Arceus-Water should not be played passively, so try to use Toxic on opposing entry hazard setters, notably Primal Groudon, before attempting to Defog.

Team Options

Because Arceus-Water is passive, it should be mainly used on balance and stall teams where its defensive qualities are appreciated, unlike on offensive teams where its passivity is an undesirable trait to have. Primal Groudon and Ho-Oh are good teammates for Arceus-Water; Primal Groudon can set Stealth Rock, phaze Geomancy Xerneas with Roar, and pivot into Thunder from Primal Kyogre, while Ho-Oh provides Defog support and checks Pokemon that both Arceus-Water and Primal Groudon struggle against, like Calm Mind Arceus-Ground and Lunala. Both Primal Groudon and Ho-Oh can threaten potentially problematic Steel-types, especially Ferrothorn, with their STAB Fire-type attacks, and they appreciate Arceus-Water's ability to pivot into Primal Kyogre, Zygarde-C, most Mega Rayquaza sets, and opposing Primal Groudon. Mega Gengar is a great teammate for Arceus-Water due to its ability to threaten opposing defensive cores, which are highly problematic for Arceus-Water, thanks to Shadow Tag and various tools at its disposal like Taunt, Perish Song, Substitute, a Toxic immunity, and its sheer power. In return, Mega Gengar appreciates Arceus-Water handling bulky foes such as Primal Groudon, Ho-Oh, and Zygarde-C, which can all take powerful attacks from Mega Gengar and KO it back. Arceus-Water has good synergy with Steel-types like Ferrothorn, Necrozma-DM, Celesteela, and Magearna due to its ability to provide a safe switch-in to Primal Groudon, support Arceus-Ground, and Zygarde-C. In return, Steel-types can switch into Toxic and provide various utility options; Necrozma-DM and Magearna also check Geomancy Xerneas. Ferrothorn can check Primal Kyogre and almost all viable support Arceus formes, and its Spikes support is appreciated by nearly every team. Necrozma-DM can provide Stealth Rock support or, with an Ultranecrozium Z set, wallbreak to weaken defensive cores that Arceus-Water struggles against. Celesteela provides an additional measure of security against Dragon Dance Mega Rayquaza and Calm Mind Arceus-Ground, both of which can overpower Arceus-Water. Magearna checks Life Orb Yveltal and Vivillon and provides momentum with Volt Switch for Arceus-Water's team. Finally, Dark-types such as Yveltal, Arceus-Dark, and Tyranitar can switch into Ghost- and Dark-types like Lunala and Yveltal for Arceus-Water. Both Yveltal and Arceus-Dark can run Defog to remove entry hazards, and Tyranitar can set Stealth Rock. Tyranitar is particularly notable for its ability to Pursuit trap Mega Gengar and Gothitelle, which greatly helps out Arceus-Water. In return, Arceus-Water can check Primal Groudon, Zygarde-C, and Marshadow for it.

ou.overview: Thanks to an insanely high Base Power STAB attack in V-create, a great coverage option in Bolt Strike, and utility in U-turn and Trick, Victini can operate effectively in OU as either a Choice Scarf or Choice Band user. Victini's unique typing and good bulk gives it many opportunities to switch in against common threats in the OU tier such as Magearna and Tapu Lele and wreak havoc. Alternatively, Victini can use a Z-Celebrate set to boost all its stats once per match, becoming a terrifying late-game sweeper that can be difficult to revenge kill. Stored Power is very strong after a boost, and with a useful coverage option in Focus Blast, Victini has the ability to shred through common defensive cores as well as offensive teams. Its good bulk and somewhat useful resistances give Victini plenty of chances to setup. Unfortunately, Victini's average attacking stats forces it to heavily rely on Z-Celebrate's boosts in order to pose much of a threat when running this set. Furthermore, Victini's typing causes it to be weak to every form of entry hazard as well as common priority, such as Sucker Punch and Water Shuriken.
ou.comments:
Other Options

Victini has an expansive offensive movepool, featuring good options such as Glaciate, Blue Flare, Thunder, Energy Ball, Shadow Ball. Victini can use said movepool to function as either a mixed or special attacker with an Expert Belt or Choice Specs, though it usually breaks much more of the metagame when functioning as a physical wallbreaker. Trick Room is an option for taking advantage of V-create's Speed drops; however, Victini is often too fast to make use of Trick Room and is more effective as a moderately fast wallbreaker anyway.

Checks and Counters

Dragon-types: Garchomp and Mega Charizard X can somewhat reliably check Victini thanks to their resistance to V-create and Bolt Strike. Mega Latios and Mega Latias are also troublesome due to their resistances to Victini's STAB attacks.

Bulky Water-types: Water-types such as Slowbro and Alomomola resist V-create and only really need to watch out for Choice Banded Bolt Strike, which they can pivot into and switch to the appropriate teammate thanks to Regenerator.

Ground-types: Some of OU's Ground-type Pokemon are bulky enough to tank an attack from Victini and threaten it with super effective Ground-type attacks. Examples include Mega Swampert, Gastrodon, and Hippowdon, which can also use Whirlwind to get rid of Victini's boosts.

Pursuit: Pursuit trappers such as Weavile and Tyranitar are able to trap Victini if it's locked into Zen Headbutt or sometimes even V-create in Tyranitar's case. Victini is also very vulnerable to being revenge killed by them after using V-create.

Faster Pokemon: Due to Victini's average Speed, it is outsped and threatened by common Pokemon in Greninja, Tapu Koko, Mega Diancie, and Choice Scarf Landorus-T. It can also be picked off by Mega Mawile's Sucker Punch and Ash-Greninja's Water Shuriken. All of these Pokemon have to be wary of Victini after a Z-Celebrate, however.

Choice Scarf.description:
Moves

U-turn allows Victini to gain momentum and deal chip damage to Fire-resistant switch-ins like Tyranitar and Mega Latias. Final Gambit lets Victini quickly remove or force damage on a problematic Pokemon. It's particularly useful for getting rid of checks like Mega Latias, Heatran, and Toxapex, which may open the door for a teammate that shares these checks with Victini. Trick cripples walls such as Toxapex. If the opponent has multiple defensive stops to Victini such as Tyranitar, Heatran, and Gliscor, the move ensures that Victini isn't limited to getting a single KO with Final Gambit. Bolt Strike can be run over Final Gambit to hit Water-types such as Toxapex and Tapu Fini.

Set Details

Maximum HP investment ensures that Final Gambit deals as much damage as possible when Victini is healthy. If Victini is running Bolt Strike, maximum Attack investment should be used instead to secure the 2HKO on Toxapex and Tapu Fini. Choice Scarf turns Victini into an effective revenge killer, letting it outspeed threats such as Mega Medicham, Mega Alakazam, and non-Choice Scarf Kartana.

Usage Tips

Think twice before using V-create if the opponent has an obvious switch-in to it, such as Heatran, Toxapex, or Tyranitar. U-turn is often a safer play, especially if Victini has another teammate that can deal with the threat that's in front of it. Consider using Final Gambit if doing so will significantly help out one of Victini's teammates by removing a shared check. For example, removing Mega Latias is highly beneficial for teammates like Kartana and Swords Dance Gliscor. Preserve Victini's health as much as possible before using Final Gambit; don't unnecessarily switch it into Stealth Rock or strong attacks. Final Gambit can be used early-game in order to immediately force a trade, which can be helpful against offensive teams. Trick should be used against defensive teams that rely on walls like Toxapex to check Victini.

Team Options

Pokemon that benefit from Victini's ability to lure in checks like Mega Latias, Heatran, and Toxapex and KO them with Final Gambit make for good teammates. These include Pokemon such as Kartana, Swords Dance Gliscor, and Mega Scizor. Victini is susceptible to all entry hazards and has a Stealth Rock weakness, so it really appreciates Defog support. Tapu Fini is an excellent Defogger to pair with Victini because it can reliably switch into entry hazard setters like Heatran, Ash-Greninja, and Toxapex that trouble it. Gliscor is another great Defogger that can deal with Heatran, Toxapex, Tyranitar, and most Ground-types. Tornadus-T and Zapdos are solid Defoggers that can switch into Ground-type attacks for Victini as well. Solid answers to Water-types, particularly Ash-Greninja, are needed. Kommo-o checks Ash-Greninja, Tyranitar, and Heatran for Victini and pressures defensive cores with its Z-Move and coverage options. Assault Vest Tangrowth checks Ash-Greninja and Ground-types like Landorus-T and Garchomp, and it can use Earthquake or Knock Off in order to weaken Heatran. Rotom-Wash deals with Ground-types like Landorus-T, Mega Swampert, and Hippowdon in addition to Heatran and brings Victini in against Grass-types with Volt Switch, making it an exemplary partner. Wallbreakers benefit from the U-turn support Victini provides and help to break through defensive cores. Mega Medicham and Hoopa-U are notable examples, since they threaten many of Victini's switch-ins including Heatran, Tyranitar, Toxapex, and Mega Latias.

Choice Band.description:
Moves

Bolt Strike is strong coverage, nailing Toxapex and other Water-types and significantly chunking Heatran. U-turn not only gives Victini a strong move to pivot with but also does substantial damage to Mega Latios and Tyranitar. Zen Headbutt is a secondary STAB attack that can be occasionally useful to ease prediction, such as against the core Toxapex + Landorus-T. Brick Break OHKOes Tyranitar one-on-one, preventing it from Pursuit trapping Victini, and 2HKOes bulkier Heatran variants that are only 3HKOed by Bolt Strike. Trick can cripple certain targets, but few Pokemon manage to wall Choice Band Victini anyway.

Usage Tips

Use Victini's good defensive typing to bring it in as often as possible, such as against Tapu Lele, Clefable, and Tapu Bulu or Power Whip from Ferrothorn, Giga Drain from Tangrowth, Leaf Blade and Sacred Sword from Kartana, and Fleur Cannon from Magearna. Play aggressively with Victini; good prediction skills are important to effectively wallbreak against common cores such as Landorus-T + Heatran. Be wary of using V-create against teams with Tyranitar or Weavile, as it leaves Victini very prone to being trapped by Pursuit.

Team Options

Tapu Koko is an excellent partner, using Volt Switch or U-turn to bring in Victini against bulky Grass-types to fire off strong V-creates. It also sets Electric Terrain, helping Victini muscle through Heatran. Defog support is paramount; Stealth Rock and Spikes wear down Victini incredibly quickly, preventing it from checking Tapu Lele and Tapu Bulu effectively. Toxic Spikes are a nuisance for Victini, too, putting it on a timer. Good options for Defoggers include Zapdos and Mega Latios, the latter of which checks Heatran and baits in Ferrothorn, Celesteela, and Scizor for Victini. Good Ash-Greninja checks are also important partners; while any of Victini's moves will OHKO it, Ash-Greninja is very effective at coming in after a KO or on a double switch and applying pressure with strong STAB attacks, so Ferrothorn, Tangrowth, and Magearna are good partners.

Z-Celebrate.description:
Moves

Celebrate works in conjunction with Normalium Z to give Victini a +1 boost in all of its stats except for accuracy and evasion, turning it into a lethal sweeper under the right conditions and making it tough to revenge kill thanks to the defensive boosts. Blue Flare is incompatible with Celebrate, which makes Searing Shot the best Fire-type STAB move for this set; it does good damage after a boost, though it's weak unboosted. STAB Stored Power gets boosted to 120-Base Power after Z-Celebrate is used. It's used over other Psychic-type moves like Psychic and Psyshock because it allows Victini to OHKO Toxapex, thus avoiding Haze from it, as well as Alolan Marowak and Tapu Koko. Focus Blast hits Heatran and Tyranitar super effectively, which otherwise wall this set.

Usage Tips

Z-Celebrate can only be used once, so ensure that Victini's checks and counters are worn down or eliminated before it attempts to sweep. Once Victini's set up, all it has to do is pick the right coverage move and start getting KOs. Victini can attempt to spread burns early-game in some matchups thanks to Searing Shot's high burn chance, though that's pretty much all it can do before setting up due to its poor coverage without Stored Power and lack of breaking power without a boost. If there's a Choice Scarf user on the opposing team like Garchomp or Keldeo, it should try to avoid taking too much damage while setting up in order to survive a Hydro Pump from Keldeo or an Earthquake from Garchomp. When facing stall, Victini can't do anything until Chansey is removed, so try to remove it either through trapping it or with a lure. While Unaware Clefable may seem like another roadblock for Victini, it can't wall Victini if it loses its Leftovers because Searing Shot's burns will slowly wear it down and put it in range of Victini's attacks.

Team Options

Victini is weak to Stealth Rock and doesn't like being poisoned by Toxic Spikes, so Defog users like Mew and Mega Scizor make for good teammates for an easier time sweeping. Bulky Water-types such as Mantine and Gastrodon need to be weakened for Victini to clean up more effectively, so teammates like Ash-Greninja and Heatran that can pressure them early-game are appreciated. Ash-Greninja can also set up Spikes for it. Spikes users like Ferrothorn and Greninja help Victini muscle through bulkier foes such as Mew thanks to the additional chip damage. Victini can't threaten Chansey even after a boost due to its sky-high Special Defense, which gives it a bad stall matchup as long as Chansey is alive. Therefore, teammates that can lure in or pressure Chansey like Tapu Koko and Tapu Lele can help Victini in this regard. Pursuit users like Tyranitar and Weavile can remove Mega Latias for Victini, which can be a pain to break through. They can also force mind games against Chansey and weaken it for Victini. Smeargle is an interesting partner, as it sets up Sticky Web for Victini, thus making it impossible to revenge kill after the Z-Celebrate boost.

1v1.overview: Victini is a good Pokemon in 1v1 because of its Fire typing and its access to V-create, allowing it to beat common threats such as Magearna, Mega Charizard Y, and Genesect. Fire is generally a good offensive type and V-create is a supremely powerful STAB move, allowing Victini to beat many of the omnipresent bulky Steel-types, like Celesteela and Mega Mawile. Defensively, Victini's resistance to Fairy-type STAB attacks from popular Pokemon like Tapu Lele and Mega Gardevoir allows it to beat them when it's running a physical set. It can also be quite versatile with its base 100 stats across the board and nice movepool that includes moves such as Blue Flare, Celebrate, Magic Coat, Will-O-Wisp, and Glaciate, allowing it to run a variety of viable sets to beat diverse threats. A Z-Celebrate set can also be used to beat threats to the Choice Band set like Mega Charizard X and Kommo-o. By running a mixed attacker set, Victini is able to beat Zeraora reliably. It is also able to viably run Taunt for some stall Pokemon like Type: Null and Mega Altaria. However, Victini lacks decent spammable boosting moves, only having Z-Celebrate, Power-Up Punch, and Work Up, and, as a result, competes with other Fire-types like Mega Charizard X, Heatran, and Incineroar due to their ability to raise their damage output by using moves like Dragon Dance, Metal Sound, and Bulk Up. Furthermore, Victini's rather lacking offensive stats leave its coverage moves without much force behind them, meaning it loses to Pokemon that can withstand V-create and are too bulky for its coverage moves, like Mega Gyarados, Mega Slowbro, and Mega Tyranitar.
1v1.comments:
Other Options

A physical Psychium Z set with V-create / Bolt Strike / Zen Headbutt / Light Screen or Magic Coat can be run. Physical sets retain the ability to beat Pokemon like Tapu Lele, Mega Gardevoir, and Kommo-o. Magic Coat or Light Screen can also beat either variant of Tapu Fini, given that you predict Tapu Fini's set correctly, by using Z-Magic Coat or Light Screen against Waterium Z variants and directly using Bolt Strike against Tapunium Z variants. This Victini set can also beat Choice Specs Greninja with Z-Magic Coat followed by Bolt Strike or V-create depending on Greninja's move. Z-Light Screen can allow Victini to beat Heatran and Primarina most of the time. Both Z-Magic Coat and Z-Light Screen sets can also force Volcarona into mind games. An Icium Z set with Will-O-Wisp / Blue Flare / Taunt / Glaciate can be run to beat Pokemon that are weak to Ice like Dragonite, Zygarde, Landorus-T, and Donphan. However, because this set will make Victini's STAB moves especially lackluster, it should only be used to lure in and beat Dragonite. Firium Z can be run to beat Aegislash without Victini having to run Substitute. It can also somewhat consistently beat Donphan with Z-Will-O-Wisp. A faster Choice Band set can be used to retain the offensive power of Choice Band while outspeeding Pokemon like Normalium Z Porygon-Z.

Checks and Counters

Rock- and Ground-types: Pokemon such as Zygarde, Landorus-T, Mega Tyranitar, and Garchomp can all survive Victini's attacks and KO it with super effective STAB moves.

Bulky Offense: Pokemon such as Mega Gyarados, Incineroar, and Choice Scarf Dragonite resist V-create, are too bulky for Victini's much weaker coverage moves, and can defeat Victini with powerful STAB moves.

Stall Mega Evolutions and Z-Move Users: Mega Slowbro, Kyurem, and Psychium Z Deoxys-S can set up using boosting moves, then stall Victini out while whittling it down because of its lack of good boosting moves and their immunity to Trick.

Aegislash: King's Shield blocks V-create and prevents Victini from OHKOing Aegislash, which OHKOes Victini in return with Never-Ending Nightmare.

Choice Band.description:
Moves

V-create is Victini's strongest move by far, and it is used to burst Steel-types like Magearna, Mega Mawile, and Celesteela. It can also be used to beat Pokemon that are unable to effectively hit Victini such as Mega Gardevoir and Tapu Lele. Bolt Strike is used against Tapunium Z Tapu Fini and Heatran. It also is a powerful weapon against opposing Victini and can sometimes land an OHKO against Primarina. Flame Charge is used against Pokemon that will avoid fainting to V-create such as Magnezone, Flail Mega Pinsir, and Flail Mega Lopunny. It can also be used to outspeed SubSeed users like Jumpluff and Serperior. Zen Headbutt is used against Poison-types like Mega Venusaur and Naganadel. Trick can shut down stall Pokemon that do not use Z-Crystals or Mega Stones like Type: Null and Pyukumuku, as well as give Victini a chance against Porygon2, albeit an unreliable one. It can also be used to force Deoxys-S into guessing games between using Taunt against Trick or Iron Defense against V-create.

Set Details

240 HP and 4 Special Defense EVs are used to increase Victini's bulk, particularly for Modest Magnezone's Gigavolt Havoc, forcing it to try to paralyze Victini with regular Zap Cannon. Additionally, the 4 Special Defense EVs prevent a Special Attack Download boost for Pokemon like Genesect and Porygon2. The HP investment helps Victini survive physical attacks like Mega Lopunny's Fake Out followed by Giga Impact. 20 Speed EVs are used to outspeed base 60 Speed Pokemon, particularly Timid Magnezone. 244 Attack EVs with an Adamant nature alongside Choice Band are used to deal as much damage as possible.

Usage Tips

Use Flame Charge if the Speed boost will let Victini outspeed and KO the foe on the next turn, like against Substitute users such as Mega Pinsir, Serperior, and Mega Lopunny. The matchup against Substitute + Earthquake Mega Metagross is a coinflip, requiring Victini to use Flame Charge if Mega Metagross chooses to use Substitute and V-create if it does not use Substitute.

Team Options

Fast Electric- and Grass-type Pokemon like Electrium Z Zeraora and Choice Scarf Tapu Bulu can beat Water-types like Mega Gyarados, Greninja, and Mega Slowbro. In return, Victini can take care of Pokemon like Mega Mawile, Mega Gardevoir, and Mega Venusaur. Mold Breaker Outrage users like Choice Scarf Haxorus and Mega Gyarados can beat Dragon-types like Dragonite, Mega Charizard X, and Kommo-o. Victini can cover Pokemon like Magearna, Celesteela, and most Mega Metagross variants in return. Bulky Water-type Pokemon like Primarina and Tapu Fini can take care of Ground-types like Donphan, Zygarde, and Landorus-T. Synergistically, Victini can defeat Pokemon like Mega Charizard Y, Mega Venusaur, and Kartana.

Z-Celebrate.description:
Moves

Celebrate is required for this set to function, allowing Victini to boost up all of its stats with Z-Celebrate as well as raise Stored Power's Base Power to 120. Stored Power allows Victini to hit foes like Mega Charizard X, Kommo-o, and boosted Bulk Up Zeraora. V-create is also a must-have, sporting a huge 180 Base Power on top of STAB and an Attack boost from Z-Celebrate to beat threats that resist Stored Power like Gardevoir and Magearna, as well as Zeraora that has used Charge. Taunt allows Victini to shut down stall Pokemon and Substitute users that would otherwise wall it, such as Mega Altaria and Mega Audino. Alternatively, Hidden Power Ground can be run to beat Heatran as well as ease the Substitute + Earthquake Mega Metagross matchup.

Set Details

212 Special Attack EVs along with a Rash nature allow Victini to OHKO offensive Mega Charizard X after a Z-Celebrate boost, while 232 Speed EVs allow Victini to outspeed Adamant Choice Scarf Haxorus after a boost. 16 Attack and 48 HP EVs give Victini the best chances of simultaneously OHKOing a bulky Charge-boosted Zeraora with V-create, tanking two Outrages from specially defensive Mega Charizard X, and tanking specially defensive Kommo-o's Clangorous Soulblaze followed by Clanging Scales.

Usage Tips

Unfortunately, because of this set's lack of bulk investment, hard-hitting hyper offensive Pokemon, even if they're weak to Psychic or Fire, can threaten Victini and should be avoided. Victini is OHKOed by Naganadel, relies on damage rolls for taking out foes like Mega Lopunny, and gives a Special Attack Download boost to Genesect, causing offensive Choice Specs sets to have a favorable damage roll against Victini. The only times where Victini may not want to use Z-Celebrate immediately are during scenarios where it must consider using Taunt first in order to prevent a crucial status move. These two exceptions are against Mega Mawile and non-Occa Berry Taunt Whimsicott; both of them are coinflips. Against Mega Mawile, Victini must either use Taunt if Mega Mawile uses Swords Dance or use Z-Celebrate if Mega Mawile attacks immediately. Against Whimsicott, Victini must either use V-create immediately if Whimsicott uses Taunt or use its own Taunt if Whimsicott does not. Against Mega Charizard X, simply use Z-Celebrate followed by Stored Power, which will OHKO offensive sets and 2HKO Mega Charizard X if it is specially defensive; specially defensive Mega Charizard X will be both unable to outspeed Victini after a Dragon Dance and unable to 2HKO it with unboosted Outrage. Against Zeraora, after using Z-Celebrate turn one, act according to what move Zeraora uses. If Zeraora attacks immediately and does not get the small chance of KOing or uses Charge, use V-create for the OHKO. If it uses Bulk Up, use Stored Power. Even if Stored Power does not OHKO, Zeraora will be unable to KO Victini before another Stored Power KOes it.

Team Options

Fast Electric- and Grass-type Pokemon like Electrium Z Zeraora and Choice Scarf Tapu Bulu can beat Water-types like Mega Gyarados, Greninja, and Mega Slowbro. In return, Victini can take care of Pokemon like Ferrothorn, Mega Gardevoir, and Mega Venusaur. Mold Breaker Outrage users, namely Choice Scarf Haxorus and Mega Gyarados, can beat Dragonite, one of the greatest threats in 1v1. Victini can cover Pokemon like Magearna, Celesteela, and most Mega Metagross variants in return. Bulky Water-type Pokemon like Primarina and Tapu Fini can take care of Ground-types like Donphan, Zygarde, and Landorus-T. Synergistically, Victini can defeat Pokemon like Mega Charizard Y, Mega Venusaur, and Kartana.

Z-Psychic.description:
Moves

Psychium Z powers Psychic up into Shattered Psyche, which is used most specifically for KOing Kommo-o, but also Pokemon like Mega Venusaur and Mega Lopunny. It is the highest Base Power move on the set, so it is used to KO Pokemon like Donphan after Sturdy is broken. Blue Flare takes out Pokemon weak to Fire such as Magearna, Celesteela, Mega Metagross, and Serperior. Glaciate can slow down the opposing Pokemon while also dealing chip damage, which is useful against foes like offensive Mega Charizard X and slow or Choice Band Dragonite sets. It can also beat Zygarde most of the time. Will-O-Wisp can be used to cripple physical attackers as well as do a little bit of chip damage to beat Donphan, Golem, and physical Dragonite.

Set Details

80 HP and 248 Defense EVs is are the most efficient way to tank both burned Golem's Tectonic Rage followed by Sucker Punch, as well as special Dragonite's Supersonic Skystrike followed by Extreme Speed. The extra 180 EVs are put into Special Attack with a Modest nature for maximized reliability in matchups reliant on damage rolls.

Usage Tips

Use Glaciate if Victini can survive the current turn and will outspeed the foe on the next turn. This is useful if the foe already outspeeds Victini or is using a Speed-boosting move, like in the case of offensive Mega Charizard X or special Dragonite. Victini should use Will-O-Wisp if there is an ability like Multiscale or Sturdy that only works with maximum HP, such as against Dragonite or Donphan. Against Kommo-o, go for Shattered Psyche, which should always OHKO it as long as Victini is faster. This variant of Victini can lure in Donphan, Golem, and slow Dragonite sets as well as Choice Band Dragonite, as Victini usually has a poor matchup against these threats. Keep in mind that Victini will not reliably beat a Dragonite that outspeeds it and will lose to Choice Scarf variants. If Donphan is running Bulldoze, Victini will have to anticipate it with Glaciate, although Bulldoze Donphan is not very common. Victini will also have to predict Mega Metagross's use of Substitute by using Blue Flare immediately rather than Will-O-Wisp.

Team Options

Fast Electric- and Grass-type Pokemon like Electrium Z Zeraora and Choice Scarf Tapu Bulu can beat Water-types like Mega Gyarados, Greninja, and Mega Slowbro. In return, Victini will take care of Pokemon like Mega Mawile, Mega Venusaur, and Donphan. Fairy-type Pokemon like Mega Altaria and Mega Diancie can beat Dragon-types like Garchomp and Mega Charizard X as well as Dark-types like Mega Gyarados and Mega Tyaranitar. Victini can cover Pokemon like Magearna, Celesteela, and Mega Metagross in return. Bulky Water-type Pokemon like Primarina and Tapu Fini can take care of Ground-types like Mega Tyranitar, Krookodile, and Landorus-T. Synergistically, Victini can defeat Pokemon like Mega Charizard Y, Mega Venusaur, and Kartana.

Choice Scarf.description:
Moves

V-create is Victini’s strongest move by far, and it can be used to burst Steel-types like Magearna, Celesteela, and Genesect or beat Pokemon that are unable to effectively hit Victini, and generally frail Pokemon such as Mega Gardevoir, Tapu Lele, non-Timid Choice Scarf Porygon-Z, and Volcarona. Bolt Strike can be used against Water-types like Tapunium Z Tapu Fini and Greninja as well as Flying-types like Choice Scarf Togekiss. Zen Headbutt can be used against Poison-types like Mega Venusaur, Nihilego, and Naganadel. Trick can shut down stall Pokemon that do not use Z-Crystals or Mega Stones like Type: Null and Pyukumuku. It can also be used to force Deoxys-S into a coinflip between using Taunt against Trick or Iron Defense against V-create.

Set Details

252 Attack EVs alongside an Adamant nature are used to deal as much damage as possible. 252 Speed EVs and Choice Scarf are used to outspeed as many foes as possible. A Jolly nature can also be used to outspeed +1 base 90 Speed Pokemon like Timid Choice Scarf Porygon-Z.

Usage Tips

Use Trick against stall Pokemon without a Z-Crystal or Mega Stone like Type: Null that do not want to be locked into a single move. Victini will outspeed and OHKO non-Timid Choice Scarf Porygon-Z and occasionally OHKO bulkier Normalium Z Porygon-Z variants. It will also only sometimes OHKO Bulk Up Outrage Zeraora and 2HKO Kommo-o. In the case of Kommo-o, the significant flinch chance of two Zen Headbutts can sometimes remedy this.

Team Options

Electric- and Grass-type Pokemon like Electrium Z Zeraora and Tapu Bulu can beat Water-types like Mega Gyarados, Primarina, and Mega Slowbro, while Victini can take care of Pokemon like Choice Scarf Porygon-Z, Mega Gardevoir, and Mega Venusaur. Mold Breaker Outrage users like Choice Scarf Haxorus and Mega Gyarados can beat Dragon-types like Dragonite, Mega Charizard X, and Garchomp. Victini can cover Pokemon like Magearna, Celesteela, and most Mega Metagross in return. Bulky Water-type Pokemon like Primarina and Tapu Fini can take care of Ground-types like Donphan, Zygarde, and Landorus-T. Synergistically, Victini can defeat Pokemon like Mega Charizard Y, Mega Venusaur, and Kartana.

monotype.overview:
Psychic

Victini plays a big role on Psychic teams as a check to Bug- and Steel-types thanks to its Fire typing. It's especially useful in checking Volcarona, which is a huge threat to Psychic teams, as it can Speed tie with it, take a +1 Bug Buzz, and always OHKO it with V-create. Its base 100 stats across the board give it decent bulk, offensive capabilities, and speed. Victini has access to an insanely powerful STAB move in V-create, which allows it to function as a great wallbreaker, especially with Choice Band. Victini is also a great Choice Scarf user thanks to its good Speed and pivoting capabilities with U-turn. It has a great movepool that includes coverage options like Bolt Strike and a great tool in Blue Flare, which helps it sweep Bug teams. Unfortunately, its Fire typing gives it a weakness to Stealth Rock, which heavily limits its pivoting capabilities, as well as to common offensive types in Water, Ground, and Rock. Although it sits at a solid Speed tier, Victini can be outsped and revenge killed by faster Pokemon like Terrakion, Keldeo, and Mega Diancie, especially after a Speed drop from V-create.

Fire

Thanks to Fire's ability to provide sun support, Choice Band Victini is capable of at least 2HKOing almost every Pokemon that is not immune to Fire-type attacks with its powerful V-create, making it the strongest wallbreaker in Monotype. Notably, Victini's V-create is capable of breaking every defensive core that typically gives Fire trouble, including Normal's, Poison's, and Water's, meaning it hardly needs to predict in spite of using a Choice item. Victini can also use extra supportive options in Bolt Strike to KO almost all Water-types and Fire-immune Pokemon and U-turn to avoid Pursuit trappers and pivot into teammates. It has decent defensive stats for an offensive Pokemon, allowing it to take some weaker hits relatively easily, particularly Scald from Water-type walls in sun. Unfortunately, V-create's Defense and Special Defense drops make Victini very easy to revenge kill, a problem only compounded by the accompanying loss in Speed allowing even slower Pursuit trappers like Scizor to trap and KO Victini. To make the Speed loss even more of an issue, its natural Speed is already rather average, making it only really able to beat defensive Pokemon and a handful of the slowest offensive Pokemon like Mamoswine. Victini does still have trouble fitting onto some Fire teams, as it doesn't help with the more important offensive threats to the type in Nihilego and Mega Diancie, and other Fire-type Pokemon like Mega Charizard X and Infernape can wallbreak while compressing other roles such as setup sweeper and priority revenge killer.
monotype.comments:
Other Options

Psychic

Flame Plate can be used on Trick Room teams to turn V-create into a strong spammable STAB move while enabling Victini to switch moves.

Fire

Victini's other options are outclassed or generally unviable.

Checks and Counters

Psychic

Heatran: Heatran checks Victini thanks to its Flash Fire ability. However, offensive Heatran needs to watch out for Choice Band-boosted Bolt Strike, which 2HKOes it.

Dragon-types: Dragon-type Pokemon such as Garchomp and Dragonite can take all of Victini's moves and force it to switch out.

Gastrodon: Gastrodon can switch into any Victini set and recover back to good health or fire off a STAB move; however, it needs to be wary of switching into Trick.

Physically Defensive Walls: Physically defensive Pokemon such as Porygon2 and Slowbro wall Victini unless it's running a Choice Band, in which case it can 2HKO both with the appropriate move.

Fire-resistant Pokemon: Water-, Fire-, and Rock-types like Keldeo, Mega Charizard X, and Terrakion can easily switch into Victini and take it out. Most Water-types, however, cannot switch into Bolt Strike well.

Dark-types: Dark-type Pokemon such as Greninja and Hydreigon can easily take out Victini with their STAB moves. Additionally, Pursuit trappers like Weavile and Alolan Muk can take advantage of Victini's Defense drop after using V-create to KO it. However, they don't appreciate taking a hit from Victini.

Ground-types: Bulky Ground-types like Gastrodon and Hippowdon can easily take a hit from Victini and KO it back with their STAB moves. Hippowdon cannot switch into Choice Band Victini, however. Sand Rush Excadrill can take out Choice Scarf Victini in sand, while Landorus can take out Choice Band Victini. Dugtrio can prevent Victini from switching out and takes any hit thanks to Focus Sash.

Revenge Killers: Victini is prone to being revenge killed after dropping its defenses and Speed with V-create. Priority users like Azumarill and Bisharp can take it out with Aqua Jet and Sucker Punch, respectively. Faster Pokemon like Terrakion, Mega Diancie, and Greninja can also take it out easily.

Fire

Mega Slowbro: Mega Slowbro is always capable of switching into any of Victini's moves when Stealth Rock isn't up because it is immune to Trick and can survive two hits from V-create and Bolt Strike. Mega Slowbro can then freely use Victini as setup fodder.

Pursuit: Because Victini's Defense and Speed drop after using V-create, it is very easy to Pursuit trap. For example, even Adamant Choice Band Scizor can outspeed a -1 Victini, and Pursuit almost always OHKOes even if Victini stays in, making it a surefire check for Bug teams.

Revenge Killers: Victini's average Speed even before V-create makes it very susceptible to many Pokemon that can revenge kill it, such as Keldeo, Garchomp, and Mega Gallade. Like with Pursuit users, the Defense and Special Defense drops incurred by V-create make it even easier to OHKO.

Opposing Weather: If sun is not active, Victini can be walled. Sand teams can wall it with physically defensive Gastrodon, which can spam Toxic or Scald after switching in. Rain is even more dangerous, as V-create's damage is not only unboosted but halved too, meaning it can be stopped by Mega Swampert.

Choice Scarf (Psychic).description:
Moves

V-create is Victini's strongest STAB move and is easily spammable due to its incredibly high Base Power. It's useful for hitting Bug-, Steel-, Grass-, and Ice-types such as Volcarona, Celesteela, Serperior, and Alolan Sandslash. Bolt Strike targets Water-types that attempt to switch in on a Fire-type move such as Gyarados and Azumarill. U-turn lets Victini pivot around and gain momentum when predicting the foe to switch out. Blue Flare is Victini's secondary Fire-type STAB move and is useful for late-game cleaning against Steel- and Bug-type teams, since it doesn't cause stat drops like V-create.

Set Details

Maximum investment in Speed with a Hasty nature and Choice Scarf is used to outspeed or Speed tie with threats like +1 Mega Gyarados, +1 Porygon-Z, and +1 Volcarona. Maximum investment is made in Attack in order to maximize Victini's damage output. A Hasty nature is preferred over Naive to allow Victini to deal with Volcarona better. Victory Star increases the accuracy of V-create, Bolt Strike, and Blue Flare.

Usage Tips

Keep Stealth Rock off the field, as it limits Victini's pivoting capabilities. Choice Scarf Victini is a great revenge killer because it outspeeds most unboosted Pokemon and can hit them with its powerful V-create. However, the drop in its Speed and defenses after using V-create makes it easy to revenge kill or set up on, which forces it to switch out. Be wary of using V-create when there are Pursuit trappers, as they can take advantage of the -1 Defense to deal huge damage to Victini. Switching Victini in on entry hazards should be avoided to preserve its health and longevity. Keep Victini healthy, especially in the Bug and Steel matchups where it needs to check threats like Volcarona and Mega Scizor. Locking Victini into a coverage move can sometimes turn it into setup bait. For example, while it may seem that Blue Flare can be spammed against Bug teams, Volcarona can use Victini to set up if it locks itself into Blue Flare. Therefore, use Blue Flare to clean up Bug teams after Volcarona is gone. Victini can often be used as a lead and can scout the opponent's play with U-turn. U-turn should also be used to pivot out of checks like Porygon2 and Gastrodon. Although Victini's bulk is decent, it should avoid switching in on powerful attacks such as Tapu Koko's Thunderbolt and Scolipede's Megahorn. Keep Victini away from poison and paralysis; poison harms its longevity and limits its ability to pivot around, and paralysis halves its Speed, rendering it almost useless.

Team Options

Choice Scarf Victini is a staple pick on Psychic teams due to its ability to check Bug- and Steel-types as well as revenge kill. Jirachi is a great partner to Victini, as it can pivot into strong special attacks as well as check Rock-types like Nihilego. Jirachi can also set Stealth Rock, bring Victini in safely through a slow U-turn, and give Victini another chance to clean up with Wish. Mew can set Stealth Rock while being able to stallbreak and remove common checks to Victini such as Porygon2 and Quagsire. Double Dance Mew appreciates having Victini bring it in safely via U-turn and give it more opportunities to set up. In return, Mew can wallbreak with +2 Genesis Supernova and set Psychic Terrain, which protects Victini from priority moves like Sucker Punch. Celebi can switch into Water- and Ground-types easily. It can also absorb status thanks to its great ability in Natural Cure and set Stealth Rock. Slowbro can switch into and check many physical attackers that threaten Victini such as Terrakion and Rhyperior. With a Colbur Berry, it can additionally check Dark-types like Mega Sharpedo and Mega Gyarados with Thunder Wave and Grass Knot. Mega Slowbro and Victini can take out Steel teams more easily together. Mega Slowbro appreciates having Victini wear down the opposing team with V-create, as that allows it to set up and clean up more easily. Conversely, Mega Slowbro is a great switch-in to Knock Off for Victini.

Deoxys-S can stack entry hazards such as Spikes and Stealth Rock to wear down the opposing team, making it easier for Victini to clean up. Latios and Mega Latias can get rid of Stealth Rock with Defog. They also provide a much-appreciated Ground immunity and switch-in to Water-types like Rotom-Wash. Mega Gardevoir and Mega Gallade are excellent wallbreakers that can weaken Victini's checks in addition to checking Dark-types. Furthermore, they can break through Poison's defensive core of Toxapex, Alolan Muk, and Mega Venusaur, allowing Victini to clean up with ease. Mega Alakazam is a good special attacker that can beat many of Victini's checks, such as Heatran and Kingdra, thanks to its Trace ability. Meloetta is a great check to Ghost-types like Alolan Marowak and Choice Scarf Gengar thanks to its Normal typing. It can also wallbreak and let Victini clean up more easily.

Choice Band (Psychic).description:
Moves

V-create is Victini's strongest and most spammable attack because it deals a massive amount of damage to Pokemon that don't resist it, often 2HKOing them. Walls that do resist it like Mantine and Torkoal still take a huge amount of damage. It's especially useful for hitting Bug- and Steel-types that Psychic teams have trouble dealing with. Bolt Strike takes care of Water-types that try to switch in on V-create such as Toxapex and Mega Slowbro. U-turn lets Victini pivot around or get momentum when predicting the foe to switch out. Trick allows Victini to cripple passive Pokemon that can be annoying to take out such as Gastrodon.

Set Details

Maximum investment in Attack with a Choice Band allows Victini to hit as hard as possible, enabling it to KO walls like Landorus-T, Hippowdon, and Toxapex with the appropriate move. Maximum investment in Speed is used along with a Jolly nature to let Victini Speed tie with other base 100 Speed Pokemon such as Volcarona and Manaphy, outspeed Pokemon like Landorus-T and Kyurem-B, and outspeed Rotom-Wash even at -1. Victory Star increases the accuracy of Victini's V-create and Bolt Strike.

Usage Tips

Victini can be sent out at any point of the game to wallbreak and weaken foes for teammates like Latios and Mega Alakazam to clean up. Victini can bluff a Choice Scarf set in order to lure in and KO walls like Hippowdon and Slowbro. Choice Band should be revealed when trying to surprise the opponent with a strong Choice Band-boosted V-create. Gaining momentum with U-turn is much more effective once the opponent knows Victini's using Choice Band. V-create can be spammed with freedom because it can break almost all of Victini's defensive checks. However, Victini will be forced to switch out the turn after due to the stat drops. Trick should be used against Steel teams to allow Victini to switch between Bolt Strike and V-create, effectively breaking the team. Keep in mind that Victini may receive a useless item like Rocky Helmet after using Trick, however. Barring the Steel matchup, though, losing Choice Band is almost never worth the move freedom. Victini should be kept away from entry hazards to remain as healthy as possible throughout the game.

Team Options

Since this Victini set needs to switch out more often, pivots such as Jirachi, Celebi, and Slowbro are great partners. Jirachi and Celebi can set Stealth Rock, giving Victini an easier time wallbreaking. Additionally, Jirachi can bring it in safely through a U-turn, restore its health with Wish, and cripple faster Pokemon with Thunder Wave, and Celebi can absorb status and switch into Ground- and Water-types for Victini. Thanks to its amazing bulk, Slowbro can check most physical attackers. It can also cripple faster Pokemon with Thunder Wave. Deoxys-S can stack entry hazards like Spikes and Stealth Rock, which increases Victini's offensive presence tremendously, as well as set up dual screens, which help keep Victini safe and are useful against offensive teams. Due to the lack of Choice Scarf on this set, alternate Choice Scarf users like Meloetta and Latios can be used. Meloetta can check Ghost-types like Gengar thanks to its Normal typing. Latios can remove entry hazards with Defog and wallbreak alongside Victini. Additionally, Choice Scarf Latios outspeeds common Choice Scarf users such as Keldeo, Terrakion, and Hydreigon and puts tremendous pressure on Dragon teams. Mega Latias can also remove entry hazards with Defog, provide a Ground immunity, and switch into Water-types like Keldeo. Calm Mind Mega Latias capitalizes on Victini's ability to take out its checks. Cleaners like Double Dance Mew and Mega Alakazam appreciate Victini's wallbreaking abilities. Mega Gardevoir can check Dark-types thanks to its Fairy typing and weather sweepers like Excadrill and Kingdra thanks to its pre-Mega ability in Trace.

Choice Band (Fire).description:
Moves

V-create makes Victini an unstoppable wallbreaker under sun, able to hit almost anything for at least a 2HKO at the cost of almost forcing it to switch out after every attack. When sun isn't up to boost V-create's damage output, Bolt Strike pressures Water teams by being able to 2HKO even Toxapex and Mega Slowbro with Stealth Rock support, as only Electric-immune Water-types can switch into it and it doesn't drop Victini's Speed. U-turn allows Victini to switch out to a teammate on a forced switch, which lets it gain momentum in matchups where it is afraid to KO foes because of Pursuit trappers like Scizor. Because sun-boosted V-create and Bolt Strike cover almost the entire metagame, Trick is rarely used, but it is a decent filler option in specific circumstances such as for crippling Gastrodon on sand teams or if sun is no longer an option.

Set Details

Choice Band and maximum Attack investment make Victini's V-create as strong as possible, and Victory Star makes sure it can never miss. A Jolly nature and 252 Speed EVs are used to make sure Victini can outspeed Pokemon such as Hydreigon, Mega Garchomp, and Kyurem-B that would otherwise be able to KO it.

Usage Tips

Victini should be sent in as often as possible when sun is up, as it is all but guaranteed a KO with V-create if it is in against a slower Pokemon. If sun is up and there are no Fire-immune Pokemon on the opposing team, V-create is almost always spammable, as even Pokemon that resist it can be easily KOed. However, be careful of Pursuit users, as Victini is a sitting duck after using V-create and will almost certainly be taken out by them. For example, be careful of spamming V-create too much against Poison teams, as Alolan Muk can outspeed a -3 Victini and be guaranteed to Pursuit trap it. Don't be afraid to take Toxic from walls to KO them, as Victini rarely stays in long enough for the scaling poison damage to matter. You should be aware of V-create's 8 PP, as it can disappear rather quickly, and Victini is an unimpressive wallbreaker without V-create. This is especially problematic against Pressure Pokemon or Protect users that can stall additional PP out. Victini is also very dependent on Choice Band to make its V-create strong enough to wallbreak, so it should avoid letting even weaker Knock Off users like Tornadus-T remove its item. Victini will need to switch in and out frequently due to V-create's drops, so be diligent in removing Stealth Rock to make sure Victini is as healthy as possible. Bolt Strike should mainly be used only against Fire-immune Pokemon or against Water teams when Victini can possibly be setup fodder after using V-create, as Pokemon like Suicune and Keldeo can only set up on V-create. In other circumstances, even against Pokemon that resist V-create, Bolt Strike is usually not worth needing to predict around. Trick should almost never be used, but if your sun setter is KOed, Victini can use it to cripple its switch-ins.

Team Options

Torkoal is a necessary teammate for Victini, as it provides sun support, Stealth Rock, Rapid Spin, and a defensive pivot, all of which are essential to making Victini's job possible. Outside of Torkoal, Victini doesn't need much team support and helps its teammates more instead. However, Rotom-Heat can be a substitute for Torkoal on more offensive teams, as its dual screens support can protect Victini from Pursuit trappers, and it can use Defog to remove Stealth Rock as well while giving Victini free switches with Volt Switch. However, lacking sun support does noticeably lower Victini's damage output against faster Pokemon that can now switch into one V-create and threaten to revenge kill. If Torkoal is replaced for Rotom-Heat, Mega Charizard Y is a decent replacement that can still set sun for Victini. A Choice Scarf user in either Blacephalon or Infernape can be useful to take out faster Pokemon like Gengar, Mega Diancie, and Nihilego for Victini. Heatran can also beat Mega Diancie and Nihilego with its Steel typing while providing Stealth Rock if necessary. Setup sweepers like Mega Charizard X and Volcarona appreciate Victini's ability to break almost all defensive Pokemon that can stop them, making them even more threatening. Volcanion can be helpful for switching into Water-types when Victini is forced out after using V-create. Notably, it is immune to Azumarill's Aqua Jet, making it useful for checking Z-Belly Drum Azumarill if Victini locks into V-create outside of sun.

mixandmega.overview: Red Orb Victini is a dangerous wallbreaker capable of circumventing conventional physical walls like Buzzwole, Gliscor, Toxapex, and Arceus-Ground. Its Desolate Land allows it to come into Water-type attacks with ease. However, giving Victini Red Orb means that Primal Groudon is unavailable for the team. Victini is capable of wearing down common Fire switch-ins, like Primal Groudon, but it isn't capable of outright beating them without running certain coverage. Several of Victini's moves have low PP, making them hard to spam in long matches. Victini's Speed is unaffected by Primal Reversion, which means that it is somewhat slow compared to other threats in Mix and Mega.
mixandmega.comments:
Other Options

Metagrossite allows Victini to boost the power of Bolt Strike, hit Blue Orb and Red Orb users harder and have stronger contact moves overall but forgoes being a mixed attacker. Lucarionite allows Victini to retain a mixed attacker role and powers up Psychic, which hits different Blue Orb targets such as Buzzwole, but such a Victini cannot force out Blue Orb users. Psychic is an option to hit both Blue Orb users and Giratina, but Bolt Strike handles most Blue Orb users already and isn't resisted by Steel. Fusion Bolt and Fusion Flare are weaker but more accurate than Bolt Strike and Blue Flare.

Checks and Counters

Dragon-types: Many common Dragon-types, like Arceus-Dragon and Giratina, easily handle Victini. Other Dragon-types like Zygarde-C and Mega Salamence must be wary of Glaciate.

Ground-types: Ground-types holding Venusaurite, Primal Groudon, and Lucarionite Zygarde easily handle the different Fire-type moves from Victini, although Glaciate threatens the Ground-types that are 4x weak to Ice.

Blue Orb users: Blue Orb users like Skarmory and Magearna can switch into V-create and Blue Flare with impunity, although Bolt Strike can punish some of them.

Fire-types: Fire-types like Entei and Primal Groudon can easily tank V-create or Blue Flare and retaliate with a super effective move. Victini can wear those down throughout the match, however.

Faster Pokemon with Super Effective Coverage: Faster Pokemon like Diancite Darkrai and Terrakion are able to outspeed and OHKO Victini with super effective moves.

Lunala: Lunala can tank a hit if Shadow Shield is active and strike back with super effective attack.

Pursuit: Pursuit users like Weavile can come in after Victini has gotten a Defense drop from V-create and threaten to KO it.

Red Orb.description:
Moves

V-create is capable of dealing massive damage to neutral targets under harsh sun. Bolt Strike hits Blue Orb users that might attempt to switch into V-create or Blue Flare such as Golisopod and Skarmory. Blue Flare is able to better hit physical walls like Hippowdon. Glaciate hits Ground-types like Zygarde, Landorus-T, and Gliscor for super effective damage and can make Victini faster than switch-ins. Work Up enables Victini to hit even harder. Taunt shuts down Shuckle and helps Victini break certain Dragon-types, like Giratina without Dragon Tail. It also prevents defensive Pokemon such as Gliscor from recovering their health against Victini. U-turn is an option that allows Victini to pivot at the cost of missing out on coverage or utility.

Set Details

A Hasty nature is best for Victini's mixed attacker role. Red Orb lets Victini hit hard with V-create and Blue Flare thanks to the excellent stats boosts and Desolate Land given. An alternative spread of 160 HP / 252 Atk / 24 SpA / 72 Spe with a Lonely nature lets it beat Z-Geomancy Xerneas, taking an uninvested Moonblast after a drop from V-create, and makes it bulkier.

Usage Tips

Victini should be used aggressively, since its consistent checks are not common. Standard Fire switch-ins will often find themselves 3HKOed by its coverage. Despite its low PP, V-create is usually the safest option to use if in doubt thanks to its general power. Bolt Strike should be used in case of a predicted Blue Orb user switch-in, like Skarmory or Golisopod Blue Flare is better used for physical walls like Zapdos, Manectite Mew, Gliscor, and Hippowdon, as it's able to take advantage of their lower Special Defense and has a chance to burn them. It also doesn't drop Victini's Speed, allowing it to stay in and attack again. Work Up should be used when it's safe, such as on forced switches against Mew or Blue Orb users. If running Taunt, Victini can act as an anti-lead against Shuckle.

Team Options

While Victini breaks a lot of walls, it's not capable of doing it as easily if it gets chipped every time it comes in, so Defog support from teammates like Giratina and Arceus-Fairy is appreciated. Dragon-types wall Victini fairly easily, so any Pokemon that can threaten them out such as Xerneas, Tapu Lele, and Altarianite Zygarde are appreciated. Victini can also pair with a Blue Orb user, such as Kyogre, to create a core that pressures Dragon-types. Magearna is an exceptional teammate to Victini, as it is capable of taking advantage of the switch-ins that Victini forces and not many Pokemon are capable of walling both. Ground-types like Lucarionite Zygarde, Gliscor, and Arceus-Ground are good teammates, as they are capable of pivoting into a weakened Primal Groudon and deal with it.

doublesou.overview: Victini finds a unique niche in the Doubles OU metagame thanks to the vast utility provided by its unique moveset and all-around solid stats. Sporting an almost-exclusive combination of Fire and Psychic typing, Victini is easily able to switch into and check prominent metagame threats like Kartana and Mega Metagross. Moreover, its coveted access to both Glaciate and Incinerate allow Victini to support its team in a wide variety of ways. As a Fire-type, Victini is naturally walled by every common Water-type as well as the omnipresent Incineroar, but Victini can easily pivot out of tough matchups or turn its focus to its less damage-oriented roles when facing these threats. In addition, Victini can quite successfully run a Choice Scarf set thanks to its high Speed and access to Final Gambit, which can often take out a problematic enemy in one hit at the cost of its own life.
doublesou.comments:
Other Options

Energy Ball can be used over Incinerate on the bulky set to provide coverage against Gastrodon and Tapu Fini. An offensive Trick Room set provides an archetype that typically struggles with Amoonguss a strong offensive answer, though it’s left wholly walled by one of the most commonly-used Pokemon in Incineroar. Choice Scarf sets could use Trick to cripple bulky Pokemon that would otherwise sit in front of it fairly safely like Porygon2 or Cresselia. Normalium Z Celebrate sets take advantage of the Z-Move’s omniboosting effect and can work well with spread damage in Heat Wave and a powerful Stored Power; however, they’re typically too weak to get through common Pokemon like Landorus-T and have generally poor coverage. Access to Final Gambit also offers Victini the potential for a strong Fighting-type Z-Final Gambit that can nab a surprise KO on Incineroar and Tyranitar, two of its erstwhile most effective checks.

Checks and Counters

Water-types: Bulky Victini has no way to significantly damage the common bulky Water-types in the tier, and Milotic can take advantage of Glaciate to get a Competitive boost. Despite having access to Bolt Strike, Choice Scarf Victini also has issues beating the most common Water-types in the format, such as Tapu Fini, Suicune, and Volcanion, as it simply can't hit hard enough. Choice Scarf sets are also outrun and OHKOed by Swift Swim Kingdra, leaving Victini with no possible options for retaliation. They should be wary of switching into a Final Gambit, however, which easily OHKOes most of the tier's common Water-types.

Incineroar: Incineroar's typing and defenses make it an easy answer to any Victini set, often taking even a healthy Victini's Final Gambit. In addition, its Intimidate, access to Knock Off, and ability to chip away at Victini's health with Fake Out can all cripple Victini.

Tyranitar: Tyranitar makes a strong switch-in to all Victini's moves and also activates a sandstorm as it switches in, slowly whittling away Victini's HP and potentially neutering the power of Final Gambit in the process.

Opposing Speed Control: Since Choice Scarf Victini relies heavily on moving first to effectively conduct Final Gambit trades and hit with fast and strong V-creates, it struggles against teams that manage to get Trick Room or Tailwind up. Diancie and Porygon2 easily set Trick Room in Victini's face, while Suicune and Mega Salamence can reliably use Tailwind.

Stealth Rock: Assault Vest Victini relies on being healthy and pivoting often to do its job effectively and Choice Scarf sets need their HP to keep the power of Final Gambit. Stealth Rock removing 25% of its health on each switchin greatly inhibits this, and common setters such as Landorus-T and Tyranitar also threaten Victini with super effective STAB moves.

Bulky Support.description:
Moves

Supportive Victini has a pretty straightforward moveset with little need for variation. An attack like Blue Flare should be used at any given opportunity, and Assault Vest Victini is no exception. Victini is one of three Pokemon with access to Glaciate, which is essentially just a stronger Icy Wind. This allows Victini to provide its team with valuable speed control while also hitting the various Ice-weak Pokemon of the format, such as Landorus-T and Zygarde, for significant damage. U-turn lets Victini function as an effective pivot. Incinerate may seem like an odd choice at first, but it has incredible utility in a metagame full of Berries such as Sitrus and the various pinch Berries like Mago and Wiki. If Victini is instead holding an Iapapa Berry, it may opt for Protect.

Set Details

A Timid nature with the given Speed EVs allows Victini to outspeed all Deoxys-A after one Glaciate. 96 HP and 128 Special Defense EVs ensure that Assault Vest Victini will always survive two Earth Powers from standard bulky Landorus-T, which packs a Modest nature and 176 Special Attack EVs. Even without an Assault Vest, this spread allows Victini to take one Earth Power after taking Stealth Rock damage. As a consequence, Victini will always survive a Choice Band-boosted Thousand Arrows from Zygarde and almost always take two Stomping Tantrums from -1 Mega Metagross. The remaining EVs are dumped into Special Attack, which allows Victini to 2HKO the standard 252 HP / 28 SpD Landorus-T with Glaciate. With an Iapapa Berry equipped, Victini can receive a boost of recovery when it’s chipped low, also opening the door to run Protect and lessen the harm Stealth Rock can inflict.

Usage Tips

In general, Victini wants to come in on weak special attacks and use Glaciate once or twice before pivoting to a teammate that can effectively take advantage of the opponent's reduced Speed. If facing down Pokemon that typically hold a Berry, Incinerate is a great option for effectively removing a big chunk of their overall health. While it won't be scoring many KOs on its own, Blue Flare has acceptable damage output at worst and can allow Victini to prime opposing Pokemon for knockouts at the hands of its partners. Victini's nearly unique typing and above average bulk allow it to function as a very effective pivot into some very common Pokemon in the tier, such as Kartana and Kyurem-B. However, Victini's typing also burdens it with a weakness to such common attacks in Doubles OU as Earthquake, Rock Slide, and Knock Off, the last of which gets a special mention for removing Victini's important Assault Vest. That said, you must be selective about when to let Victini take the field; if it comes in at the wrong time, it can be crippled for the remainder of the game and lose most of its usefulness. In a similar vein, you must also be careful about letting Victini take Stealth Rock damage. Victini can still do its job from 75% of its health most of the time, but losing a quarter of its health multiple times severely hampers its staying power. Finally, Victini users must be very careful when facing Incineroar, which will take very little damage from any of Victini's attacks and can essentially switch into Victini for free and threaten with a powerful Knock Off. This means that it can be advantageous to use U-turn much more aggressively before opposing Incineroar are knocked out in order to prevent giving it a free turn.

Team Options

Pokemon that are naturally fast enough to take advantage of Glaciate Speed drops are great partners for Victini. While this pool of Pokemon is slightly narrower than that of other methods of speed control like Tailwind, there is still a wide selection of effective beneficiaries, such as Mega Metagross and Kyurem-B. Mega Metagross specifically can benefit a lot from having Assault Vest Victini as a partner, since it appreciates Victini's ability to roast troublesome Steel-types—just be careful about stacking Ground-type weaknesses. Pokemon weak to Grass-type attacks are also great partners for Victini, as Victini firmly handles the most common Grass-types in the tier, Kartana and Tapu Bulu. Thus, Victini is often seen with Tapu Fini, and the two create a strong core both offensively and defensively. Calm Mind Tapu Fini benefits from Glaciate, chip damage, Berry removal, and the elimination of one of its biggest checks in Kartana, while defensive Tapu Fini can keep Victini healthy with Heal Pulse. Grass-types make great partners for Victini due to their ability to check opposing Water-types like Tapu Fini and Milotic. Tapu Fini specifically can come in pretty easily on Victini and start setting up Calm Minds, so Pokemon like Kartana and Tapu Bulu can help to keep opposing Tapu Fini at bay. Both of these Pokemon also offer offensive options against Incineroar with their Fighting-type coverage moves, while Tapu Bulu is a very reliable switch-in to Ground-type Pokemon like Zygarde and Landorus-T. Victini also partners well with Intimidate users such as Landorus-T and Mega Manectric for a few reasons. Both of these Pokemon form a powerful pivoting core with Victini thanks to U-turn and Volt Switch while covering for Victini's uninvested Defense. Mega Manectric and Victini cast a wide net with their type coverage, always combining for Electric + Fire + Ice attacks between the two regardless of Mega Manectric's moveset. Mega Manectric's Snarl can also augment Victini's ability to sponge special attacks. Landorus-T, on the other hand, gets a special mention for its Ground-type immunity and ability to check Incineroar quite effectively. Mega Manectric and Landorus-T also both help offensively check Volcanion, which is one of Victini's best counters. Finally, Incineroar checks are mandatory on teams that carry Victini. A few previously mentioned Pokemon like Tapu Fini and Landorus-T fill this role well, but other Pokemon like Zygarde or Diancie take little damage from Incineroar's attacks and can fire back with powerful STAB moves.

Choice Scarf.description:
Moves

Final Gambit allows Victini to easily trade itself for the removal of a crucial attacker or pivot from an opposing team, generally without much counterplay. V-create is an alternate source of damage that doesn't sacrifice Victini, but unfortunately, it lowers Victini's defenses and Speed, leaving it vulnerable to damage that could lower Final Gambit's effective power or even outright KO Victini. Bolt Strike acts as a strong coverage move to hit Water-types such as Tapu Fini and Volcanion, while U-turn rounds out the set, allowing Victini to easily pivot out of unfavorable situations.

Set Details

The given EV spread focuses on allowing Victini to effectively use Final Gambit: the HP investment gives Victini the same HP stat as fully invested Zapdos, and equivalently other base 90 HP foes, allowing Victini to OHKO it with Final Gambit. Meanwhile, its Speed is maximized to allow it to outspeed Choice Scarf Genesect to threaten it with a V-create. The remaining EVs are invested into Attack to get the most damage out of its other moves.

Usage Tips

Victini is most effectively used as a lead, with the capacity to efficiently trade itself for a key threat on the opposing side or to U-turn out if no viable target presents itself. However, if it doesn't trade itself off early-game, it should be played cautiously later on—generally, one should keep Victini's health high in order to preserve its damage output from Final Gambit, so it should be brought into play primarily off free switches or off the back of a slow U-turn or Volt Switch. In the same vein, Victini should generally be played to avoid chip damage from Stealth Rock or priority moves like Fake Out and Zygarde's Extreme Speed; though these might seem like sources of insignificant chip damage, Victini needs to be near or at full health in order to OHKO some of its key targets, including Zapdos and Landorus-T, with Final Gambit. Furthermore, when using its non-Final Gambit moves, Victini should be going for guaranteed KOs, since it doesn't want to risk taking unnecessary damage and hamper its Final Gambit damage. Finally, when using V-create, one should be wary of the stat drops the move causes, especially the Speed drop, which nullifies the Choice Scarf boost and may force Victini to leave the field and return later before it can pose a significant threat.

Team Options

Victini's best use is alongside an ally that needs to set up in some way, as it helps to alleviate the offensive pressure exerted on its partner by removing a key threat on the opposing side with Final Gambit. Good examples of such teammates include Dragon Dance Mega Salamence and Zygarde, which can easily get an important boost to chunk teams early-game or clean up late-game. Aurora Veil Alolan Ninetales is a more passive example of a partner that requires this setup opportunity, but it can nonetheless make use of it to ease other teammates' setup, conveniently aided by the free switch Victini creates after fainting from Final Gambit. Similarly, offensive Trick Room setters like Stakataka appreciate Victini as a more permanent solution to their threats, in the form of Final Gambit incapacitating a foe for the remainder of the match instead of just for a single turn. Allies like Tapu Fini that typically struggle with opposing Grass-types will also appreciate Victini's strong Fire-type STAB attacks.

lc.overview: Snivy's niche comes from the ability Contrary and the move Leaf Storm, which when paired together give Snivy a 130-Base Power move that also provides a +2 boost to its Special Attack, making it one of the best wallbreakers and the best offensive Grass-type Pokemon in Little Cup. Contrary also has several other uses, including making Snivy one of the best Sticky Web checks in the metagame by giving it a +1 boost to Speed every time it comes in when the entry hazard is up. In addition, Defog lets it support its teammates by clearing entry hazards. However, Snivy's poor offensive movepool forces it to rely on Hidden Power for coverage against the wide variety of Pokemon that resist Leaf Storm. Additionally, Snivy hits 17 Speed, which, while decent, leaves it susceptible to being revenge killed by faster Pokemon; couple this with its mediocre defenses, and its sweeping potential becomes rather limited.
lc.comments:
Other Options

Other Hidden Power types are a possibility on any set if a team needs coverage for a specific Pokemon. Hidden Power Rock is a notable option that allows Snivy to lure in and dispatch Larvesta as well as being able to hit both other Fire-types and Flying-types fairly hard, but it requires that Snivy run 16 Speed. Snivy also has access to Taunt, but most Pokemon can't set up on it anyway because of its ability to boost its stats while dealing damage. Giga Drain is an option as a secondary Grass-type STAB attack that provides recovery but is usually less useful than Snivy's other options. Snivy also has access to Light Screen and Reflect, giving it potential as one of the more offensively powerful screen setters in Little Cup, but dual screens tends not to be a particularly useful strategy in LC, and Snivy doesn't have the bulk to set them especially well. Lastly, Snivy's access to Aromatherapy lets it heal status ailments of itself and its teammates, but it comes from an event that requires Snivy to run a Hardy nature.

Checks and Counters

Grass-resistant Pokemon: Due to Snivy's shallow coverage movepool, Pokemon that resist Leaf Storm can reliably check it so long as Snivy is not running the specific Hidden Power that deals with them. Poison-types, such as Croagunk and Alolan Grimer, as well as Fire-types, such as Ponyta and Larvesta, deal with non-Hidden Power Ground variants well, although Ponyta fears Glare against other sets. Foongus and Flying-types such as Vullaby can deal with non-Hidden Power Ice variants. Lastly, Steel-types, such as Pawniard and Magnemite, check non-Hidden Power Ground or Hidden Power Fire variants effectively. Pawniard is especially notable, since it also punishes Snivy's use of Defog with its ability Defiant. Most of these Pokemon can check Snivy once even if it is running the appropriate Hidden Power, but they can quickly be worn down enough such that, if running the right coverage move, Snivy can take them out.

Revenge Killers: Snivy is extremely prone to being revenge killed. Doduo, Gastly, and Ponyta, which naturally outspeed it, and Choice Scarf users can all revenge kill Snivy.

Eviolite Wallbreaker.description:
Moves

Leaf Storm hits anything that doesn't resist it hard and boosts Snivy's Special Attack. Defog allows Snivy to support its teammates by clearing entry hazards. Glare paralyzes switch-ins to Snivy, slowing them down for Snivy or a teammate to more easily handle. Knock Off is an alternative that cripples defensive switch-ins to make it easier for teammates to break through them. Synthesis increases Eviolite Snivy's longevity by giving it a form of recovery. The final slot goes to the Hidden Power that gives Snivy the best coverage given what its team needs. Hidden Power Ice is the most generally useful option, allowing Snivy to take care of Vullaby and Foongus. Hidden Power Ground is useful for hitting Fire-, Steel-, and Poison-types. Hidden Power Fire allows Snivy to hit Steel- and Grass-types, but because of the required Speed IV drop, it only allows Snivy to hit 16 Speed.

Set Details

240 Special Attack EVs maximize Snivy's Special Attack, allowing it to hit as hard as possible. 252 Speed EVs and a Timid nature bring Snivy to 17 Speed, allowing it to Speed tie with Drilbur and Archen and outspeed Pawniard. If Hidden Power Fire is run, Snivy only can hit 16 Speed, but this lets it use a spread of 76 HP / 240 SpA / 176 Spe to gain a point of mixed bulk. An Eviolite gives Snivy the bulk to act as a more reliable answer to Ground-type Pokemon defensively while still breaking down teams efficiently offensively. Contrary gives Snivy a +2 Special Attack boost every time it uses Leaf Storm and has other more niche uses, such as allowing Snivy to gain Speed against Sticky Web teams and deter Memento users.

Usage Tips

With an Eviolite, Snivy can take on more of a pivot role, being able to switch into Drilbur, Mudbray, and Chinchou reliably and immediately go on the offensive. Leaf Storm deals enormous amounts of damage to anything that doesn't resist it. Snivy can use its Hidden Power to deal with the Grass-resistant foes that switch in to deal with it, as well as paralyze switch-ins with Glare if the move is run. Defog should be used to clear entry hazards as necessary to support its team. Synthesis should be used periodically to allow Snivy to keep attacking, but it forfeits momentum when it is used. Despite having an Eviolite, Snivy should try not to switch into attacks it does not resist.

Team Options

This Snivy set works best on teams that need more defensive utility from a Grass-type but don't want to sacrifice momentum. Fire-type checks are helpful to Snivy, such as Ponyta and Chinchou. Flying-type checks, too, are important, notably Omanyte, Chinchou, Tirtouga, and Onix. Entry hazard support from the likes of Dwebble and Mudbray helps break down opposing teams. Snivy also works well as a teammate with Pokemon that need entry hazards such as Stealth Rock cleared, such as offensive Vullaby and Doduo.

Berry Juice.description:
Moves

Leaf Storm hits anything that doesn't resist it hard and boosts Snivy's Special Attack. Substitute allows Snivy to take advantage of the switches it forces and to force Pawniard into mind games if it attempts to revenge kill Snivy with Sucker Punch. Substitute can also help Snivy avoid the occasional status condition, particularly paralysis. Defog allows Snivy to support its team by clearing entry hazards. Knock Off is an alternative that cripples defensive switch-ins to make it easier for teammates to break through them later. Glare paralyzes switch-ins to Snivy, slowing them down for Snivy or a teammate to more easily handle or allowing Snivy to get a Substitute up. The final slot goes to the Hidden Power that gives Snivy the best coverage given what its team needs. Hidden Power Ice is the most generally useful option, allowing Snivy to take care of Vullaby and Foongus. Hidden Power Ground is useful for hitting Fire-, Steel-, and Poison-types. Hidden Power Fire allows Snivy to hit Steel- and Grass-types, but because the move requires a Speed IV drop, running it only allows Snivy to hit 16 Speed.

Set Details

Maximizing Snivy's Special Attack and Speed allows it to hit as hard and outrun as much of the metagame as possible. With a Timid nature, Snivy hits 17 Speed, allowing it to Speed tie with Drilbur and Archen and reliably outspeed Pawniard and fast Vullaby variants. With the Hidden Power Fire Speed IV drop, Snivy can still outspeed most of the walls it aims to break, but it is more susceptible to being revenge killed by 17 Speed Pokemon, and Pawniard and Vullaby check it more reliably. If running Hidden Power Fire, Snivy should be given an EV spread of 76 HP / 240 SpA / 176 Spe to gain an HP point in exchange for the lost Speed point. Snivy is equipped with a Berry Juice to restore its health once during a match, which is often all it needs to break down opposing walls and clear the way for a sweeper. Contrary gives Snivy a +2 Special Attack boost every time it uses Leaf Storm and has other, more niche uses, such as allowing Snivy to gain Speed against Sticky Web teams and deter Memento users.

Usage Tips
