Without cleric support, switching Chesnaught into these Pokemon, despite its typing and resistances, can cripple it for the remainder of the game.

Team Options

Chesnaught fits best on bulky offense and balance teams that need a physically defensive Pokemon with a good matchup against several of the tier's most threatening Dark-types. It appreciates Flying-type checks such as Rotom-H, Nihilego, and Diancie greatly, as they can pivot into foes like Moltres and Togekiss that Chesnaught is forced out by and appreciate Chesnaught dealing with more specially defensive foes such as Blissey. Stealth Rock support from teammates such as the aforementioned Nihilego and Diancie as well as other options such as Hippowdon, Mega Steelix, and Mega Aggron helps Chesnaught by stacking residual damage with Spikes and further punishing switches. The latter two options as well as other Steel-types such as Scizor can help Chesnaught in the matchup against Fairy- and Psychic-types such as Mega Altaria and Latias too. Bulky Water-types such as Slowbro, Tentacruel, and Empoleon can take care of threatening Fire-types such as Infernape and Volcanion for Chesnaught and appreciate its ability to switch into several physical attackers such as Crawdaunt that these Pokemon struggle with. Due to Chesnaught's susceptibility to status, cleric support from teammates such as Togekiss, Blissey, and Florges is appreciated, allowing it to switch into Scald and Toxic more freely to check certain Water-types or set up Spikes. The latter two can also provide Wish support to make Chesnaught less reliant on Synthesis. Immediate offensive threats such as Latias, Choice Band Crawdaunt, and Nidoking can help to make up for Chesnaught's overall passivity, preventing it from letting in too many opposing threats or giving bulkier foes more opportunities to recover HP. Chesnaught offers these Pokemon Spikes support for chip damage on foes as a result; Bisharp is an especially good teammate, providing offensive presence, being able to deter Defog with Defiant, and taking advantage of Spikes support immensely. Due to Chesnaught's role as a Spikes setter, having other team options that can punish opposing entry hazard removal, such as Taunt Hydreigon, Electrium Z Latias, and Pursuit Mega Aerodactyl, is extremely useful.

lc.overview: Fennekin can utilize Magician to make Solar Beam with Power Herb a viable coverage option. However, its stats are so low that it's outsped by most offensive Pokemon, not strong enough to KO neutral foes, and unable to take even neutral hits. Fennekin is always an inferior choice over Ponyta thanks to the latter's much higher stats and better movepool overall.

Magician.description: Fennekin can attempt to catch Fire-resistant Pokemon such as Staryu, Onix, and Mudbray with a super effective Power Herb-boosted Solar Beam and is best run on Sticky Web teams. But, this set is still outclassed by Grassium Z Ponyta because it is stronger, faster, bulkier, and has better options to aid in a late-game sweep such as Flame Charge and Hypnosis.

nu.overview: Delphox is a threatening Pokemon in NU due to its high Speed and Special Attack, great offensive typing, and fairly vast movepool that allows it to fulfill a number of roles, including a setup sweeper that breaks through defensive cores, a Wish passer, and a revenge killer that can also clean late-game. While it isn't perfect defensively, Delphox's typing in tandem with its decent bulk gives it the ability to soft check some of the most common special attackers such as Magmortar and Whimsicott as well as Fighting-types like Hariyama and Passimian. Delphox's access to useful coverage moves in Dazzling Gleam and Grass Knot also allows it to bypass a lot of typical Fire-type checks such as Guzzlord, Seismitoad, and Rhydon, and its access to moves such as Calm Mind, Trick, and Wish gives it the ability to support both itself and its teammates. However, Delphox suffers from an unfortunate weakness to Stealth Rock, which limits its ability to check the previously mentioned Pokemon consistently. Delphox's typing also leaves it vulnerable to Dark- and Rock-types such as Sneasel, Houndoom, and Aerodactyl as well as their STAB moves in Pursuit, Sucker Punch, and Stone Edge.
nu.comments:
Other Options

A Substitute + Calm Mind set with Salac Berry can be used to improve Delphox's chances of sweeping more offensive teams while allowing it to avoid status conditions and Pursuit from faster Dark-types, though Delphox doesn't appreciate dropping a move for Substitute. Choice Specs gives Delphox more immediate power at the cost of being unable to alternate between moves while not improving its matchup against faster, more offensive teams like Choice Scarf does.

Checks and Counters

Dark-types and Pursuit Trappers: Houndoom and Incineroar resist both of Delphox's STAB types and are only hit neutrally by Dazzling Gleam; furthermore, both can set up on Delphox with Nasty Plot and Swords Dance, respectively. Aerodactyl and Sneasel outspeed non-Choice Scarf Delphox and threaten to OHKO it or trap it with Pursuit.

Bulky Water-types: Bulky Water-types such as Slowking, Vaporeon, and Blastoise can take an unboosted Grass Knot rather well and retaliate with either a strong Scald or Toxic. However, they have a harder time checking Delphox if it has already used Calm Mind or is a Bloom Doom variant.

Bulky Rock-types: Rhydon can easily switch into any move other than Grass Knot from Delphox and threaten it out with Earthquake, while Aerodactyl outspeeds Delphox and OHKOes it with Stone Edge.

Specially Defensive Pokemon: Certain specially defensive Pokemon like Mega Audino, bulky Incineroar, and Druddigon can handle even boosted attacks from Calm Mind Delphox and either retaliate with strong STAB attacks or put it on a timer with Toxic. Other than Mega Audino, though, they must be wary of switching in on a potential Trick.

Revenge Killers: Naturally faster Pokemon such as Mismagius and Sneasel as well as faster Choice Scarf users such as Braviary and Passimian outspeed non-Choice Scarf Delphox and threaten to KO it with either strong or super effective attacks. Certain priority users like Decidueye are also capable of revenge killing Delphox, though they can't switch in.

Calm Mind.description:
Moves

Calm Mind increases Delphox's Special Attack and Special Defense by one stage, allowing it break through bulkier teams more easily. Fire Blast is Delphox's main Fire-type STAB move, dealing a lot of damage to non-Fire-resistant Pokemon like Gallade after a boost in power from Calm Mind. Psychic provides Delphox with a secondary STAB move that is more reliable. Alternatively, Dazzling Gleam can be used to nail bulkier Dark- and Dragon-type Pokemon such as Scrafty, Incineroar, and Druddigon, which would otherwise be a massive annoyance to Delphox. Grass Knot rounds out Delphox's coverage by giving it the ability to threaten bulky Ground-, Rock-, and Water-types such as Palossand, Rhydon, and Slowking.

Set Details

The investment in Speed and Special Attack makes Delphox as strong and as fast as possible, with a Timid nature being used to outspeed foes such as Rotom and Sigilyph. Firium Z turns Fire Blast into Inferno Overdrive, which gives Delphox access to a strong and reliable one-time attack that can be used to break through typical checks like Mega Audino. Alternatively, Grassium Z can be used to turn Grass Knot into Bloom Doom, which is capable of heavily damaging bulky Rock- and Water-types like Rhydon, Slowking, and Pyukumuku even unboosted. Colbur Berry can be used over either Z-Crystal if Delphox's team already has a Z-Move user, allowing Delphox to take Dark-type moves such as Knock Off from Sneasel and Passimian before KOing them with Fire Blast. Fairium Z is another option that can be used to break through Pokemon like Incineroar, but Firium Z and Grassium Z are more consistently threatening for teams to deal with. Blaze increases Fire Blast's power when Delphox is low on HP, which can potentially give it an easier time powering through foes such as Mega Audino with Inferno Overdrive after it uses Calm Mind.

Usage Tips

Since Delphox excels against slower, more defensive teams, avoid playing recklessly against them and letting Delphox acquire too much damage beforehand in order to use it to its fullest potential. If Delphox is not holding a Colbur Berry, it is rather vulnerable to Dark-types and Pursuit trappers, meaning that preserving it until these Pokemon have been removed may prove useful; however, if a teammate needs a certain defensive core broken through in order to reliably sweep late-game, Delphox can be used to wallbreak for them instead. Exercise caution in regard to using Firium Z. It should mainly be used after Delphox has used Calm Mind in order to break through bulkier foes such as Mega Audino and Piloswine or if Delphox really can't afford to miss against foes like Steelix. While Delphox doesn't appreciate taking a lot of damage before it attempts to set up, it is capable of taking resisted special attacks from Pokemon such as Sceptile.

Team Options

Calm Mind Delphox fits well on bulky offensive teams that are in need of a setup sweeper that can break through common defensive cores. Entry hazard support from Pokemon such as Steelix, Garbodor, and Piloswine is appreciated, as the chip damage gives Delphox an easier time breaking through bulkier Pokemon like Slowking and Incineroar. Due to Delphox's weakness to Stealth Rock, it also appreciates having teammates such as Rotom, Blastoise, and Silvally-Steel that can remove entry hazards. Silvally-Steel can put bulkier foes on a timer with Toxic and make use of Parting Shot in order to pivot Delphox in, while Rotom can cripple physical attackers with Will-O-Wisp and get Delphox in safely against bulkier Grass-types like Dhelmise with Volt Switch. Delphox's weakness to Dark means that checks to Dark-types are indispensable teammates. Fighting-type Pokemon such as Hariyama and Passimian can offensively check Dark-types and wallbreak for Delphox, which they have a much easier time doing due to Delphox removing their checks. Mega Audino can also check Dark-types and come to Delphox's aid against revenge killers such as Choice Scarf Braviary. Additionally, Mega Audino can provide cleric support, which helps in maintaining Delphox's longevity. Sneasel makes for a good teammate due to its ability to pressure bulky Pokemon that Delphox can struggle with breaking through unboosted like Druddigon and Aerodactyl as well as potentially remove Slowking with Pursuit. In return, Delphox can eliminate physically bulky Pokemon that Sneasel can struggle with like Vaporeon and Steelix as well as soft check Fighting-types like Hariyama.

Wish + Protect.description:
Moves

Wish heals Delphox and its teammates, which allows it to reliably use Toxic to stall foes out. Protect guarantees that Delphox will regain HP after using Wish, generates a free turn of Leftovers recovery, forces badly poisoned Pokemon to take an additional turn of damage, and allows Delphox to scout for moves. Mystical Fire is the preferred Fire-type attack, since it lets Delphox prevent Pokemon like Comfey and opposing Delphox from boosting their Special Attack so that they can break through it. Toxic gives Delphox the ability to cripple defensive Pokemon that would otherwise completely wall it such as Rhydon and Slowking as well as more offensive checks like Guzzlord.

Set Details

28 Special Attack EVs let Delphox 2HKO Xatu with Mystical Fire after Stealth Rock, while 252 HP EVs enable it to switch into Pokemon like Sceptile and Comfey. The remaining EVs go into Speed alongside a Timid nature so that Delphox can outspeed Mega Glalie. Leftovers gives Delphox a minor form of recovery, which lessens its reliance on Wish. Blaze increases the power of Delphox's Fire-type attack when it is low on HP, though Wish in combination with this set's more defensive nature prevent Delphox from taking complete advantage of it.

Usage Tips

Delphox should mainly switch in on special attackers that it checks such as Mega Abomasnow and Whimsicott; however, Delphox must be wary of Earthquake from Mega Abomasnow. Using Wish against these Pokemon as well as others like Steelix is ideal, since Delphox forces them out and can safely use Protect on the following turn to regain HP. Against Choice-locked Pokemon such as Guzzlord and Sneasel, use Protect in order to scout which move they lock themselves into and act accordingly. Toxic should be used whenever Delphox anticipates a Pokemon that it cannot otherwise deal with such as Incineroar, Slowking, or Vaporeon to switch in. Be wary of Toxic from Pokemon such as Mega Audino, as it greatly hinders this set and limits Delphox's ability to check Pokemon like Klinklang while still maintaining longevity. Refrain from switching in if Stealth Rock is up, as this heavily pressures Delphox and forces it to use Wish more often than it would like to.

Team Options

Wish Delphox fits best on bulky offensive and balance teams with teammates that lack recovery and are easier to wear down, as these Pokemon appreciate the support that Delphox provides. Entry hazard removers such as Blastoise, Silvally-Steel, and Whimsicott are important teammates due to Delphox's weakness to Stealth Rock preventing it from switching in and out as freely as it would like if it is up. All three of them can deal with bulky Ground- and Rock-types for Delphox. In return, Delphox can keep these Pokemon consistently healthy with Wish on top of switching into Grass-types. Fighting-types such as Hariyama and Passimian offensively check Dark-types and appreciate Delphox placing pressure on their checks like Vaporeon and Dhelmise. Mega Audino ability to reliably switch into and threaten out most Dark-types is very much appreciated, and it also provides cleric support in Heal Bell to prevent status from hindering Delphox. Bulkier setup sweepers like Comfey and Scrafty appreciate being passed Wishes, as it allows them to break early-game and take chip damage without it being detrimental in their attempt to sweep late-game. Delphox also pressures Steel- and Poison-types, which the two struggle against.

Choice Scarf.description:
Moves

Fire Blast is Delphox's strongest Fire-type STAB move, hitting Pokemon such as Sneasel, Steelix, and Whimsicott super effectively. Psychic threatens Fighting- and Poison-type Pokemon such as Passimian, Garbodor, and Golbat, and it also hits certain Fire-resistant Pokemon like Magmortar fairly hard. Psyshock can be used over Psychic to hit Pokemon such as Assault Vest Hariyama and Magmortar harder. Dazzling Gleam gives Delphox super effective coverage for certain Dark- and Dragon-type Pokemon such as Scrafty, Guzzlord, and Druddigon and is also useful for hitting foes such as Houndoom and Incineroar neutrally. Alternatively, Grass Knot can be used to hit Ground- and Water-type Pokemon such as Rhydon, Slowking, and Seismitoad harder than any of Delphox's other attacks. Finally, Trick cripples specially defensive Pokemon that Delphox is incapable of breaking through, such as Slowking and Vaporeon, while also allowing Delphox to switch between moves afterwards.

Set Details

The investment in Special Attack and Speed maximizes Delphox's offensive presence while making it as fast as possible, with a Timid nature and a Choice Scarf allowing Delphox to outpace the entire unboosted metagame as well as some boosted threats like Shell Smash Omastar. Blaze increases the power of Fire Blast when Delphox is low on HP, which can prove useful when attempting to clean late-game.

Usage Tips

Delphox should mainly be used as a revenge killer due to its high Speed and Special Attack, although it is capable of serving as a late-game cleaner as well. Exercise caution when it comes to using Psychic if the opposing team has a Dark-type like Incineroar or Sneasel, since they can switch into Delphox after it KOes a foe and either set up on it as it switches out or remove it with Pursuit. Delphox should mainly switch in on resisted special attacks such as Moonblast from Whimsicott and Fire Blast from Magmortar; however, note that Stealth Rock will limit its ability to handle these attacks. Trick should mainly be used against defensive teams, as losing Delphox's Choice Scarf isn't as detrimental against them compared to offensive teams and it can effectively hamper bulkier Pokemon like Slowking. However, be sure to scout for Z-Moves on Pokemon like Blastoise before using Trick, since it will fail and force Delphox out.

Team Options

Choice Scarf Delphox fits well on both offensive and bulky offensive teams that are in need of a way to keep faster foes in check and a powerful revenge killer. Delphox appreciates having teammates that can remove entry hazards due to its vulnerability to all forms of them, most notably Stealth Rock, so Pokemon such as Golbat, Rotom, Silvally-Steel, and Whimsicott are good partners. While Delphox doesn't appreciate entry hazards on its side of the field, it certainly appreciates being paired with entry hazard setters such as Rhydon and Steelix in order to pressure bulkier teams. Since Choice Scarf Delphox can struggle with breaking through certain bulky Pokemon such as Vaporeon and Slowking, it appreciates being paired with wallbreakers that can pressure these Pokemon and make cleaning up late-game easier, such as Heliolisk, Guzzlord, and Passimian. The former two can check Water-types, while the latter checks Dark-types, and Delphox can check Fairy-, Fighting-, and Ice-types for them in return. Setup sweepers that can take advantage of opposing Pokemon being locked into Knock Off and Pursuit such as Comfey, Scrafty, and Klinklang are good teammates, as Delphox appreciates having them to fall back on against the likes of Sneasel and Choice Scarf Houndoom. Scrafty can also set up on other checks to Delphox like Vaporeon and Slowking. In return, Delphox can break through Steel- and Grass-type Pokemon such as Steelix and Dhelmise for them. Mega Audino makes for a good teammate due to its ability to reliably switch into Knock Off, check Dark-types, circumvent Delphox's lack of recovery and vulnerability to entry hazards courtesy of Wish, and provide Heal Bell support in case Delphox is inflicted by status, while Delphox can remove Poison- and Steel-types for it.

lc.overview: Froakie has a unique ability in Protean as well as decent Speed and amazing coverage. However, Froakie depends on OHKOing foes before taking damage, as it is very frail and outran by the likes of Gastly and Staryu. Froakie is outclassed as a wallbreaker by the aforementioned Gastly and Staryu, both of which provide much better offensive and defensive utility.

Life Orb.description: This set attempts to make Froakie become an offensive pivot with its decent coverage and U-turn. However, Froakie is outclassed in this role by Gastly and Staryu, as both of them provide better offensive and defensive utility. Gastly has useful Normal- and Fighting-type immunities while Staryu has has Analytic to punish switch-ins.

1v1.overview: Greninja is a threatening Pokemon in the 1v1 metagame, with a good Special Attack and an amazing Speed tier that make it very threatening, being able to OHKO many threats like Mega Swampert, Zygarde-C, and Dragonite. Backing up that statline is access to Protean with a great movepool, giving it more offensive pressure with a STAB boost on all of its moves and a way to evade powerful attacks by changing to a type that resists them or is immune to them. A Substitute + Torrent set can also be used to beat threats to the Choice Specs set like specially defensive Mega Charizard X and Y, Mega Metagross, and Type: Null. By using the increased utility from forgoing coverage moves for options like Substitute, Work Up, and Taunt, Greninja can pump out a huge boosted Hydro Cannon while still using status moves to lock down foes. However, it is horribly frail, so any super effective moves against it will likely OHKO it, and it also falls to some strong neutral STAB attacks such as Adamant Haxorus's Outrage, Mega Lopunny's Giga Impact, and Mega Gyarados's Outrage. Greninja can also be defeated by faster Pokemon that can take advantage of its low defenses like Zeraora and bulkier ones that aren't afraid to take its hits like Kyurem
1v1.comments:
Other Options

Greninja is extremely versatile with its mixed attacking stats and Protean, so it has many options to use in combating what would have been losses before. A Waterium Z Greninja with Shadow Sneak can be used in order to reliably beat Porygon-Z, reacting to Porygon-Z's chosen coverage option. Greninja's extensive physical movepool can be used to make a Choice Band set, with Giga Impact for high Base Power, Gunk Shot to deal with Fairy-types like Mega Gardevoir, Tapu Lele, and Tapu Bulu, and Low Kick for special walls or heavy targets like Chansey and Kyurem. Greninja also has fantastic physical coverage in Ice Punch, Waterfall, Night Slash, and Rock Slide to fit the team. However, Greninja is no longer able to deal with some threats with a Choice Band set, as Ice Punch no longer OHKOes Dragonite in Ice Beam's place. A Modest Choice Scarf set can be used with one of these coverage moves to bait faster Pokemon, such as using Hidden Power Ground on a Zeraora to take an Electric-type attack, outspeeding Choice Scarf Haxorus and OHKOing it with Ice Beam, or outstripping Mega Blaziken's Speed tier even after Protect and washing it away with Hydro Cannon. This is generally a subpar option because Greninja loses its immense power from a Choice Specs or Choice Band. A Life Orb can be used to have Protean take a more defensive role, as Greninja changing its typing can help afterwards when taking down the opposing Pokemon. A Z-Crystal can also be used to give Greninja the same power, if not more, of Choice Specs on one move and the freedom it gets from Life Orb. Notable options of this are Darkinium Z to OHKO Mega Metagross and Icium Z to have the most consistent matchup against specially defensive Dragonite. However, both of these options have subpar power in comparison to Choice Specs, as OHKOing targets such as Dragonite and Mega Gyarados at the same time becomes much harder when Greninja doesn't have a flat boost to all of its attacks as high as from Choice Specs or Choice Band.

Checks and Counters

Faster Pokemon: Greninja is liable to being OHKOed by strong STAB moves or super effective moves from faster Pokemon such as Zeraora, Mega Lopunny, and Choice Scarf Haxorus unless it has a Choice Scarf itself.

Sturdy: Since Sturdy Pokemon can always absorb a hit from Greninja, they’re really effective at OHKOing it. Donphan is a good example, as it survives everything and OHKOes Greninja with neutral Tectonic Rage. However, Greninja can survive or avoid this attack and strike back with priority to win, depending on the set.

Bulky Pokemon: Bulkier Pokemon can take Greninja's attacks and OHKO it in return. However, Greninja's insane amount of versatility can usually help it get by these walls depending on the set. Bulky PP stall Kyurem can survive anything from Choice Specs easily and 2HKO Greninja with Ice Beam or Earth Power depending on what it's locked into. Mega Venusaur 2HKOes Greninja with Sludge Bomb and only fears Extrasensory, while Chansey is extremely consistent and only fears Choice Band sets.

Choice Specs.description:
Moves

Hydro Cannon is Greninja's attack with the highest Base Power, and it can score an OHKO on threats such as Heatran and Mega Diancie with relative ease. Grass Knot is chosen in the second slot to hit the Water-types that resist Hydro Cannon for super effective damage, and it's Greninja's best option for dealing with Mega Slowbro, Mega Gyarados, and Mega Swampert. Ice Beam is fantastic coverage, as it obliterates Pokemon that are weak to it such as Dragonite, Landorus-T, and Naganadel. Dark Pulse gives Greninja good coverage, beating Ghostium Z Aegislash and Mega Slowbro, and it is also a great option in dealing with Mirror Coat users like Avalugg, as Greninja keeping the Dark typing prevents the move from working. Hidden Power Fire is Greninja’s best option against Ferrothorn, Mega Scizor, and Magearna. Ferrothorn and Scizor are both easily OHKOed, while Magearna is 2HKOed. Another benefit of using Hidden Power Fire is that Magearna often will see Greninja as an easy KO, and luring it is very important. Hidden Power Ground can be used to gain an immunity to Electrium Z Magnezone. Blizzard gives Greninja another Ice-type coverage option that hits a bit harder, giving Greninja more consistent KOs on the bulky sets of Dragonite, Kommo-o, and Mega Altaria; however, its 70% accuracy can cause losses. Extrasensory is Greninja’s best option to deal with Mega Venusaur. Hidden Power Electric can be used against Mega Gyarados to confound it, OHKOing normal Gyarados while Grass Knot OHKOes Mega Gyarados. Hidden Power Steel can be run in order to consistently beat Tapu Lele, but this requires heavy Special Defense investment. Gunk Shot can be run in order to gain better matchups against Fairy-types like Mega Gardevoir and offensive Tapu Lele, without drastically shifting EV investment, unlike Hidden Power Steel. Shadow Sneak be used in order to play mind games with Choice-locked Porygon-Z using Hyper Beam.

Set Details

Maximum Special Attack and Speed EVs are used to let Greninja hit as hard and fast as possible. A Timid nature is chosen so that Greninja can outspeed targets such as Mega Diancie, Blacephalon, Naganadel, and Mega Latios. Choice Specs is used because it gives Greninja as much power as possible to OHKO its targets. Protean gives Greninja STAB on every move, giving it the power it needs to OHKO its targets.

A spread of 4 HP / 48 SpA / 204 SpD / 252 Spe with a Timid nature is ideal for using Hidden Power Steel, in order to tank a Shattered Psyche from Tapu Lele. If Greninja is running Gunk Shot, use a Naive nature instead of Timid.

Usage Tips

Sometimes moves that will allow Greninja to attack again are the better option if Greninja can’t OHKO the opposing Pokemon, such as changing Greninja's type with Hidden Power Fire to resist Magearna's Twinkle Tackle. Some options to cheese a victory in unfavorable matchups can come from Greninja’s moves’ secondary effects. Dark Pulse's 20% flinch rate can be used to cheese a win from a Donphan or Magnezone, but it's not reliable for swinging the matchup. Ice Beam's freeze chance of 10% is less reliable than Dark Pulse's flinch rate, so that move should never be used for its secondary effect unless the Pokemon resists Dark Pulse but not Ice Beam. Despite being a Fire-type Pokemon, both Mega Charizard X and Y can beat Greninja if given proper EV investment, so you will need to predict if your opponent is running bulky sets or not.

Team Options

Magnezone is a fantastic partner for Greninja, as it helps it deal with unfavorable matchups in Meloetta, Primarina, Mega Charizard Y, and Magearna. It also has a good matchup against Sturdy Pokemon such as Avalugg and Crustle. Greninja also beats many threats to Magnezone in Dragonite, Kommo-o, Zygarde, and Mega Charizard X. Zygarde has a fantastic matchup against almost every Sturdy Pokemon in the tier, which Greninja mostly universally loses to. It also helps Greninja in matchups against faster Pokemon like Mega Lopunny and Zeraora. Greninja can also help Zygarde by making quick work of Dragonite, other Zygarde, and Mega Charizard X. Dragonite is another good Pokemon to partner with Greninja, as it has fantastic matchups against Mega Venusaur, Meloetta, Mega Charizard Y, and Magnezone. Greninja also helps Dragonite in shaky matchups against Mega Charizard X and Aegislash. Heatran is a great option because it more reliably beats Charizard and Magearna, letting Greninja use Dark Pulse or a different Hidden Power. Heatran also appreciates Greninja's targeting of Zygarde and Dragonite. Other Electric-types like Raikou and Zapdos can also be used as team options because they are much more reliable at dealing with Gyarados than Magnezone while also beating Primarina, Tapu Fini, and Mega Charizard Y.

Substitute + Torrent.description:
Moves

Substitute is required for this set to function, allowing Greninja to safely defeat both Mega Charizard X and Y by using Substitute until Torrent and Petaya Berry are activated. Hydro Cannon is also a must-have, sporting a huge 150-Base Power on top of STAB, a Torrent boost, and Petaya Berry or Waterium Z to do incredible amounts of damage. Taunt allows Greninja to shut down stall Pokemon and Substitute users that would wall it, such as Mega Audino and Jumpluff . Work Up helps Greninja defeat Pokemon like Type: Null and non-Hyper Voice Mega Gardevoir that would attempt to boost their defenses to beat it. Alternatively, Water Shuriken can be used to beat Sturdy users like Golem as well as potentially Donphan and Crustle. This move is especially good when paired with a Petaya Berry, allowing Greninja to KO most Sturdy users in three hits instead of four. Haze can also be used as an alternative to Work Up, removing the foe's stat boosts, as well as guaranteeing a win against Dragon Dance Mega Charizard X. Ice Beam can also be used to beat Infestation Jumpluff and non-Choice Scarf Garchomp, but it loses so many other matchups that it's not worth using most of the time. Waterfall can also be used in conjunction with Work Up, as it guarantees a win against other Pokemon that would try to boost their Special Defense like Magearna and allows Greninja to run a mixed offensive set using Waterium Z.

Set Details

76 HP EVs and 108 Defense EVs prevent a Mega Charizard X's Flame Charge from breaking Greninja's Substitute. Additionally, the 76 HP EVs mean that Petaya Berry activates after 3 Substitutes, protecting Greninja from many priority moves that it resists. In addition to this, Greninja can now take 3 Seismic Tosses from Registeel, guaranteeing a win in this matchup. 176 Speed EVs with a Timid nature allow Greninja to outspeed maximum Speed Mega Lucario. Although the Mega Lucario matchup isn't a guaranteed win for Greninja, you lose nothing by investing the necessary EVs to outspeed it. The rest of the EVs are put into Special Attack to hit as hard as possible. Petaya Berry and Torrent in conjunction with Substitute allow Greninja to repeatedly use Substitute until the Berry and ability activate, allowing it to unleash a massively boosted Hydro Cannon. Waterium Z is an alternative that provides more consistency and power right out of the gate at the cost of total power; despite the increased accuracy, certain matchups such as Mega Swampert, Magearna, and Mega Gardevoir are made less consistent, making Petaya Berry generally the better option. It also improves certain matchups against Substitute users like Jumpluff, where you need to hit two turns in a row to win.

Usage Tips

Greninja should be sent out against slower Pokemon without a resistance to Water and stall Pokemon that are weak to Taunt. Avoid using Greninja against Pokemon that can bypass its Substitute like Meloetta. Unless the foe is exclusively a status user like Jumpluff or Type: Null, on turn 1, use Substitute. If the opponent elects to use a Speed-boosting move like Flame Charge or Dragon Dance, keep using Substitute until Greninja hits 25% health, after which you should use Hydro Cannon. If a foe such as Magearna or Mega Gardevoir tries to boost their Special Defense, use Work Up until both Pokemon are at +6, and then use Substitute until at 25% health, or use Haze to nullify their setup. Without Haze, certain matchups like Magearna are a toss-up, as if their Special Defense boosts reach +6, the benefit from Petaya Berry is lost. If you're using Haze, make sure to not Haze away your Petaya Berry boost. Only use Water Shuriken against Sturdy users. Unless the foe uses multi-hit moves and will faint to an unboosted Water Shuriken, like Golem, use Substitute to reach 25% health to get the Torrent and Petaya Berry boosts and then use it to hopefully KO the foe. If an opposing Pokemon uses a move like Shell Smash to boost their Speed, keep using Substitute, as they cannot eliminate Greninja if it is behind a Substitute. Between Petaya Berry and Waterium Z, they play largely similarly except against status users and Pokemon that can survive a hit from a Petaya Berry-boosted Hydro Cannon. Waterium Z allows you to use Hydro Vortex followed by Hydro Cannon the next turn, beating some Substitute users. In addition to this, with Petaya Berry, you cannot let the foe reach +6, as the advantage gained from Petaya Berry is lost. However, you can safely get to +6 with Waterium Z, as you still keep the damage boost.

Team Options

Pokemon that can deal with common threats to this set like Dragonite, Mega Gyarados, Mega Lopunny, and Choice Scarf users such as Landorus-T, Porygon-Z, and Sawk are very good partners. Examples include Magearna, Mega Metagross, and Tapu Lele, all of which have their weaknesses to Mega Charizard X and Y, Magearna, and Jumpluff covered by Greninja. Pokemon such as Zeraora and Magnezone that can deal with the bulky Water-types that typically beat Greninja like Tapu Fini and Primarina are great teammates as well and appreciate having their matchups against Mega Charizard X and Y and non-Choice Scarf Landorus-T covered.

monotype.overview:
Water

Greninja is the most versatile Water-type thanks to Protean giving it STAB on all of its attacks, enabling it to use almost any attack for coverage and still do great damage. It has an amazing movepool to maximize use of Protean including Ice Beam, Gunk Shot, Extrasensory, and many other coverage moves, which makes it a fantastic wallbreaker if it has the appropriate super effective attack. Expert Belt allows Greninja to take advantage of that fantastic coverage and ability Protean, allowing it to take on Flying, Water, and Ground teams quite easily. Greninja's amazing Speed makes it hard to revenge kill when it uses a Choice Scarf, able to outspeed almost the entire metagame, and allows Greninja to act as a great offensive pivot. In a completely different capacity, Greninja is also one of the few reliable ways to beat Poison teams for Water with its Groundium Z set. As a result of its many sets, Greninja is highly unpredictable and fits on almost every Water team, being able to fill any role the team needs. However, other than its Speed, Greninja has awful base stats, with almost no bulk to speak of and poor offensive stats. Furthermore, while its Speed is its only good stat, it still falls short of Tapu Koko, which is one of the biggest threats to Water teams, and can be easily revenge killed if it lacks Choice Scarf when considering its awful bulk. Greninja relies heavily on super effective damage to patch up its offensive stats, making it struggle to choose four moves from its huge movepool. Greninja will simply always be walled by something due to this restriction.

Dark

Greninja is one of the best offensive Pokemon that Dark teams have access to thanks to its powerful ability in Protean and to its diverse coverage options such as Gunk Shot, Ice Beam, U-turn, and Extrasensory making it an unpredictable threat. Protean also comes in handy defensively; for example, Greninja can become Psychic-type by using Extrasensory to avoid getting KOed by Keldeo's Secret Sword. Greninja sits at a splendid Speed tier, outspeeding common threats such as Garchomp, Mega Diancie, and non-Choice Scarf Keldeo. Greninja's use of an Expert Belt is complemented by its ability Protean, making it painful for many teams to deal with including Flying, Ground, and Water teams. When equipped with a Choice Scarf, Greninja functions as a Dark team's revenge killer, outspeeding threats such as Mega Lopunny, Tapu Koko, and other Choice Scarf users such as Tapu Bulu and Latios. Greninja has exploitable defensive stats, however, making it unable to take several hits and easy to revenge kill with priority attacks and faster attackers. Although Protean boosts attacks, Greninja is still held back by its average offensive stats, which means it's reliant on Life Orb to further boost its damage output. Greninja also lacks the room in its moveset to check every threat Dark teams might face.
monotype.comments:
Other Options

Water

The Choice Scarf set can use Hydro Pump for its great damage output, but the coverage is disappointingly redundant with Ice Beam and coverage is far more important due to Protean. U-turn is also an option for Expert Belt Greninja to bluff Choice Scarf even more effectively, but it tends to be much worse than more useful coverage. Taunt is a utility option that can help Greninja deal with bulkier walls it otherwise needs to switch out against.

Dark

Grassium Z can be used in place of an Expert Belt in order to unleash a powerful Bloom Doom, which is capable of OHKOing some of Greninja's best checks such as Rotom-Wash and Suicune. However, this trade-off comes at the cost of an Expert Belt netting other important KOs; for example, Greninja fails to 2HKO Toxapex with Hidden Power Electric without Expert Belt. Extrasensory can be utilized as a means of breaking through Fighting- and Poison-types such as Kommo-o and Mega Venusaur, though it comes at the cost of one of Greninja's other, more important coverage moves. Spikes could be utilized over Toxic Spikes as an immediate way of dealing damage to the foe upon entry, but keep in mind that the poison damage granted through Toxic Spikes is generally better against Greninja's checks. Hydro Pump might be used over Toxic Spikes to give Dark teams a better chance against threatening foes such as Mega Steelix, but not having Toxic Spikes utility may make Greninja less of a threat. For the Choice Scarf set, Hidden Power Fire gives Greninja a reliable way of removing Mega Scizor and Ferrothorn. Low Kick allows Greninja to easily deal with threats such as Ferrothorn and Tyranitar. However, these coverage moves aren't as great as those in the main sets because its teammates often cover these matchups.

Checks and Counters

Water

Chansey: No Greninja set can break Chansey, making it the best counter to Greninja. However, Greninja is capable of U-turning out of it.

Specially Defensive Walls: Most specially defensive walls that aren't weak to Gunk Shot or to the specific Greninja set's coverage can completely wall Greninja. Appropriate scouting for Greninja's moveset should be done to keep these checks safe.

Revenge Killers: Sets without Choice Scarf are very vulnerable to being outsped and revenge killed by a wide range of faster Pokemon including Tapu Koko, Mega Lopunny, and most Choice Scarf users due to Greninja's poor bulk. Powerful priority such as Choice Band Dragonite's Extreme Speed is also similarly capable of revenge killing Greninja.

Paralysis: Greninja tends to be incapable of outright OHKOing most Pokemon, so those that can survive a hit and paralyze it back, such as Jirachi, can cripple its Speed and prevent it from being a threat.

Dark

Chansey: Chansey completely walls all of Greninja's attacks and can stall it out with Toxic + Soft-Boiled.

Special Walls: Special walls such as Celesteela and Alolan Muk can take repeated attacks. Celesteela can stall out Greninja with Leech Seed, while Alolan Muk can cripple Greninja with Knock Off and poison it with Poison Touch. Greninja also takes a great deal of damage from Pursuit after a change in type.

Bulky Water-types: Bulky Water-types such as Gastrodon and Suicune can easily tank Greninja's attacks. Gastrodon can use Toxic on Greninja, while Suicune can set up Calm Mind on it.

Revenge Killers: Without a Choice Scarf, Greninja is outsped and KOed by revenge killers such as Tapu Koko, Mega Lopunny, and Choice Scarf users such as Tapu Bulu and Terrakion.

Priority: With Greninja's low defenses and its variable typing due to Protean, it's easily revenge killed by Mach Punch Breloom, Extreme Speed Dragonite, and Bullet Punch Mega Scizor.

Status and Entry Hazards: Greninja cannot afford to be inflicted with status, as paralysis completely ruins its impressive Speed and poison wears it down more quickly. Entry hazards are also problematic in limiting Greninja's opportunities to switch in and making it easier to revenge kill.

Expert Belt (Water).description:
Moves

Ice Beam hits Dragon-, Flying-, Ground-, and Grass-type Pokemon such as Kommo-o, Tornadus-T, Garchomp, and Tapu Bulu, all of which are very threatening for Water teams. Grass Knot nails Water- and Ground-type Pokemon such as Mega Swampert, Gastrodon, and Hippowdon. Hidden Power Electric is coverage that allows Greninja to specifically target Mantine, which easily switches into its other attacks, while also hitting Toxapex hard. Extrasensory allows Greninja to hit Poison- and Fighting-type threats such as Mega Venusaur, Toxapex, and Keldeo, making Greninja a consistent answer to Poison teams when in combination with Hidden Power Electric.

Set Details

Maximum Special Attack and Speed investment alongside a Timid nature allow Greninja to hit as fast and hard as possible. Protean allows Greninja to gain STAB on all of its moves attacks, making it an incredible all-out attacker. Expert Belt increases damage done by super effective attacks, giving it enough damage to 2HKO Toxapex after Stealth Rock damage.

Usage Tips

Greninja has amazing coverage that it can easily take advantage of. Since it commonly runs Choice Scarf, it can spam one attack to bluff a Choice Scarf and lure in Pokemon that resist the coverage move it is pretending to be locked into. Greninja is amazing in the mirror matchup, as with its combined coverage of Grass Knot and Hidden Power Electric, it can easily hit every Water-type Pokemon super effectively, making it a dangerous threat late-game. The same thing goes for the Flying and Ground matchups, as its Ice- and Grass-type coverage can hit all Pokemon bar Excadrill and Mega Steelix for super effective damage in the Ground matchup. Greninja is frail and therefore weak to common priority attacks such as Dragonite's Extreme Speed and Breloom's Mach Punch, so it should switch out to a teammate such as Toxapex to handle these attacks. Furthermore, it should switch out of offensive Pokemon that it can't OHKO such as Kyurem-B, since it is so frail that oftentimes they will be able to OHKO Greninja in return. Because of this, Greninja should only be brought in safely to avoid taking unnecessary damage. Additionally, while Greninja certainly does not appreciate the chip damage from being poisoned or burned, it should absolutely at all costs avoid paralysis, as it severely cripples its ability to act as a fast revenge killer and allows it to get OHKOed by slower threats such as Kommo-o.

Team Options

Toxapex is a great defensive pivot that can switch into threats such as Mega Venusaur for Greninja and makes a solid wall thanks to Recover. Additionally, it provides Toxic Spikes support, chipping down Greninja's threats and allowing it to clean late-game more easily. Swampert and Mega Swampert provide Stealth Rock support and an Electric-type immunity. Swampert is a solid defensive tank that can switch into threats such as Tapu Koko and Terrakion for Greninja. Mega Swampert on the other hand is a more offensive option that is extremely threatening with rain, taking on Greninja's checks such as Tapu Koko and Volcarona with Earthquake and Waterfall. Keldeo and Greninja share similar checks and can help break each other's down. Keldeo can break bulky cores from types such as Normal and Flying with Calm Mind and Taunt or be a more offensive threat and just muscle through Pokemon such as Chansey with Choice Specs-boosted Secret Sword. It also takes on Steel-types such as Mega Scizor and Ferrothorn that otherwise wall Greninja. Mega Sharpedo is a great late-game cleaner that appreciates Greninja's ability to weaken many of its checks such as Hippowdon and Celesteela, allowing it to clean more easily. It is also able to outspeed threats such as Tapu Koko and Mega Lopunny for Greninja. Running Mega Sharpedo allows Greninja to run Extrasensory, allowing it to take on Pokemon such as Mega Venusaur that would otherwise wall it. Rotom-Wash and Mantine can clear entry hazards for Greninja as well as provide it with a Ground immunity. Rotom-Wash can provide a slow pivot with Volt Switch and cripple physical attackers such as Azumarill with Will-O-Wisp. On the other hand, Mantine is a solid special wall with access to Roost, allowing it to easily switch into attacks such as Latios's Draco Meteor. Gyarados can support Greninja by taking on its checks such as Mega Venusaur and Chansey with boosted Supersonic Skystrike. In return, Greninja can break past physical walls for Gyarados such as Celesteela and Swampert. Additionally, it provides Greninja with a solid switch-in to Ground-type attacks. Thanks to rain and Choice Specs-boosted Hurricane, Pelipper is able to take on a plethora of Grass- and Poison-type Pokemon for Greninja such as Ferrothorn, Mega Venusaur, and Toxapex. Additionally, it can pivot in Greninja safely with U-turn, can clear hazards with Defog, and shares similar checks with Greninja, allowing them to both help break down the other's checks. Manaphy helps break down Poison-type threats to Greninja such as Alolan Muk and Mega Venusaur after one Tail Glow boost thanks to Surf and Psychic, respectively.

Choice Scarf (Water).description:
Moves

U-turn provides switch momentum by allowing Greninja to pivot out of incoming walls into a teammate. Ice Beam gives Greninja a strong option to hit a wide range of threats including Dragon-types like Dragonite and Flying-types like Zapdos. Gunk Shot lets Greninja revenge kill Fairy-types, most importantly Tapu Koko, which is one of the most threatening Pokemon to Water teams. Defensively, it also provides Greninja with a Poison typing, making it a solid choice for 2HKOing Mega Charizard Y and Mega Diancie, both of which cannot OHKO a Poison-type Greninja with Solar Beam and Moonblast, respectively. Dark Pulse is a reliable STAB move that has fantastic coverage with Greninja's other moves and importantly hits Psychic-type walls like Mew, Jirachi, and Slowbro for a lot of damage. Depending on the user's team, Greninja's final moveslot can easily be replaced with more specific coverage moves to hit certain threats in exchange for losing out on the spammable Dark Pulse. For offensive teams that lack defensive switch-ins to these threats, Rock Slide is a solid coverage option that notably OHKOes Volcarona and Mega Charizard Y while 2HKOing Mantine and Kyurem-B. Low Kick is the only option that can OHKO Kyurem-B after Stealth Rock damage or two hits of Life Orb damage. It also 2HKOes Ferrothorn, almost always OHKOes Heatran, and always OHKOes Tyranitar. Hidden Power Fire is useful for 2HKOing both Ferrothorn and Klefki, which often try to switch into Greninja, but it has no other useful targets. Entry hazards in the form of either Spikes or Toxic Spikes are also a viable final option on offensive teams to punish the opposing team's switches.

Set Details

252 Speed EVs, a Naive nature, and a Choice Scarf make Greninja as fast as possible, outspeeding almost the entire metagame including Adamant Sand Rush Excadrill and Swift Swim Kingdra. A Naive nature is important to use instead of Hasty to make sure Choice Band Dragonite's Extreme Speed and other powerful priority are not able to KO Greninja. Greninja should use either 252 Special Attack or 252 Attack EVs depending on its fourth moveslot, as that slot typically relies heavily on investment to net the intended KOs. Protean changes Greninja's type to the typing of the move it uses, giving it permanent STAB and defensive flexibility.

Usage Tips

Greninja can serve as a fantastic lead thanks to its incredible Speed and use of U-turn to get switch advantage from the very beginning of the match, as almost no leads are capable of anti-leading Greninja. It is also a very reliable revenge killer, able to outspeed even many boosted sweepers. If Greninja isn't able to OHKO the threat, though, U-turn can be used to get chip damage at the cost of a teammate taking a hit. Greninja has rather poor damage output when lacking super effective coverage and can rarely touch walls, so if you predict one to switch into Greninja, U-turn should be used to preserve momentum. Once these walls are weakened, though, Greninja is more than capable of serving as a late-game sweeper with its STAB-boosted attacks. In most cases, try to use teammates such as Rotom-Wash to pivot into Greninja safely, as it can't take hits very well at all and should not switch into most attacks outside of those that are Psychic-type. However, when already in play, remember that Protean can be used defensively to give Greninja unusual resistances, such as using Gunk Shot against Mega Diancie's Moonblast or Mega Charizard Y's Solar Beam.

Team Options

Greninja is best when paired with wallbreakers and stallbreakers such as Choice Specs Keldeo and Kingdra, Perish Trap Azumarill, and Suicune that can take on the walls it can't touch. Greninja's ability to bait walls in and pivot on them with U-turn makes it an even better teammate for these Pokemon. Specifically, this set can't touch the Poison defensive core, so a Pokemon like Gyarados that can beat it is important to have. Other pivots such as Rotom-Wash are great for forming a VoltTurn core with Greninja, able to keep up momentum for each other or for other teammates. While Toxapex lacks a pivoting move, it is still a fantastic option due to its ability Regenerator. It also frequently uses Toxic Spikes, which is crucial for wearing down Greninja's checks to enable a late-game sweep. Pokemon such as Swampert are almost necessary for their Stealth Rock support, which further punishes the switches that Greninja can easily force. Because Greninja likes to switch in and out frequently, hazard control from the likes of Mantine and Empoleon for your side of the field is crucial to avoid letting it get worn down too quickly. Being almost unparalleled in Speed, Greninja is very useful for taking out opposing revenge killers for sweepers, such as Gyarados and Mega Sharpedo. Mega Sharpedo is notable in being able to check Psychic-types, meaning Greninja can more easily choose to use a different coverage option from Dark Pulse.

All-out Attacker (Water).description:
Moves

Ice Beam is used for its coverage, hitting Flying-, Grass-, and Dragon-types including Zapdos and Cradily super effectively and 2HKOing even Kyurem-B. Gunk Shot hits Fairy-types and special walls such as Mantine hard, making Greninja a mixed attacking threat. Dark Pulse deals wallbreaking damage to Psychic-types, able to at least 2HKO almost every Psychic-type, while having decent spammability on even neutral targets. Greninja can choose from a wide range of options for its last move, selecting whatever its team needs most. Hidden Power Fire can OHKO many Steel-types including Ferrothorn, which tends to be a difficult Pokemon to break. Alternatively, Hidden Power Electric with Ice Beam 2HKOes almost every Flying-type other than Celesteela, making Greninja very difficult to check in that matchup. If these coverage combinations are unneeded, Hydro Pump is Greninja's strongest attack and can be used over Dark Pulse for wallbreaking, as it notably can 2HKO even specially defensive Mega Sableye, but Water-type coverage is relatively redundant with Ice Beam. If Hydro Pump is used, Rock Slide can be used alongside it because it OHKOes Mega Charizard Y and still breaks most Flying teams. Greninja can use Spikes or Toxic Spikes quite effectively, as it forces switches and can take that opportunity to set up entry hazards.

Set Details

Maximum investment into Special Attack and Speed and a Naive nature make Greninja as strong and as fast as possible. Protean makes Greninja deal significant damage with all of its attacks thanks to STAB. Life Orb gives Greninja great damage on all of its attacks at the cost of recoil damage. To avoid recoil damage, Expert Belt can be used instead and to bluff other sets, but Greninja's neutral damage is pitiful and Hydro Pump should not be used with it.

Usage Tips

This set looks to come in as often as possible and fire off powerful super effective attacks whenever possible. As a result, try to pivot into it on double switches to Pokemon it outspeeds. It can also be used as a revenge killer with its good Speed, either KOing or forcing out threats like Mega Gallade that Water struggles with. Be careful with Greninja's health, as it has rather poor bulk and Life Orb will chip at Greninja over time. Avoid letting Greninja take hits it doesn't resist, as even neutral damage from weak walls can deal serious damage. Protean can be used for this purpose, giving Greninja unusual resistances to allow it to take hits it otherwise wouldn't be able to. Greninja has a huge range of moves it can viably use, so use that to your advantage, as your opponent will try hard to scout out your moveset. While Greninja's moves are unknown, it has a very easy time firing off attacks without fear. If Greninja uses Expert Belt, bluffing Choice Scarf or Groundium Z is a good strategy for netting surprise KOs.

Team Options

Even though this is one of Greninja's more powerful sets, it still doesn't have particularly fantastic damage output, so pairing Greninja with a wallbreaker is a good idea to dismantle balance and defensive teams. Choice Specs Keldeo can be a great option for breaking the Normal defensive core, which Greninja has no way of touching. Swift Swim Kingdra can be a great anti-offense option, as it can revenge kill Pokemon like Tapu Koko that outspeed Greninja. Rain in general is useful if Greninja packs Hydro Pump, as rain-boosted Hydro Pump is the only way Greninja can 2HKO Celesteela. Be aware, though, that rain will make Greninja's Hidden Power Fire deal insignificant damage. On more balanced teams, Perish Trap Azumarill can be an unorthodox way of taking out walls for Greninja. Greninja benefits greatly from having its switch-ins chipped away at, so support such as Stealth Rock and Toxic Spikes from Swampert and Toxapex is always appreciated. A way to beat the Poison defensive core is needed, so a specific check such as Flyinium Z Gyarados should be used for this purpose.

Poison Killer (Water).description:
Moves

Extrasensory is the primary attack for this set, able to 2HKO almost every Pokemon on a Poison team including Toxapex and Mega Venusaur. Dig completes the necessary coverage to allow this set to sweep Poison, as Tectonic Rage always OHKOes Alolan Muk, the only commonly used Poison-type that Extrasensory cannot touch. Ice Beam is used for its great coverage to give Greninja a strong, spammable move that no Pokemon is immune to. The final moveslot is used to complete coverage combinations to counter certain types, as this set lacks power if its moves are not super effective. With Tectonic Rage dealing crippling damage to Klefki, Gunk Shot is a great move that can pressure Fairy teams, although Greninja is still outsped by Tapu Koko. While it doesn't pair particularly well with Tectonic Rage, Hidden Power Electric forms the well-known BoltBeam coverage with Ice Beam and can 2HKO Mantine and Mega Charizard Y to break Flying teams. Hidden Power Fire can be used as well, as Heatran is OHKOed by Tectonic Rage, enabling Greninja to spam Hidden Power Fire safely against Steel teams.

Set Details

Maximum investment into Special Attack gives Greninja enough damage to 2HKO Toxapex and Mega Venusaur. 4 Attack EVs are used to guarantee the OHKO on Alolan Muk. A Naive nature and 252 Speed EVs make sure Greninja outspeeds Pokemon such as Latios, Gengar, Keldeo, and Mega Diancie. Protean gives Greninja's moves STAB, enabling it to deal enough damage to break the Poison teams it's built for. Groundium Z enables Greninja to use Tectonic Rage.

Usage Tips

Because Tectonic Rage only has one use, be very careful to not waste it needlessly. For Poison teams, Alolan Muk will often be baited in to Pursuit a Psychic-type Greninja, so it is generally safe to use it after it has switched in. Against Fairy teams, though, because Klefki will be able to set Prankster Reflect, it is necessary to hit it on the switch, so try to predict its switch in. Klefki will often try to switch into Gunk Shot, so luring it in by giving Greninja a free switch into Tapu Bulu or even Tapu Koko is relatively easy. In many matchups, Tectonic Rage can be a good surprise for hitting special walls as well. For example, Ground teams expecting Choice Scarf Ice Beam like to switch into Seismitoad on Greninja, and Tectonic Rage almost always OHKOes standard Seismitoad after it switches into Ice Beam. Because Greninja tends to not run Hydro Pump, Tectonic Rage is also typically good for hitting Pokemon like Heatran and Tyranitar that don't expect to take a huge amount of damage. Even though it may be dangerous, many expect Choice Scarf Greninja, so as long as you haven't revealed a teammate's Choice Scarf, it is very possible to bluff it to lure in one of Tectonic Rage's targets. Against Poison teams, it is also very possible to bluff other items too such as Expert Belt before Extrasensory is used. However, Extrasensory is not used outside of this set too often without Life Orb, so once Greninja has used Extrasensory and does not take Life Orb recoil, it is difficult to bluff another set. Due to Greninja's great movepool, it is difficult for your opponent to predict its coverage move. Try to preserve that deception as long as possible, especially if you haven't revealed Dig yet, as the wide range of moves Greninja can pack is part of its strength. Make sure to avoid taking unnecessary damage on Greninja, as it lacks a damage-boosting item and may need to take a hit or two to break walls. As a result, it is best to pair this set with a pivot that can bring Greninja in safely, such as U-turn Pelipper. Ground is a very unusual typing for Greninja to access with Protean, so use that to your advantage against Electric-types that expect to be able to fire off an attack safely. Even though Dig is a two-turn move, it still has utility for this purpose.

Team Options

Water teams generally have a very rough time beating the Poison defensive core, so almost any team that lacks an alternative solution can use this set. Rain teams in particular appreciate Greninja's support. However, rain weakens Greninja's Hidden Power Fire, so that coverage move should not be used on rain teams. Pelipper can use a slow U-turn to effectively get Greninja into play safely while also packing Defog to protect Greninja from Toxic Spikes and other entry hazards. Rotom-Wash is capable of fulfilling a similar role to Pelipper on non-rain teams. Sweepers such as Swift Swim Kingdra, Mega Gyarados, and Suicune all appreciate Greninja removing their Poison-type checks. This set lacks power when not battling its specific targets, so wallbreakers, such as Choice Band Azumarill, can help break walls for Greninja. Hazard support from Swampert and Toxapex can be helpful for putting Pokemon such as Crobat into range of being OHKOed to alleviate the damage output issue. This set lacks the Speed of Choice Scarf, so it's important to have a teammate like Choice Scarf Keldeo that can help revenge kill Pokemon that can force out Greninja.

All-out Attacker (Dark).description:
Moves

Ice Beam is a strong coverage option that can be used to take down various offensive and defensive threats alike, such as Latios, Tapu Bulu, Gliscor, and Zapdos. Hidden Power Electric is used against bulky Flying- and Water-types such as Celesteela, Mantine, and Toxapex. Grass Knot is used against specific foes such as Swampert, Gastrodon, and Seismitoad, as they can comfortably take on Greninja's other attacks by virtue of ability and typing. Toxic Spikes is great for residual damage against most foes, and the increasing poison damage helps combat most of Greninja's checks such as Chansey and Mega Sableye.

Set Details

Maximum Special Attack and Speed investment coupled with a Timid nature allows Greninja to hit as hard and as fast as possible. Expert Belt strengthens the power of its moves whenever they are super effective, which can be important in some cases. For example, Expert Belt-boosted Hidden Power Electric allows Greninja to 2HKO Toxapex. Protean blesses Greninja with the ability to change its typing depending on the move it uses, granting it STAB on all of its moves in the process and thus giving it an incredible offensive presence.

Usage Tips

Greninja should utilize this set to lure in and remove would-be checks such as Mantine and Toxapex, as its wide movepool and variety of sets makes it very unpredictable. Greninja also should use one move at a time to bluff a potential Choice Scarf set, as it makes luring in foes such as Celesteela and Mantine much more effective, as well as threaten would-be checks such as Mega Lopunny and Tapu Koko out. However, it should still avoid special walls such as Chansey and Ferrothorn, as their incredible special bulk can let them comfortably take any attack it can dish out. Greninja should be conserved as much as possible against Flying, Ground, and Water teams, as its incredible coverage serves as an invaluable asset against them. It shouldn't be immediately switched into attacks, as it's incredibly frail. It should also avoid paralysis, as Greninja relies on its high Speed in order to threaten fast foes such as Mega Diancie and Latios. Greninja should also avoid chip damage from entry hazards and status, as it needs to be as healthy as possible in order to effectively threaten foes.

Team Options

Mega Sableye can use its typing and well rounded defenses to comfortably handle Greninja's checks, such as Chansey, Ferrothorn, and Mega Gallade, while also providing a critical Fighting-type immunity. Additionally, Mega Sableye can prevent entry hazards that would chip away at Greninja's health from being set through Magic Bounce. Mandibuzz assists Greninja through its various potential utility moves, including Defog, Taunt, and U-turn. It can also use its high Defense and Ground-type immunity to switch into foes such as Mega Lopunny and Choice Band Excadrill in sand for Greninja. Tyranitar's acts as a strong special wall and supporter under sand, being able to stomach attacks from foes such as Latios and Tapu Koko for Greninja while also providing Stealth Rock support for it. It can also act as a setup sweeper with its combination of Dragon Dance, strong physical moves, and Rockium Z to break down special walls such as Chansey and Mega Venusaur. Alternatively, Mega Tyranitar can also perform the same role as base Tyranitar, exchanging Rockium Z for much better stats and a better Speed tier for outspeeding foes that base Tyranitar wouldn't be able to with one Dragon Dance boost, such as Tapu Koko and Weavile. Alolan Muk can use its typing and high Special Defense to sponge special attacks such as Latios's Draco Meteor and Tapu Koko's Dazzling Gleam for Greninja. Additionally, its access to Knock Off means that it can weaken foes such as Porygon2 and Toxapex, making it easier for Greninja to remove them. Krookodile serves as a solid lead for Greninja, being able to set up Stealth Rock and prevent slower foes from setting their own entry hazards with Taunt. Additionally, Choice Scarf variants can be run to outspeed and revenge kill foes such as Tapu Koko. Hydreigon can stallbreak foes that Greninja has trouble with, such as Chansey and Steel-types such as Choice Scarf Excadrill, Ferrothorn, and Mega Scizor. Additionally, it can utilize Dragonium Z to devastate slower, bulkier Pokemon such as Porygon2 and Rotom-Wash.

Choice Scarf (Dark).description:
Moves

Gunk Shot is necessary for Greninja to check Fairy-types, and it making Greninja Poison-type has some use in avoiding Toxic and resisting Grass. U-turn helps maintain momentum and take advantage of forced switches such as Landorus fearing Ice Beam. Ice Beam lets Greninja hit annoying Flying-types such as Zapdos as well as Dragon- and Ground-types such as Hydreigon and Landorus. Hydro Pump targets threats such as Excadrill and Heatran, 2HKOes Klefki, and does slightly more damage than Gunk Shot to +1 Volcarona. Spikes is a great utility move, and with Greninja's offensive presence and coverage moves forcing so many switches, it's able to get set up, applying pressure on grounded Pokemon. Rock Slide is a reliable move for KOing threats that are really weak to it such as Mega Charizard Y and Volcarona.

Set Details

Maximum Speed EVs with a Naive nature and a Choice Scarf make Greninja as fast as possible, outspeeding threats such as Tapu Koko, Mega Lopunny, Choice Scarf users such as Tapu Bulu, Latios, Adamant Excadrill in sand, and Modest Kingdra in rain. A Naive nature alongside 4 Attack EVs keeps Greninja from weakening Gunk Shot. 252 Special Attack EVs maximizes Greninja's damage output. Protean is the ability of choice to change Greninja's typing and gain STAB from it.

Usage Tips

Choice Scarf Greninja takes on the role of a revenge killer, outspeeding and taking on threats such as Tapu Koko, Mega Lopunny, and slower Choice Scarf users. Greninja can also utilize its high Speed to clean late-game, and it can be an effective lead thanks to U-turn and how many Pokemon it forces out. Greninja should try setting up Spikes early-game to begin putting pressure on teams. It needs to come in safely from a slow U-turn user such as Mandibuzz or a fainted teammate because of its frailty. Make sure to take advantage of U-turn so Greninja can escape any possible disadvantages it may encounter. Be careful about what Greninja is locked into, since getting forced out or becoming setup fodder for Pokemon like Terrakion is a momentum drain; it's best to make sure that all of Greninja's checks and counters are gone or weakened so it can sweep late-game. Be aware that even with Protean, Greninja doesn't hit as hard with Choice Scarf; bulky threats will be able to switch in comfortably, so avoid having Greninja take them on. Greninja should avoid paralysis at all costs, as its role as a revenge killer will be ruined.

Team Options

Mega Tyranitar is an excellent teammate, as it can help wallbreak early- or mid-game and dismantle teams for Greninja to clean late-game. Tyranitar and Krookodile provide Stealth Rock support for Greninja to KO threats more easily. Tyranitar can also paralyze foes with Thunder Wave and tank special attacks, whereas Krookodile can switch into Electric-type moves, supply utility with Knock Off, and revenge kill threats thanks to its Focus Sash. Intimidate from Krookodile can also assist in softening physical attacks for Greninja. Other Knock Off users such as Mega Sableye, Bisharp, and Alolan Muk cripple item-reliant Pokemon, especially Eviolite and Leftovers users such as Porygon2 and Zapdos. Mega Sableye can block status moves, while Bisharp and Alolan Muk can be additional checks to Fairy-types. Mandibuzz can switch into physical attackers for Greninja and punish Swords Dance and Dragon Dance sweepers such as Mega Scizor and Dragonite with Foul Play. Since Greninja will be pivoting out often with U-turn, it also benefits from Mandibuzz's Defog. Hydreigon can wallbreak for Greninja thanks to Choice Specs and switch into Ground-type attacks. Mega Sharpedo and Greninja can help one another clean up late-game, and Mega Sharpedo can use Psychic Fangs to pressure Fighting-types. Cacturne is a great check to problematic Water-types such as Suicune and Z-Belly Drum Azumarill.

Offensive (Dark).description:
Moves

Hydro Pump is Greninja's strongest move for hitting threats such as Mega Diancie, Heatran, and Excadrill. Ice Beam is great for taking care of Dragon- and Flying-types such as Mega Altaria, Gliscor, and Zapdos. Gunk Shot gives Greninja coverage for Fairy-types such as Clefable, notably OHKOing Azumarill. Extrasensory hits Fighting- and Poison-types that threaten Dark teams such as Keldeo, Mega Venusaur, and Toxapex.

Set Details

Maximum Speed EVs with a Naive nature allow Greninja to be as fast as possible, outspeeding anything under base 122 Speed with the exception of Choice Scarf users. A Naive nature also keeps Gunk Shot from being weakened. Maximum Special Attack investment grants Greninja more attacking power. Protean is necessary for Greninja to have STAB on all of its attacks. Greninja can't do a lot of damage without a boosting item, so Life Orb is the item of choice.

Usage Tips

Because Greninja is generally frail, it should switch in for free or on weak, resisted attacks. It can also attempt to come in from a double switch. Greninja's terrifying coverage and decent offensive stats are just enough for it to force switches, so capitalize on that by immediately switching to a teammate that's able to take on the opposing team's check to Greninja. Make sure to save Greninja for fast threats that it'll be able to revenge kill such as Life Orb Latios and Gengar. It's always best to keep Greninja away from revenge killers and Choice Scarf users because Greninja is often needed in later parts of the match thanks to its wide coverage. Remember that Protean can be used to your defensive advantage; for example, Greninja will resist Moonblast after using Gunk Shot. Make sure to keep Greninja away from paralysis, burns, and poison, which will ruin its Speed or longevity.

Team Options

Greninja doesn't appreciate being worn down by entry hazards, so Mega Sableye and Mandibuzz make for good partners. Mega Sableye also offers protection from Thunder Wave, Toxic, Knock Off, and Fighting-type attacks. Mandibuzz, on the other hand, can get Greninja in safely with its slow U-turn and tank attacks with its physical bulk. Mega Tyranitar can assist Greninja in pressuring teams. With Greninja taking on physically defensive threats, Mega Tyranitar gets rid of special walls such as Chansey. Specially defensive Tyranitar can switch into special attacks for Greninja and provide Thunder Wave support so Greninja can outspeed even Choice Scarf users. Mega Sharpedo can help clean up late-game after Greninja has dealt enough damage to the opposing team. Hydreigon and Greninja together are great in at pressuring teams. Hydreigon can specifically take out Steel-types such as Celesteela and Ferrothorn. Choice Scarf Hydreigon is also a valuable teammate, revenge killing threats Greninja has weakened. Bisharp and Alolan Muk help Greninja take on annoying Fairy-types such as Tapu Bulu and Azumarill, and both can provide Knock Off support. Bisharp specifically can check Ice-types, while Alolan Muk can switch into special attacks. Krookodile is another good Stealth Rock and Knock Off user that is also able to check Electric-types for Greninja. Cacturne can check bulky Water-types like Suicune and Z-Belly Drum Azumarill, which would otherwise give Greninja trouble.

ubers.overview:
• Access to Spikes and Taunt and a Speed tier that allows it to outspeed Arceus formes provide Greninja with a nice niche as a dedicated lead in the Ubers tier.
  • Greninja's Water / Dark typing allows it to also be a great anti-lead against other common dedicated leads such as Cloyster and Deoxys-S, as it naturally resists Cloyster's attacks, outspeeds it, and can use Taunt against it, and it is able to 2HKO and force predictions against Deoxys-S. Furthermore, unlike Cloyster, Necrozma-DM is unable to lead against it.
  • Greninja does, however, struggle to really dish out any damage prior to activating Battle Bond, which can make it difficult to effectively provide offensive pressure, as it needs to claim a KO in order to do so. This low damage output results in it being completely shut down by the tier's two Magic Bounce users in Mega Diancie and Mega Sableye, which are able to bounce back entry hazards and use Taunt against it while failing to be 2HKOed by any of its attacks.
  • Its subpar bulk also means that it can often struggle to get many entry hazards up against setup sweepers, as it is forced to use Taunt on them to prevent them from setting up but is also very often brought down to its Focus Sash even without boosts. If these setup sweepers have access to a priority move, Greninja can completely fail to get up any entry hazards.
ubers.comments:
Other Options

  • Greninja has a very specific niche in the Ubers tier, so despite its impressive movepool, it isn't really able to utilize the majority of these.
  • Water Shuriken or Shadow Sneak could be potentially useful to improve the matchup against Deoxys-S by preventing it from getting up multiple entry hazards; however, Greninja would much prefer to run either Ice Beam or Substitute in this slot due to the coverage or utility options these moves offer.
  • Hydro Pump can be used as a fourth move in order to pressure Mega Diancie; however, this would be sacrificing the coverage options that Ice Beam could offer or the security of Substitute.
  • A suicide lead set with Protean containing Spikes + Toxic Spikes + Taunt + Shadow Sneak with the ability Protean can be run, utilizing Greninja's ability to set dual entry hazards and spinblock with Shadow Sneak; however, this takes away Greninja's niche with Battle Bond and tends to be outclassed by other entry hazard setters such as Deoxys-S.

Checks and Counters

Magic Bounce: Both of the viable Magic Bounce users in Mega Diancie and Mega Sableye aren't too fazed by any of Greninja's attacks and can bounce back Spikes and Taunt thanks to their ability. Mega Diancie is able to bring Greninja down to its Focus Sash with Moonblast, while Mega Sableye is able to avoid the 2HKO and stall it out with Toxic + Recover. It does, however, have to be cautious of Dark Pulse flinches.

Smeargle: Smeargle can be a real hassle for Greninja, as it is able to bounce back its entry hazards, Taunt it with Magic Coat, and paralyze it with Nuzzle; it also causes a nuisance to the type of teams Greninja thrives on by slowing down the whole grounded team with Sticky Web.

Setup Sweepers: Setup sweepers are able to potentially completely prevent or limit the amount of entry hazards that Greninja is able to set, as it is forced to Taunt them to prevent them from sweeping, rather than focusing on setting entry hazards. Setup sweepers with priority attacks such as Arceus and Mega Lucario are able to potentially completely deter Greninja from setting entry hazards, as Arceus is able to 2HKO Greninja with Extreme Speed and Mega Lucario is able to bring Greninja down to its Focus Sash and then pick it off with Bullet Punch.

Faster Offensive Threats: Ultra Necrozma, Choice Scarf Yveltal, and Choice Scarf Xerneas all have enough natural bulk to be able to survive a single hit from Greninja and can 2HKO it or bring it down to its Focus Sash with any of their attacks, limiting Greninja to only being able to set up one entry hazard at most.

Lead.description:
Moves

  • Spikes is a really effective means of punishing grounded Pokemon, as it deals up to 25% of the maximum HP in damage to any Pokemon that switches in. This allows your team to more effectively pressure Steel-type threats such as Necrozma-DM and Magearna, which otherwise take minimal damage from Stealth Rock.
  • Taunt stops setup, entry hazards being put up, status spreading, and entry hazard removal, thus being crucial in order for Greninja to effectively perform its role as a suicide lead. Dark Pulse prevents Greninja from being completely passive, preventing it from becoming setup fodder for offensive Necrozma-DM at Team Preview. It also allows Greninja to utilize its ability in Battle Bond, allowing it to become a more offensive threat, most notably outspeeding Mega Gengar and Ultra Necrozma and being able to OHKO them both, as well as 2HKOing Trick Room Necrozma-DM.
  • Substitute is primarily used to stop Smeargle from paralyzing Greninja with Nuzzle, as Taunt doesn't prevent Smeargle from using this move. Once Greninja is behind a Substitute, this puts it in a situation of mind games, rather than Greninja being at a disadvantage.
  • Ice Beam allows Greninja to pressure Mega Salamence and Zygarde better, as it is able to OHKO Salamence even without Battle Bond, whereas after transformation, it's able to outspeed +1 offensive Zygarde-C and OHKO it. It also gives it a chance of 2HKOing Mega Diancie, which otherwise would be able to prevent Greninja from setting up entry hazards, and is immune to Taunt thanks to Magic Bounce, and is able to bring Greninja down to its Focus Sash with Moonblast.

Set Details

  • This is a classic offensive set with maximum Special Attack investment for the highest possible damage output and maximum Speed investment so Greninja moves first. A Timid nature is required in order for Greninja to outspeed Arceus formes, which is crucial to prevent it them from using Defog.

Usage Tips

  • Greninja's main focus should be to set Spikes and prevent the opposing team from either setting up in front of it, removing these Spikes or setting their own entry hazards by clicking Taunt.
  • Against setup sweepers, such as Rock Polish Primal Groudon and Extreme Killer Arceus, Greninja should prioritize clicking Taunt, as the offensive builds that Greninja fits best on tend to struggle to have the tools to deal with these threats.
  • If it's not able to activate Battle Bond, Greninja should be used to chip away at the foe with either Dark Pulse or Ice Beam, providing its teammates with an easier time of setting up to sweep. Due to its relatively low bulk and damage output prior to activating Battle Bond, if entry hazards are on your side of the field or if its Focus Sash has been broken, Greninja is best used as a sacrifice fodder to provide you with an opportunity to bring in a teammate without taking any extra damage.
  • If Greninja is able to activate Battle Bond, it can be preserved, as it can become a potential revenge killer for weakened foes, as it's only naturally outsped by Deoxys-A, Pheromosa, and Mega Mewtwo Y, and it's able to outspeed a +1 Zygarde.

Team Options

  • As Greninja's primary role is to provide offensive pressure by setting Spikes and it is only really used as a dedicated lead, its teammates need to also be offensive Pokemon to compensate for its general lack of offensive pressure and to ensure that Greninja's entry hazards stay on the battlefield after it has been KOed.
  • Strong wallbreakers such as Xerneas, Necrozma-DM or Ultra Necrozma, and Mega Salamence are all incredible partners for Greninja, as the addition of Spikes on the battlefield makes it harder for opposing Pokemon to switch into them. Futhermore, all of these Pokemon are able to punish any attempts to remove entry hazards by setting up with their dedicated boosting move, ultimately making them harder to switch into.
  • Checks to the tier's Magic Bounce users in Mega Sableye and Mega Diancie as well as Fairy-type answers are crucial teammates for Greninja, as Magic Bounce completely removes Greninja's ability to set entry hazards.
  • Offensive Stealth Rock Primal Groudon sets are almost mandatory on teams with Greninja, as Stealth Rock is still able to punish all Ground-immune foes that take no damage from Spikes such as Yveltal, Ho-Oh, and Lugia, providing additional damage to grounded foes. Furthermore, it is able to provide teams with a much-needed answer to Xerneas and is able to comfortably anti-lead against Mega Sableye and Mega Diancie.
